And the waning which takes place in the first portal in its season, till one hundred and seventy-seven days are accomplished, reckoned according to weeks, twenty-five weeks and two days.
And so the year is accurately completed in conformity with their world-stations and the stations of the moon, and the stations of the sun, which rise and set in those portals, for thirty days each.

And in those days the angel Uriel answered and said to me: Behold, I have shown you everything, Chanokh, and I have revealed everything to you that you should see this sun and this moon, and the leaders of the stars of the heaven and all those who turn them, their tasks and times and departures.

And in the days of the sinners the years shall be shortened, and their seed shall be tardy on their lands and fields, and all things on the earth shall alter, and shall not appear in their time, and the rain shall be kept back and the heaven shall withhold it.
And in those times the fruits of the earth shall be backward, and shall not grow in their time, and the fruits of the trees shall be withheld in their time.
And the moon shall alter her order, and not appear at her time.
And in those days the sun shall be seen and he shall journey in the evening on the extremity of the great chariot in the west and shall shine more brightly than accords with the order of light.
And many chiefs of the stars shall transgress the order prescribed, and these shall alter their orbits and tasks, and not appear at the seasons prescribed to them.

And the whole order of the stars shall be concealed from the sinners, and the thoughts of those on the earth shall err concerning them, and they shall be altered from all their ways — yea, they shall err and take them to be deities.
And he said unto me: Chanokh, look at the book of the tablets of heaven, and read what is written thereon, and mark every individual fact.

And I looked at everything in the tablets of heaven, and I read everything which was written thereon and understood everything, and read the book of all the deeds of men, and of all the children of flesh that shall be upon the earth to the remotest generations.

And forthwith I blessed the great Creator the King of Glory for ever, in that he has made all the works of the world, and I praised YHWH because of his patience, and blessed him because of the children of men.
And after that I said: Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness and goodness, concerning whom there is no book of unrighteousness written, and against whom no day of judgment shall be found.

And those seven holy ones brought me and placed me on the earth before the door of my house, and said to me: Declare everything to your son Metushelakh, and show to all your children that no flesh is righteous in the sight of YHWH, for he is their Creator.

For one year we will leave you with your son, till you give your last commands, that you may teach your children and record it for them, and testify to all your children — and in the second year they shall take you from their midst.
And now, my son, go and tell your son Metushelakh all these things, and show to all your children that no flesh is righteous before YHWH, for he is their Creator.

For I will leave you one year of peace with your son, that you may give commandment to your children regarding it, and record it for them, and testify to all your children — and in the second year they shall take you from their midst.

And now, my son Metushelakh, all these things I am recounting to you and writing down for you — I have revealed to you and given you the book concerning all these things. Preserve, my son Metushelakh, the books from your father's hand, and see that you deliver them to the generations of the world.
I have given wisdom to you and to your children, and your children that shall be to you, that they may give it to their children for generations — this wisdom namely that passes their understanding.
And those who understand it shall not sleep, but shall listen with the ear that they may learn this wisdom, and it shall please those that eat thereof better than good food.

Blessed are all the righteous, blessed are all those who walk in the way of righteousness and sin not as the sinners, in the reckoning of all their days in which the sun traverses the heaven, entering into and departing from the portals for thirty days with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four which are intercalated which divide the four portions of the year, which lead them and enter with them four days.
And these are the names of those who lead them, who watch that they enter at their times, in their orders, in their seasons, in their months, in their periods of dominion, and in their positions.

Their four leaders who divide the four parts of the year enter first, and after them the twelve leaders of the orders who divide the months — and for the three hundred and sixty there are heads over thousands who divide the days, and for the four intercalary days there are the leaders which sunder the four parts of the year.
And the name of the one is Melkiel, who is named Tame'el and the sun, and the name of all those whom he leads with him are Hesfael, Keel, Peeel, and the name of their head is Kerael.
And now, my son Metushelakh, I will show you all my visions which I have seen, recounting them before you.
Two visions I saw before I took a wife, and the one was quite unlike the other — the first when I was learning to write, the second before I took your mother, when I saw a terrible vision.
And regarding them I prayed to YHWH.
I had laid me down in the house of my grandfather Mahalale'el, when I saw in a vision how the heaven collapsed and was borne off and fell to the earth.

And when it fell to the earth I saw how the earth was swallowed up in a great abyss, and mountains were suspended on mountains, and hills sank down on hills, and high trees were rent from their stems, and hurled down and sunk in the abyss.
And thereupon a word fell into my mouth, and I lifted up my voice to cry aloud, and said: The earth is destroyed.
And my grandfather Mahalale'el waked me as I lay near him, and said unto me: Why do you cry so, my son, and why do you make such lamentation?

And I recounted to him the whole vision which I had seen, and he said unto me: A terrible thing have you seen, my dear son, and of grave moment is your dream-vision as to the secrets of all the sin of the earth — it must sink into the abyss and be destroyed with a great destruction.
And now, my son, arise and make petition to the the Creator of Glory, since you are a believer, that a remnant may remain on the earth, and that he may not destroy the whole earth.
My son, from heaven all this will come upon the earth, and upon the earth there will be great destruction.
After that I arose and prayed and implored and besought, and wrote down my prayer for the generations of the world, and I will show everything to you, my son Metushelakh.
Then I fell on my face and my whole body melted, and my spirit was transfigured, and I cried with a loud voice, with the spirit of power, and blessed and glorified and extolled.
And these blessings which went forth from my mouth were well pleasing before that Head of Days.
And that Head of Days came with Mikha'el and Gavri'el, Rafa'el and Fanuel, thousands and ten thousands of angels without number.
And that angel came to me and greeted me with his voice, and said unto me: You are the man of faith to whom belongeth the word, and the light.

And when he came and greeted me with his voice, I fell before him and worshipped, and he blessed me, and said: Fear not, Chanokh, you righteous man and scribe of righteousness — approach hither and hear my voice.
Go, say to the Watchers of heaven, who have sent you to intercede for them: You should intercede for men, and not men for you.
After the death of Moshe the servant of YHWH, YHWH said to Yehoshua the son of Nun, Moshe's assistant,
Moshe my servant is dead. Now therefore arise, go over this Yarden, you and all this people, into the land that I am giving to them, to the people of Yisra'EL.
Every place that the sole of your foot will tread upon I have given to you, just as I promised to Moshe.
From the wilderness and this Lebanon as far as the great river, the river Perat, all the land of the Khittites to the Great Sea toward the going down of the sun shall be your territory.
No man shall be able to stand before you all the days of your life. Just as I was with Moshe, so I will be with you. I will not leave you or forsake you.
Be strong and courageous, for you shall cause this people to inherit the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.

Only be strong and very courageous, being careful to do according to all the Torah that Moshe my servant commanded you. Do not turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may have good success wherever you go.

This Book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do according to all that is written in it. For then you will make your way prosperous, and then you will have good success.
Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be frightened, and do not be dismayed, for YHWH your Creator is with you wherever you go.
And Yehoshua commanded the officers of the people,

Pass through the midst of the camp and command the people, Prepare your provisions, for within three days you are to pass over this Yarden to go in to take possession of the land that YHWH your Creator is giving you to possess.
And to the Reuvenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Menasheh Yehoshua said,
Remember the word that Moshe the servant of YHWH commanded you, saying, YHWH your Creator is providing you a place of rest and will give you this land.

Your wives, your little ones, and your livestock shall remain in the land that Moshe gave you beyond the Yarden, but all the men of valor among you shall pass over armed before your brothers and shall help them,

Until YHWH gives rest to your brothers as he has to you, and they also take possession of the land that YHWH your Creator is giving them. Then you shall return to the land of your possession and shall possess it, the land that Moshe the servant of YHWH gave you beyond the Yarden toward the sunrise.
And they answered Yehoshua, All that you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.
Just as we obeyed Moshe in all things, so we will obey you. Only may YHWH your Creator be with you, as he was with Moshe.
Whoever rebels against your commandment and disobeys your words, whatever you command him, shall be put to death. Only be strong and courageous.

And Yehoshua the son of Nun sent two men secretly from Shittim as spies, saying, Go, view the land, especially Yerikho. And they went and came into the house of a prostitute whose name was Rakhav and lodged there.
And it was told to the king of Yerikho, Behold, men of Yisra'EL have come here tonight to search out the land.
Then the king of Yerikho sent to Rakhav, saying, Bring out the men who have come to you, who entered your house, for they have come to search out all the land.
But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. And she said, True, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.
And when the gate was about to be closed at dark, the men went out. I do not know where the men went. Pursue them quickly, for you will overtake them.
But she had brought them up to the roof and hid them with the stalks of flax that she had laid in order on the roof.
So the men pursued after them on the way to the Yarden as far as the fords. And the gate was shut as soon as the pursuers had gone out.
Before the men lay down, she came up to them on the roof
And said to the men, I know that YHWH has given you the land, and that the fear of you has fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land melt away before you.

For we have heard how YHWH dried up the water of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Yarden, to Sikhon and Og, whom you devoted to destruction.
And as soon as we heard it, our hearts melted, and there was no spirit left in any man because of you, for YHWH your Creator, he is Creator in the heavens above and on the earth beneath.
Now then, please swear to me by YHWH that, as I have dealt kindly with you, you also will deal kindly with my father's house, and give me a sure sign
That you will save alive my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them, and deliver our lives from death.
And the men said to her, Our life for yours even to death. If you do not tell this business of ours, then when YHWH gives us the land we will deal kindly and faithfully with you.
Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was built into the city wall, so that she lived in the wall.
And she said to them, Go into the hills, or the pursuers will encounter you, and hide there three days until the pursuers have returned. Then afterward you may go your way.
The men said to her, We will be guiltless with respect to this oath of yours that you have made us swear.

Behold, when we come into the land, you shall tie this scarlet cord in the window through which you let us down, and you shall gather into your house your father and mother, your brothers, and all your father's household.

Then if anyone goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood shall be on his own head, and we shall be guiltless. But if a hand is laid on anyone who is with you in the house, his blood shall be on our head.
But if you tell this business of ours, then we shall be guiltless with respect to your oath that you have made us swear.
And she said, According to your words, so be it. Then she sent them away, and they departed. And she tied the scarlet cord in the window.
They departed and went into the hills and remained there three days until the pursuers returned, and the pursuers searched all along the way and found nothing.
Then the two men returned. They came down from the hills and passed over and came to Yehoshua the son of Nun, and they told him all that had happened to them.
And they said to Yehoshua, Truly YHWH has given all the land into our hands. And also, all the inhabitants of the land melt away because of us.
Then Yehoshua rose early in the morning and they set out from Shittim. And they came to the Yarden, he and all the people of Yisra'EL, and lodged there before they passed over.
At the end of three days the officers went through the camp
And commanded the people, As soon as you see the Ark of the Covenant of YHWH your Creator being carried by the Levitical priests, then you shall set out from your place and follow it.
Yet there shall be a distance between you and it, about 2,000 cubits in length. Do not come near it, in order that you may know the way you shall go, for you have not passed this way before.
Then Yehoshua said to the people, Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow YHWH will do wonders among you.
And Yehoshua said to the priests, Take up the Ark of the Covenant and pass on before the people. So they took up the Ark of the Covenant and went before the people.
YHWH said to Yehoshua, Today I will begin to exalt you in the sight of all Yisra'EL, that they may know that, as I was with Moshe, so I will be with you.
And as for you, command the priests who bear the Ark of the Covenant, When you come to the brink of the waters of the Yarden, you shall stand still in the Yarden.
And Yehoshua said to the people of Yisra'EL, Come here and hear the words of YHWH your Creator.

And Yehoshua said, Here is how you shall know that the living Creator is among you and that he will without fail drive out from before you the Kena'anites, the Khittites, the Khivvites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Yevusites.
Behold, the Ark of the Covenant of the YHWH of all the earth is passing over before you into the Yarden.
Now therefore take twelve men from the tribes of Yisra'EL, from each tribe a man.

And when the soles of the feet of the priests bearing the Ark of YHWH, the YHWH of all the earth, shall rest in the waters of the Yarden, the waters of the Yarden shall be cut off from flowing, and the waters coming down from above shall stand in one heap.
So when the people set out from their tents to pass over the Yarden with the priests bearing the Ark of the Covenant before the people,

And as soon as those bearing the Ark had come as far as the Yarden, and the feet of the priests bearing the Ark were dipped in the brink of the water — now the Yarden overflows all its banks throughout the time of harvest —

The waters coming down from above stood and rose up in a heap very far away, at Adam, the city that is beside Tzaretan, and those flowing down toward the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, were completely cut off. And the people passed over opposite Yerikho.

Now the priests bearing the Ark of the Covenant of YHWH stood firmly on dry ground in the midst of the Yarden, and all Yisra'EL was passing over on dry ground until all the nation finished passing over the Yarden.
When all the nation had finished passing over the Yarden, YHWH said to Yehoshua,
Take twelve men from the people, from each tribe a man,

And command them, saying, Take twelve stones from here out of the midst of the Yarden, from the very place where the priests' feet stood firmly, and bring them over with you and lay them down in the place where you lodge tonight.
Then Yehoshua called the twelve men from the people of Yisra'EL, whom he had appointed, a man from each tribe.

And Yehoshua said to them, Pass on before the Ark of YHWH your Creator into the midst of the Yarden, and take up each of you a stone upon his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the people of Yisra'EL,
That this may be a sign among you. When your children ask in time to come, What do those stones mean to you?

Then you shall tell them that the waters of the Yarden were cut off before the Ark of the Covenant of YHWH. When it passed over the Yarden, the waters of the Yarden were cut off. So these stones shall be to the people of Yisra'EL a memorial forever.

And the people of Yisra'EL did just as Yehoshua commanded and took up twelve stones out of the midst of the Yarden, according to the number of the tribes of the people of Yisra'EL, just as YHWH told Yehoshua. And they carried them over with them to the place where they lodged and laid them down there.
And Yehoshua set up twelve stones in the midst of the Yarden, in the place where the feet of the priests bearing the Ark of the Covenant had stood. And they are there to this day.

For the priests bearing the Ark stood in the midst of the Yarden until everything was finished that YHWH commanded Yehoshua to tell the people, according to all that Moshe had commanded Yehoshua. The people passed over in haste.
And when all the people had finished passing over, the Ark of YHWH and the priests passed over before the people.
The sons of Reuven and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh passed over armed before the people of Yisra'EL, as Moshe had told them.
About 40,000 ready for war passed over before YHWH for battle, to the plains of Yerikho.
On that day YHWH exalted Yehoshua in the sight of all Yisra'EL, and they stood in awe of him just as they had stood in awe of Moshe, all the days of his life.
And YHWH said to Yehoshua,
Command the priests bearing the Ark of the Testimony to come up out of the Yarden.
So Yehoshua commanded the priests, Come up out of the Yarden.

And when the priests bearing the Ark of the Covenant of YHWH came up from the midst of the Yarden, and the soles of the priests' feet were lifted up on dry ground, the waters of the Yarden returned to their place and overflowed all its banks, as before.
The people came up out of the Yarden on the tenth day of the first month, and they encamped at Gilgal on the east border of Yerikho.
And those twelve stones, which they took out of the Yarden, Yehoshua set up at Gilgal.
And he said to the people of Yisra'EL, When your children ask their fathers in times to come, What do these stones mean?
Then you shall let your children know, Yisra'EL passed over this Yarden on dry ground.
For YHWH your Creator dried up the waters of the Yarden for you until you passed over, as YHWH your Creator did to the Red Sea, which he dried up for us until we passed over,
So that all the peoples of the earth may know that the hand of YHWH is mighty, that you may fear YHWH your Creator forever.

As soon as all the kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Yarden to the west, and all the kings of the Kena'anites who were by the sea, heard that YHWH had dried up the waters of the Yarden for the people of Yisra'EL until they had crossed over, their hearts melted and there was no longer any spirit in them because of the people of Yisra'EL.
At that time YHWH said to Yehoshua, Make flint knives and circumcise the sons of Yisra'EL again the second time.
So Yehoshua made flint knives and circumcised the sons of Yisra'EL at Giv'at Ha'aralot.
And this is the reason why Yehoshua circumcised them: all the males of the people who came out of Egypt, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way after they had come out of Egypt.
Though all the people who came out had been circumcised, yet all the people who were born on the way in the wilderness after they had come out of Egypt had not been circumcised.

For the people of Yisra'EL walked forty years in the wilderness, until all the nation, the men of war who came out of Egypt, perished, because they did not obey the voice of YHWH. YHWH swore to them that he would not let them see the land that YHWH had sworn to their fathers to give to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
So it was their children, whom he raised up in their place, that Yehoshua circumcised. For they were uncircumcised, because they had not been circumcised on the way.
When the circumcising of the whole nation was finished, they remained in their places in the camp until they were healed.
And YHWH said to Yehoshua, Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you. And so the name of that place is called Gilgal to this day.
While the people of Yisra'EL were encamped at Gilgal, they kept the Pesach on the fourteenth day of the month in the evening on the plains of Yerikho.
And the day after the Pesach, on that very day, they ate of the produce of the land, unleavened cakes and parched grain.
And the manna ceased the day after they ate of the produce of the land. And there was no longer manna for the people of Yisra'EL, but they ate of the fruit of the land of Kena'an that year.

When Yehoshua was by Yerikho, he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man was standing before him with his drawn sword in his hand. And Yehoshua went to him and said to him, Are you for us, or for our adversaries?
And he said, No, but I am the commander of the army of YHWH. Now I have come. And Yehoshua fell on his face to the earth and worshiped and said to him, What does my Sovereign say to his servant?
And the commander of the army of YHWH said to Yehoshua, Take off your sandals from your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy. And Yehoshua did so.
Now Yerikho was shut up inside and outside because of the people of Yisra'EL. None went out, and none came in.
And YHWH said to Yehoshua, See, I have given Yerikho into your hand, with its king and mighty men of valor.
You shall march around the city, all the men of war going around the city once. Thus shall you do for six days.
Seven priests shall bear seven trumpets of rams' horns before the Ark. On the seventh day you shall march around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the trumpets.

And when they make a long blast with the ram's horn, when you hear the sound of the trumpet, then all the people shall shout with a great shout, and the wall of the city will fall down flat, and the people shall go up, everyone straight before him.
So Yehoshua the son of Nun called the priests and said to them, Take up the Ark of the Covenant and let seven priests bear seven trumpets of rams' horns before the Ark of YHWH.
And he said to the people, Go forward. March around the city and let the armed men pass on before the Ark of YHWH.

And just as Yehoshua had commanded the people, the seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams' horns before YHWH went forward, blowing the trumpets, with the Ark of the Covenant of YHWH following them.
The armed men were walking before the priests who were blowing the trumpets, and the rear guard was walking after the Ark, while the trumpets blew continually.
But Yehoshua commanded the people, You shall not shout or make your voice heard, neither shall any word go out of your mouth, until the day I tell you to shout. Then you shall shout.
So he caused the Ark of YHWH to circle the city, going about it once. And they came into the camp and spent the night in the camp.
Then Yehoshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the Ark of YHWH.

And the seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams' horns before the Ark of YHWH walked on, and they blew the trumpets continually. And the armed men were walking before them, and the rear guard was walking after the Ark of YHWH, while the trumpets blew continually.
And the second day they marched around the city once, and returned into the camp. So they did for six days.
On the seventh day they rose early, at the dawn of day, and marched around the city in the same manner seven times. It was only on that day that they marched around the city seven times.
And at the seventh time, when the priests had blown the trumpets, Yehoshua said to the people, Shout, for YHWH has given you the city.

And the city and all that is within it shall be devoted to YHWH for destruction. Only Rakhav the prostitute and all who are with her in her house shall live, because she hid the messengers whom we sent.

But you, keep yourselves from the things devoted to destruction, lest when you have devoted them you take any of the devoted things and make the camp of Yisra'EL a thing for destruction and bring trouble upon it.
But all silver and gold, and every vessel of bronze and iron, are holy to YHWH. They shall go into the treasury of YHWH.

So the people shouted, and the trumpets were blown. As soon as the people heard the sound of the trumpet, the people shouted a great shout, and the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they captured the city.
Then they devoted all in the city to destruction, both men and women, young and old, oxen, sheep, and donkeys, with the edge of the sword.
But to the two men who had spied out the land, Yehoshua said, Go into the prostitute's house and bring out from there the woman and all who belong to her, as you swore to her.

So the young men who had been spies went in and brought out Rakhav and her father and mother and brothers and all who belonged to her. And they brought all her relatives and put them outside the camp of Yisra'EL.
And they burned the city with fire, and everything in it. Only the silver and gold, and the vessels of bronze and of iron, they put into the treasury of the house of YHWH.

But Rakhav the prostitute and her father's household and all who belonged to her, Yehoshua saved alive. And she has lived in the midst of Yisra'EL to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Yehoshua sent to spy out Yerikho.

Yehoshua laid an oath on them at that time, saying, Cursed before YHWH be the man who rises up and rebuilds this city, Yerikho. At the cost of his firstborn shall he lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest son shall he set up its gates.
So YHWH was with Yehoshua, and his fame was in all the land.

But the people of Yisra'EL broke faith in regard to the devoted things, for Akhan the son of Karmi, son of Zavdi, son of Zerakhi, of the tribe of Yehudah, took some of the devoted things. And the anger of YHWH burned against the people of Yisra'EL.
Yehoshua sent men from Yerikho to Ai, which is near Beit-Aven, east of Beit-El, and said to them, Go up and spy out the land. And the men went up and spied out Ai.

And they returned to Yehoshua and said to him, Do not have all the people go up, but let about two or three thousand men go up and attack Ai. Do not make the whole people toil up there, for they are few.
So about three thousand men went up there from the people. And they fled before the men of Ai,
And the men of Ai killed about thirty-six of their men and chased them before the gate as far as Shevarim and struck them at the descent. And the hearts of the people melted and became as water.
Then Yehoshua tore his clothes and fell to the earth on his face before the Ark of YHWH until the evening, he and the elders of Yisra'EL. And they put dust on their heads.

And Yehoshua said, Alas, O YHWH Creator, why have you brought this people over the Yarden at all, to give us into the hands of the Amorites, to destroy us? Would that we had been content to dwell beyond the Yarden.
O YHWH, what can I say, when Yisra'EL has turned their backs before their enemies?
For the Kena'anites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it and will surround us and cut off our name from the earth. And what will you do for your great name?
YHWH said to Yehoshua, Get up. Why have you fallen on your face?
Yisra'EL has sinned — they have transgressed my covenant that I commanded them — they have taken some of the devoted things — they have stolen and lied and put them among their own belongings.

Therefore the people of Yisra'EL cannot stand before their enemies. They turn their backs before their enemies, because they have become devoted for destruction. I will be with you no more, unless you destroy the devoted things from among you.

Get up. Consecrate the people and say, Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow — for thus says YHWH, Creator of Yisra'EL: There are devoted things in your midst, O Yisra'EL. You cannot stand before your enemies until you take away the devoted things from among you.

In the morning therefore you shall be brought near by your tribes. And the tribe that YHWH takes by lot shall come near by clans. And the clan that YHWH takes shall come near by households. And the household that YHWH takes shall come near man by man.

And he who is taken with the devoted things shall be burned with fire, he and all that he has, because he has transgressed the covenant of YHWH, and because he has done an outrageous thing in Yisra'EL.
So Yehoshua rose early in the morning and brought Yisra'EL near tribe by tribe, and the tribe of Yehudah was taken.
And he brought near the clans of Yehudah, and the clan of the Zerakhites was taken. And he brought near the clan of the Zerakhites man by man, and Zavdi was taken.
And he brought near his household man by man, and Akhan the son of Karmi, son of Zavdi, son of Zerakhi, of the tribe of Yehudah, was taken.
Then Yehoshua said to Akhan, My son, give glory to YHWH Creator of Yisra'EL and give praise to him. And tell me now what you have done — do not hide it from me.
And Akhan answered Yehoshua, Truly I have sinned against YHWH Creator of Yisra'EL, and this is what I did:

When I saw among the spoil a beautiful cloak from Shinar, and 200 shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing 50 shekels, then I coveted them and took them. And see, they are hidden in the earth inside my tent, with the silver underneath.
So Yehoshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. And behold, it was hidden in his tent with the silver underneath.
And they took them out of the tent and brought them to Yehoshua and to all the people of Yisra'EL. And they laid them down before YHWH.

And Yehoshua and all Yisra'EL with him took Akhan the son of Zerakhi, and the silver and the cloak and the bar of gold, and his sons and daughters and his oxen and donkeys and sheep and his tent and all that he had. And they brought them up to the Valley of Akhor.
And Yehoshua said, Why did you bring trouble on us? YHWH brings trouble on you today. And all Yisra'EL stoned him with stones. They burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.
And they raised over him a great heap of stones that remains to this day. Then YHWH turned from his burning anger. Therefore, to this day the name of that place is called the Valley of Akhor.

And YHWH said to Yehoshua, Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Take all the fighting men with you, and arise, go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, and his people, his city, and his land.
And you shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Yerikho and its king. Only its spoil and its livestock you shall take as plunder for yourselves. Lay an ambush against the city, behind it.
So Yehoshua and all the fighting men arose to go up to Ai. And Yehoshua chose 30,000 mighty men of valor and sent them out by night.
And he commanded them, Behold, you shall lie in ambush against the city, behind it. Do not go very far from the city, but all of you remain ready.
And I and all the people who are with me will approach the city. And when they come out against us just as before, we shall flee before them.
And they will come out after us, until we have drawn them away from the city. For they will say, They are fleeing from us, just as before. So we will flee before them.
Then you shall rise up from the ambush and seize the city, for YHWH your Creator will give it into your hand.
And as soon as you have taken the city, you shall set the city on fire. You shall do according to the word of YHWH. See, I have commanded you.
So Yehoshua sent them out. And they went to the place of ambush and lay between Beit-El and Ai, to the west of Ai, but Yehoshua spent that night among the people.
Yehoshua arose early in the morning and mustered the people and went up, he and the elders of Yisra'EL, before the people to Ai.
And all the fighting men who were with him went up and drew near before the city and encamped on the north side of Ai, with a ravine between them and Ai.
He took about 5,000 men and set them in ambush between Beit-El and Ai, to the west of the city.
So they stationed the forces, the main encampment that was north of the city and its rear guard west of the city. But Yehoshua spent that night in the valley.

And as soon as the king of Ai saw this, he and all his people, the men of the city, hurried and went out early to the appointed place toward the Aravah to meet Yisra'EL in battle. But he did not know that there was an ambush against him behind the city.
And Yehoshua and all Yisra'EL pretended to be beaten before them and fled in the direction of the wilderness.
So all the people who were in the city were called together to pursue them, and as they pursued Yehoshua they were drawn away from the city.
Not a man was left in Ai or Beit-El who did not go out after Yisra'EL. They left the city open and pursued Yisra'EL.
Then YHWH said to Yehoshua, Stretch out the javelin that is in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand. And Yehoshua stretched out the javelin that was in his hand toward the city.
And the men in the ambush rose quickly out of their place, and as soon as he had stretched out his hand, they ran and entered the city and captured it. And they hurried to set the city on fire.

So when the men of Ai looked back, behold, the smoke of the city went up to heaven, and they had no power to flee this way or that, for the people who fled to the wilderness turned back against the pursuers.
And when Yehoshua and all Yisra'EL saw that the men in the ambush had captured the city, and that the smoke of the city went up, then they turned back and struck down the men of Ai.

And the others came out from the city against them, so they were in the midst of Yisra'EL, some on this side, and some on that side. And Yisra'EL struck them down, until there was left none that survived or escaped.
But the king of Ai they took alive, and brought him near to Yehoshua.

When Yisra'EL had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the open wilderness where they pursued them, and all of them to the very last had fallen by the edge of the sword, all Yisra'EL returned to Ai and struck it down with the edge of the sword.
And all who fell that day, both men and women, were 12,000, all the people of Ai.
But Yehoshua did not draw back his hand with which he stretched out the javelin until he had devoted all the inhabitants of Ai to destruction.
Only the livestock and the spoil of that city Yisra'EL took as their plunder, according to the word of YHWH that he commanded Yehoshua.
So Yehoshua burned Ai and made it forever a heap of ruins, as it is to this day.

And he hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening. And at sunset Yehoshua commanded, and they took his body down from the tree and threw it at the entrance of the gate of the city and raised over it a great heap of stones, which stands there to this day.
At that time Yehoshua built an altar to YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, on Mount Eval,

Just as Moshe the servant of YHWH had commanded the people of Yisra'EL, as it is written in the Book of the Torah of Moshe, an altar of uncut stones, upon which no man has wielded an iron tool. And they offered on it burnt offerings to YHWH and sacrificed peace offerings.
And there, in the presence of the people of Yisra'EL, he wrote on the stones a copy of the Torah of Moshe, which he had written.

And all Yisra'EL, sojourner as well as native born, with their elders and officers and their judges, stood on opposite sides of the Ark before the Levitical priests who carried the Ark of the Covenant of YHWH, half of them in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Eval, just as Moshe the servant of YHWH had commanded at the first, to bless the people of Yisra'EL.
And afterward he read all the words of the Torah, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the Book of the Torah.
There was not a word of all that Moshe commanded that Yehoshua did not read before all the assembly of Yisra'EL, and the women, and the little ones, and the sojourners who lived among them.

When all the kings who were beyond the Yarden, in the hill country and in the lowland and all the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon, the Khittites, the Amorites, the Kena'anites, the Perizzites, the Khivvites, and the Yevusites, heard of this,
They gathered together with one accord to fight against Yehoshua and Yisra'EL.
But when the inhabitants of Giv'on heard what Yehoshua had done to Yerikho and to Ai,
They on their part acted with cunning and went and made ready provisions and took worn-out sacks for their donkeys, and wineskins, worn-out and torn and mended,
With worn-out, patched sandals on their feet, and worn-out clothes. And all their provisions were dry and crumbly.
And they went to Yehoshua in the camp at Gilgal and said to him and to the men of Yisra'EL, We have come from a distant country, so now make a covenant with us.
But the men of Yisra'EL said to the Khivvites, Perhaps you live among us — then how can we make a covenant with you?
They said to Yehoshua, We are your servants. And Yehoshua said to them, Who are you? And where do you come from?
They said to him, From a very distant country your servants have come, because of the name of YHWH your Creator. For we have heard a report of him, and all that he did in Egypt,
And all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Yarden, Sikhon the king of Kheshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtarot.

So our elders and all the inhabitants of our country said to us, Take provisions in your hand for the journey and go to meet them and say to them, We are your servants. Come now, make a covenant with us.
Here is our bread. It was still warm when we took it from our houses as our food for the journey on the day we set out to come to you, but now, behold, it is dry and crumbly.
These wineskins were new when we filled them, and behold, they have burst. And these garments and sandals of ours are worn out from the very long journey.
So the men took some of their provisions, but did not ask counsel from the mouth of YHWH.
And Yehoshua made peace with them and made a covenant with them, to let them live, and the leaders of the congregation swore to them.
At the end of three days after they had made a covenant with them, they heard that they were their neighbors and that they lived among them.
And the people of Yisra'EL set out and reached their cities on the third day. Now their cities were Giv'on, Kefira, Be'erot, and Kiryat-Ye'arim.
But the people of Yisra'EL did not attack them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them by YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL. Then all the congregation murmured against the leaders.
But all the leaders said to all the congregation, We have sworn to them by YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, and now we may not touch them.
This we will do to them: let them live, lest wrath come upon us, because of the oath that we swore to them.
And the leaders said to them, Let them live. So they became cutters of wood and drawers of water for all the congregation, just as the leaders had said of them.
Yehoshua summoned them, and he said to them, Why did you deceive us, saying, We are very far from you, when you dwell among us?
Now therefore you are cursed, and some of you shall never be anything but servants, cutters of wood and drawers of water for the house of my Creator.

They answered Yehoshua, Because it was told to your servants for a certainty that YHWH your Creator had commanded his servant Moshe to give you all the land and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land from before you — so we feared greatly for our lives because of you and did this thing.
And now, behold, we are in your hand. Whatever seems good and right in your sight to do to us, do it.
So he did this to them and delivered them out of the hand of the people of Yisra'EL, and they did not kill them.
But Yehoshua made them that day cutters of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of YHWH, to this day, in the place that he should choose.

As soon as Adoni-Tzedek king of Yerushalayim heard how Yehoshua had captured Ai and had devoted it to destruction, doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Yerikho and its king, and how the inhabitants of Giv'on had made peace with Yisra'EL and were among them,
He feared greatly, because Giv'on was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all its men were warriors.
So Adoni-Tzedek king of Yerushalayim sent to Hoham king of Khevron, to Piram king of Yarmut, to Yafiya king of Lakhish, and to Devir king of Eglon, saying,
Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Giv'on. For it has made peace with Yehoshua and with the people of Yisra'EL.

Then the five kings of the Amorites, the king of Yerushalayim, the king of Khevron, the king of Yarmut, the king of Lakhish, and the king of Eglon, gathered their forces and went up with all their armies and encamped against Giv'on and made war against it.

And the men of Giv'on sent to Yehoshua at the camp in Gilgal, saying, Do not relax your hand from your servants. Come up to us quickly and save us and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who dwell in the hill country are gathered against us.
So Yehoshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty men of valor.
And YHWH said to Yehoshua, Do not fear them, for I have given them into your hands. Not a man of them shall stand before you.
So Yehoshua came upon them suddenly, having marched up all night from Gilgal.
And YHWH threw them into a panic before Yisra'EL, who struck them with a great blow at Giv'on and chased them by the way of the ascent of Beit-Kharon and struck them as far as Azekah and Maqkedah.

And as they fled before Yisra'EL, while they were going down the ascent of Beit-Kharon, YHWH threw down large stones from heaven on them as far as Azekah, and they died. There were more who died because of the hailstones than the sons of Yisra'EL killed with the sword.

At that time Yehoshua spoke to YHWH in the day when YHWH gave the Amorites over to the sons of Yisra'EL, and he said in the sight of Yisra'EL, Sun, stand still at Giv'on, and moon, in the Valley of Ayalon.

And the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation took vengeance on their enemies. Is this not written in the Book of the Upright? The sun stopped in the midst of heaven and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.
There has been no day like it before or since, when YHWH heeded the voice of a man, for YHWH fought for Yisra'EL.
So Yehoshua returned, and all Yisra'EL with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
These five kings fled and hid themselves in the cave at Maqkedah.
And it was told to Yehoshua, The five kings have been found, hidden in the cave at Maqkedah.
And Yehoshua said, Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave and set men by it to guard them,
But do not stay there yourselves. Pursue your enemies — attack their rear guard. Do not let them enter their cities, for YHWH your Creator has given them into your hand.
When Yehoshua and the sons of Yisra'EL had finished striking them with a great blow until they were wiped out, and when the remnant that remained of them had entered into the fortified cities,
All the people returned safe to Yehoshua in the camp at Maqkedah. Not a man moved his tongue against any of the people of Yisra'EL.
Then Yehoshua said, Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me from the cave.
And they did so, and brought those five kings out to him from the cave, the king of Yerushalayim, the king of Khevron, the king of Yarmut, the king of Lakhish, and the king of Eglon.

And when they brought those kings out to Yehoshua, Yehoshua summoned all the men of Yisra'EL and said to the chiefs of the men of war who had gone with him, Come near and put your feet on the necks of these kings. And they came near and put their feet on their necks.
And Yehoshua said to them, Do not be afraid or dismayed — be strong and courageous. For thus YHWH will do to all your enemies against whom you fight.
And afterward Yehoshua struck them and put them to death, and he hanged them on five trees. And they hung on the trees until evening.

But at the time of the going down of the sun, Yehoshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden themselves, and they set large stones against the mouth of the cave, which remain to this very day.

As for Maqkedah, Yehoshua captured it on that day and struck it, and its king, with the edge of the sword. He devoted to destruction every person in it — he left none remaining. And he did to the king of Maqkedah just as he had done to the king of Yerikho.
Then Yehoshua and all Yisra'EL with him passed on from Maqkedah to Livnah and fought against Livnah.

And YHWH gave it also and its king into the hand of Yisra'EL. And he struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person in it — he left none remaining in it. And he did to its king as he had done to the king of Yerikho.
Then Yehoshua and all Yisra'EL with him passed on from Livnah to Lakhish and laid siege to it and fought against it.
And YHWH gave Lakhish into the hand of Yisra'EL, and he captured it on the second day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person in it, as he had done to Livnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lakhish. And Yehoshua struck him and his people, until he left none remaining.
Then Yehoshua and all Yisra'EL with him passed on from Lakhish to Eglon. And they laid siege to it and fought against it.
And they captured it on that day, and struck it with the edge of the sword. And every person in it he devoted to destruction that day, as he had done to Lakhish.
Then Yehoshua and all Yisra'EL with him went up from Eglon to Khevron. And they fought against it

And captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king and its towns, and every person in it. He left none remaining, as he had done to Eglon, and devoted it to destruction and every person in it.
Then Yehoshua and all Yisra'EL with him turned back to Devir and fought against it

And he captured it with its king and all its towns. And they struck them with the edge of the sword and devoted to destruction every person in it — he left none remaining. Just as he had done to Khevron and to Livnah and its king, so he did to Devir and to its king.

So Yehoshua struck the whole land, the hill country and the Negev and the lowland and the slopes, and all their kings. He left none remaining, but devoted to destruction all that breathed, just as YHWH Creator of Yisra'EL commanded.
And Yehoshua struck them from Kadesh-Barnea as far as Azzah, and all the country of Goshen, as far as Giv'on.
And Yehoshua captured all these kings and their land at one time, because YHWH Creator of Yisra'EL fought for Yisra'EL.
Then Yehoshua returned, and all Yisra'EL with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
When Yavin king of Khatzor heard of this, he sent to Yovav king of Madon, and to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Akhshaph,
And to the kings who were in the northern hill country, and in the Aravah south of Kinneroth, and in the lowland, and in Naphot-Dor on the west,
To the Kena'anites in the east and the west, the Amorites, the Khittites, the Perizzites, and the Yevusites in the hill country, and the Khivvites under Hermon in the land of Mitzpah.
And they came out with all their troops, a great horde, in number like the sand that is on the seashore, with very many horses and chariots.
And all these kings joined their forces and came and encamped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Yisra'EL.
And YHWH said to Yehoshua, Do not be afraid of them, for tomorrow at this time I will give over all of them, slain, to Yisra'EL. You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.
So Yehoshua and all his warriors came suddenly against them by the waters of Merom and fell upon them.

And YHWH gave them into the hand of Yisra'EL, who struck them and chased them as far as Great Tzidon and Misrephot-Maim, and eastward as far as the Valley of Mitzpeh. And they struck them until he left none remaining.
And Yehoshua did to them just as YHWH said to him — he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
And Yehoshua turned back at that time and captured Khatzor and struck its king with the sword, for Khatzor formerly was the head of all those kingdoms.
And they struck with the sword all who were in it, devoting them to destruction — there was none left that breathed. And he burned Khatzor with fire.
And Yehoshua captured all the cities of those kings, and all their kings, and struck them with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction, just as Moshe the servant of YHWH had commanded.
But none of the cities that stood on mounds did Yisra'EL burn, except Khatzor alone — that Yehoshua burned.

And all the spoil of these cities and the livestock, the people of Yisra'EL took for their plunder. But every person they struck with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them, and they did not leave any who breathed.
Just as YHWH had commanded Moshe his servant, so Moshe commanded Yehoshua, and so Yehoshua did. He left nothing undone of all that YHWH had commanded Moshe.
So Yehoshua took all that land, the hill country and all the Negev and all the land of Goshen and the lowland and the Aravah and the hill country of Yisra'EL and its lowland
From Mount Khalak, which rises toward Se'ir, as far as Ba'al-Gad in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon. And he captured all their kings and struck them and put them to death.
Yehoshua made war a long time with all those kings.
There was not a city that made peace with the people of Yisra'EL except the Khivvites, the inhabitants of Giv'on. They took all in battle.

For it was YHWH's doing to harden their hearts that they should come against Yisra'EL in battle, in order that they should be devoted to destruction and should receive no mercy but be destroyed, just as YHWH commanded Moshe.

And Yehoshua came at that time and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Khevron, from Devir, from Anav, and from all the hill country of Yehudah, and from all the hill country of Yisra'EL. Yehoshua devoted them to destruction with their cities.
There was none of the Anakim left in the land of the people of Yisra'EL. Only in Azzah, in Gat, and in Ashdod did some remain.

So Yehoshua took the whole land, according to all that YHWH had spoken to Moshe. And Yehoshua gave it for an inheritance to Yisra'EL according to their tribal allotments. And the land had rest from war.

Now these are the kings of the land whom the people of Yisra'EL defeated and took possession of their land beyond the Yarden toward the sunrise, from the Valley of Arnon to Mount Hermon, with all the Aravah to the east:

Sikhon king of the Amorites who lived at Kheshbon and ruled from Aro'er, which is on the edge of the Valley of Arnon, and from the middle of the valley as far as the river Yabbok, the boundary of the Ammonites, that is, half of Gil'ad,
And the Aravah to the Sea of Kinneroth eastward, and in the direction of Beit-Yeshimot, to the Sea of the Aravah, the Salt Sea, southward to the foot of the slopes of Pisgah.
And Og king of Bashan, one of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtarot and at Edre'i
And ruled over Mount Hermon and Salkhah and all Bashan to the boundary of the Geshurites and the Ma'akhathites, and over half of Gil'ad to the boundary of Sikhon king of Kheshbon.
Moshe, the servant of YHWH, and the people of Yisra'EL defeated them. And Moshe the servant of YHWH gave their land for a possession to the Reuvenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Menasheh.

And these are the kings of the land whom Yehoshua and the people of Yisra'EL defeated on the west side of the Yarden, from Ba'al-Gad in the Valley of Lebanon to Mount Khalak, that rises toward Se'ir — and Yehoshua gave their land to the tribes of Yisra'EL as a possession according to their allotments,

In the hill country, in the lowland, in the Aravah, in the slopes, in the wilderness, and in the Negev, the land of the Khittites, the Amorites, the Kena'anites, the Perizzites, the Khivvites, and the Yevusites:
The king of Yerikho, one — the king of Ai, which is beside Beit-El, one —
The king of Yerushalayim, one — the king of Khevron, one —
The king of Yarmut, one — the king of Lakhish, one —
The king of Eglon, one — the king of Gezer, one —
The king of Devir, one — the king of Geder, one —
The king of Khormah, one — the king of Arad, one —
The king of Livnah, one — the king of Adullam, one —
The king of Maqkedah, one — the king of Beit-El, one —
The king of Tappuakh, one — the king of Khefer, one —
The king of Afek, one — the king of Lashsharon, one —
The king of Madon, one — the king of Khatzor, one —
The king of Shimron-Meron, one — the king of Akhshaph, one —
The king of Ta'anakh, one — the king of Megiddo, one —
The king of Kedesh, one — the king of Yokne'am in Karmel, one —
The king of Dor in Naphot-Dor, one — the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one —
The king of Tirzah, one — in all, thirty-one kings.
Now Yehoshua was old and advanced in years, and YHWH said to him, You are old and advanced in years, and there remains yet very much land to possess.
This is the land that yet remains: all the regions of the Pelishtim, and all those of the Geshurites

From the Shihor, which is east of Egypt, northward to the boundary of Ekron, it is counted as Kena'anite — the five lords of the Pelishtim, those of Azzah, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gat, and Ekron, and those of the Avvim,
In the south, all the land of the Kena'anites, and Me'arah that belongs to the Tzidonians, to Afek, to the boundary of the Amorites,
And the land of the Giblites, and all Lebanon, toward the sunrise, from Ba'al-Gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-Khamath,

All the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephot-Maim, even all the Tzidonians. I myself will drive them out from before the people of Yisra'EL. Only allot the land to Yisra'EL for an inheritance, as I have commanded you.
Now therefore divide this land for an inheritance to the nine tribes and half the tribe of Menasheh.
With the other half of Menasheh the Reuvenites and the Gadites received their inheritance, which Moshe gave them, beyond the Yarden eastward, as Moshe the servant of YHWH gave them:
From Aro'er, which is on the edge of the Valley of Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the tableland of Medeva as far as Divon,
And all the cities of Sikhon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Kheshbon, as far as the boundary of the Ammonites,
And Gil'ad, and the region of the Geshurites and Ma'akhathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan to Salkhah,
All the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtarot and in Edre'i — he alone was left of the remnant of the Rephaim — these Moshe had defeated and driven out.
Yet the people of Yisra'EL did not drive out the Geshurites or the Ma'akhathites, but Geshur and Ma'akhat dwell in the midst of Yisra'EL to this day.
To the tribe of Levi alone Moshe gave no inheritance. The offerings by fire to YHWH Creator of Yisra'EL are their inheritance, as he said to them.
And Moshe gave an inheritance to the tribe of the people of Reuven according to their clans.
So their territory was from Aro'er, which is on the edge of the Valley of Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the tableland by Medeva,
With Kheshbon, and all its cities that are in the tableland — Divon, Bamot-Ba'al, Beit-Ba'al-Me'on,
Yahatz, Kedemot, Mefa'at,
Kiryatayim, Sivmah, Tzeret-Shakhar on the hill of the valley,
Beit-Pe'or, the slopes of Pisgah, Beit-HaYeshimot,

All the cities of the tableland, and all the kingdom of Sikhon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Kheshbon, whom Moshe defeated with the leaders of Midyan, Evi, Rekem, Tzur, Khur, and Reva, the princes of Sikhon, who lived in the land.
Bil'am also, the son of Be'or, the one who practiced divination, was killed with the sword by the people of Yisra'EL among the rest of their slain.
And the border of the people of Reuven was the Yarden as their western boundary. This was the inheritance of the people of Reuven, according to their clans with their cities and villages.
And Moshe gave an inheritance also to the tribe of Gad, to the people of Gad, according to their clans.
Their territory was Ya'zer, and all the cities of Gil'ad, and half the land of the Ammonites, to Aro'er, which is east of Rabbah,
And from Kheshbon to Ramat-Mitzpeh and Betonim, and from Makhanayim to the territory of Devir,

And in the valley Beit-Haram, Beit-Nimrah, Sukkot, and Tzafon, the rest of the kingdom of Sikhon king of Kheshbon, with the Yarden as the boundary, to the lower end of the Sea of Kinneroth, beyond the Yarden eastward.
This is the inheritance of the people of Gad according to their clans, with their cities and villages.
And Moshe gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Menasheh. It was allotted to the half-tribe of the people of Menasheh according to their clans.
Their region extended from Makhanayim, through all of Bashan, the whole kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Ya'ir, which are in Bashan, sixty cities,

And half of Gil'ad, and Ashtarot, and Edre'i, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan. These were allotted to the people of Makhir the son of Menasheh for the half of the people of Makhir according to their clans.
These are the inheritances that Moshe distributed in the plains of Moav, beyond the Yarden east of Yerikho.
But to the tribe of Levi, Moshe gave no inheritance. YHWH Creator of Yisra'EL is their inheritance, as he said to them.

These are the inheritances that the people of Yisra'EL received in the land of Kena'an, which Ele'azar the priest and Yehoshua the son of Nun and the heads of the fathers' houses of the tribes of the people of Yisra'EL gave them to inherit.
Their inheritance was by lot, just as YHWH had commanded by the hand of Moshe for the nine and one-half tribes.
For Moshe had given an inheritance to the two and one-half tribes beyond the Yarden, but to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.

For the people of Yosef were two tribes, Menasheh and Efrayim. And no portion was given to the Levites in the land, but only cities to dwell in, with their pasturelands for their livestock and their substance.
The people of Yisra'EL did as YHWH commanded Moshe — they allotted the land.

Then the people of Yehudah came to Yehoshua at Gilgal. And Kalev the son of Yefunneh the Kenizzite said to him, You know what YHWH said to Moshe the man of Creator in Kadesh-Barnea concerning you and me.
I was forty years old when Moshe the servant of YHWH sent me from Kadesh-Barnea to spy out the land, and I brought him word again as it was in my heart.
But my brothers who went up with me made the heart of the people melt — yet I wholly followed YHWH my Creator.
And Moshe swore on that day, saying, Surely the land on which your foot has trodden shall be an inheritance for you and your children forever, because you have wholly followed YHWH my Creator.

And now, behold, YHWH has kept me alive, just as he said, these forty-five years since the time that YHWH spoke this word to Moshe, while Yisra'EL walked in the wilderness. And now, behold, I am this day eighty-five years old.
I am still as strong today as I was in the day that Moshe sent me — my strength now is as my strength was then, for war and for going and coming.

So now give me this hill country of which YHWH spoke on that day, for you heard on that day how the Anakim were there, with great fortified cities. It may be that YHWH will be with me, and I shall drive them out just as YHWH said.
Then Yehoshua blessed him, and he gave Khevron to Kalev the son of Yefunneh for an inheritance.
Therefore Khevron became the inheritance of Kalev the son of Yefunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he wholly followed YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL.
Now the name of Khevron formerly was Kiryat-Arba. Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war.
The allotment for the tribe of the people of Yehudah according to their clans reached southward to the boundary of Edom, to the wilderness of Tzin at the farthest south.
And their south boundary ran from the end of the Salt Sea, from the bay that faces southward.
It goes out southward of the ascent of Akrabbim, passes along to Tzin, and goes up south of Kadesh-Barnea, along by Khetzron, up to Addar, turns about to Karka,
Passes along to Atzmon, goes out by the Brook of Egypt, and the boundary comes to an end at the sea. This shall be your south boundary.
And the east boundary is the Salt Sea, to the mouth of the Yarden. And the boundary on the north side runs from the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Yarden.
And the boundary goes up to Beit-Khoglah and passes along north of Beit-Aravah. And the boundary goes up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuven.

And the boundary goes up to Devir from the Valley of Akhor, and so northward, turning toward Gilgal, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim, which is on the south side of the valley. And the boundary passes along to the waters of En-Shemesh and ends at En-Rogel.

Then the boundary goes up by the Valley of the Son of Hinnom at the southern shoulder of the Yevusite — that is, Yerushalayim. And the boundary goes up to the top of the mountain that lies before the Valley of Hinnom, on the west, at the northern end of the Valley of Refa'im.

Then the boundary extends from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Neftokha, and from there to the cities of Mount Efron. Then the boundary bends to Ba'alah — that is, Kiryat-Ye'arim.
And the boundary circles west of Ba'alah to Mount Se'ir, passes along to the northern shoulder of Mount Ye'arim — that is, Kesalon — and goes down to Beit-Shemesh and passes along by Timnah.

The boundary goes out to the shoulder of Ekron to the north, then the boundary bends to Shikkeron and passes along to Mount Ba'alah and goes out to Yavne'el. Then the boundary comes to an end at the sea.
And the west boundary was the Great Sea with its coastline. This is the boundary around the people of Yehudah according to their clans.
According to the commandment of YHWH to Yehoshua, he gave to Kalev the son of Yefunneh a portion among the people of Yehudah, Kiryat-Arba, the city of Arba the father of Anak — that is, Khevron.
And Kalev drove out from there the three sons of Anak, Sheshai and Akhiman and Talmai, the descendants of Anak.
And he went up from there against the inhabitants of Devir. Now the name of Devir formerly was Kiryat-Sefer.
And Kalev said, Whoever strikes Kiryat-Sefer and captures it, to him will I give Akhsah my daughter as wife.
And Otni'el the son of Kenaz, the brother of Kalev, captured it. And he gave him Akhsah his daughter as wife.
When she came to him, she urged him to ask her father for a field. And she got off her donkey, and Kalev said to her, What do you want?
She said to him, Give me a blessing. Since you have given me the land of the Negev, give me also springs of water. And he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the people of Yehudah according to their clans.
The cities belonging to the tribe of the people of Yehudah in the extreme south, toward the boundary of Edom, were Kavtze'el, Eder, Yagur,
Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,
Kedesh, Khattzor, Itnan,
Ziph, Telem, Be'alot,
Khattzor-Khadattah, Keriot-Khetzron — that is, Khattzor —
Amam, Shema, Moladah,
Khattzar-Gaddah, Kheshmon, Beit-Pelet,
Khattzar-Shu'al, Be'er-Sheva, Bizyoteyah,
Ba'alah, Iyim, Etzem,
Eltolad, Kesil, Khormah,
Tziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,
Levavot, Shilkhim, Ayin, and Rimmon — in all, twenty-nine cities with their villages.
And in the lowland, Eshtaol, Tzorah, Ashnah,
Zanoakh, En-Gannim, Tappuakh, Enam,
Yarmut, Adullam, Sokhoh, Azekah,
Sha'arayim, Aditayim, Gederah, Gederotayim — fourteen cities with their villages.
Tzenan, Khadashah, Migdal-Gad,
Dil'an, Mitzpeh, Yokthe'el,
Lakhish, Botzkat, Eglon,
Kabbon, Lakhmam, Kitlish,
Gederot, Beit-Dagon, Na'amah, and Maqkedah — sixteen cities with their villages.
Livnah, Eter, Ashan,
Yiftakh, Ashnah, Netziv,
Ke'ilah, Akhziv, and Mareshah — nine cities with their villages.
Ekron, with its towns and its villages.
From Ekron to the sea, all that were by the side of Ashdod, with their villages.
Ashdod, its towns and its villages — Azzah, its towns and its villages — to the Brook of Egypt, and the Great Sea with its coastline.
And in the hill country, Shamir, Yattir, Sokhoh,
Dannah, Kiryat-Sannah — that is, Devir —
Anav, Eshtemoh, Anim,
Goshen, Kholon, and Giloh — eleven cities with their villages.
Arab, Dumah, Eshan,
Yanum, Beit-Tappuakh, Afekah,
Khumtah, Kiryat-Arba — that is, Khevron — and Tziyor — nine cities with their villages.
Ma'on, Karmel, Ziph, Yuttah,
Yizre'el, Yokde'am, Zanoakh,
Kayin, Giv'ah, Timnah — ten cities with their villages.
Khal-Kul, Beit-Tzur, Gedor,
Ma'arat, Beit-Anot, and Eltekon — six cities with their villages.
Kiryat-Ba'al — that is, Kiryat-Ye'arim — and Rabbah — two cities with their villages.
In the wilderness, Beit-Aravah, Middin, Sekhakhah,
Nivshan, the City of Salt, and En-Gedi — six cities with their villages.
But the Yevusites, the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, the people of Yehudah could not drive out, so the Yevusites dwell with the people of Yehudah at Yerushalayim to this day.
The allotment of the people of Yosef went from the Yarden by Yerikho, east of the waters of Yerikho, into the wilderness, going up from Yerikho into the hill country to Beit-El.
Then going from Beit-El to Luz, it passes along to Atarot, the territory of the Arkhites.
Then it goes down westward to the territory of the Yafletites, as far as the territory of Lower Beit-Kharon, then to Gezer, and it ends at the sea.
The people of Yosef, Menasheh and Efrayim, received their inheritance.
The territory of the people of Efrayim by their clans was as follows: the boundary of their inheritance on the east was Atrot-Addar as far as Upper Beit-Kharon,
And the boundary goes from there to the sea. On the north is Mikhmetat. Then on the east the boundary turns around toward Tana'at-Shiloh, and passes along beyond it on the east to Yanoakh,
Then it goes down from Yanoakh to Atarot and to Na'arah, and touches Yerikho, ending at the Yarden.
The boundary goes from Tappuakh westward to the brook Kanah, and ends at the sea. Such is the inheritance of the tribe of the people of Efrayim by their clans,
Together with the towns that were set apart for the people of Efrayim within the inheritance of the people of Menasheh, all those towns with their villages.
However, they did not drive out the Kena'anites who lived in Gezer, so the Kena'anites have lived in the midst of Efrayim to this day but have been made to do forced labor.

Then allotment was made to the tribe of Menasheh, for he was the firstborn of Yosef. To Makhir the firstborn of Menasheh, the father of Gil'ad, were allotted Gil'ad and Bashan, because he was a man of war.

And allotments were made to the rest of the people of Menasheh by their clans, Avi-ezer, Khelek, Asri'el, Shekhem, Khefer, and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Menasheh the son of Yosef, by their clans.

Now Tzelofkhad the son of Khefer, son of Gil'ad, son of Makhir, son of Menasheh, had no sons, but only daughters, and these are the names of his daughters: Makhlah, No'ah, Khoglah, Milkah, and Tirtzah.

They approached Ele'azar the priest and Yehoshua the son of Nun and the leaders and said, YHWH commanded Moshe to give us an inheritance among our brothers. So according to the mouth of YHWH he gave them an inheritance among the brothers of their father.
Thus there fell to Menasheh ten portions, besides the land of Gil'ad and Bashan, which is on the other side of the Yarden,
Because the daughters of Menasheh received an inheritance along with his sons. The land of Gil'ad was allotted to the rest of the people of Menasheh.
The territory of Menasheh reached from Asher to Mikhmetat, which is east of Shekhem. Then the boundary goes along southward to the inhabitants of En-Tappuakh.
The land of Tappuakh belonged to Menasheh, but the town of Tappuakh on the boundary of Menasheh belonged to the people of Efrayim.

Then the boundary goes down to the brook Kanah. These cities, to the south of the brook, among the cities of Menasheh, belong to Efrayim. The boundary of Menasheh goes along the north side of the brook and ends at the sea.
The land to the south is Efrayim's and that to the north is Menasheh's, with the sea forming its boundary. On the north Asher is reached, and on the east Yissaskhar.

Also in Yissaskhar and in Asher, Menasheh had Beit-She'an and its villages, Yivle'am and its villages, the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, the inhabitants of En-Dor and its villages, the inhabitants of Ta'anakh and its villages, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages — the third is Naphot.
Yet the people of Menasheh could not take possession of those cities, but the Kena'anites persisted in dwelling in that land.
When the people of Yisra'EL grew strong, they put the Kena'anites to forced labor, but did not utterly drive them out.
Then the people of Yosef spoke to Yehoshua, saying, Why have you given me but one lot and one portion as an inheritance, although I am a numerous people, since all along YHWH has blessed me?

And Yehoshua said to them, If you are a numerous people, go up by yourselves to the forest, and there clear ground for yourselves in the land of the Perizzites and the Refa'im, since the hill country of Efrayim is too narrow for you.

The people of Yosef said, The hill country is not enough for us. Yet all the Kena'anites who dwell in the plain have chariots of iron, both those in Beit-She'an and its villages and those in the Valley of Yizre'el.
Then Yehoshua said to the house of Yosef, to Efrayim and Menasheh, You are a numerous people and have great power. You shall not have one allotment only,

But the hill country shall be yours, for though it is a forest, you shall clear it and possess it to its farthest borders. For you shall drive out the Kena'anites, though they have chariots of iron, and though they are strong.
Then the whole congregation of the people of Yisra'EL assembled at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there. The land lay subdued before them.
There remained among the people of Yisra'EL seven tribes whose inheritance had not yet been apportioned.
So Yehoshua said to the people of Yisra'EL, How long will you put off going in to take possession of the land, which YHWH, the Creator of your fathers, has given you?

Provide three men from each tribe, and I will send them out that they may set out and go up and down the land. They shall write a description of it with a view to their inheritances, and then come to me.
They shall divide it into seven portions. Yehudah shall continue in his territory on the south, and the house of Yosef shall continue in their territory on the north.
And you shall describe the land in seven portions and bring the description here to me. And I will cast lots for you here before YHWH our Creator.

The Levites have no portion among you, for the priesthood of YHWH is their heritage. And Gad and Reuven and half the tribe of Menasheh have received their inheritance beyond the Yarden eastward, which Moshe the servant of YHWH gave them.

So the men arose and went, and Yehoshua charged those who went to write the description of the land, saying, Go up and down in the land and write a description and return to me. And I will cast lots for you here before YHWH in Shiloh.
So the men went and passed up and down in the land and wrote in a book a description of it by towns in seven divisions. Then they came to Yehoshua to the camp at Shiloh,
And Yehoshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before YHWH. And there Yehoshua apportioned the land to the people of Yisra'EL, to each his portion.
The lot of the tribe of the people of Binyamin according to its clans came up, and the territory allotted to it fell between the people of Yehudah and the people of Yosef.

On the north side their boundary began at the Yarden. Then the boundary goes up to the shoulder north of Yerikho, then up through the hill country westward, and it ends at the wilderness of Beit-Aven.

From there the boundary passes along southward in the direction of Luz, to the shoulder of Luz — the same is Beit-El — then the boundary goes down to Atarot-Addar, on the mountain that lies south of Lower Beit-Kharon.

Then the boundary goes in another direction, turning on the western side southward from the mountain that lies to the south, opposite Beit-Kharon, and it ends at Kiryat-Ba'al — that is, Kiryat-Ye'arim — a city belonging to the people of Yehudah. This forms the western side.
And the southern side begins at the outskirts of Kiryat-Ye'arim. And the boundary goes from there westward, and it goes to the spring of the waters of Neftokha.

Then the boundary goes down to the border of the mountain that overlooks the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, which is at the north end of the Valley of Refa'im. And it then goes down the Valley of Hinnom, south of the shoulder of the Yevusites, and downward to En-Rogel.
Then it bends in a northerly direction going to En-Shemesh, and from there goes to Gelilot, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim. Then it goes down to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuven.
Passing along north of the shoulder of Beit-Aravah, it goes down to the Aravah.
Then the boundary passes along to the north of the shoulder of Beit-Khoglah. And the boundary ends at the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the south end of the Yarden. This is the southern boundary.
The Yarden forms its boundary on the eastern side. This is the inheritance of the people of Binyamin, according to their clans, boundary by boundary all around.
Now the cities of the tribe of the people of Binyamin according to their clans were Yerikho, Beit-Khoglah, Emek-Ketzitz,
Beit-Aravah, Tzemarayim, Beit-El,
Avvim, Parah, Ofrah,
Kefar-Ammonai, Ofni, and Geva — twelve cities with their villages.
Giv'on, Ramah, Be'erot,
Mitzpeh, Kefira, Moza,
Rekem, Irpe'el, Tar'alah,
Tzela, Elef, Yevus — that is, Yerushalayim — Giv'at, and Kiryat — fourteen cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the people of Binyamin according to their clans.
The second lot came out for Shim'on, for the tribe of the people of Shim'on, according to their clans, and their inheritance was in the midst of the inheritance of the people of Yehudah.
And they had for their inheritance Be'er-Sheva, Sheva, Moladah,
Khattzar-Shu'al, Balah, Etzem,
Eltolad, Betul, Khormah,
Tziklag, Beit-Markabot, Khattzar-Susah,
Beit-Levavot, and Sharukhен — thirteen cities with their villages.
Ayin, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan — four cities with their villages —
Together with all the villages around these cities as far as Ba'alat-Be'er, Ramat of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the people of Shim'on according to their clans.

The inheritance of the people of Shim'on formed part of the territory of the people of Yehudah. Because the portion of the people of Yehudah was too large for them, the people of Shim'on obtained an inheritance in the midst of their inheritance.
The third lot came up for the people of Zevulun, according to their clans. And the territory of their inheritance reached as far as Sarid.
Then their boundary goes up westward and on to Mar'alah and touches Dabbesheth, then the brook that is east of Yokne'am.
From Sarid it goes in the other direction eastward toward the sunrise to the boundary of Kislot-Tavor. From there it goes to Daberath, then up to Yafiya.
From there it passes along on the east toward the sunrise to Gat-Khefer, to Ittah-Katzin, and going on to Rimmon it bends toward Neah,
Then on the north the boundary turns about to Khannathon, and it ends at the Valley of Yiftakh-El —
Kattat, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Beit-Lekhem — twelve cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the people of Zevulun, according to their clans — these cities with their villages.
The fourth lot came out for Yissaskhar, for the people of Yissaskhar, according to their clans.
Their territory included Yizre'el, Kesullot, Shunem,
Khafarayim, Shion, Anakharat,
Rabbith, Kishyon, Evetz,
Remmet, En-Gannim, En-Khaddah, Beit-Patztzetz.
The boundary also touches Tavor, Shahatzumah, and Beit-Shemesh, and their boundary ends at the Yarden — sixteen cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the people of Yissaskhar, according to their clans — the cities with their villages.
The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the people of Asher according to their clans.
Their territory included Khelkat, Khali, Beten, Akhshaph,
Alammelekh, Amad, and Mishal. On the west it touches Karmel and Shikhор-Livnat.
Then it turns eastward, goes to Beit-Dagon, and touches Zevulun and the Valley of Yiftakh-El northward to Beit-Emek and Ne'i'el. Then it continues in the north to Kavul,
Evron, Rekhov, Khamon, Kanah, as far as Great Tzidon.
Then the boundary turns to Ramah, reaching to the fortified city of Tzor. Then the boundary turns to Khosah, and it ends at the sea — Akhdav,
Ummah, Afek, and Rekhov — twenty-two cities with their villages.
