This is the inheritance of the tribe of the people of Asher according to their clans — these cities with their villages.
The sixth lot came out for the people of Naftali, for the people of Naftali, according to their clans.
And their boundary ran from Khelef, from the oak in Za'anannim, and Adami-Nekev, and Yavenl, as far as Lakkum, and it ended at the Yarden.
Then the boundary turns westward to Aznot-Tavor and goes from there to Khukok, touching Zevulun at the south and Asher on the west and Yehudah on the east at the Yarden.
The fortified cities are Tziddim, Tzer, Khamath, Rakkat, Kinnereth,
Adamah, Ramah, Khattzor,
Kedesh, Edre'i, En-Khattzor,
Yiron, Migdal-El, Khorem, Beit-Anat, and Beit-Shemesh — nineteen cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the people of Naftali according to their clans — the cities with their villages.
The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the people of Dan, according to their clans.
And the territory of its inheritance included Tzorah, Eshtaol, Ir-Shemesh,
Sha'alavvin, Ayalon, Yitlah,
Elon, Timnah, Ekron,
Eltekeh, Gibbeton, Ba'alat,
Yehud, Benei-Berak, Gat-Rimmon,
Me-Yarkon, and Rakkon, with the territory over against Yafo.

When the territory of the people of Dan was lost to them, the people of Dan went up and fought against Leshem, and after capturing it and striking it with the sword they took possession of it and settled in it, calling Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their ancestor.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the people of Dan, according to their clans — these cities with their villages.
When they had finished distributing the several territories of the land as inheritances, the people of Yisra'EL gave an inheritance among them to Yehoshua the son of Nun.
By command of YHWH they gave him the city that he asked, Timnat-Serakha in the hill country of Efrayim. And he rebuilt the city and settled in it.

These are the inheritances that Ele'azar the priest and Yehoshua the son of Nun and the heads of the fathers' houses of the tribes of the people of Yisra'EL distributed by lot at Shiloh before YHWH, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. So they finished dividing the land.
Then YHWH said to Yehoshua,
Say to the people of Yisra'EL, Appoint the cities of refuge, of which I spoke to you through Moshe,
That the manslayer who strikes any person without intent or unknowingly may flee there. They shall be for you a refuge from the avenger of blood.

He shall flee to one of these cities and shall stand at the entrance of the gate of the city and explain his case to the elders of that city. Then they shall take him into the city and give him a place, and he shall remain with them.
And if the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not give up the manslayer into his hand, because he struck his neighbor unknowingly, and did not hate him in the past.

And he shall remain in that city until he has stood before the congregation for judgment, until the death of him who is high priest at the time. Then the manslayer may return to his own town and his own home, to the town from which he fled.
So they set apart Kedesh in Galil in the hill country of Naftali, and Shekhem in the hill country of Efrayim, and Kiryat-Arba — that is, Khevron — in the hill country of Yehudah.

And beyond the Yarden east of Yerikho, they appointed Betzer in the wilderness on the tableland, from the tribe of Reuven, and Ramot in Gil'ad, from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Menasheh.

These were the cities designated for all the people of Yisra'EL and for the stranger sojourning among them, that anyone who killed a person without intent could flee there, so that he might not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, till he stood before the congregation.
Then the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites came to Ele'azar the priest and to Yehoshua the son of Nun and to the heads of the fathers' houses of the tribes of the people of Yisra'EL.
And they said to them at Shiloh in the land of Kena'an, YHWH commanded through Moshe that we be given cities to dwell in, along with their pasturelands for our livestock.
So by command of YHWH the people of Yisra'EL gave to the Levites the following cities and pasturelands out of their inheritance.
The lot came out for the clans of the Kohathites. And the Levites who were descendants of Aharon the priest received by lot from the tribes of Yehudah, Shim'on, and Binyamin, thirteen cities.
And the rest of the Kohathites received by lot from the clans of the tribe of Efrayim, from the tribe of Dan, and the half-tribe of Menasheh, ten cities.
The Gershonites received by lot from the clans of the tribe of Yissaskhar, from the tribe of Asher, from the tribe of Naftali, and from the half-tribe of Menasheh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
The Merarites according to their clans received from the tribe of Reuven, the tribe of Gad, and the tribe of Zevulun, twelve cities.
These cities and their pasturelands the people of Yisra'EL gave by lot to the Levites, as YHWH had commanded through Moshe.
Out of the tribe of the people of Yehudah and the tribe of the people of Shim'on they gave the following cities mentioned by name,
Which went to the descendants of Aharon, one of the clans of the Kohathites who belonged to the people of Levi — for the lot fell to them first.
They gave them Kiryat-Arba — Arba being the father of Anak — that is, Khevron, in the hill country of Yehudah, along with the pasturelands around it.
But the fields of the city and its villages had been given to Kalev the son of Yefunneh as his possession.
And to the descendants of Aharon the priest they gave Khevron, the city of refuge for the manslayer, with its pasturelands, Livnah with its pasturelands,
Yattir with its pasturelands, Eshtemoa with its pasturelands,
Kholon with its pasturelands, Devir with its pasturelands,
Ayin with its pasturelands, Yuttah with its pasturelands, Beit-Shemesh with its pasturelands — nine cities out of these two tribes.
And out of the tribe of Binyamin, Giv'on with its pasturelands, Geva with its pasturelands,
Anatot with its pasturelands, and Almon with its pasturelands — four cities.
The cities of the descendants of Aharon, the priests, were in all thirteen cities with their pasturelands.
And the rest of the Kohathites belonging to the Kohathite clans of the Levites received their allotted cities from the tribe of Efrayim.
To them were given Shekhem, the city of refuge for the manslayer, with its pasturelands in the hill country of Efrayim, Gezer with its pasturelands,
Kivtzayim with its pasturelands, Beit-Kharon with its pasturelands — four cities.
And out of the tribe of Dan, Eltekeh with its pasturelands, Gibbeton with its pasturelands,
Ayalon with its pasturelands, Gat-Rimmon with its pasturelands — four cities.
And out of the half-tribe of Menasheh, Ta'anakh with its pasturelands, and Gat-Rimmon with its pasturelands — two cities.
The cities of the clans of the rest of the Kohathites were ten in all, with their pasturelands.

And to the Gershonites, one of the clans of the Levites, were given out of the half-tribe of Menasheh, Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands, the city of refuge for the manslayer, and Be-Eshterah with its pasturelands — two cities.
And out of the tribe of Yissaskhar, Kishyon with its pasturelands, Daberath with its pasturelands,
Yarmut with its pasturelands, En-Gannim with its pasturelands — four cities.
And out of the tribe of Asher, Mishal with its pasturelands, Avdon with its pasturelands,
Khelkat with its pasturelands, and Rekhov with its pasturelands — four cities.
And out of the tribe of Naftali, Kedesh in Galil with its pasturelands, the city of refuge for the manslayer, Khammot-Dor with its pasturelands, and Kartan with its pasturelands — three cities.
The cities of the several clans of the Gershonites were in all thirteen cities with their pasturelands.
And to the rest of the Levites, the Merarite clans, were given out of the tribe of Zevulun, Yokne'am with its pasturelands, Kartah with its pasturelands,
Dimnah with its pasturelands, Nahalal with its pasturelands — four cities.
And out of the tribe of Reuven, Betzer with its pasturelands, Yahatz with its pasturelands,
Kedemot with its pasturelands, and Mefa'at with its pasturelands — four cities.
And out of the tribe of Gad, Ramot in Gil'ad with its pasturelands, the city of refuge for the manslayer, Makhanayim with its pasturelands,
Kheshbon with its pasturelands, Ya'zer with its pasturelands — four cities in all.
As for the cities of the several Merarite clans, that is, the remainder of the clans of the Levites, those allotted to them were twelve cities in all.
The cities of the Levites in the midst of the possession of the people of Yisra'EL were in all forty-eight cities with their pasturelands.
These cities each had its pasturelands around it. So it was with all these cities.
Thus YHWH gave to Yisra'EL all the land that he swore to give to their fathers. And they took possession of it, and they settled there.
And YHWH gave them rest on every side just as he had sworn to their fathers. Not one of all their enemies had withstood them, for YHWH had given all their enemies into their hands.
Not one word of all the good promises that YHWH had made to the house of Yisra'EL had failed — all came to pass.
At that time Yehoshua summoned the Reuvenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Menasheh,
And said to them, You have kept all that Moshe the servant of YHWH commanded you and have obeyed my voice in all that I have commanded you.
You have not forsaken your brothers these many days, down to this day, but have been careful to keep the charge of YHWH your Creator.

And now YHWH your Creator has given rest to your brothers, as he promised them. Therefore turn and go to your tents in the land where your possession lies, which Moshe the servant of YHWH gave you on the other side of the Yarden.

Only be very careful to observe the commandment and the Torah that Moshe the servant of YHWH commanded you, to love YHWH your Creator, and to walk in all his ways and to keep his commandments and to cling to him and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul.
So Yehoshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their tents.

Now to the one half of the tribe of Menasheh Moshe had given a possession in Bashan, but to the other half Yehoshua had given a possession beside their brothers on the west side of the Yarden. And when Yehoshua sent them away to their homes and blessed them,
He said to them, Go back to your tents with much wealth and with very much livestock, with silver, gold, bronze, and iron, and with much clothing. Divide the spoil of your enemies with your brothers.

So the people of Reuven and the people of Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh returned home, parting from the people of Yisra'EL at Shiloh, which is in the land of Kena'an, to go to the land of Gil'ad, their own land of which they had taken possession by command of YHWH through Moshe.

And when they came to the region of the Yarden that is in the land of Kena'an, the people of Reuven and the people of Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh built there an altar by the Yarden, an altar of great appearance.

And the people of Yisra'EL heard it said, Behold, the people of Reuven and the people of Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh have built the altar at the frontier of the land of Kena'an, in the region about the Yarden, on the side that belongs to the people of Yisra'EL.
And when the people of Yisra'EL heard of it, the whole assembly of the people of Yisra'EL gathered at Shiloh to make war against them.
Then the people of Yisra'EL sent to the people of Reuven and the people of Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh, in the land of Gil'ad, Pinkhas the son of Ele'azar the priest,
And with him ten chiefs, one from each of the tribal families of Yisra'EL, every one of them the head of a family among the clans of Yisra'EL.
And they came to the people of Reuven, the people of Gad, and the half-tribe of Menasheh, in the land of Gil'ad, and they said to them,

Thus says the whole congregation of YHWH, What is this breach of faith that you have committed against the Creator of Yisra'EL in turning away this day from following YHWH by building yourselves an altar this day in rebellion against YHWH?
Have we not had enough of the sin at Pe'or from which even yet we have not cleansed ourselves, and for which there came a plague upon the congregation of YHWH,
That you too must turn away this day from following YHWH? And if you too rebel against YHWH today then tomorrow he will be angry with the whole congregation of Yisra'EL.

But now, if the land of your possession is unclean, pass over into YHWH's land where YHWH's tabernacle stands, and take for yourselves a possession among us. Only do not rebel against YHWH or make us rebels by building for yourselves an altar other than the altar of YHWH our Creator.
Did not Akhan the son of Zerakhi break faith in the matter of the devoted things, and wrath fell upon all the congregation of Yisra'EL? And he was not the only one who died for his iniquity.
Then the people of Reuven, the people of Gad, and the half-tribe of Menasheh said in answer to the heads of the families of Yisra'EL,
YHWH, Creator of creators, YHWH, Creator of creators — he knows — and Yisra'EL itself shall know. If it was in rebellion or in breach of faith against YHWH, do not spare us today
For building an altar to turn away from following YHWH. Or if we did so to offer burnt offerings or grain offerings or peace offerings on it, may YHWH himself take vengeance.
No, but we did it from fear that in time to come your children might say to our children, What have you to do with YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL?
For YHWH has made the Yarden a boundary between us and you, you people of Reuven and people of Gad. You have no portion in YHWH. So your children might make our children cease to worship YHWH.
Therefore we said, Let us now build an altar, not for burnt offering, nor for sacrifice,

But to be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we do perform the service of YHWH in his presence with our burnt offerings and sacrifices and peace offerings, so your children will not say to our children in time to come, You have no portion in YHWH.

And we thought, If this should be said to us or to our descendants in time to come, we should say, Behold, the copy of the altar of YHWH, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings, nor for sacrifice, but to be a witness between us and you.

Far be it from us that we should rebel against YHWH and turn away this day from following YHWH by building an altar for burnt offering, grain offering, or sacrifice, other than the altar of YHWH our Creator that stands before his tabernacle.

When Pinkhas the priest and the chiefs of the congregation, the heads of the families of Yisra'EL who were with him, heard the words that the people of Reuven and the people of Gad and the people of Menasheh spoke, it was good in their eyes.

And Pinkhas the son of Ele'azar the priest said to the people of Reuven and the people of Gad and the people of Menasheh, Today we know that YHWH is in our midst, because you have not committed this breach of faith against YHWH. Now you have delivered the people of Yisra'EL from the hand of YHWH.

Then Pinkhas the son of Ele'azar the priest, and the chiefs, returned from the people of Reuven and the people of Gad in the land of Gil'ad to the land of Kena'an, to the people of Yisra'EL, and brought back word to them.

And the report was good in the eyes of the people of Yisra'EL. And the people of Yisra'EL blessed Creator and spoke no more of making war against them to destroy the land where the people of Reuven and the people of Gad were settled.
The people of Reuven and the people of Gad called the altar Witness, For, they said, it is a witness between us that YHWH is Creator.
A long time afterward, when YHWH had given rest to Yisra'EL from all their surrounding enemies, and Yehoshua was old and well advanced in years,
Yehoshua summoned all Yisra'EL, its elders and heads, its judges and officers, and said to them, I am now old and well advanced in years.
And you have seen all that YHWH your Creator has done to all these nations for your sake, for it is YHWH your Creator who has fought for you.
Behold, I have allotted to you as an inheritance for your tribes those nations that remain, along with all the nations that I have already cut off, from the Yarden to the Great Sea in the west.
YHWH your Creator will push them back before you and drive them out of your sight. And you shall possess their land, just as YHWH your Creator promised you.
Therefore, be very strong to keep and to do all that is written in the Book of the Torah of Moshe, turning aside from it neither to the right hand nor to the left,
That you may not mix with these nations remaining among you or make mention of the names of their gods or swear by them or serve them or bow down to them,
But you shall cling to YHWH your Creator just as you have done to this day.
For YHWH has driven out before you great and strong nations. And as for you, no man has been able to withstand you to this day.
One man of you puts to flight a thousand, since it is YHWH your Creator who fights for you, just as he promised you.
Be very careful, therefore, to love YHWH your Creator.
For if you turn back and cling to the remnant of these nations remaining among you and make marriages with them, so that you associate with them and they with you,

Know for certain that YHWH your Creator will no longer drive out these nations before you, but they shall be a snare and a trap for you, a whip on your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from off this good land that YHWH your Creator has given you.

And now I am about to go the way of all the earth, and you know in your hearts and souls, all of you, that not one word has failed of all the good things that YHWH your Creator promised concerning you. All have come to pass for you — not one of them has failed.

But just as all the good things that YHWH your Creator promised concerning you have been fulfilled for you, so YHWH will bring upon you all the evil things, until he has destroyed you from off this good land that YHWH your Creator has given you,

If you transgress the covenant of YHWH your Creator, which he commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them. Then the anger of YHWH will be kindled against you, and you shall perish quickly from off the good land that he has given you.
Yehoshua gathered all the tribes of Yisra'EL to Shekhem and summoned the elders, the heads, the judges, and the officers of Yisra'EL. And they presented themselves before Creator.

And Yehoshua said to all the people, Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, Long ago, your fathers lived beyond the Euphrates, Terakha, the father of Avraham and of Nakhor, and they served other gods.
Then I took your father Avraham from beyond the River and led him through all the land of Kena'an, and made his offspring many. I gave him Yitzhak.
And to Yitzhak I gave Yaakov and Esav. And I gave Esav the hill country of Se'ir to possess, but Yaakov and his children went down to Egypt.
And I sent Moshe and Aharon, and I plagued Egypt with what I did in the midst of it, and afterward I brought you out.
Then I brought your fathers out of Egypt, and you came to the sea. And the Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.

And when they cried to YHWH, he put darkness between you and the Egyptians and made the sea come upon them and cover them. And your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. And you lived in the wilderness a long time.

Then I brought you to the land of the Amorites, who lived on the other side of the Yarden. They fought with you, and I gave them into your hand, and you took possession of their land, and I destroyed them before you.
Then Balak the son of Tzippor, king of Moav, arose and fought against Yisra'EL. And he sent and invited Bil'am the son of Be'or to curse you,
But I would not listen to Bil'am. Indeed, he blessed you. So I delivered you out of his hand.

And you went over the Yarden and came to Yerikho, and the leaders of Yerikho fought against you, and also the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Kena'anites, the Khittites, the Girgashites, the Khivvites, and the Yevusites. And I gave them into your hand.
And I sent the hornet before you, which drove them out before you, the two kings of the Amorites — it was not by your sword or by your bow.
I gave you a land on which you had not labored and cities that you had not built, and you dwell in them. You eat the fruit of vineyards and olive orchards that you did not plant.
Now therefore fear YHWH and serve him in sincerity and in faithfulness. Put away the gods that your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve YHWH.

And if it is evil in your eyes to serve YHWH, choose this day whom you will serve, whether the gods your fathers served in the region beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But as for me and my house, we will serve YHWH.
Then the people answered, Far be it from us that we should forsake YHWH to serve other gods,

For it is YHWH our Creator who brought us and our fathers up from the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and who did those great signs in our sight and preserved us in all the way that we went, and among all the peoples through whom we passed.
And YHWH drove out before us all the peoples, the Amorites who lived in the land. Therefore we also will serve YHWH, for he is our Creator.
But Yehoshua said to the people, You are not able to serve YHWH, for he is a holy Creator. He is a jealous Creator — he will not forgive your transgressions or your sins.
If you forsake YHWH and serve foreign gods, then he will turn and do you harm and consume you, after having done you good.
And the people said to Yehoshua, No, but we will serve YHWH.
Then Yehoshua said to the people, You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen YHWH, to serve him. And they said, We are witnesses.
He said, Then put away the foreign gods that are among you, and incline your heart to YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL.
And the people said to Yehoshua, YHWH our Creator we will serve, and his voice we will obey.
So Yehoshua made a covenant with the people that day, and put in place statutes and rules for them at Shekhem.
And Yehoshua wrote these words in the Book of the Torah of Creator. And he took a large stone and set it up there under the terebinth that was by the sanctuary of YHWH.

And Yehoshua said to all the people, Behold, this stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words of YHWH that he spoke to us. Therefore it shall be a witness against you, lest you deal falsely with your Creator.
So Yehoshua sent the people away, every man to his inheritance.
After these things Yehoshua the son of Nun, the servant of YHWH, died, being 110 years old.
And they buried him in his own inheritance at Timnat-Serakha, which is in the hill country of Efrayim, north of the mountain of Ga'ash.
Yisra'EL served YHWH all the days of Yehoshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Yehoshua and had known all the work that YHWH did for Yisra'EL.

As for the bones of Yosef, which the people of Yisra'EL brought up from Egypt, they buried them at Shekhem, in the piece of land that Yaakov bought from the sons of Khamor the father of Shekhem for a hundred pieces of money. It became an inheritance of the descendants of Yosef.
And Ele'azar the son of Aharon died, and they buried him at Giv'at-Pinkhas, which had been given to Pinkhas his son in the hill country of Efrayim.
After the death of Yehoshua, the people of Yisra'EL inquired of YHWH, Who shall go up first for us against the Kena'anites, to fight against them?
YHWH said, Yehudah shall go up — behold, I have given the land into his hand.

And Yehudah said to Shim'on his brother, Come up with me into the territory allotted to me, that we may fight against the Kena'anites. And I likewise will go with you into the territory allotted to you. So Shim'on went with him.
Then Yehudah went up and YHWH gave the Kena'anites and the Perizzites into their hand, and they defeated ten thousand of them at Bezek.
They found Adoni-Bezek at Bezek and fought against him and defeated the Kena'anites and the Perizzites.
Adoni-Bezek fled, but they pursued him and caught him and cut off his thumbs and his big toes.

And Adoni-Bezek said, Seventy kings with their thumbs and their big toes cut off used to pick up scraps under my table. As I have done, so Creator has repaid me. And they brought him to Yerushalayim, and he died there.
And the people of Yehudah fought against Yerushalayim and captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword and set the city on fire.
And afterward the people of Yehudah went down to fight against the Kena'anites who lived in the hill country, in the Negev, and in the lowland.
And Yehudah went against the Kena'anites who lived in Khevron — now the name of Khevron was formerly Kiryat-Arba — and they defeated Sheshai and Akhiman and Talmai.
From there they went against the inhabitants of Devir. The name of Devir was formerly Kiryat-Sefer.
And Kalev said, Whoever strikes Kiryat-Sefer and captures it, I will give him Akhsah my daughter as wife.
And Otni'el the son of Kenaz, Kalev's younger brother, captured it. And he gave him Akhsah his daughter as wife.
When she came to him, she urged him to ask her father for a field. And she dismounted from her donkey, and Kalev said to her, What do you want?
She said to him, Give me a blessing. Since you have given me the land of the Negev, give me also springs of water. And Kalev gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.

And the descendants of the Kenite, Moshe's father-in-law, went up with the people of Yehudah from the city of palms into the wilderness of Yehudah, which lies in the Negev near Arad, and they went and settled with the people.
And Yehudah went with Shim'on his brother, and they defeated the Kena'anites who inhabited Tzefat and devoted it to destruction. So the name of the city was called Khormah.
Yehudah also captured Azzah with its territory, and Ashkelon with its territory, and Ekron with its territory.
And YHWH was with Yehudah, and he took possession of the hill country, but he could not drive out the inhabitants of the plain because they had chariots of iron.
And Khevron was given to Kalev, as Moshe had said. And he drove out from it the three sons of Anak.
But the people of Binyamin did not drive out the Yevusites who lived in Yerushalayim, so the Yevusites have lived with the people of Binyamin in Yerushalayim to this day.
The house of Yosef also went up against Beit-El, and YHWH was with them.
And the house of Yosef scouted out Beit-El. Now the name of the city was formerly Luz.
And the spies saw a man coming out of the city, and they said to him, Please show us the way into the city, and we will deal kindly with you.
And he showed them the way into the city. And they struck the city with the edge of the sword, but they let the man and all his family go.
And the man went to the land of the Khittites and built a city and called its name Luz. That is its name to this day.

Menasheh did not drive out the inhabitants of Beit-She'an and its villages, or Ta'anakh and its villages, or the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, or the inhabitants of Yivle'am and its villages, or the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages, for the Kena'anites persisted in dwelling in that land.
When Yisra'EL grew strong, they put the Kena'anites to forced labor, but did not drive them out completely.
And Efrayim did not drive out the Kena'anites who lived in Gezer, so the Kena'anites lived in Gezer among them.
Zevulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron, or the inhabitants of Nahalol, so the Kena'anites lived among them, but became subject to forced labor.
Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Akko, or the inhabitants of Tzidon or of Akhlav or of Akhziv or of Khelbah or of Afik or of Rekhov,
So the Asherites lived among the Kena'anites, the inhabitants of the land, for they did not drive them out.

Naftali did not drive out the inhabitants of Beit-Shemesh, or the inhabitants of Beit-Anat, so they lived among the Kena'anites, the inhabitants of the land. Nevertheless, the inhabitants of Beit-Shemesh and of Beit-Anat became subject to forced labor for them.
The Amorites pressed the people of Dan back into the hill country, for they did not allow them to come down to the plain.
The Amorites persisted in dwelling in Mount Kheres, in Ayalon, and in Sha'albim, but the hand of the house of Yosef rested heavily on them, and they became subject to forced labor.
And the border of the Amorites ran from the ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela and upward.

Now the angel of YHWH went up from Gilgal to Bokhim. And he said, I brought you up from Egypt and brought you into the land that I swore to give to your fathers. I said, I will never break my covenant with you,
And you shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land — you shall break down their altars. But you have not obeyed my voice. What is this you have done?
So now I say, I will not drive them out before you, but they shall become thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare to you.
As soon as the angel of YHWH spoke these words to all the people of Yisra'EL, the people lifted up their voices and wept.
And they called the name of that place Bokhim. And they sacrificed there to YHWH.
When Yehoshua dismissed the people, the people of Yisra'EL went each to his inheritance to take possession of the land.
And the people served YHWH all the days of Yehoshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Yehoshua, who had seen all the great work that YHWH had done for Yisra'EL.
And Yehoshua the son of Nun, the servant of YHWH, died at the age of 110 years.
And they buried him within the boundaries of his inheritance in Timnat-Kheres, in the hill country of Efrayim, north of the mountain of Ga'ash.
And all that generation also were gathered to their fathers. And there arose another generation after them who did not know YHWH or the work that he had done for Yisra'EL.
And the people of Yisra'EL did what was evil in the sight of YHWH and served the Ba'als.

And they abandoned YHWH, the Creator of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt. They went after other gods, from among the gods of the peoples who were around them, and bowed down to them. And they provoked YHWH to anger.
They abandoned YHWH and served the Ba'als and the Ashtarots.

So the anger of YHWH was kindled against Yisra'EL, and he gave them over to plunderers, who plundered them. And he sold them into the hand of their surrounding enemies, so that they could no longer withstand their enemies.
Whenever they marched out, the hand of YHWH was against them for harm, as YHWH had warned, and as YHWH had sworn to them. And they were in terrible distress.
Then YHWH raised up judges, who saved them out of the hand of those who plundered them.

Yet they did not listen to their judges, for they whored after other gods and bowed down to them. They soon turned aside from the way in which their fathers had walked, who had obeyed the commandments of YHWH, and they did not do so.

Whenever YHWH raised up judges for them, YHWH was with the judge, and he saved them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge. For YHWH was moved to pity by their groaning because of those who afflicted and oppressed them.

But whenever the judge died, they turned back and were more corrupt than their fathers, going after other gods, serving them and bowing down to them. They did not drop any of their practices or their stubborn ways.
So the anger of YHWH was kindled against Yisra'EL, and he said, Because this people have transgressed my covenant that I commanded their fathers and have not obeyed my voice,
I will no longer drive out before them any of the nations that Yehoshua left when he died,
In order to test Yisra'EL by them, whether they will take care to walk in the way of YHWH as their fathers did, or not.
So YHWH left those nations, not driving them out quickly, and he did not give them into the hand of Yehoshua.
Now these are the nations that YHWH left, to test Yisra'EL by them, that is, all in Yisra'EL who had not experienced all the wars in Kena'an.
It was only in order that the generations of the people of Yisra'EL might know war, to teach war to those who had not known it before.
These are the nations: the five lords of the Pelishtim, and all the Kena'anites and the Tzidonians and the Khivvites who lived on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Ba'al-Hermon as far as Lebo-Khamath.
They were for the testing of Yisra'EL, to know whether Yisra'EL would obey the commandments of YHWH, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moshe.
So the people of Yisra'EL lived among the Kena'anites, the Khittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Khivvites, and the Yevusites.
And their daughters they took to themselves for wives, and their own daughters they gave to their sons, and they served their gods.
And the people of Yisra'EL did what was evil in the sight of YHWH. They forgot YHWH their Creator and served the Ba'als and the Asherot.
Therefore the anger of YHWH was kindled against Yisra'EL, and he sold them into the hand of Kushan-Rishatayim king of Mesopotamia. And the people of Yisra'EL served Kushan-Rishatayim eight years.
But when the people of Yisra'EL cried out to YHWH, YHWH raised up a deliverer for the people of Yisra'EL, who saved them — Otni'el the son of Kenaz, Kalev's younger brother.
The Spirit of YHWH was upon him, and he judged Yisra'EL. He went out to war, and YHWH gave Kushan-Rishatayim king of Mesopotamia into his hand. And his hand prevailed over Kushan-Rishatayim.
So the land had rest forty years. Then Otni'el the son of Kenaz died.
And the people of Yisra'EL again did what was evil in the sight of YHWH, and YHWH strengthened Eglon the king of Moav against Yisra'EL, because they had done what was evil in the sight of YHWH.
He gathered to himself the Ammonites and the Amalekites, and went and defeated Yisra'EL. And they took possession of the city of palms.
And the people of Yisra'EL served Eglon the king of Moav eighteen years.

But when the people of Yisra'EL cried out to YHWH, YHWH raised up for them a deliverer — Ehud, the son of Gera, the Binyaminite, a left-handed man. The people of Yisra'EL sent tribute by him to Eglon the king of Moav.
And Ehud made for himself a sword with two edges, a cubit in length, and he bound it on his right thigh under his clothes.
And he presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moav. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
And when Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the people who carried the tribute.
But he himself turned back at the idols near Gilgal and said, I have a secret message for you, O king. And he commanded, Silence. And all his attendants went out from his presence.
And Ehud came to him as he was sitting alone in his cool roof chamber. And Ehud said, I have a message from Creator for you. And he arose from his seat.
And Ehud reached with his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly.
And the hilt also went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not pull the sword out of his belly, and the dung came out.
Then Ehud went out into the porch and closed the doors of the roof chamber behind him and locked them.
When he had gone, the servants came, and when they saw that the doors of the roof chamber were locked, they thought, Surely he is relieving himself in the closet of the cool chamber.
And they waited till they were embarrassed. But when he still did not open the doors of the roof chamber, they took the key and opened them, and there was their master fallen dead on the floor.
Ehud escaped while they delayed, and he passed beyond the idols and escaped to Se'irah.
When he arrived, he sounded the trumpet in the hill country of Efrayim. Then the people of Yisra'EL went down with him from the hill country, and he was their leader.

And he said to them, Follow after me, for YHWH has given your enemies the Moavites into your hand. So they went down after him and seized the fords of the Yarden against the Moavites and did not allow anyone to pass over.
And they killed at that time about ten thousand of the Moavites, all strong, able-bodied men. Not a man escaped.
So Moav was subdued that day under the hand of Yisra'EL. And the land had rest eighty years.
After him was Shamgar the son of Anat, who killed six hundred of the Pelishtim with an oxgoad, and he also saved Yisra'EL.
And the people of Yisra'EL again did what was evil in the sight of YHWH after Ehud died.
And YHWH sold them into the hand of Yavin king of Kena'an, who reigned in Khatzor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Kharoshet-Haggoyim.
Then the people of Yisra'EL cried out to YHWH for help, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron and he oppressed the people of Yisra'EL cruelly for twenty years.
Now Devorah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidot, was judging Yisra'EL at that time.
She used to sit under the palm of Devorah between Ramah and Beit-El in the hill country of Efrayim, and the people of Yisra'EL came up to her for judgment.

She sent and summoned Barak the son of Avino'am from Kedesh-Naftali and said to him, Has not YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, commanded you, Go, gather your men at Mount Tavor, taking ten thousand from the people of Naftali and the people of Zevulun.
And I will draw out Sisera, the general of Yavin's army, to meet you by the river Kishon with his chariots and his troops, and I will give him into your hand?
Barak said to her, If you will go with me, I will go, but if you will not go with me, I will not go.

And she said, I will surely go with you. Nevertheless, the road on which you are going will not lead to your glory, for YHWH will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. Then Devorah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
And Barak called out Zevulun and Naftali to Kedesh. And ten thousand men went up at his heels, and Devorah went up with him.
Now Khever the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, the descendants of Khovav the father-in-law of Moshe, and had pitched his tent as far away as the oak in Tza'ananim, which is near Kedesh.
When Sisera was told that Barak the son of Avino'am had gone up to Mount Tavor,
Sisera called out all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the men who were with him, from Kharoshet-Haggoyim to the river Kishon.

And Devorah said to Barak, Up, for this is the day in which YHWH has given Sisera into your hand. Does not YHWH go out before you? So Barak went down from Mount Tavor with ten thousand men following him.
And YHWH routed Sisera and all his chariots and all his army before Barak by the edge of the sword. And Sisera got down from his chariot and fled away on foot.
And Barak pursued the chariots and the army to Kharoshet-Haggoyim, and all the army of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword — not a man was left.
But Sisera fled away on foot to the tent of Ya'el, the wife of Khever the Kenite, for there was peace between Yavin the king of Khatzor and the house of Khever the Kenite.
And Ya'el came out to meet Sisera and said to him, Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me — do not be afraid. So he turned aside to her into the tent, and she covered him with a rug.
And he said to her, Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty. So she opened a skin of milk and gave him a drink and covered him.
And he said to her, Stand at the opening of the tent, and if any man comes and asks you, Is anyone here? say, No.

But Ya'el the wife of Khever took a tent peg, and took a hammer in her hand. Then she went softly to him and drove the peg into his temple until it went down into the ground while he was lying fast asleep from weariness. So he died.

And behold, as Barak was pursuing Sisera, Ya'el went out to meet him and said to him, Come, and I will show you the man whom you are seeking. So he went in to her tent, and there lay Sisera dead, with the tent peg in his temple.
So on that day Creator subdued Yavin the king of Kena'an before the people of Yisra'EL.
And the hand of the people of Yisra'EL pressed harder and harder against Yavin the king of Kena'an, until they destroyed Yavin king of Kena'an.
Then sang Devorah and Barak the son of Avino'am on that day:
That the leaders took the lead in Yisra'EL, that the people offered themselves willingly, bless YHWH.
Hear, O kings — give ear, O princes — to YHWH I will sing — I will make melody to YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL.
YHWH, when you went out from Se'ir, when you marched from the region of Edom, the earth trembled and the heavens dropped, yes, the clouds dropped water.
The mountains quaked before YHWH, even Sinai before YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL.
In the days of Shamgar, son of Anat, in the days of Ya'el, the highways were abandoned, and travelers kept to the byways.
The villagers ceased in Yisra'EL — they ceased to be — until I arose, Devorah arose, a mother in Yisra'EL.
When new gods were chosen, then war was in the gates. Was shield or spear to be seen among forty thousand in Yisra'EL?
My heart goes out to the commanders of Yisra'EL who offered themselves willingly among the people. Bless YHWH.
Tell of it, you who ride on white donkeys, you who sit on rich carpets and you who walk by the way.

To the sound of musicians at the watering places, there they repeat the righteous triumphs of YHWH, the righteous triumphs of his villagers in Yisra'EL. Then down to the gates marched the people of YHWH.
Awake, awake, Devorah — awake, awake, break out in a song. Arise, Barak, lead away your captives, O son of Avino'am.
Then down marched the remnant of the noble — the people of YHWH marched down for me against the mighty.

From Efrayim their root they marched down into the valley, following you, Binyamin, with your kinsmen — from Makhir marched down the commanders, and from Zevulun those who bear the lieutenant's staff.
The princes of Yissaskhar came with Devorah, and Yissaskhar faithful to Barak — into the valley they rushed at his heels. Among the clans of Reuven there were great searchings of heart.
Why did you sit still among the sheepfolds, to hear the whistling for the flocks? Among the clans of Reuven there were great searchings of heart.
Gil'ad stayed beyond the Yarden — and Dan, why did he stay with the ships? Asher sat still at the coast of the sea, staying by his landings.
Zevulun is a people who risked their lives to the death — Naftali too, on the heights of the field.
The kings came, they fought — then fought the kings of Kena'an, at Ta'anakh, by the waters of Megiddo — they got no spoils of silver.
From heaven the stars fought, from their courses they fought against Sisera.
The torrent Kishon swept them away, the ancient torrent, the torrent Kishon. March on, my soul, with might.
Then loud beat the horses' hoofs with the galloping, galloping of his steeds.
Curse Meroz, says the angel of YHWH, curse its inhabitants thoroughly, because they did not come to the help of YHWH, to the help of YHWH against the mighty.
Most blessed of women be Ya'el, the wife of Khever the Kenite, of tent-dwelling women most blessed.
He asked for water and she gave him milk — she brought him curds in a noble's bowl.
She sent her hand to the tent peg and her right hand to the workmen's mallet — she struck Sisera, she crushed his head, she shattered and pierced his temple.
Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay still — between her feet he sank, he fell — where he sank, there he fell dead.
Out of the window she peered, the mother of Sisera wailed through the lattice: Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why tarry the hoofbeats of his chariots?
Her wisest princesses answer — indeed, she answers herself:

Have they not found and divided the spoil? — a womb or two for every man — spoil of dyed materials for Sisera, spoil of dyed materials embroidered, two pieces of dyed work embroidered for the neck as spoil?
So may all your enemies perish, O YHWH. But your friends be like the sun as he rises in his might. And the land had rest forty years.
The people of Yisra'EL did what was evil in the sight of YHWH, and YHWH gave them into the hand of Midyan seven years.
And the hand of Midyan overpowered Yisra'EL, and because of Midyan the people of Yisra'EL made for themselves the dens that are in the mountains and the caves and the strongholds.
For whenever the people of Yisra'EL planted crops, the Midyanites and the Amalekites and the people of the East would come up against them.
They would encamp against them and devour the produce of the land, as far as Azzah, and leave no sustenance in Yisra'EL and no sheep or ox or donkey.
For they would come up with their livestock and their tents — they would come like locusts in number, both they and their camels could not be counted. So they laid waste the land as they came in.
And Yisra'EL was brought very low because of Midyan. And the people of Yisra'EL cried out for help to YHWH.
When the people of Yisra'EL cried out to YHWH on account of the Midyanites,
YHWH sent a prophet to the people of Yisra'EL. And he said to them, Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL: I led you up from Egypt and brought you out of the house of slavery.
And I delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of all who oppressed you, and drove them out before you and gave you their land.
And I said to you, I am YHWH your Creator — you shall not fear the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But you have not obeyed my voice.
Now the angel of YHWH came and sat under the terebinth at Ofrah, which belonged to Yo'ash the Aviezrite, while his son Gid'on was beating out wheat in the winepress to hide it from the Midyanites.
And the angel of YHWH appeared to him and said to him, YHWH is with you, O mighty man of valor.

And Gid'on said to him, Please, my lord, if YHWH is with us, why then has all this happened to us? And where are all his wonderful deeds that our fathers recounted to us, saying, Did not YHWH bring us up from Egypt? But now YHWH has forsaken us and given us into the hand of Midyan.
And YHWH turned to him and said, Go in this might of yours and save Yisra'EL from the hand of Midyan — do I not send you?
And he said to him, Please, YHWH, how can I save Yisra'EL? Behold, my clan is the weakest in Menasheh, and I am the least in my father's house.
And YHWH said to him, But I will be with you, and you shall strike the Midyanites as one man.
And he said to him, If now I have found favor in your eyes, then show me a sign that it is you who speak with me.
Please do not depart from here until I come to you and bring out my present and set it before you. And he said, I will stay till you return.

So Gid'on went into his house and prepared a young goat and unleavened cakes from an ephah of flour. The meat he put in a basket, and the broth he put in a pot, and brought them to him under the terebinth and presented them.
And the angel of Creator said to him, Take the meat and the unleavened cakes, and put them on this rock, and pour the broth over them. And he did so.

Then the angel of YHWH reached out the tip of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes. And fire sprang up from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened cakes. And the angel of YHWH vanished from his sight.
Then Gid'on perceived that he was the angel of YHWH. And Gid'on said, Alas, O YHWH Creator, for now I have seen the angel of YHWH face to face.
But YHWH said to him, Peace be to you. Do not fear — you shall not die.
Then Gid'on built an altar there to YHWH and called it, YHWH Is Peace. To this day it still stands at Ofrah, which belongs to the Aviezrites.
That night YHWH said to him, Take your father's bull, and the second bull seven years old, and pull down the altar of Ba'al that your father has, and cut down the Asherah that is beside it

And build an altar to YHWH your Creator on the top of the stronghold here, with stones laid in due order. Then take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah that you shall cut down.
So Gid'on took ten men of his servants and did as YHWH had told him. But because he was too afraid of his father's household and the men of the town to do it by day, he did it by night.

When the men of the town rose early in the morning, behold, the altar of Ba'al was broken down, and the Asherah beside it was cut down, and the second bull was offered on the altar that had been built.
And they said to one another, Who has done this thing? And after they had searched and inquired, they said, Gid'on the son of Yo'ash has done this thing.
Then the men of the town said to Yo'ash, Bring out your son, that he may die, for he has broken down the altar of Ba'al and cut down the Asherah beside it.

But Yo'ash said to all who stood against him, Will you contend for Ba'al? Or will you save him? Whoever contends for him shall be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself, because his altar has been broken down.
Therefore on that day Gid'on was called Yeruba'al, that is to say, Let Ba'al contend against him, because he broke down his altar.
Now all the Midyanites and the Amalekites and the people of the East came together, and they crossed the Yarden and encamped in the Valley of Yizre'el.
But the Spirit of YHWH clothed Gid'on, and he sounded the trumpet, and the Aviezrites were called out to follow him.
And he sent messengers throughout all Menasheh, and they too were called out to follow him. And he sent messengers to Asher, Zevulun, and Naftali, and they went up to meet them.
Then Gid'on said to Creator, If you will save Yisra'EL by my hand, as you have said,

Behold, I am laying a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew on the fleece alone, and it is dry on all the ground, then I shall know that you will save Yisra'EL by my hand, as you have said.
And it was so. When he rose early next morning and squeezed the fleece, he wrung enough dew from the fleece to fill a bowl with water.

Then Gid'on said to Creator, Let not your anger burn against me — let me speak just once more. Please let me test just once more with the fleece. Please let it be dry on the fleece only, and on all the ground let there be dew.
And Creator did so that night — and it was dry on the fleece only, and on all the ground there was dew.

Then Yeruba'al — that is, Gid'on — and all the people who were with him rose early and encamped beside the spring of Kharod. And the camp of Midyan was north of them, by the hill of Moreh, in the valley.
YHWH said to Gid'on, The people with you are too many for me to give the Midyanites into their hand, lest Yisra'EL boast over me, saying, My own hand has saved me.

Now therefore proclaim in the ears of the people, saying, Whoever is fearful and trembling, let him return home and hurry away from Mount Gilead. Then twenty-two thousand of the people returned, and ten thousand remained.

And YHWH said to Gid'on, The people are still too many. Take them down to the water, and I will test them for you there, and anyone of whom I say to you, This one shall go with you, shall go with you, and anyone of whom I say to you, This one shall not go with you, shall not go.

So he brought the people down to the water. And YHWH said to Gid'on, Every one who laps the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, you shall set by himself. Likewise, every one who kneels down to drink.
And the number of those who lapped, putting their hands to their mouths, was three hundred men, but all the rest of the people knelt down to drink water.
And YHWH said to Gid'on, With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you and give the Midyanites into your hand, and let all the others go every man to his home.

So the people took provisions in their hands, and their trumpets. And he sent all the rest of Yisra'EL every man to his tent, but retained the three hundred men. And the camp of Midyan was below him in the valley.
That same night YHWH said to him, Arise, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.
But if you are afraid to go down, go down to the camp with Purah your servant.

And you shall hear what they say, and afterward your hands shall be strengthened to go down against the camp. Then he went down with Purah his servant to the outposts of the armed men who were in the camp.

And the Midyanites and the Amalekites and all the people of the East lay along the valley like locusts in abundance, and their camels were without number, as the sand that is on the seashore in abundance.

When Gid'on came, behold, a man was telling a dream to his comrade. And he said, Behold, I dreamed a dream, and behold, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the camp of Midyan and came to the tent and struck it so that it fell and turned it upside down, so that the tent lay flat.
And his comrade answered, This is no other than the sword of Gid'on the son of Yo'ash, a man of Yisra'EL. Creator has given into his hand Midyan and all the camp.
As soon as Gid'on heard the telling of the dream and its interpretation, he worshiped. And he returned to the camp of Yisra'EL and said, Arise, for YHWH has given the host of Midyan into your hand.
And he divided the three hundred men into three companies and put trumpets into the hands of all of them and empty jars, with torches inside the jars.
And he said to them, Look at me, and do likewise. When I come to the outskirts of the camp, do as I do.
When I blow the trumpet, I and all who are with me, then blow the trumpets also on every side of all the camp and shout, For YHWH and for Gid'on.

So Gid'on and the hundred men who were with him came to the outskirts of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, when they had just set the watch. And they blew the trumpets and smashed the jars that were in their hands.

Then the three companies blew the trumpets and broke the jars. They held in their left hands the torches, and in their right hands the trumpets to blow. And they cried out, A sword for YHWH and for Gid'on.
Every man stood in his place around the camp, and all the army ran — they cried out and fled.

When they blew the three hundred trumpets, YHWH set every man's sword against his comrade and against all the army. And the army fled as far as Beit-Hashitah toward Tzerera, as far as the border of Avel-Mekholah, by Tabbat.
And the men of Yisra'EL were called out from Naftali and from Asher and from all Menasheh, and they pursued after Midyan.

Gid'on sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Efrayim, saying, Come down against the Midyanites and capture the waters against them, as far as Beit-Barah, and also the Yarden. So all the men of Efrayim were called out, and they captured the waters as far as Beit-Barah, and also the Yarden.

And they captured the two princes of Midyan, Orev and Ze'ev. They killed Orev at the rock of Orev, and Ze'ev they killed at the winepress of Ze'ev. Then they pursued Midyan, and they brought the heads of Orev and Ze'ev to Gid'on across the Yarden.
Then the men of Efrayim said to him, What is this that you have done to us, not to call us when you went to fight against Midyan? And they accused him fiercely.
And he said to them, What have I done now in comparison with you? Is not the gleaning of the grapes of Efrayim better than the grape harvest of Aviezer?
Creator has given into your hands the princes of Midyan, Orev and Ze'ev. What have I been able to do in comparison with you? Then their anger against him subsided when he said this.
And Gid'on came to the Yarden and crossed over, he and the three hundred men who were with him, exhausted yet pursuing.
So he said to the men of Sukkot, Please give loaves of bread to the people who follow me, for they are exhausted, and I am pursuing after Zevakh and Tzalmunna, the kings of Midyan.
And the officials of Sukkot said, Are the hands of Zevakh and Tzalmunna already in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?
So Gid'on said, Well then, when YHWH has given Zevakh and Tzalmunna into my hand, I will flail your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers.
And from there he went up to Penu'el, and spoke to them in the same way, and the men of Penu'el answered him as the men of Sukkot had answered.
And he said to the men of Penu'el, When I come again in peace, I will break down this tower.

Now Zevakh and Tzalmunna were in Karkor with their army, about fifteen thousand men, all who were left of all the army of the people of the East, for there had fallen one hundred and twenty thousand men who drew the sword.
And Gid'on went up by the way of the tent dwellers east of Novakh and Yogbehah and attacked the army, for the army felt secure.
And Zevakh and Tzalmunna fled, and he pursued them and captured the two kings of Midyan, Zevakh and Tzalmunna, and he threw all the army into a panic.
Then Gid'on the son of Yo'ash returned from the battle by the ascent of Kheres.
And he captured a young man of Sukkot and questioned him. And he wrote down for him the officials and elders of Sukkot, seventy-seven men.

And he came to the men of Sukkot and said, Behold Zevakh and Tzalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, Are the hands of Zevakh and Tzalmunna already in your hand, that we should give bread to your men who are exhausted?
And he took the elders of the city, and he took thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Sukkot a lesson.
And he broke down the tower of Penu'el and killed the men of the city.
Then he said to Zevakh and Tzalmunna, Where are the men whom you killed at Tavor? They answered, As you are, so were they. Every one of them resembled the son of a king.
And he said, They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As YHWH lives, if you had saved them alive, I would not kill you.
So he said to Yeter his firstborn, Rise and kill them. But the young man did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still a young man.

Then Zevakh and Tzalmunna said, Rise yourself and fall upon us, for as the man is, so is his strength. And Gid'on arose and killed Zevakh and Tzalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments that were on the necks of their camels.
Then the men of Yisra'EL said to Gid'on, Rule over us, you and your son and your grandson also, for you have saved us from the hand of Midyan.
Gid'on said to them, I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you — YHWH will rule over you.
And Gid'on said to them, Let me make a request of you: every one of you give me the earrings from his spoil. For they had golden earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.
And they answered, We will willingly give them. And they spread a cloak, and every man threw in it the earrings of his spoil.

And the weight of the golden earrings that he requested was seventeen hundred shekels of gold, besides the crescent ornaments and the pendants and the purple garments worn by the kings of Midyan, and besides the collars that were around the necks of their camels.
And Gid'on made an ephod of it and put it in his city, in Ofrah. And all Yisra'EL whored after it there, and it became a snare to Gid'on and to his family.
So Midyan was subdued before the people of Yisra'EL, and they raised their heads no more. And the land had rest forty years in the days of Gid'on.
Yeruba'al the son of Yo'ash went and lived in his own house.
Now Gid'on had seventy sons, his own offspring, for he had many wives.
And his concubine who was in Shekhem also bore him a son, and he called his name Avimэlekh.
And Gid'on the son of Yo'ash died in a good old age and was buried in the tomb of Yo'ash his father, at Ofrah of the Aviezrites.
As soon as Gid'on died, the people of Yisra'EL turned again and whored after the Ba'als and made Ba'al-Berit their god.
And the people of Yisra'EL did not remember YHWH their Creator, who had delivered them from the hand of all their enemies on every side,
And they did not show steadfast love to the family of Yeruba'al — that is, Gid'on — in return for all the good that he had done to Yisra'EL.
Now Avimelekh the son of Yeruba'al went to Shekhem to his mother's brothers and said to them and to the whole clan of his mother's father,

Say in the ears of all the leaders of Shekhem, Which is better for you, that all seventy of the sons of Yeruba'al rule over you, or that one rule over you? Remember also that I am your bone and your flesh.
And his mother's brothers spoke all these words on his behalf in the ears of all the leaders of Shekhem, and their hearts inclined to follow Avimelekh, for they said, He is our brother.
And they gave him seventy pieces of silver out of the house of Ba'al-Berit with which Avimelekh hired worthless and reckless fellows, who followed him.
And he went to his father's house at Ofrah and killed his brothers the sons of Yeruba'al, seventy men, on one stone. But Yotam the youngest son of Yeruba'al was left, for he hid himself.
And all the leaders of Shekhem and all Beit-Milo came together, and they went and made Avimelekh king, by the oak of the pillar at Shekhem.
When it was told to Yotam, he went and stood on top of Mount Gerizim and cried aloud and said to them, Listen to me, you leaders of Shekhem, that Creator may listen to you.
The trees once went out to anoint a king over them, and they said to the olive tree, Reign over us.
But the olive tree said to them, Shall I leave my abundance, by which gods and men are honored, and go hold sway over the trees?
And the trees said to the fig tree, You come and reign over us.
But the fig tree said to them, Shall I leave my sweetness and my good fruit and go hold sway over the trees?
And the trees said to the vine, You come and reign over us.
But the vine said to them, Shall I leave my wine that cheers creators and men and go hold sway over the trees?
Then all the trees said to the bramble, You come and reign over us.

And the bramble said to the trees, If in good faith you are anointing me king over you, then come and take refuge in my shade, but if not, let fire come out of the bramble and devour the cedars of Lebanon.
Now therefore, if you acted in good faith and integrity when you made Avimelekh king, and if you have dealt well with Yeruba'al and his house and have done to him as his deeds deserved —
For my father fought for you and risked his life and delivered you from the hand of Midyan,

And you have risen up against my father's house this day and have killed his sons, seventy men on one stone, and have made Avimelekh, the son of his female servant, king over the leaders of Shekhem, because he is your relative —
If you then have acted in good faith and integrity with Yeruba'al and with his house this day, then rejoice in Avimelekh, and let him also rejoice in you.
But if not, let fire come out from Avimelekh and devour the leaders of Shekhem and Beit-Milo, and let fire come out from the leaders of Shekhem and from Beit-Milo and devour Avimelekh.
And Yotam ran away and fled and went to Be'er and lived there, because of Avimelekh his brother.
Avimelekh ruled over Yisra'EL three years.
And Creator sent an evil spirit between Avimelekh and the leaders of Shekhem, and the leaders of Shekhem dealt treacherously with Avimelekh,

That the violence done to the seventy sons of Yeruba'al might come, and their blood be laid on Avimelekh their brother, who killed them, and on the men of Shekhem, who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.
And the leaders of Shekhem put men in ambush against him on the mountaintops, and they robbed all who passed by them along that way. And it was told to Avimelekh.
And Ga'al the son of Eved moved into Shekhem with his relatives, and the leaders of Shekhem put their trust in him.
And they went out into the field and gathered the grapes from their vineyards and trod them and held a festival and went into the house of their god and ate and drank and reviled Avimelekh.

And Ga'al the son of Eved said, Who is Avimelekh, and who are we of Shekhem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Yeruba'al, and is not Zevul his officer? Serve the men of Khamor the father of Shekhem, but why should we serve him?
Would that this people were under my hand. Then I would remove Avimelekh. I would say to Avimelekh, Increase your army, and come out.
When Zevul the ruler of the city heard the words of Ga'al the son of Eved, his anger was kindled.
And he sent messengers to Avimelekh secretly, saying, Behold, Ga'al the son of Eved and his relatives have come to Shekhem, and they are stirring up the city against you.
Now therefore, go by night, you and the people who are with you, and set an ambush in the field.
Then in the morning, as soon as the sun is up, rise early and rush upon the city. And when he and the people who are with him come out against you, you may do to them as your hand finds to do.
So Avimelekh and all the men who were with him rose up by night and set an ambush against Shekhem in four companies.
And Ga'al the son of Eved went out and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city, and Avimelekh and the people who were with him rose from the ambush.
And when Ga'al saw the people, he said to Zevul, Behold, people are coming down from the mountaintops. And Zevul said to him, You mistake the shadow of the mountains for men.
Ga'al spoke again and said, Behold, people are coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming from the direction of the Diviners' Oak.
Then Zevul said to him, Where is your mouth now, you who said, Who is Avimelekh, that we should serve him? Are not these the people whom you despised? Go out now and fight with them.
And Ga'al went out before the leaders of Shekhem and fought with Avimelekh.
And Avimelekh chased him, and he fled before him. And many fell wounded, up to the entrance of the gate.
And Avimelekh lived at Arumah, and Zevul drove out Ga'al and his relatives, so that they could not dwell at Shekhem.
On the following day, the people went out into the field, and it was told to Avimelekh.
He took his people and divided them into three companies and set an ambush in the fields. And he looked and saw the people coming out of the city. So he rose against them and killed them.
Avimelekh and the company that was with him rushed forward and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city, while the two companies rushed upon all who were in the field and killed them.
And Avimelekh fought against the city all that day. He captured the city and killed the people who were in it, and he razed the city and sowed it with salt.
When all the leaders of the Tower of Shekhem heard of it, they entered the stronghold of the house of El-Berit.
Avimelekh was told that all the leaders of the Tower of Shekhem were gathered together.

And Avimelekh went up to Mount Tzalmon, he and all the people who were with him. And Avimelekh took an axe in his hand and cut down a bundle of brushwood and took it up and laid it on his shoulder. And he said to the people who were with him, What you have seen me do, hurry and do as I have done.

So every one of the people cut down his bundle and following Avimelekh put it against the stronghold, and they set the stronghold on fire over them, so that all the people of the Tower of Shekhem also died, about a thousand men and women.
Then Avimelekh went to Tevetz and encamped against Tevetz and captured it.
But there was a strong tower within the city, and all the men and women and all the leaders of the city fled to it and shut themselves in, and they went up to the roof of the tower.
And Avimelekh came to the tower and fought against it and drew near to the door of the tower to burn it with fire.
And a certain woman threw an upper millstone on Avimelekh's head and crushed his skull.
Then he called quickly to the young man his armor-bearer and said to him, Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, A woman killed him. And his young man thrust him through, and he died.
And when the men of Yisra'EL saw that Avimelekh was dead, everyone departed to his home.
Thus Creator returned the evil of Avimelekh, which he committed against his father in killing his seventy brothers.
And Creator also made all the evil of the men of Shekhem return on their heads, and upon them came the curse of Yotam the son of Yeruba'al.
After Avimelekh there arose to save Yisra'EL Tola the son of Pu'ah, son of Dodo, a man of Yissaskhar, and he lived at Shamir in the hill country of Efrayim.
And he judged Yisra'EL twenty-three years. Then he died and was buried at Shamir.
After him arose Ya'ir the Gil'adite, who judged Yisra'EL twenty-two years.
And he had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty cities, called Khayyot-Ya'ir to this day, which are in the land of Gil'ad.
And Ya'ir died and was buried in Kamon.

The people of Yisra'EL again did what was evil in the sight of YHWH and served the Ba'als and the Ashtarots, the gods of Aram, the gods of Tzidon, the gods of Moav, the gods of the Ammonites, and the gods of the Pelishtim. And they forsook YHWH and did not serve him.
So the anger of YHWH was kindled against Yisra'EL, and he sold them into the hand of the Pelishtim and into the hand of the Ammonites,

And they crushed and oppressed the people of Yisra'EL that year. For eighteen years they oppressed all the people of Yisra'EL who were beyond the Yarden in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gil'ad.
And the Ammonites crossed the Yarden to fight also against Yehudah and against Binyamin and against the house of Efrayim, so that Yisra'EL was severely distressed.
And the people of Yisra'EL cried out to YHWH, saying, We have sinned against you, because we have forsaken our Creator and have served the Ba'als.
And YHWH said to the people of Yisra'EL, Did I not save you from the Egyptians and from the Amorites, from the Ammonites and from the Pelishtim?
The Tzidonians also, and the Amalekites and the Maonites oppressed you, and you cried out to me, and I saved you out of their hand.
Yet you have forsaken me and served other gods — therefore I will save you no more.
Go and cry out to the gods whom you have chosen — let them save you in the time of your distress.
And the people of Yisra'EL said to YHWH, We have sinned — do to us whatever seems good to you. Only please deliver us this day.
So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served YHWH, and he became impatient over the misery of Yisra'EL.
Then the Ammonites were called to arms, and they encamped in Gil'ad. And the people of Yisra'EL came together and encamped at Mitzpah.
And the people, the leaders of Gil'ad, said one to another, Who is the man who will begin to fight against the Ammonites? He shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gil'ad.
Now Yiftakh the Gil'adite was a mighty warrior, but he was the son of a prostitute. Gil'ad was the father of Yiftakh.

And Gil'ad's wife also bore him sons. And when his wife's sons grew up, they drove Yiftakh out and said to him, You shall not have an inheritance in our father's house, for you are the son of another woman.
Then Yiftakh fled from his brothers and lived in the land of Tov, and worthless fellows collected around Yiftakh and went out with him.
After a time the Ammonites made war against Yisra'EL.
And when the Ammonites made war against Yisra'EL, the elders of Gil'ad went to bring Yiftakh from the land of Tov.
And they said to Yiftakh, Come and be our leader, that we may fight against the Ammonites.
But Yiftakh said to the elders of Gil'ad, Did you not hate me and drive me out of my father's house? Why have you come to me now when you are in distress?
And the elders of Gil'ad said to Yiftakh, That is why we have turned to you now, that you may go with us and fight against the Ammonites and be our head over all the inhabitants of Gil'ad.
Yiftakh said to the elders of Gil'ad, If you bring me home again to fight against the Ammonites, and YHWH gives them over to me, I will be your head.
And the elders of Gil'ad said to Yiftakh, YHWH will be witness between us, if we do not do as you say.
So Yiftakh went with the elders of Gil'ad, and the people made him head and leader over them. And Yiftakh spoke all his words before YHWH at Mitzpah.
And Yiftakh sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites and said, What do you have against me, that you have come to me to fight against my land?

And the king of the Ammonites answered the messengers of Yiftakh, Because Yisra'EL on coming up from Egypt took away my land, from the Arnon to the Yabbok and to the Yarden. Now therefore restore it peaceably.
Yiftakh again sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites
And said to him, Thus says Yiftakh: Yisra'EL did not take away the land of Moav or the land of the Ammonites,
But when they came up from Egypt, Yisra'EL went through the wilderness to the Red Sea and came to Kadesh.

Yisra'EL then sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, Please let me pass through your land, but the king of Edom would not listen. And they also sent to the king of Moav, but he would not consent. So Yisra'EL remained at Kadesh.

Then they journeyed through the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moav and arrived on the east side of the land of Moav and camped on the other side of the Arnon. But they did not enter the territory of Moav, for the Arnon was the boundary of Moav.
Yisra'EL then sent messengers to Sikhon king of the Amorites, king of Kheshbon, and Yisra'EL said to him, Please let us pass through your land to our country.
But Sikhon did not trust Yisra'EL to pass through his territory, so Sikhon gathered all his people together and encamped at Yahatz and fought with Yisra'EL.

And YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, gave Sikhon and all his people into the hand of Yisra'EL, and they defeated them. So Yisra'EL took possession of all the land of the Amorites, who inhabited that country.
And they took possession of all the territory of the Amorites from the Arnon to the Yabbok and from the wilderness to the Yarden.
So then YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Yisra'EL, and are you to take possession of them?
Will you not possess what Kemosh your god gives you to possess? And all that YHWH our Creator has dispossessed before us, we will possess.
And now are you any better than Balak the son of Tzippor, king of Moav? Did he ever contend against Yisra'EL, or did he ever go to war with them?

While Yisra'EL lived in Kheshbon and its villages, and in Aro'er and its villages, and in all the cities that are on the banks of the Arnon, three hundred years, why did you not deliver them within that time?
I therefore have not sinned against you, and you do me wrong by making war on me. May YHWH, the Judge, decide this day between the people of Yisra'EL and the people of Ammon.
But the king of the Ammonites did not listen to the words of Yiftakh that he sent to him.
Then the Spirit of YHWH was upon Yiftakh, and he passed through Gil'ad and Menasheh and passed on to Mitzpah of Gil'ad, and from Mitzpah of Gil'ad he passed on to the Ammonites.
And Yiftakh made a vow to YHWH and said, If you will give the Ammonites into my hand,
Then whatever comes out from the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the Ammonites shall be YHWH's, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering.
So Yiftakh crossed over to the Ammonites to fight against them, and YHWH gave them into his hand.
And he struck them from Aro'er to the neighborhood of Minnit, twenty cities, and as far as Avel-Keramim, with a great blow. So the Ammonites were subdued before the people of Yisra'EL.
Then Yiftakh came to his home at Mitzpah. And behold, his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines and with dances. She was his only child — beside her he had neither son nor daughter.

And as soon as he saw her, he tore his clothes and said, Alas, my daughter. You have brought me very low, and you have become the cause of great trouble to me. For I have opened my mouth to YHWH, and I cannot take back my vow.
And she said to him, My father, you have opened your mouth to YHWH — do to me according to what has gone out of your mouth, now that YHWH has avenged you on your enemies, on the Ammonites.
So she said to her father, Let this thing be done for me: leave me alone two months, that I may go up and down on the mountains and weep for my virginity, I and my companions.
So he said, Go. Then he sent her away for two months, and she departed, she and her companions, and wept for her virginity on the mountains.
And at the end of two months, she returned to her father, who did with her according to his vow that he had made. She had never known a man, and it became a custom in Yisra'EL
That the daughters of Yisra'EL went year by year to lament the daughter of Yiftakh the Gil'adite four days in the year.

The men of Efrayim were called to arms, and they crossed to Tzafon and said to Yiftakh, Why did you cross over to fight against the Ammonites and did not call us to go with you? We will burn your house over you with fire.
And Yiftakh said to them, I and my people had a great dispute with the Ammonites, and when I called you, you did not save me from their hand.

And when I saw that you would not save me, I took my life in my hand and crossed over against the Ammonites, and YHWH gave them into my hand. Why then have you come up to me this day to fight against me?

Then Yiftakh gathered all the men of Gil'ad and fought with Efrayim. And the men of Gil'ad struck Efrayim, because they said, You are fugitives of Efrayim, you Gil'adites, in the midst of Efrayim and Menasheh.

And the Gil'adites captured the fords of the Yarden against the Efrayimites. And when any of the fugitives of Efrayim said, Let me go over, the men of Gil'ad said to him, Are you an Efrayimite? When he said, No,

They said to him, Then say Shibboleth, and he said Sibboleth, for he could not pronounce it right. Then they seized him and slaughtered him at the fords of the Yarden. At that time forty-two thousand of the Efrayimites fell.
Yiftakh judged Yisra'EL six years. Then Yiftakh the Gil'adite died and was buried in his city in Gil'ad.
After him Ivtzan of Beit-Lekhem judged Yisra'EL.
He had thirty sons, and thirty daughters he gave in marriage outside his clan, and thirty daughters he brought in from outside for his sons. And he judged Yisra'EL seven years.
Then Ivtzan died and was buried at Beit-Lekhem.
After him Elon the Zevulunite judged Yisra'EL, and he judged Yisra'EL ten years.
Then Elon the Zevulunite died and was buried at Ayalon in the land of Zevulun.
After him Avdon the son of Hillel the Pirathanite judged Yisra'EL.
He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys, and he judged Yisra'EL eight years.
Then Avdon the son of Hillel the Pirathanite died and was buried at Piraton in the land of Efrayim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.
And the people of Yisra'EL again did what was evil in the sight of YHWH, so YHWH gave them into the hand of the Pelishtim for forty years.
There was a certain man of Tzorah, of the tribe of the Danites, whose name was Manoakh. And his wife was barren and had no children.
And the angel of YHWH appeared to the woman and said to her, Behold, you are barren and have not borne children, but you shall conceive and bear a son.
Therefore be careful and drink no wine or strong drink, and eat nothing unclean,
