Moreover, as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against YHWH by ceasing to pray for you, and I will instruct you in the good and the right way.
Only fear YHWH and serve him faithfully with all your heart. For consider what great things he has done for you.
But if you still do wickedly, you shall be swept away, both you and your king.
Sha'ul was... years old when he began to reign, and he reigned... and two years over Yisra'EL.

Sha'ul chose three thousand men of Yisra'EL. Two thousand were with Sha'ul in Mikhmas and the hill country of Beit-El, and a thousand were with Yonatan in Giv'ah of Binyamin. The rest of the people he sent home, every man to his tent.
Yonatan defeated the garrison of the Pelishtim that was at Geva, and the Pelishtim heard of it. And Sha'ul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, Let the Hebrews hear.

And all Yisra'EL heard it said that Sha'ul had defeated the garrison of the Pelishtim, and also that Yisra'EL had become a stench to the Pelishtim. And the people were called out to join Sha'ul at Gilgal.

And the Pelishtim mustered to fight with Yisra'EL, thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen and troops like the sand on the seashore in multitude. They came up and encamped in Mikhmas, to the east of Beit-Aven.
When the men of Yisra'EL saw that they were in trouble — for the people were hard pressed — the people hid themselves in caves and in holes and in rocks and in tombs and in cisterns,
And some Hebrews crossed the fords of the Yarden to the land of Gad and Gil'ad. Sha'ul was still at Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.
He waited seven days, the time appointed by Shemu'el. But Shemu'el did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.
So Sha'ul said, Bring the burnt offering here to me, and the peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering.
As soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, behold, Shemu'el came. And Sha'ul went out to meet him and greet him.

Shemu'el said, What have you done? And Sha'ul said, When I saw that the people were scattering from me, and that you did not come within the days appointed, and that the Pelishtim had mustered at Mikhmas,
I said, Now the Pelishtim will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the favor of YHWH. So I forced myself, and offered the burnt offering.

And Shemu'el said to Sha'ul, You have done foolishly. You have not kept the command of YHWH your Creator, which he commanded you. For then YHWH would have established your kingdom over Yisra'EL forever.
But now your kingdom shall not continue. YHWH has sought out a man after his own heart, and YHWH has commanded him to be prince over his people, because you have not kept what YHWH commanded you.

And Shemu'el arose and went up from Gilgal. The rest of the people went up after Sha'ul to meet the army. They went up from Gilgal to Giv'ah of Binyamin. And Sha'ul numbered the people who were present with him, about six hundred men.
And Sha'ul and Yonatan his son and the people who were present with them stayed in Giva of Binyamin, but the Pelishtim encamped at Mikhmas.
And raiders came out of the camp of the Pelishtim in three companies. One company turned toward Ofrah, to the land of Shu'al,
Another company turned toward Beit-Kheron, and another company turned toward the border that looks down on the Valley of Tzevoyim toward the wilderness.
Now there was no blacksmith to be found throughout all the land of Yisra'EL, for the Pelishtim said, Lest the Hebrews make themselves swords or spears.
But every one of the Yisra'ELites went down to the Pelishtim to sharpen his plowshare, his mattock, his axe, or his sickle,
And the charge was two-thirds of a shekel for the plowshares and for the mattocks, and a third of a shekel for sharpening the axes and for setting the goads.
So on the day of the battle there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people with Sha'ul and Yonatan, but Sha'ul and Yonatan his son had them.
And the garrison of the Pelishtim went out to the pass of Mikhmas.
One day Yonatan the son of Sha'ul said to the young man who carried his armor, Come, let us go over to the Pelishti garrison on the other side. But he did not tell his father.
Sha'ul was sitting under the pomegranate tree that is at Migron. The people who were with him were about six hundred men,
And Akhiyah the son of Akhituv, the brother of Ikhavod, son of Pinkhas, son of Eli, the priest of YHWH in Shiloh, was wearing an ephod. And the people did not know that Yonatan had gone.

Within the passes, by which Yonatan sought to go over to the Pelishti garrison, there was a rocky crag on the one side and a rocky crag on the other side. The name of the one was Botzetz, and the name of the other Seneh.
The one crag rose on the north in front of Mikhmas, and the other on the south in front of Geva.

Yonatan said to the young man who carried his armor, Come, let us go over to the garrison of these uncircumcised. It may be that YHWH will work for us, for nothing can hinder YHWH from saving by many or by few.
And his armor-bearer said to him, Do all that is in your heart. Do as you wish. Behold, I am with you heart and soul.
Then Yonatan said, Behold, we will cross over to the men, and we will show ourselves to them.
If they say to us, Wait until we come to you, then we will stand still in our place, and we will not go up to them.
But if they say, Come up to us, then we will go up, for YHWH has given them into our hand. And this shall be the sign to us.
So both of them showed themselves to the garrison of the Pelishtim. And the Pelishtim said, Look, Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they have hidden themselves.

And the men of the garrison hailed Yonatan and his armor-bearer and said, Come up to us, and we will show you a thing. And Yonatan said to his armor-bearer, Come up after me, for YHWH has given them into the hand of Yisra'EL.
Then Yonatan climbed up on his hands and feet, and his armor-bearer after him. And they fell before Yonatan, and his armor-bearer killed them after him.
And that first strike, which Yonatan and his armor-bearer made, killed about twenty men within as it were half a furrow's length in an acre of land.
And there was a panic in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. The garrison and even the raiders trembled, the earth quaked, and it became a very great panic.
And the watchmen of Sha'ul in Giv'ah of Binyamin looked, and behold, the multitude was dispersing here and there.
Then Sha'ul said to the people who were with him, Count and see who has gone from us. And when they had counted, behold, Yonatan and his armor-bearer were not there.
And Sha'ul said to Akhiyah, Bring the ark of Creator here. For the ark of Creator was with the people of Yisra'EL at that time.
While Sha'ul was talking to the priest, the tumult in the camp of the Pelishtim increased more and more. So Sha'ul said to the priest, Withdraw your hand.
Then Sha'ul and all the people who were with him rallied and went into the battle. And behold, every Pelishti's sword was against his fellow, and there was very great confusion.
Now the Hebrews who had been with the Pelishtim before that time and who had gone up with them into the camp, even they also turned to be with the Yisra'ELites who were with Sha'ul and Yonatan.
Likewise, when all the men of Yisra'EL who had hidden themselves in the hill country of Efrayim heard that the Pelishtim were fleeing, they too followed hard after them in the battle.
So YHWH saved Yisra'EL that day. And the battle passed beyond Beit-Aven.

And the men of Yisra'EL had been hard pressed that day, so Sha'ul had laid an oath on the people, saying, Cursed be the man who eats food until it is evening and I am avenged on my enemies. So none of the people had tasted food.
Now when all the people came to the forest, behold, there was honey on the ground.
And when the people entered the forest, behold, the honey was dripping, but no one put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.

But Yonatan had not heard his father charge the people with the oath, so he put out the tip of the staff that was in his hand and dipped it in the honeycomb and put his hand to his mouth, and his eyes became bright.
Then one of the people said, Your father strictly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man who eats food this day. And the people were faint.
Then Yonatan said, My father has troubled the land. See how my eyes have become bright because I tasted a little of this honey.
How much better if the people had eaten freely today of the spoil of their enemies that they found. For now the defeat among the Pelishtim has not been great.
They struck down the Pelishtim that day from Mikhmas to Ayalon. And the people were very faint.
The people pounced on the spoil and took sheep and oxen and calves and slaughtered them on the ground. And the people ate them with the blood.
Then they told Sha'ul, Behold, the people are sinning against YHWH by eating with the blood. And he said, You have dealt treacherously. Roll a great stone to me here.

And Sha'ul said, Disperse yourselves among the people and say to them, Let every man bring his ox or his sheep and slaughter them here and eat, and do not sin against YHWH by eating with the blood. So every one of the people brought his ox with him that night and they slaughtered them there.
And Sha'ul built an altar to YHWH — it was the first altar that he built to YHWH.

Then Sha'ul said, Let us go down after the Pelishtim by night and plunder them until the morning light — let us not leave a man of them. And they said, Do whatever seems good to you. But the priest said, Let us draw near to Creator here.
And Sha'ul inquired of Creator, Shall I go down after the Pelishtim? Will you give them into the hand of Yisra'EL? But he did not answer him that day.
And Sha'ul said, Come here, all you leaders of the people, and know and see how this sin has arisen today.
For as YHWH lives who saves Yisra'EL, though it be in Yonatan my son, he shall surely die. And there was not a man among all the people who answered him.
Then he said to all Yisra'EL, You shall be on one side, and I and Yonatan my son will be on the other side. And the people said to Sha'ul, Do what seems good to you.

Therefore Sha'ul said, O YHWH Creator of Yisra'EL, why have you not answered your servant this day? If this guilt is in me or in Yonatan my son, O YHWH, Creator of Yisra'EL, give Urim. But if this guilt is in your people Yisra'EL, give Thummim. And Yonatan and Sha'ul were taken, but the people escaped.
Then Sha'ul said, Cast the lot between me and my son Yonatan. And Yonatan was taken.
Then Sha'ul said to Yonatan, Tell me what you have done. And Yonatan told him, I tasted a little honey with the tip of the staff that was in my hand. Here I am — I will die.
And Sha'ul said, God do so to me and more also — you shall surely die, Yonatan.

Then the people said to Sha'ul, Shall Yonatan die, who has worked this great salvation in Yisra'EL? Far from it. As YHWH lives, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground, for he has worked with Creator this day. So the people ransomed Yonatan, and he did not die.
Then Sha'ul went up from pursuing the Pelishtim, and the Pelishtim went to their own place.

When Sha'ul had taken the kingship over Yisra'EL, he fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moav, against the Ammonites, against Edom, against the kings of Tzovah, and against the Pelishtim. Wherever he turned he routed them.
And he did valiantly and struck the Amalekites and delivered Yisra'EL out of the hands of those who plundered them.
Now the sons of Sha'ul were Yonatan, Yishvi, and Malkishua. And the names of his two daughters: the name of the firstborn was Merav, and the name of the younger Mikhal.
And the name of Sha'ul's wife was Akhinoam the daughter of Akhima'atz. And the name of the commander of his army was Avner the son of Ner, Sha'ul's uncle.
Kish was the father of Sha'ul, and Ner the father of Avner was the son of Aviel.
There was hard fighting against the Pelishtim all the days of Sha'ul. And when Sha'ul saw any strong man, or any valiant man, he attached him to himself.
And Shemu'el said to Sha'ul, YHWH sent me to anoint you king over his people Yisra'EL — now therefore listen to the words of YHWH.
Thus says YHWH of hosts, I have noted what Amalek did to Yisra'EL in opposing them on the way when they came up out of Egypt.
Now go and strike Amalek and devote to destruction all that they have. Do not spare them, but kill both man and woman, child and infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.
So Sha'ul summoned the people and numbered them in Telaim, two hundred thousand men on foot, and ten thousand men of Yehudah.
And Sha'ul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley.

Then Sha'ul said to the Kenites, Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them. For you showed kindness to all the people of Yisra'EL when they came up out of Egypt. So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.
And Sha'ul defeated the Amalekites from Khavila as you go to Shur, which is east of Egypt.
And he took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive and devoted to destruction all the people with the edge of the sword.

But Sha'ul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep and of the oxen and of the fattened calves and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not utterly destroy them. All that was despised and worthless they devoted to destruction.
The word of YHWH came to Shemu'el:
I regret that I have made Sha'ul king, for he has turned back from following me and has not performed my commandments. And Shemu'el was angry, and he cried to YHWH all night.
And Shemu'el rose early to meet Sha'ul in the morning. And it was told Shemu'el, Sha'ul came to Karmel, and behold, he set up a monument for himself and turned and passed on and went down to Gilgal.
And Shemu'el came to Sha'ul, and Sha'ul said to him, Blessed be you to YHWH. I have performed the commandment of YHWH.
And Shemu'el said, What then is this bleating of the sheep in my ears and the lowing of the oxen that I hear?
Sha'ul said, They have brought them from the Amalekites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen to sacrifice to YHWH your Creator, and the rest we have devoted to destruction.
Then Shemu'el said to Sha'ul, Stop — I will tell you what YHWH said to me this night. And he said to him, Speak.
And Shemu'el said, Though you are little in your own eyes, are you not the head of the tribes of Yisra'EL? YHWH anointed you king over Yisra'EL.
And YHWH sent you on a mission and said, Go, devote to destruction the sinners, the Amalekites, and fight against them until they are consumed.
Why then did you not obey the voice of YHWH? Why did you pounce on the spoil and do what was evil in the sight of YHWH?

And Sha'ul said to Shemu'el, I have obeyed the voice of YHWH. I have gone on the mission on which YHWH sent me. I have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and I have devoted the Amalekites to destruction.
But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the best of the things devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to YHWH your Creator in Gilgal.
And Shemu'el said, Has YHWH as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of YHWH? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to listen than the fat of rams.
For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and presumption is as iniquity and idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of YHWH, he has also rejected you from being king.
Sha'ul said to Shemu'el, I have sinned, for I have transgressed the commandment of YHWH and your words, because I feared the people and obeyed their voice.
Now therefore, please pardon my sin and return with me that I may worship YHWH.
And Shemu'el said to Sha'ul, I will not return with you. For you have rejected the word of YHWH, and YHWH has rejected you from being king over Yisra'EL.
As Shemu'el turned to go away, Sha'ul seized the skirt of his robe, and it tore.
And Shemu'el said to him, YHWH has torn the kingdom of Yisra'EL from you this day and has given it to a neighbor of yours, who is better than you.
And also the Glory of Yisra'EL will not lie or have regret, for he is not a man, that he should have regret.
Then he said, I have sinned. Yet honor me now before the elders of my people and before Yisra'EL, and return with me, that I may bow before YHWH your Creator.
So Shemu'el turned back after Sha'ul, and Sha'ul bowed before YHWH.
Then Shemu'el said, Bring here to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came to him cheerfully. Agag said, Surely the bitterness of death is past.
And Shemu'el said, As your sword has made women childless, so shall your mother be childless among women. And Shemu'el hacked Agag to pieces before YHWH in Gilgal.
Then Shemu'el went to Ramah, and Sha'ul went up to his house in Giv'ah of Sha'ul.
And Shemu'el did not see Sha'ul again until the day of his death, but Shemu'el grieved over Sha'ul. And YHWH regretted that he had made Sha'ul king over Yisra'EL.

YHWH said to Shemu'el, How long will you grieve over Sha'ul, since I have rejected him from being king over Yisra'EL? Fill your horn with oil, and go. I will send you to Yishai the Beit-Lekhemite, for I have provided for myself a king among his sons.
And Shemu'el said, How can I go? If Sha'ul hears it, he will kill me. And YHWH said, Take a heifer with you and say, I have come to sacrifice to YHWH.
And invite Yishai to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you shall do. And you shall anoint for me him whom I declare to you.
Shemu'el did what YHWH commanded and came to Beit-Lekhem. The elders of the city came to meet him trembling and said, Do you come peaceably?
And he said, Peaceably. I have come to sacrifice to YHWH. Consecrate yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice. And he consecrated Yishai and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.
When they came, he looked on Eliav and thought, Surely YHWH's anointed is before him.

But YHWH said to Shemu'el, Do not look on his appearance or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him. For YHWH sees not as man sees — man looks on the outward appearance, but YHWH looks on the heart.
Then Yishai called Avinadav and made him pass before Shemu'el. And he said, Neither has YHWH chosen this one.
Then Yishai made Shammah pass by. And he said, Neither has YHWH chosen this one.
And Yishai made seven of his sons pass before Shemu'el. And Shemu'el said to Yishai, YHWH has not chosen these.

Then Shemu'el said to Yishai, Are all your sons here? And he said, There remains yet the youngest, but behold, he is keeping the sheep. And Shemu'el said to Yishai, Send and get him, for we will not sit down till he comes here.
And he sent and brought him in. Now he was ruddy and had beautiful eyes and was handsome. And YHWH said, Arise, anoint him, for this is he.
Then Shemu'el took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers. And the Spirit of YHWH rushed upon Dawid from that day forward. And Shemu'el rose up and went to Ramah.
Now the Spirit of YHWH departed from Sha'ul, and a harmful spirit from YHWH tormented him.
And Sha'ul's servants said to him, Behold now, a harmful spirit from Creator is tormenting you.

Let our lord now command your servants who are before you to seek out a man who is skillful in playing the lyre, and when the harmful spirit from Creator is upon you, he will play it, and you will be well.
So Sha'ul said to his servants, Provide for me a man who can play well and bring him to me.

One of the young men answered, Behold, I have seen a son of Yishai the Beit-Lekhemite, who is skillful in playing, a man of valor, a man of war, prudent in speech, and a man of good presence, and YHWH is with him.
Therefore Sha'ul sent messengers to Yishai and said, Send me Dawid your son, who is with the sheep.
And Yishai took a donkey loaded with bread and a skin of wine and a young goat and sent them by Dawid his son to Sha'ul.
And Dawid came to Sha'ul and entered his service. And Sha'ul loved him greatly, and he became his armor-bearer.
And Sha'ul sent to Yishai, saying, Let Dawid remain in my service, for he has found favor in my sight.
And whenever the harmful spirit from Creator was upon Sha'ul, Dawid took the lyre and played it with his hand. So Sha'ul was refreshed and was well, and the harmful spirit departed from him.
Now the Pelishtim gathered their armies for battle. And they were gathered at Sokhoh, which belongs to Yehudah, and encamped between Sokhoh and Azekah, in Efes-Dammim.
And Sha'ul and the men of Yisra'EL were gathered and encamped in the Valley of Elah, and drew up in line of battle against the Pelishtim.
And the Pelishtim stood on the mountain on the one side, and Yisra'EL stood on the mountain on the other side, with a valley between them.
And there came out from the camp of the Pelishtim a champion named Golyat of Gat, whose height was six cubits and a span.
He had a helmet of bronze on his head, and he was armed with a coat of mail, and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of bronze.
And he had bronze armor on his legs, and a javelin of bronze slung between his shoulders.
The shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam, and his spear's head weighed six hundred shekels of iron. And his shield-bearer went before him.

He stood and shouted to the ranks of Yisra'EL, Why have you come out to draw up for battle? Am I not a Pelishtim, and are you not servants of Sha'ul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.
If he is able to fight with me and kill me, then we will be your servants. But if I prevail against him and kill him, then you shall be our servants and serve us.
And the Pelishtim said, I defy the ranks of Yisra'EL this day. Give me a man, that we may fight together.
When Sha'ul and all Yisra'EL heard these words of the Pelishtim, they were dismayed and greatly afraid.
Now Dawid was the son of an Efrathite of Beit-Lekhem in Yehudah, named Yishai, who had eight sons. In the days of Sha'ul the man was already old and advanced in years.
The three oldest sons of Yishai had followed Sha'ul to the battle. And the names of his three sons who went to the battle were Eliav the firstborn, and next to him Avinadav, and the third Shammah.
Dawid was the youngest. The three eldest followed Sha'ul,
But Dawid went back and forth from Sha'ul to feed his father's sheep at Beit-Lekhem.
For forty days the Pelishtim came forward and took his stand, morning and evening.
And Yishai said to Dawid his son, Take for your brothers an ephah of this parched grain, and these ten loaves, and carry them quickly to the camp to your brothers.
Also take these ten cheeses to the commander of their thousand. See if your brothers are well, and bring some token from them.
Now Sha'ul and they and all the men of Yisra'EL were in the Valley of Elah, fighting with the Pelishtim.

And Dawid rose early in the morning and left the sheep with a keeper and took the provisions and went, as Yishai had commanded him. And he came to the encampment as the host was going out to the battle line, shouting the war cry.
And Yisra'EL and the Pelishtim drew up for battle, army against army.
And Dawid left the things in charge of the keeper of the baggage and ran to the ranks and went and greeted his brothers.
As he talked with them, behold, the champion, the Pelishti of Gat, Golyat by name, came up out of the ranks of the Pelishtim and spoke the same words as before. And Dawid heard him.
All the men of Yisra'EL, when they saw the man, fled from him and were much afraid.

And the men of Yisra'EL said, Have you seen this man who has come up? Surely he has come up to defy Yisra'EL. And the king will enrich the man who kills him with great riches and will give him his daughter and make his father's house free in Yisra'EL.

And Dawid said to the men who stood by him, What shall be done for the man who kills this Pelishtim and takes away the reproach from Yisra'EL? For who is this uncircumcised Pelishtim, that he should defy the armies of the living Creator?
And the people answered him in the same way, So shall it be done to the man who kills him.

Now Eliav his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men. And Eliav's anger was kindled against Dawid, and he said, Why have you come down? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your presumption and the evil of your heart, for you have come down to see the battle.
And Dawid said, What have I done now? Was it not but a word?
And he turned away from him toward another, and spoke in the same way, and the people answered him again as before.
When the words that Dawid spoke were heard, they reported them before Sha'ul, and he sent for him.
And Dawid said to Sha'ul, Let no man's heart fail because of him. Your servant will go and fight with this Pelishtim.
And Sha'ul said to Dawid, You are not able to go against this Pelishtim to fight with him, for you are but a youth, and he has been a man of war from his youth.
But Dawid said to Sha'ul, Your servant used to keep sheep for his father. And when there came a lion, or a bear, and took a lamb from the flock,
I went after him and struck him and delivered it out of his mouth. And if he arose against me, I caught him by his beard and struck him and killed him.
Your servant has struck down both lions and bears, and this uncircumcised Pelishtim shall be like one of them, for he has defied the armies of the living Creator.
And Dawid said, YHWH who delivered me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear will deliver me from the hand of this Pelishtim. And Sha'ul said to Dawid, Go, and YHWH be with you.
Then Sha'ul clothed Dawid with his armor. He put a helmet of bronze on his head and clothed him with a coat of mail.

And Dawid strapped his sword over his armor. And he tried in vain to go, for he had not tested them. Then Dawid said to Sha'ul, I cannot go with these, for I have not tested them. So Dawid put them off.
Then he took his staff in his hand and chose five smooth stones from the brook and put them in his shepherd's pouch. His sling was in his hand, and he approached the Pelishtim.
And the Pelishtim moved forward and came near to Dawid, with his shield-bearer in front of him.
And when the Pelishtim looked and saw Dawid, he disdained him, for he was but a youth, ruddy and handsome in appearance.
And the Pelishtim said to Dawid, Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks? And the Pelishtim cursed Dawid by his gods.
The Pelishtim said to Dawid, Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the air and to the beasts of the field.

Then Dawid said to the Pelishtim, You come to me with a sword and with a spear and with a javelin, but I come to you in the name of YHWH of hosts, the Creator of the armies of Yisra'EL, whom you have defied.

This day YHWH will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you down and cut off your head. And I will give the dead bodies of the host of the Pelishtim this day to the birds of the air and to the wild beasts of the earth, that all the earth may know that there is a Creator in Yisra'EL,
And that all this assembly may know that YHWH saves not with sword and spear. For the battle is YHWH's, and he will give you into our hand.
When the Pelishtim arose and came and drew near to meet Dawid, Dawid ran quickly toward the battle line to meet the Pelishtim.
And Dawid put his hand in his bag and took out a stone and slung it and struck the Pelishtim on his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.
So Dawid prevailed over the Pelishtim with a sling and with a stone, and struck the Pelishtim and killed him. There was no sword in the hand of Dawid.

Then Dawid ran and stood over the Pelishtim and took his sword and drew it out of its sheath and killed him and cut off his head with it. When the Pelishtim saw that their champion was dead, they fled.

And the men of Yisra'EL and Yehudah rose with a shout and pursued the Pelishtim as far as Gat and the gates of Ekron, so that the wounded Pelishtim fell on the way from Sha'araim as far as Gat and Ekron.
And the people of Yisra'EL came back from chasing the Pelishtim, and they plundered their camp.
And Dawid took the head of the Pelishtim and brought it to Yerushalayim, but he put his armor in his tent.
As soon as Sha'ul saw Dawid go out against the Pelishtim, he said to Avner, the commander of the army, Avner, whose son is this youth? And Avner said, As your soul lives, O king, I do not know.
And the king said, Inquire whose son the boy is.
And as soon as Dawid returned from the striking down of the Pelishtim, Avner took him and brought him before Sha'ul with the head of the Pelishtim in his hand.
And Sha'ul said to him, Whose son are you, young man? And Dawid answered, I am the son of your servant Yishai the Beit-Lekhemite.
As soon as he had finished speaking to Sha'ul, the soul of Yonatan was knit to the soul of Dawid, and Yonatan loved him as his own soul.
And Sha'ul took him that day and would not let him return to his father's house.
Then Yonatan made a covenant with Dawid, because he loved him as his own soul.
And Yonatan stripped himself of the robe that was on him and gave it to Dawid, and his armor, and even his sword and his bow and his belt.

And Dawid went out and was successful wherever Sha'ul sent him, so that Sha'ul set him over the men of war. And this was good in the sight of all the people and also in the sight of Sha'ul's servants.

As they were coming home, when Dawid returned from striking down the Pelishtim, the women came out of all the cities of Yisra'EL, singing and dancing, to meet King Sha'ul, with tambourines, with songs of joy, and with musical instruments.
And the women sang to one another as they celebrated, Sha'ul has struck down his thousands, and Dawid his ten thousands.
And Sha'ul was very angry, and this saying displeased him. He said, They have ascribed to Dawid ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed thousands, and what more can he have but the kingdom?
And Sha'ul eyed Dawid from that day on.
The next day a harmful spirit from Creator rushed upon Sha'ul, and he raved within his house while Dawid was playing the lyre, as he did day by day. Sha'ul had his spear in his hand.
And Sha'ul hurled the spear, for he thought, I will pin Dawid to the wall. But Dawid evaded him twice.
Sha'ul was afraid of Dawid because YHWH was with him but had departed from Sha'ul.
So Sha'ul removed him from his presence and made him a commander of a thousand. And he went out and came in before the people.
And Dawid had success in all his undertakings, for YHWH was with him.
And when Sha'ul saw that he had great success, he stood in fearful awe of him.
But all Yisra'EL and Yehudah loved Dawid, for he went out and came in before them.

Then Sha'ul said to Dawid, Here is my elder daughter Merav. I will give her to you for a wife. Only be valiant for me and fight YHWH's battles. For Sha'ul thought, Let not my hand be against him, but let the hand of the Pelishtim be against him.
And Dawid said to Sha'ul, Who am I, and who are my relatives, my father's clan in Yisra'EL, that I should be son-in-law to the king?
But at the time when Merav, Sha'ul's daughter, should have been given to Dawid, she was given to Adriel the Mekholathite for a wife.
Now Sha'ul's daughter Mikhal loved Dawid. And they told Sha'ul, and the thing pleased him.

Sha'ul thought, Let me give her to him, that she may be a snare for him and that the hand of the Pelishtim may be against him. Therefore Sha'ul said to Dawid a second time, You shall now be my son-in-law.
And Sha'ul commanded his servants, Speak to Dawid in private and say, Behold, the king has delight in you, and all his servants love you. Now then become the king's son-in-law.
And Sha'ul's servants spoke those words in the ears of Dawid. And Dawid said, Does it seem to you a little thing to become the king's son-in-law, since I am a poor man and have no reputation?
And the servants of Sha'ul told him, Thus and so did Dawid speak.

Then Sha'ul said, Thus shall you say to Dawid, The king desires no bride-price except a hundred foreskins of the Pelishtim, that he may be avenged of the king's enemies. Now Sha'ul planned to make Dawid fall by the hand of the Pelishtim.
And when his servants told Dawid these words, it pleased Dawid well to be the king's son-in-law. Before the time had expired,

Dawid arose and went, along with his men, and killed two hundred of the Pelishtim. And Dawid brought their foreskins, which were given in full number to the king, that he might become the king's son-in-law. And Sha'ul gave him his daughter Mikhal for a wife.
But when Sha'ul saw and knew that YHWH was with Dawid, and that Mikhal, Sha'ul's daughter, loved him,
Sha'ul was even more afraid of Dawid. So Sha'ul was Dawid's enemy continually.
Then the commanders of the Pelishtim came out to battle, and as often as they came out Dawid had more success than all the servants of Sha'ul, so that his name was highly esteemed.
And Sha'ul spoke to Yonatan his son and to all his servants, that they should kill Dawid. But Yonatan, Sha'ul's son, delighted much in Dawid.
And Yonatan told Dawid, Sha'ul my father seeks to kill you. Therefore be on your guard in the morning. Stay in a secret place and hide yourself.
And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak to my father about you. And if I learn anything I will tell you.

And Yonatan spoke well of Dawid to Sha'ul his father and said to him, Let not the king sin against his servant Dawid, because he has not sinned against you, and because his deeds have brought good to you.

For he took his life in his hand and he struck down the Pelishtim, and YHWH worked a great salvation for all Yisra'EL. You saw it, and rejoiced. Why then will you sin against innocent blood by killing Dawid without cause?
And Sha'ul listened to the voice of Yonatan. Sha'ul swore, As YHWH lives, he shall not be put to death.
And Yonatan called Dawid, and Yonatan reported to him all these things. And Yonatan brought Dawid to Sha'ul, and he was in his presence as before.
And there was war again. And Dawid went out and fought with the Pelishtim and struck them with a great blow, so that they fled before him.
Then a harmful spirit from YHWH came upon Sha'ul, as he sat in his house with his spear in his hand. And Dawid was playing the lyre.
And Sha'ul sought to pin Dawid to the wall with the spear, but he eluded Sha'ul, so that he struck the spear into the wall. And Dawid fled and escaped that night.

Sha'ul sent messengers to Dawid's house to watch him, that he might kill him in the morning. But Mikhal, Dawid's wife, told him, If you do not escape with your life tonight, tomorrow you will be killed.
So Mikhal let Dawid down through the window, and he fled away and escaped.
Mikhal took an image and laid it on the bed and put a pillow of goats' hair at its head and covered it with the clothes.
And when Sha'ul sent messengers to take Dawid, she said, He is sick.
Then Sha'ul sent the messengers to see Dawid, saying, Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may kill him.
And when the messengers came in, behold, the image was in the bed, with the pillow of goats' hair at its head.
Sha'ul said to Mikhal, Why have you deceived me thus and let my enemy go, so that he has escaped? And Mikhal answered Sha'ul, He said to me, Let me go. Why should I kill you?
Now Dawid fled and escaped, and he came to Shemu'el at Ramah and told him all that Sha'ul had done to him. And he and Shemu'el went and lived at Nayot.
And it was told Sha'ul, Behold, Dawid is at Nayot in Ramah.

Then Sha'ul sent messengers to take Dawid, and when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, and Shemu'el standing as head over them, the Spirit of Creator came upon the messengers of Sha'ul, and they also prophesied.
When it was told Sha'ul, he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And Sha'ul sent messengers again the third time, and they also prophesied.
Then he himself went to Ramah and came to the great well that is in Sekhu. And he asked, Where are Shemu'el and Dawid? And one said, Behold, they are at Nayot in Ramah.
And he went there to Nayot in Ramah. And the Spirit of Creator came upon him also, and as he went he prophesied until he came to Nayot in Ramah.
And he too stripped off his clothes, and he too prophesied before Shemu'el and lay naked all that day and all that night. Therefore they say, Is Sha'ul also among the prophets?
Then Dawid fled from Nayot in Ramah and came and said before Yonatan, What have I done? What is my guilt? And what is my sin before your father, that he seeks my life?
And he said to him, Far from it. You shall not die. Behold, my father does nothing either great or small without disclosing it to me. And why should my father hide this from me? It is not so.

But Dawid vowed again, saying, Your father knows well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he thinks, Do not let Yonatan know this, lest he be grieved. But truly, as YHWH lives and as your soul lives, there is but a step between me and death.
Then Yonatan said to Dawid, Whatever you say, I will do for you.
Dawid said to Yonatan, Behold, tomorrow is the new moon, and I should not fail to sit at table with the king. But let me go, that I may hide myself in the field till the third day at evening.
If your father misses me at all, then say, Dawid earnestly asked leave of me to run to Beit-Lekhem his city, for there is a yearly sacrifice there for all the clan.
If he says, Good, it will be well with your servant, but if he is angry, then know that harm is determined by him.
Therefore deal kindly with your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of YHWH with you. But if there is guilt in me, kill me yourself, for why should you bring me to your father?
And Yonatan said, Far be it from you. If I knew that it was determined by my father that harm should come to you, would I not tell you?
Then Dawid said to Yonatan, Who will tell me if your father answers you roughly?
And Yonatan said to Dawid, Come, let us go out into the field. So they both went out into the field.

And Yonatan said to Dawid, YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, be witness. When I have sounded out my father, about this time tomorrow, or the third day, behold, if he is well disposed toward Dawid, shall I not then send and disclose it to you?

But should it please my father to do you harm, YHWH do so to Yonatan and more also if I do not disclose it to you and send you away, that you may go in safety. May YHWH be with you, as he has been with my father.
If I am still alive, show me the steadfast love of YHWH, that I may not die.
And do not cut off your steadfast love from my house forever, when YHWH cuts off every one of the enemies of Dawid from the face of the earth.
And Yonatan made a covenant with the house of Dawid, saying, May YHWH take vengeance on Dawid's enemies.
And Yonatan made Dawid swear again by his love for him, for he loved him as he loved his own soul.
Then Yonatan said to him, Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, because your seat will be empty.
On the third day go down quickly to the place where you hid yourself when the matter was in hand, and remain beside the stone heap.
And I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as though I shot at a mark.

And behold, I will send the boy, saying, Go, find the arrows. If I say to the boy, Look, the arrows are on this side of you, take them — then you are to come, for, as YHWH lives, it is safe for you and there is no danger.
But if I say to the youth, Look, the arrows are beyond you — then go, for YHWH has sent you away.
And as for the matter of which you and I have spoken, behold, YHWH is between you and me forever.
So Dawid hid himself in the field. And when the new moon came, the king sat down to eat food.
The king sat on his seat, as at other times, on the seat by the wall. Yonatan sat opposite, and Avner sat by Sha'ul's side, but Dawid's place was empty.
Yet Sha'ul did not say anything that day, for he thought, Something has happened to him. He is not clean — surely he is not clean.
But on the second day, the day after the new moon, Dawid's place was empty. And Sha'ul said to Yonatan his son, Why has not the son of Yishai come to the meal, either yesterday or today?
Yonatan answered Sha'ul, Dawid earnestly asked leave of me to go to Beit-Lekhem.

He said, Let me go, for our clan holds a sacrifice in the city, and my brother has commanded me to be there. So now, if I have found favor in your eyes, let me get away and see my brothers. For this reason he has not come to the king's table.

Then Sha'ul's anger was kindled against Yonatan, and he said to him, You son of a perverse, rebellious woman, do I not know that you have chosen the son of Yishai to your own shame, and to the shame of your mother's nakedness?
For as long as the son of Yishai lives on the earth, neither you nor your kingdom shall be established. Therefore send and bring him to me, for he shall surely die.
Then Yonatan answered Sha'ul his father, Why should he be put to death? What has he done?
But Sha'ul hurled his spear at him to strike him. So Yonatan knew that his father was determined to put Dawid to death.
And Yonatan rose from the table in fierce anger and ate no food the second day of the month, for he was grieved for Dawid, because his father had disgraced him.
In the morning Yonatan went out into the field to the appointment with Dawid, and with him a little boy.
And he said to his boy, Run and find the arrows that I shoot. As the boy ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.
And when the boy came to the place of the arrow that Yonatan had shot, Yonatan called after the boy and said, Is not the arrow beyond you?
And Yonatan called after the boy, Hurry. Be quick. Do not stay. So Yonatan's boy gathered up the arrows and came to his master.
But the boy knew nothing. Only Yonatan and Dawid knew the matter.
And Yonatan gave his weapons to his boy and said to him, Go and carry them to the city.

And as soon as the boy had gone, Dawid rose from beside the stone heap and fell on his face to the ground and bowed three times. And they kissed one another and wept with one another, Dawid weeping the most.

And Yonatan said to Dawid, Go in peace, because we have sworn both of us in the name of YHWH, saying, YHWH shall be between me and you, and between my offspring and your offspring, forever. And he rose and departed, and Yonatan went into the city.
Then Dawid came to Nov, to Akhimelekh the priest. And Akhimelekh came to meet Dawid, trembling, and said to him, Why are you alone, and no one with you?

And Dawid said to Akhimelekh the priest, The king has charged me with a matter and said to me, Let no one know anything of the matter about which I send you, and with which I have charged you. I have made an appointment with the young men for such and such a place.
Now then, what do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever is here.
And the priest answered Dawid, I have no common bread on hand, but there is holy bread — if the young men have kept themselves from women.

And Dawid answered the priest, Truly women have been kept from us as always when I go on an expedition. The vessels of the young men are holy even when it is an ordinary journey. How much more today will their vessels be holy?
So the priest gave him the holy bread, for there was no bread there but the bread of the Presence, which is removed from before YHWH, to be replaced by hot bread on the day it is taken away.
Now a certain man of the servants of Sha'ul was there that day, detained before YHWH. His name was Do'eg the Edomite, the chief of Sha'ul's herdsmen.
And Dawid said to Akhimelekh, Then have you not here a spear or a sword at hand? For I have brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king's business required haste.

And the priest said, The sword of Golyat the Pelishtim, whom you struck down in the Valley of Elah, behold, it is here wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you will take that, take it, for there is none but that here. And Dawid said, There is none like that — give it to me.
And Dawid rose and fled that day from Sha'ul and went to Akhish the king of Gat.
And the servants of Akhish said to him, Is not this Dawid the king of the land? Did they not sing to one another of him in dances, Sha'ul has struck down his thousands, and Dawid his ten thousands?
And Dawid took these words to heart and was very much afraid of Akhish the king of Gat.
So he changed his behavior before them and pretended to be insane in their hands and made marks on the doors of the gate and let his spittle run down his beard.
Then Akhish said to his servants, Behold, you see the man is mad. Why then have you brought him to me?
Do I lack madmen, that you have brought this fellow to behave as a madman in my presence? Shall this fellow come into my house?
Dawid departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. And when his brothers and all his father's house heard it, they went down there to him.

And everyone who was in distress, and everyone who was in debt, and everyone who was bitter in soul, gathered to him. And he became commander over them. And there were with him about four hundred men.
And Dawid went from there to Mitzpeh of Moav. And he said to the king of Moav, Please let my father and my mother stay with you, till I know what Creator will do for me.
And he left them with the king of Moav, and they stayed with him all the time that Dawid was in the stronghold.
Then the prophet Gad said to Dawid, Do not remain in the stronghold — depart, and go into the land of Yehudah. So Dawid departed and went into the forest of Kheret.

Now Sha'ul heard that Dawid was discovered, and the men who were with him. Sha'ul was sitting at Giv'ah under the tamarisk tree on the height with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing about him.

And Sha'ul said to his servants who stood about him, Hear now, people of Binyamin — will the son of Yishai give every one of you fields and vineyards, will he make you all commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds,

That all of you have conspired against me? No one discloses to me when my son makes a covenant with the son of Yishai. None of you is sorry for me or discloses to me that my son has stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as at this day.
Then Do'eg the Edomite, who stood by the servants of Sha'ul, answered and said, I saw the son of Yishai coming to Nov, to Akhimelekh the son of Akhituv,
And he inquired of YHWH for him and gave him provisions and gave him the sword of Golyat the Pelishtim.
Then the king sent to summon Akhimelekh the priest, the son of Akhituv, and all his father's house, the priests who were at Nov, and all of them came to the king.
And Sha'ul said, Hear now, son of Akhituv. And he answered, Here I am, my lord.

And Sha'ul said to him, Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Yishai, in that you have given him bread and a sword and have inquired of Creator for him, so that he has risen against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
Then Akhimelekh answered the king, And who among all your servants is so faithful as Dawid, who is the king's son-in-law, and captain over your bodyguard, and honored in your house?

Is today the first time that I have inquired of Creator for him? No. Let not the king impute anything to his servant or to all the house of my father, for your servant has known nothing of all this, much or little.
And the king said, You shall surely die, Akhimelekh, you and all your father's house.

And the king said to the guard who stood about him, Turn and kill the priests of YHWH, because their hand also is with Dawid, and they knew that he fled and did not disclose it to me. But the servants of the king would not put out their hand to strike the priests of YHWH.
Then the king said to Do'eg, You turn and strike the priests. And Do'eg the Edomite turned and struck the priests, and he killed on that day eighty-five persons who wore the linen ephod.
And Nov, the city of the priests, he put to the sword — both man and woman, child and infant, ox, donkey, and sheep, he put to the sword.
But one of the sons of Akhimelekh the son of Akhituv, named Evyatar, escaped and fled after Dawid.
And Evyatar told Dawid that Sha'ul had killed the priests of YHWH.
And Dawid said to Evyatar, I knew on that day, when Do'eg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Sha'ul. I have occasioned the death of all the persons of your father's house.
Stay with me — do not be afraid, for he who seeks my life seeks your life. With me you shall be in safekeeping.
Now they told Dawid, Behold, the Pelishtim are fighting against Ke'ilah and are robbing the threshing floors.
Therefore Dawid inquired of YHWH, Shall I go and attack these Pelishtim? And YHWH said to Dawid, Go and attack the Pelishtim and save Ke'ilah.
But Dawid's men said to him, Behold, we are afraid here in Yehudah. How much more then if we go to Ke'ilah against the armies of the Pelishtim?
Then Dawid inquired of YHWH again. And YHWH answered him, Arise, go down to Ke'ilah, for I will give the Pelishtim into your hand.
And Dawid and his men went to Ke'ilah and fought with the Pelishtim and brought away their livestock and struck them with a great blow. So Dawid saved the inhabitants of Ke'ilah.
When Evyatar the son of Akhimelekh had fled to Dawid to Ke'ilah, he had come down with an ephod in his hand.
Now it was told Sha'ul that Dawid had come to Ke'ilah. And Sha'ul said, Creator has given him into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering a town that has gates and bars.
And Sha'ul summoned all the people to war, to go down to Ke'ilah, to besiege Dawid and his men.
Dawid knew that Sha'ul was plotting harm against him. And he said to Evyatar the priest, Bring the ephod here.
Then Dawid said, O YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, your servant has surely heard that Sha'ul seeks to come to Ke'ilah, to destroy the city on my account.
Will the men of Ke'ilah surrender me into his hand? Will Sha'ul come down, as your servant has heard? O YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, please tell your servant. And YHWH said, He will come down.
Then Dawid said, Will the men of Ke'ilah surrender me and my men into the hand of Sha'ul? And YHWH said, They will surrender you.

Then Dawid and his men, who were about six hundred, arose and departed from Ke'ilah, and they went wherever they could go. When Sha'ul was told that Dawid had escaped from Ke'ilah, he gave up the expedition.
And Dawid remained in the strongholds in the wilderness, in the hill country of the wilderness of Ziph. And Sha'ul sought him every day, but Creator did not give him into his hand.
And Dawid saw that Sha'ul had come out to seek his life. Dawid was in the wilderness of Ziph at Khoresh.
And Yonatan, Sha'ul's son, rose and went to Dawid at Khoresh, and strengthened his hand in Creator.
And he said to him, Do not fear, for the hand of Sha'ul my father shall not find you. You shall be king over Yisra'EL, and I shall be next to you. Sha'ul my father also knows this.
And the two of them made a covenant before YHWH. Dawid remained at Khoresh, and Yonatan went home.
Then the Ziphites went up to Sha'ul at Giv'ah, saying, Is not Dawid hiding among us in the strongholds at Khoresh, on the hill of Khakhilah, which is south of Yeshimon?
Now come down, O king, according to all your heart's desire to come down, and our part shall be to surrender him into the king's hand.
And Sha'ul said, May you be blessed by YHWH, for you have had compassion on me.
Go, make yet more sure. Know and see the place where his foot is, and who has seen him there, for it is told me that he is very cunning.

See therefore, and take note of all the lurking places where he hides, and come back to me with sure information. Then I will go with you. And if he is in the land, I will search him out among all the thousands of Yehudah.
And they arose and went to Ziph ahead of Sha'ul. But Dawid and his men were in the wilderness of Ma'on, in the Aravah to the south of Yeshimon.

And Sha'ul and his men went to seek him. And Dawid was told, so he went down to the rock and lived in the wilderness of Ma'on. When Sha'ul heard that, he pursued after Dawid in the wilderness of Ma'on.

Sha'ul went on one side of the mountain, and Dawid and his men on the other side of the mountain. And Dawid was hurrying to get away from Sha'ul. As Sha'ul and his men were closing in on Dawid and his men to capture them,
A messenger came to Sha'ul, saying, Hurry and come, for the Pelishtim have made a raid against the land.
So Sha'ul returned from pursuing after Dawid and went against the Pelishtim. Therefore that place was called the Rock of Escape.
And Dawid went up from there and lived in the strongholds of En-Gedi.
When Sha'ul returned from following the Pelishtim, he was told, Behold, Dawid is in the wilderness of En-Gedi.
Then Sha'ul took three thousand chosen men out of all Yisra'EL and went to seek Dawid and his men in front of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
And he came to the sheepfolds by the way, where there was a cave, and Sha'ul went in to relieve himself. Now Dawid and his men were sitting in the innermost parts of the cave.

And the men of Dawid said to him, Here is the day of which YHWH said to you, Behold, I will give your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as it shall seem good to you. Then Dawid arose and stealthily cut off a corner of Sha'ul's robe.
And afterward Dawid's heart struck him, because he had cut off a corner of Sha'ul's robe.
He said to his men, YHWH forbid that I should do this thing to my lord, YHWH's anointed, to put out my hand against him, seeing he is YHWH's anointed.
So Dawid persuaded his men with these words and did not permit them to attack Sha'ul. And Sha'ul rose up and left the cave and went on his way.
Afterward Dawid also arose and went out of the cave, and called after Sha'ul, My lord the king. And when Sha'ul looked behind him, Dawid bowed with his face to the earth and paid homage.
And Dawid said to Sha'ul, Why do you listen to the words of men who say, Behold, Dawid seeks your harm?

Behold, this day your eyes have seen how YHWH gave you today into my hand in the cave. And some told me to kill you, but I spared you. I said, I will not put out my hand against my lord, for he is YHWH's anointed.

See, my father, see the corner of your robe in my hand. For by the fact that I cut off the corner of your robe and did not kill you, you may know and see that there is no wrong or treason in my hand. I have not sinned against you, though you hunt my life to take it.
May YHWH judge between me and you, may YHWH avenge me against you, but my hand shall not be against you.
As the proverb of the ancients says, Out of the wicked comes wickedness. But my hand shall not be against you.
After whom has the king of Yisra'EL come out? After whom do you pursue? After a dead dog. After a flea.
May YHWH therefore be judge and give sentence between me and you, and see to it and plead my cause and deliver me from your hand.
As soon as Dawid had finished speaking these words to Sha'ul, Sha'ul said, Is this your voice, my son Dawid? And Sha'ul lifted up his voice and wept.
He said to Dawid, You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me good, whereas I have repaid you evil.
And you have declared this day how you have dealt well with me, in that you did not kill me when YHWH put me into your hands.
For if a man finds his enemy, will he let him go away safe? So may YHWH reward you with good for what you have done to me this day.
And now, behold, I know that you shall surely be king, and that the kingdom of Yisra'EL shall be established in your hand.
Swear to me therefore by YHWH that you will not cut off my offspring after me, and that you will not destroy my name out of my father's house.
And Dawid swore this to Sha'ul. Then Sha'ul went home, but Dawid and his men went up to the stronghold.
Now Shemu'el died. And all Yisra'EL assembled and mourned for him, and they buried him in his house at Ramah. Then Dawid rose and went down to the wilderness of Paran.
And there was a man in Ma'on whose business was in Karmel. The man was very rich — he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. He was shearing his sheep in Karmel.
Now the name of the man was Naval, and the name of his wife Avigayil. The woman was discerning and beautiful, but the man was harsh and badly behaved. He was a Kalevite.
Dawid heard in the wilderness that Naval was shearing his sheep.
So Dawid sent ten young men. And Dawid said to the young men, Go up to Karmel, and go to Naval and greet him in my name.
And thus you shall greet him: Peace be to you, and peace be to your house, and peace be to all that you have.
I hear that you have shearers. Now your shepherds have been with us, and we did not harm them, and they missed nothing all the time they were in Karmel.

Ask your young men, and they will tell you. Therefore let my young men find favor in your eyes, for we come on a feast day. Please give whatever you have at hand to your servants and to your son Dawid.
When Dawid's young men came, they said all this to Naval in the name of Dawid, and then they waited.
And Naval answered Dawid's servants, Who is Dawid? Who is the son of Yishai? There are many servants these days who are breaking away from their masters.
Shall I take my bread and my water and my meat that I have killed for my shearers and give it to men who come from I do not know where?
So Dawid's young men turned away and came back and told him all this.

And Dawid said to his men, Every man strap on his sword. And every man of them strapped on his sword. Dawid also strapped on his sword. And about four hundred men went up after Dawid, while two hundred remained with the baggage.
But one of the young men told Avigayil, Naval's wife, saying, Behold, Dawid sent messengers out of the wilderness to greet our master, and he railed at them.
Yet the men were very good to us, and we suffered no harm, and we did not miss anything when we were in the fields, as long as we went with them.
They were a wall to us both by night and by day, all the while we were with them keeping the sheep.
Now therefore know this and consider what you should do, for harm is determined against our master and against all his house, and he is such a worthless man that one cannot speak to him.

Then Avigayil made haste and took two hundred loaves and two skins of wine and five sheep already prepared and five seahs of parched grain and a hundred clusters of raisins and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on donkeys.
And she said to her young men, Go on before me — behold, I come after you. But she did not tell her husband Naval.
And as she rode on the donkey and came down under cover of the mountain, behold, Dawid and his men came down toward her, and she met them.
Now Dawid had said, Surely in vain have I guarded all that this fellow has in the wilderness, so that nothing was missed of all that belonged to him, and he has returned me evil for good.
Creator do so to Dawid and more also, if by morning I leave so much as one male of all who belong to him.
When Avigayil saw Dawid, she hurried and got down from the donkey and fell before Dawid on her face and bowed to the ground.
She fell at his feet and said, On me alone, my lord, be the guilt. Please let your servant speak in your ears, and hear the words of your servant.
Let not my lord regard this worthless fellow, Naval, for as his name is, so is he. Naval is his name, and folly is with him. But I your servant did not see the young men of my lord, whom you sent.

Now then, my lord, as YHWH lives, and as your soul lives, because YHWH has restrained you from bloodguilt and from saving with your own hand, now then let your enemies and those who seek to do evil to my lord be as Naval.
And now let this present that your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who follow my lord.

Please forgive the trespass of your servant. For YHWH will certainly make my lord a sure house, because my lord is fighting the battles of YHWH, and evil shall not be found in you so long as you live.

If men rise up to pursue you and to seek your life, the life of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of the living in the care of YHWH your Creator. And the lives of your enemies he shall sling out as from the hollow of a sling.
And when YHWH has done to my lord according to all the good that he has spoken concerning you and has appointed you prince over Yisra'EL,

My lord shall have no cause of grief or pangs of conscience for having shed blood without cause or for my lord working salvation himself. And when YHWH has dealt well with my lord, then remember your servant.
And Dawid said to Avigayil, Blessed be YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, who sent you this day to meet me.
Blessed be your discretion, and blessed be you, who have kept me this day from bloodguilt and from working salvation with my own hand.

For as surely as YHWH the Creator of Yisra'EL lives, who has restrained me from hurting you, unless you had hurried and come to meet me, truly by morning there had not been left to Naval so much as one male.
Then Dawid received from her hand what she had brought him. And he said to her, Go up in peace to your house. See, I have obeyed your voice, and I have granted your petition.

And Avigayil came to Naval, and behold, he was holding a feast in his house, like the feast of a king. And Naval's heart was merry within him, for he was very drunk. So she told him nothing at all until the morning light.
In the morning, when the wine had gone out of Naval, his wife told him these things, and his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.
And about ten days later YHWH struck Naval, and he died.

When Dawid heard that Naval was dead, he said, Blessed be YHWH who has avenged the insult I received at the hand of Naval, and has kept back his servant from wrongdoing. YHWH has returned the evil of Naval on his own head. Then Dawid sent and spoke to Avigayil, to take her as his wife.
When the servants of Dawid came to Avigayil at Karmel, they said to her, Dawid has sent us to you to take you to him as his wife.
And she rose and bowed with her face to the ground and said, Behold, your servant is a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.
And Avigayil hurried and rose and mounted a donkey, and her five young women attended her. She followed the messengers of Dawid and became his wife.
Dawid also took Akhinoam of Yizre'el, and both of them became his wives.
Sha'ul had given Mikhal his daughter, Dawid's wife, to Palti the son of Layish, who was of Gallim.
Then the Ziphites came to Sha'ul at Giv'ah, saying, Is not Dawid hiding himself on the hill of Khakhilah, which is before Yeshimon?
So Sha'ul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph with three thousand chosen men of Yisra'EL to seek Dawid in the wilderness of Ziph.
And Sha'ul encamped on the hill of Khakhilah, which is beside the road on the east of Yeshimon. But Dawid remained in the wilderness. When he saw that Sha'ul came after him into the wilderness,
Dawid sent out spies and learned that Sha'ul had indeed come.

Then Dawid arose and came to the place where Sha'ul had encamped. And Dawid saw the place where Sha'ul lay, with Avner the son of Ner, the commander of his army. Sha'ul was lying within the encampment, while the army was encamped around him.
Then Dawid said to Akhimelekh the Khittite, and to Avishai the son of Tzeruya, Yoav's brother, Who will go down with me into the camp to Sha'ul? And Avishai said, I will go down with you.
So Dawid and Avishai went to the army by night. And there lay Sha'ul sleeping within the encampment, with his spear stuck in the ground at his head, and Avner and the army lay around him.
Then Avishai said to Dawid, Creator has given your enemy into your hand this day. Now please let me pin him to the earth with one stroke of the spear, and I will not strike him twice.
But Dawid said to Avishai, Do not destroy him, for who can put out his hand against YHWH's anointed and be guiltless?
And Dawid said, As YHWH lives, YHWH will strike him, or his day will come to die, or he will go down into battle and perish.
YHWH forbid that I should put out my hand against YHWH's anointed. But take now the spear that is at his head and the jar of water, and let us go.

So Dawid took the spear and the jar of water from Sha'ul's head, and they went away. No man saw it or knew it, nor did any awake, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from YHWH had fallen upon them.
Then Dawid went over to the other side and stood far off on the top of the hill, with a great distance between them.
And Dawid called to the army, and to Avner the son of Ner, saying, Will you not answer, Avner? Then Avner answered, Who are you who calls to the king?
And Dawid said to Avner, Are you not a man? Who is like you in Yisra'EL? Why then have you not kept watch over your lord the king? For one of the people came in to destroy the king your lord.

This thing that you have done is not good. As YHWH lives, you deserve to die, because you have not kept watch over your lord, YHWH's anointed. And now see where the king's spear is and the jar of water that was at his head.
Sha'ul recognized Dawid's voice and said, Is this your voice, my son Dawid? And Dawid said, It is my voice, my lord, O king.
And he said, Why does my lord pursue after his servant? For what have I done? What evil is on my hands?

Now therefore let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If it is YHWH who has stirred you up against me, may he accept an offering, but if it is men, may they be cursed before YHWH, for they have driven me out this day that I should have no share in the heritage of YHWH, saying, Go, serve other gods.
Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth away from the presence of YHWH, for the king of Yisra'EL has come out to seek a single flea like one who hunts a partridge in the mountains.

Then Sha'ul said, I have sinned. Return, my son Dawid, for I will no more do you harm, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. Behold, I have acted foolishly, and have made a great mistake.
And Dawid answered and said, Here is the spear, O king. Let one of the young men come over and take it.
YHWH rewards every man for his righteousness and his faithfulness, for YHWH gave you into my hand today, and I would not put out my hand against YHWH's anointed.
Behold, as your life was precious this day in my sight, so may my life be precious in the sight of YHWH, and may he deliver me out of all tribulation.
Then Sha'ul said to Dawid, Blessed be you, my son Dawid. You will do many things and will succeed in them. So Dawid went his way, and Sha'ul returned to his place.

And Dawid said in his heart, Now I shall perish one day by the hand of Sha'ul. There is nothing better for me than that I should escape to the land of the Pelishtim. Then Sha'ul will despair of seeking me any longer within the borders of Yisra'EL, and I shall escape out of his hand.
So Dawid arose and went over, he and the six hundred men who were with him, to Akhish the son of Ma'okh, king of Gat.
And Dawid lived with Akhish at Gat, he and his men, every man with his household, and Dawid with his two wives, Akhinoam of Yizre'el, and Avigayil of Karmel, Naval's widow.
And when it was told Sha'ul that Dawid had fled to Gat, he no longer sought him.

Then Dawid said to Akhish, If I have found favor in your eyes, let a place be given me in one of the country towns, that I may dwell there. For why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?
So that day Akhish gave him Tziklag. Therefore Tziklag has belonged to the kings of Yehudah to this day.
And the number of the days that Dawid lived in the country of the Pelishtim was a year and four months.
Now Dawid and his men went up and made raids against the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites, for these were the inhabitants of the land from of old, as far as Shur, to the land of Egypt.
And Dawid would strike the land and would leave neither man nor woman alive, but would take away the sheep, the oxen, the donkeys, the camels, and the garments, and come back to Akhish.
When Akhish asked, Against whom have you made a raid today? Dawid would say, Against the Negev of Yehudah, or Against the Negev of the Yerakhmeel, or Against the Negev of the Kenite.

And Dawid would leave neither man nor woman alive to bring news to Gat, thinking, lest they should tell about us and say, So Dawid has done. Such was his custom all the while he lived in the country of the Pelishtim.
And Akhish trusted Dawid, thinking, He has made himself an utter stench to his people Yisra'EL. Therefore he shall always be my servant.
In those days the Pelishtim gathered their forces for war, to fight against Yisra'EL. And Akhish said to Dawid, Know that you and your men are to go out with me in the army.
Dawid said to Akhish, Very well, you shall know what your servant can do. And Akhish said to Dawid, Very well, I will make you my bodyguard for life.
Now Shemu'el had died, and all Yisra'EL had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, his own city. And Sha'ul had put the mediums and the necromancers out of the land.
The Pelishtim assembled and came and encamped at Shunem. And Sha'ul gathered all Yisra'EL, and they encamped at Gilboa.
When Sha'ul saw the army of the Pelishtim, he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.
And when Sha'ul inquired of YHWH, YHWH did not answer him, either by dreams, or by Urim, or by prophets.
Then Sha'ul said to his servants, Seek out for me a woman who is a medium, that I may go to her and inquire of her. And his servants said to him, Behold, there is a medium at En-Dor.

So Sha'ul disguised himself and put on other garments and went, he and two men with him. And they came to the woman by night. And he said, Divine for me by a spirit and bring up for me whomever I shall name to you.
The woman said to him, Surely you know what Sha'ul has done, how he has cut off the mediums and the necromancers from the land. Why then are you laying a trap for my life to bring about my death?
But Sha'ul swore to her by YHWH, As YHWH lives, no punishment shall come upon you for this thing.
Then the woman said, Whom shall I bring up for you? He said, Bring up Shemu'el for me.
When the woman saw Shemu'el, she cried out with a loud voice. And the woman said to Sha'ul, Why have you deceived me? You are Sha'ul.
The king said to her, Do not be afraid. What do you see? And the woman said to Sha'ul, I see a god coming up out of the earth.

He said to her, What is his appearance? And she said, An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a robe. And Sha'ul knew that it was Shemu'el, and he bowed with his face to the ground and paid homage.

Then Shemu'el said to Sha'ul, Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up? Sha'ul answered, I am in great distress, for the Pelishtim are warring against me, and Creator has turned away from me and answers me no more, either by prophets or by dreams. Therefore I have summoned you to tell me what I shall do.
And Shemu'el said, Why then do you ask me, since YHWH has turned from you and become your enemy?
YHWH has done to you as he spoke by me, for YHWH has torn the kingdom out of your hand and given it to your neighbor, to Dawid.
Because you did not obey the voice of YHWH and did not carry out his fierce wrath against Amalek, therefore YHWH has done this thing to you this day.

Moreover, YHWH will give Yisra'EL also with you into the hand of the Pelishtim, and tomorrow you and your sons shall be with me. YHWH will give the army of Yisra'EL also into the hand of the Pelishtim.
Then Sha'ul fell at once full length on the ground, filled with fear because of the words of Shemu'el. And there was no strength in him, for he had eaten nothing all day and all night.

And the woman came to Sha'ul, and when she saw that he was terrified, she said to him, Behold, your servant has obeyed you. I have taken my life in my hand and have listened to what you have said to me.
Now therefore, you also obey your servant. Let me set a morsel of bread before you, and eat, that you may have strength when you go on your way.
He refused and said, I will not eat. But his servants, together with the woman, urged him, and he listened to their words. So he arose from the earth and sat on the bed.
Now the woman had a fattened calf in the house, and she quickly killed it, and she took flour and kneaded it and baked unleavened bread of it,
And she put it before Sha'ul and his servants, and they ate. Then they rose and went away that night.
Now the Pelishtim had gathered all their forces at Afek. And the Yisra'ELites were encamped by the spring that is in Yizre'el.
As the lords of the Pelishtim were passing on by hundreds and by thousands, and Dawid and his men were passing on in the rear with Akhish,

The commanders of the Pelishtim said, What are these Hebrews doing here? And Akhish said to the commanders of the Pelishtim, Is this not Dawid, the servant of Sha'ul, king of Yisra'EL, who has been with me now for days and years, and since he deserted to me I have found no fault in him to this day?

But the commanders of the Pelishtim were angry with him. And the commanders of the Pelishtim said to him, Send the man back, that he may return to the place to which you have assigned him. He shall not go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he become an adversary to us. For how could this fellow reconcile himself to his lord? Would it not be with the heads of the men here?
Is not this Dawid, of whom they sing to one another in dances, Sha'ul has struck down his thousands, and Dawid his ten thousands?

Then Akhish called Dawid and said to him, As YHWH lives, you have been honest, and to me it seems right that you should march out and in with me in the campaign. For I have found nothing wrong in you from the day of your coming to me to this day. Nevertheless, the lords do not approve of you.
So return now and go peaceably, that you may not displease the lords of the Pelishtim.
And Dawid said to Akhish, But what have I done? What have you found in your servant from the day I entered your service until now, that I may not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?
And Akhish answered Dawid, I know that you are as blameless in my sight as an angel of Creator. Nevertheless, the commanders of the Pelishtim have said, He shall not go up with us to the battle.
Rise early in the morning with the servants of your lord who came with you, and start early in the morning and depart as soon as you have light.
So Dawid set out with his men early in the morning to return to the land of the Pelishtim. But the Pelishtim went up to Yizre'el.
Now when Dawid and his men came to Tziklag on the third day, the Amalekites had made a raid against the Negev and against Tziklag. They had overcome Tziklag and burned it with fire
And taken captive the women and all who were in it, both small and great. They killed no one, but carried them off and went their way.
And when Dawid and his men came to the city, they found it burned with fire, and their wives and sons and daughters taken captive.
Then Dawid and the people who were with him raised their voices and wept until they had no more strength to weep.
Dawid's two wives also had been taken captive, Akhinoam of Yizre'el and Avigayil the widow of Naval of Karmel.
And Dawid was greatly distressed, for the people spoke of stoning him, because all the people were bitter in soul, each for his sons and daughters. But Dawid strengthened himself in YHWH his Creator.
And Dawid said to Evyatar the priest, the son of Akhimelekh, Please bring me the ephod. So Evyatar brought the ephod to Dawid.
And Dawid inquired of YHWH, Shall I pursue after this band? Shall I overtake them? He answered him, Pursue, for you shall surely overtake and shall surely rescue.
So Dawid set out, and the six hundred men who were with him, and they came to the brook Besor, where those who were left behind stayed.
But Dawid pursued, he and four hundred men. Two hundred stayed behind, who were too exhausted to cross the brook Besor.
They found an Egyptian in the open country and brought him to Dawid. And they gave him bread and he ate. They gave him water to drink,
And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs and two clusters of raisins. And when he had eaten, his spirit revived, for he had not eaten bread or drunk water for three days and three nights.
And Dawid said to him, To whom do you belong? And where are you from? He said, I am a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite, and my master left me behind because I fell sick three days ago.
We had made a raid against the Negev of the Kerethites and against that which belongs to Yehudah and against the Negev of Kalev, and we burned Tziklag with fire.

And Dawid said to him, Will you take me down to this band? And he said, Swear to me by Creator that you will not kill me or deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will take you down to this band.

And when he had taken him down, behold, they were spread abroad over all the land, eating and drinking and dancing, because of all the great spoil they had taken from the land of the Pelishtim and from the land of Yehudah.
And Dawid struck them from twilight until the evening of the next day, and not a man of them escaped, except four hundred young men, who mounted camels and fled.
Dawid recovered all that the Amalekites had taken, and Dawid rescued his two wives.
Nothing was missing, whether small or great, sons or daughters, spoil or anything that had been taken. Dawid brought back all.
Dawid also captured all the flocks and herds, and the people drove the livestock before him, and said, This is Dawid's spoil.

Then Dawid came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow Dawid, and who had been left at the brook Besor. And they went out to meet Dawid and to meet the people who were with him. And when Dawid came near to the people he greeted them.

Then all the wicked and worthless fellows among the men who had gone with Dawid said, Because they did not go with us, we will not give them any of the spoil that we have recovered, except that each man may lead away his wife and children, and depart.
But Dawid said, You shall not do so, my brothers, with what YHWH has given us. He has preserved us and given into our hand the band that came against us.
Who would listen to you in this matter? For as his share is who goes down into the battle, so shall his share be who stays by the baggage. They shall share alike.
And he made it a statute and a rule for Yisra'EL from that day forward to this day.
When Dawid came to Tziklag, he sent part of the spoil to his friends, the elders of Yehudah, saying, Here is a present for you from the spoil of the enemies of YHWH.
It was for those in Beit-El, in Ramot of the Negev, in Yattir,
In Aro'er, in Sifmot, in Eshtemoa,
In Rakhel, in the cities of the Yerakhmeel, in the cities of the Kenite,
In Khormah, in Bor-Ashan, in Ataakh,
In Khevron, for all the places where Dawid and his men had roamed.
Now the Pelishtim fought against Yisra'EL, and the men of Yisra'EL fled before the Pelishtim and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
And the Pelishtim overtook Sha'ul and his sons, and the Pelishtim struck down Yonatan and Avinadav and Malkishua, the sons of Sha'ul.
The battle pressed hard against Sha'ul, and the archers found him, and he was badly wounded by the archers.
