Then Sha'ul said to his armor-bearer, Draw your sword, and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and mistreat me. But his armor-bearer would not, for he feared greatly. Therefore Sha'ul took his own sword and fell upon it.
And when his armor-bearer saw that Sha'ul was dead, he also fell upon his sword and died with him.
Thus Sha'ul died, and his three sons, and his armor-bearer, and all his men, on the same day together.

And when the men of Yisra'EL who were on the other side of the valley and those beyond the Yarden saw that the men of Yisra'EL had fled and that Sha'ul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and fled. And the Pelishtim came and lived in them.
The next day, when the Pelishtim came to strip the slain, they found Sha'ul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
So they cut off his head and stripped off his armor and sent messengers throughout the land of the Pelishtim, to carry the good news to the house of their idols and to the people.
They put his armor in the temple of the Ashtarots, and they fastened his body to the wall of Beit-She'an.
But when the inhabitants of Yavesh-Gil'ad heard what the Pelishtim had done to Sha'ul,
All the valiant men arose and went all night and took the body of Sha'ul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beit-She'an, and they came to Yavesh and burned them there.
And they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree in Yavesh and fasted seven days.
After the death of Sha'ul, when Dawid had returned from striking down the Amalekites, Dawid remained two days in Tziklag.
And on the third day, behold, a man came from Sha'ul's camp, with his clothes torn and dirt on his head. And when he came to Dawid, he fell to the ground and paid homage.
Dawid said to him, Where do you come from? And he said to him, I have escaped from the camp of Yisra'EL.
And Dawid said to him, How did it go? Tell me. And he answered, The people fled from the battle, and also many of the people have fallen and are dead, and Sha'ul and his son Yonatan are also dead.
Then Dawid said to the young man who told him, How do you know that Sha'ul and his son Yonatan are dead?
And the young man who told him said, By chance I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and there was Sha'ul leaning on his spear, and behold, the chariots and the horsemen were close upon him.
And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called to me. And I answered, Here I am.
And he said to me, Who are you? I answered him, I am an Amalekite.
And he said to me, Stand beside me and kill me, for anguish has seized me, and yet my life still lingers.

So I stood beside him and killed him, because I was sure that he could not live after he had fallen. And I took the crown that was on his head and the armlet that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.
Then Dawid took hold of his clothes and tore them, and so did all the men who were with him.
And they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Sha'ul and for Yonatan his son and for the people of YHWH and for the house of Yisra'EL, because they had fallen by the sword.
And Dawid said to the young man who told him, Where do you come from? And he answered, I am the son of a sojourner, an Amalekite.
Dawid said to him, How is it you were not afraid to put out your hand to destroy YHWH's anointed?
Then Dawid called one of the young men and said, Go, execute him. And he struck him down so that he died.
And Dawid said to him, Your blood be on your head, for your own mouth has testified against you, saying, I have killed YHWH's anointed.
And Dawid lamented with this lamentation over Sha'ul and Yonatan his son,
And he said it should be taught to the people of Yehudah — behold, it is written in the Book of the Upright.
Your glory, O Yisra'EL, is slain on your high places. How the mighty have fallen.
Tell it not in Gat, publish it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Pelishtim rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
You mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain upon you, nor fields of offerings, for there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Sha'ul, not anointed with oil.
From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Yonatan turned not back, and the sword of Sha'ul returned not empty.
Sha'ul and Yonatan, beloved and lovely, in life and in death they were not divided — they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
You daughters of Yisra'EL, weep over Sha'ul, who clothed you luxuriously in scarlet, who put ornaments of gold on your apparel.
How the mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle. Yonatan lies slain on your high places.
I am distressed for you, my brother Yonatan — very pleasant have you been to me. Your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.
How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war perished.
After this Dawid inquired of YHWH, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Yehudah? And YHWH said to him, Go up. Dawid said, To which shall I go up? And he said, To Khevron.
So Dawid went up there, and his two wives also, Akhinoam of Yizre'el and Avigayil the widow of Naval of Karmel.
And Dawid brought up his men who were with him, every one with his household, and they lived in the towns of Khevron.
And the men of Yehudah came, and there they anointed Dawid king over the house of Yehudah. When they told Dawid, The men of Yavesh-Gil'ad were those who buried Sha'ul,
Dawid sent messengers to the men of Yavesh-Gil'ad and said to them, May you be blessed by YHWH, because you showed this loyalty to Sha'ul your lord and buried him.
Now may YHWH show steadfast love and faithfulness to you. And I will do good to you because you have done this thing.
Now therefore let your hands be strong, and be valiant, for Sha'ul your lord is dead, and the house of Yehudah has anointed me king over them.
But Avner the son of Ner, commander of Sha'ul's army, had taken Ish-Boshet the son of Sha'ul and brought him over to Makhanayim.
And he made him king over Gil'ad and the Ashurites and Yizre'el and Efrayim and Binyamin and all Yisra'EL.
Ish-Boshet, Sha'ul's son, was forty years old when he began to reign over Yisra'EL, and he reigned two years. But the house of Yehudah followed Dawid.
And the time that Dawid was king in Khevron over the house of Yehudah was seven years and six months.
Avner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-Boshet the son of Sha'ul, went out from Makhanayim to Giv'on.
And Yoav the son of Tzeruya and the servants of Dawid went out and met them at the pool of Giv'on. And they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.
And Avner said to Yoav, Let the young men arise and compete before us. And Yoav said, Let them arise.
Then they arose and passed over by number, twelve for Binyamin and Ish-Boshet the son of Sha'ul, and twelve of the servants of Dawid.
And each caught his opponent by the head and thrust his sword in his opponent's side, so they fell down together. Therefore that place was called Khelkat-Hatzurim, which is at Giv'on.
And the battle was very fierce that day. And Avner and the men of Yisra'EL were beaten before the servants of Dawid.
And the three sons of Tzeruya were there, Yoav, Avishai, and Asah'el. Now Asah'el was as swift of foot as a wild gazelle.
And Asah'el pursued Avner, and as he went, he turned neither to the right hand nor to the left from following Avner.
Then Avner looked behind him and said, Is it you, Asah'el? And he answered, It is I.
Avner said to him, Turn aside to your right hand or to your left, and seize one of the young men and take his spoil. But Asah'el would not turn aside from following him.
And Avner said again to Asah'el, Turn aside from following me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How then could I lift up my face to your brother Yoav?

But he refused to turn aside. Therefore Avner struck him in the stomach with the butt of his spear, so that the spear came out at his back. And he fell there and died where he was. And all who came to the place where Asah'el had fallen and died, stood still.
But Yoav and Avishai pursued Avner. And as the sun was going down they came to the hill of Ammah, which lies before Giyakh on the way to the wilderness of Giv'on.
And the people of Binyamin gathered themselves together behind Avner and became one group and took their stand on the top of a hill.
Then Avner called to Yoav, Shall the sword devour forever? Do you not know that the end will be bitter? How long will it be before you tell your people to turn from the pursuit of their brothers?
And Yoav said, As Creator lives, if you had not spoken, surely the men would not have given up the pursuit of their brothers until the morning.
So Yoav blew the trumpet, and all the men stopped and pursued Yisra'EL no more, nor did they fight anymore.
And Avner and his men went through the Aravah all that night, and they crossed the Yarden, and marching the whole morning they came to Makhanayim.
Yoav returned from the pursuit of Avner, and when he had gathered all the people together, there were missing from Dawid's servants nineteen men besides Asah'el.
But the servants of Dawid had struck down of Binyamin three hundred and sixty of Avner's men.
And they took up Asah'el and buried him in the tomb of his father, which was at Beit-Lekhem. And Yoav and his men marched all night, and the day broke upon them at Khevron.
There was a long war between the house of Sha'ul and the house of Dawid. And Dawid grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Sha'ul became weaker and weaker.
And sons were born to Dawid at Khevron: his firstborn was Amnon, of Akhinoam of Yizre'el.
And his second, Khileyav, of Avigayil the widow of Naval of Karmel; and the third, Avshalom the son of Ma'akhah, the daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur;
And the fourth, Adoniyah the son of Khaggit; and the fifth, Shefatyah the son of Avital;
And the sixth, Yitream, of Eglah, Dawid's wife. These were born to Dawid in Khevron.
While there was war between the house of Sha'ul and the house of Dawid, Avner was making himself strong in the house of Sha'ul.
Now Sha'ul had a concubine whose name was Ritzpah, the daughter of Ayah. And Ish-Boshet said to Avner, Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?

Then Avner was very angry over the words of Ish-Boshet and said, Am I a dog's head of Yehudah? To this day I keep showing steadfast love to the house of Sha'ul your father, to his brothers, and to his friends, and have not given you into the hand of Dawid. And yet you charge me today with a fault concerning a woman.
Creator do so to Avner and more also, if I do not accomplish for Dawid what YHWH has sworn to him,
To transfer the kingdom from the house of Sha'ul and set up the throne of Dawid over Yisra'EL and over Yehudah, from Dan to Be'er-Sheva.
And Ish-Boshet could not answer Avner another word, because he feared him.
And Avner sent messengers to Dawid on his behalf, saying, To whom does the land belong? Make your covenant with me, and behold, my hand shall be with you to bring over all Yisra'EL to you.

And he said, Good — I will make a covenant with you. But one thing I require of you — that is, you shall not see my face unless you first bring Mikhal, Sha'ul's daughter, when you come to see my face.
Then Dawid sent messengers to Ish-Boshet, Sha'ul's son, saying, Give me my wife Mikhal, for whom I paid the bridal price of a hundred foreskins of the Pelishtim.
And Ish-Boshet sent and took her from her husband Paltiel the son of Layish.
But her husband went with her, weeping after her all the way to Bakhurim. Then Avner said to him, Go, return. And he returned.
And Avner conferred with the elders of Yisra'EL, saying, For some time past you have been seeking Dawid as king over you.
Now then bring it about, for YHWH has promised Dawid, saying, By the hand of my servant Dawid I will save my people Yisra'EL from the hand of the Pelishtim, and from the hand of all their enemies.
Avner also spoke to Binyamin. And then Avner went to tell Dawid at Khevron all that Yisra'EL and the whole house of Binyamin thought good to do.
When Avner came with twenty men to Dawid at Khevron, Dawid made a feast for Avner and the men who were with him.

And Avner said to Dawid, I will arise and go and will gather all Yisra'EL to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with you, and that you may reign over all that your heart desires. So Dawid sent Avner away, and he went in peace.
Just then the servants of Dawid arrived with Yoav from a raid, bringing much spoil with them. But Avner was not with Dawid at Khevron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.
When Yoav and all the army that was with him came, it was told Yoav, Avner the son of Ner came to the king, and he sent him away, and he has gone in peace.
Then Yoav went to the king and said, What have you done? Behold, Avner came to you. Why is it that you have sent him away, so that he is gone?
You know that Avner the son of Ner came to deceive you and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all that you are doing.
When Yoav came out from Dawid's presence, he sent messengers after Avner, and they brought him back from the cistern of Sirah. But Dawid did not know about it.

And when Avner returned to Khevron, Yoav took him aside into the midst of the gate to speak with him privately, and there he struck him in the stomach, so that he died, for the blood of Asah'el his brother.
Afterward, when Dawid heard of it, he said, I and my kingdom are forever guiltless before YHWH for the blood of Avner the son of Ner.

May it fall upon the head of Yoav and upon all his father's house, and may the house of Yoav never be without one who has a discharge or who is leprous or who holds a spindle or who falls by the sword or who lacks bread.
So Yoav and Avishai his brother killed Avner, because he had put their brother Asah'el to death in the battle at Giv'on.
Then Dawid said to Yoav and to all the people who were with him, Tear your clothes and put on sackcloth and mourn before Avner. And King Dawid followed the bier.
They buried Avner at Khevron. And the king lifted up his voice and wept at the grave of Avner, and all the people wept.
And the king lamented for Avner, saying, Should Avner die as a fool dies?
Your hands were not bound, your feet were not fettered — as one falls before the wicked you have fallen. And all the people wept again over him.
Then all the people came to persuade Dawid to eat bread while it was yet day. But Dawid swore, saying, Creator do so to me and more also, if I taste bread or anything else till the sun goes down.
And all the people took notice of it, and it pleased them, as everything that the king did pleased all the people.
So all the people and all Yisra'EL understood that day that it had not been the king's will to put to death Avner the son of Ner.
And the king said to his servants, Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen this day in Yisra'EL?
And I was gentle today, though anointed king. These men, the sons of Tzeruya, are more severe than I. May YHWH repay the evildoer according to his wickedness.
When Ish-Boshet, Sha'ul's son, heard that Avner had died at Khevron, his courage failed, and all Yisra'EL was dismayed.

Now Sha'ul's son had two men who were captains of raiding bands — the name of the one was Ba'anah, and the name of the other Rekhav, sons of Rimmon a man of Beeroth, who belonged to Binyamin — for Beeroth also is counted part of Binyamin.
The Beerothites fled to Gittayim and have been sojourners there to this day.

Yehonatan, Sha'ul's son, had a son who was crippled in his feet. He was five years old when the news about Sha'ul and Yonatan came from Yizre'el, and his nurse took him up and fled, and as she fled in her haste, he fell and became lame. And his name was Mefiboshet.
Now the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rekhav and Ba'anah, set out, and about the heat of the day they came to the house of Ish-Boshet as he was taking his noonday rest.
And they came into the midst of the house as if to get wheat, and they stabbed him in the stomach. Then Rekhav and Ba'anah his brother escaped.
When they came into the house, as he lay on his bed in his bedroom, they struck him and put him to death and beheaded him. They took his head and went by the way of the Aravah all night,

And brought the head of Ish-Boshet to Dawid at Khevron. And they said to the king, Here is the head of Ish-Boshet, the son of Sha'ul, your enemy, who sought your life. YHWH has avenged my lord the king this day on Sha'ul and on his offspring.
But Dawid answered Rekhav and Ba'anah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, As YHWH lives, who has redeemed my life out of every adversity,
When one told me, Behold, Sha'ul is dead, and thought he was bringing good news, I seized him and killed him at Tziklag — that was the reward I gave him for his news.
How much more, when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house on his bed, shall I not now require his blood at your hand and destroy you from the earth?

And Dawid commanded his young men, and they killed them and cut off their hands and feet and hanged them beside the pool at Khevron. But they took the head of Ish-Boshet and buried it in the tomb of Avner at Khevron.
Then all the tribes of Yisra'EL came to Dawid at Khevron and said, Behold, we are your bone and flesh.
In times past, when Sha'ul was king over us, it was you who led out and brought in Yisra'EL. And YHWH said to you, You shall be shepherd of my people Yisra'EL, and you shall be prince over Yisra'EL.
So all the elders of Yisra'EL came to the king at Khevron, and King Dawid made a covenant with them at Khevron before YHWH, and they anointed Dawid king over Yisra'EL.
Dawid was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
At Khevron he reigned over Yehudah seven years and six months, and at Yerushalayim he reigned over all Yisra'EL and Yehudah thirty-three years.

And the king and his men went to Yerushalayim against the Yevusites, the inhabitants of the land, who said to Dawid, You will not come in here, but the blind and the lame will ward you off — thinking, Dawid cannot come in here.
Nevertheless, Dawid took the stronghold of Tziyon, that is, the city of Dawid.

And Dawid said on that day, Whoever would strike the Yevusites, let him get up the water shaft to attack the lame and the blind, who are hated by Dawid's soul. Therefore it is said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house.
And Dawid lived in the stronghold and called it the city of Dawid. And Dawid built the city all around from the Millo inward.
And Dawid became greater and greater, for YHWH, the Creator of hosts, was with him.
And Khiram king of Tzor sent messengers to Dawid, and cedar trees, also carpenters and masons who built Dawid a house.
And Dawid knew that YHWH had established him king over Yisra'EL, and that he had exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people Yisra'EL.
And Dawid took more concubines and wives from Yerushalayim, after he came from Khevron, and more sons and daughters were born to Dawid.
And these are the names of those who were born to him in Yerushalayim: Shammua, Shovav, Natan, Shelomoh,
Yivkhar, Elishua, Nefeg, Yafiya,
Elishama, Elyada, and Eliefelet.
When the Pelishtim heard that they had anointed Dawid king over Yisra'EL, all the Pelishtim went up to search for Dawid. But Dawid heard of it and went down to the stronghold.
Now the Pelishtim had come and spread out in the Valley of Refa'im.
And Dawid inquired of YHWH, Shall I go up against the Pelishtim? Will you give them into my hand? And YHWH said to Dawid, Go up, for I will certainly give the Pelishtim into your hand.

And Dawid came to Ba'al-Peratzim, and Dawid defeated them there. And he said, YHWH has broken through my enemies before me like a breaking flood. Therefore the name of that place is called Ba'al-Peratzim.
And the Pelishtim left their idols there, and Dawid and his men carried them away.
And the Pelishtim came up yet again and spread out in the Valley of Refa'im.
And when Dawid inquired of YHWH, he said, You shall not go up — go around to their rear and come against them opposite the balsam trees.
And when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then rouse yourself, for then YHWH has gone out before you to strike down the army of the Pelishtim.
And Dawid did as YHWH commanded him, and struck down the Pelishtim from Geva to Gezer.
Dawid again gathered all the chosen men of Yisra'EL, thirty thousand.

And Dawid arose and went with all the people who were with him from Ba'alei-Yehudah to bring up from there the Ark of Creator, which is called by the name of YHWH of hosts who sits enthroned on the cherubim.
And they carried the Ark of Creator on a new cart and brought it out of the house of Avina'dav, which was on the hill. And Uzzah and Akhyo, the sons of Avina'dav, were driving the new cart,
With the Ark of Creator, and Akhyo went before the Ark.
And Dawid and all the house of Yisra'EL were celebrating before YHWH, with songs and lyres and harps and tambourines and castanets and cymbals.
And when they came to the threshing floor of Nakhon, Uzzah put out his hand to the Ark of Creator and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled.
And the anger of YHWH was kindled against Uzzah, and Creator struck him down there because of his error, and he died there beside the Ark of Creator.
And Dawid was angry because YHWH had broken out against Uzzah. And that place is called Perez-Uzzah, to this day.
And Dawid was afraid of YHWH that day, and he said, How can the Ark of YHWH come to me?
So Dawid was not willing to take the Ark of YHWH into the city of Dawid. But Dawid took it aside to the house of Oved-Edom the Gittite.
And the Ark of YHWH remained in the house of Oved-Edom the Gittite three months, and YHWH blessed Oved-Edom and all his household.

And it was told King Dawid, YHWH has blessed the household of Oved-Edom and all that belongs to him, because of the Ark of Creator. So Dawid went and brought up the Ark of Creator from the house of Oved-Edom to the city of Dawid with rejoicing.
And when those who bore the Ark of YHWH had gone six steps, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened animal.
And Dawid danced before YHWH with all his might. And Dawid was wearing a linen ephod.
So Dawid and all the house of Yisra'EL brought up the Ark of YHWH with shouting and with the sound of the horn.
As the Ark of YHWH came into the city of Dawid, Mikhal the daughter of Sha'ul looked out of the window and saw King Dawid leaping and dancing before YHWH, and she despised him in her heart.
And they brought in the Ark of YHWH and set it in its place, inside the tent that Dawid had pitched for it. And Dawid offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before YHWH.
And when Dawid had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of YHWH of hosts

And distributed among all the people, the whole multitude of Yisra'EL, both men and women, a cake of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins to each one. Then all the people departed, each to his house.

And Dawid returned to bless his household. But Mikhal the daughter of Sha'ul came out to meet Dawid and said, How the king of Yisra'EL honored himself today, uncovering himself today before the eyes of his servants' female servants, as one of the vulgar fellows shamelessly uncovers himself.
And Dawid said to Mikhal, It was before YHWH, who chose me above your father and above all his house, to appoint me as prince over Yisra'EL, the people of YHWH — and I will celebrate before YHWH.
I will make myself yet more contemptible than this, and I will be abased in your eyes. But by the female servants of whom you have spoken, by them I shall be held in honor.
And Mikhal the daughter of Sha'ul had no child to the day of her death.
Now when the king lived in his house and YHWH had given him rest from all his surrounding enemies,
The king said to Natan the prophet, See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the Ark of Creator dwells in a tent.
And Natan said to the king, Go, do all that is in your heart, for YHWH is with you.
But that same night the word of YHWH came to Natan,
Go and tell my servant Dawid, Thus says YHWH: Would you build me a house to dwell in?
I have not lived in a house since the day I brought up the people of Yisra'EL from Egypt to this day, but I have been moving about in a tent for my dwelling.

In all places where I have moved with all the people of Yisra'EL, did I speak a word with any of the judges of Yisra'EL, whom I commanded to shepherd my people Yisra'EL, saying, Why have you not built me a house of cedar?
Now therefore thus you shall say to my servant Dawid, Thus says YHWH of hosts, I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, that you should be prince over my people Yisra'EL.
And I have been with you wherever you went and have cut off all your enemies from before you. And I will make for you a great name, like the name of the great ones of the earth.
And I will appoint a place for my people Yisra'EL and will plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more. And violent men shall afflict them no more, as formerly,
From the time that I appointed judges over my people Yisra'EL. And I will give you rest from all your enemies. Moreover, YHWH declares to you that YHWH will make you a house.
When your days are fulfilled and you lie down with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, who shall come from your body, and I will establish his kingdom.
He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son. When he commits iniquity, I will discipline him with the rod of men, with the stripes of the sons of men,
But my steadfast love will not depart from him, as I took it from Sha'ul, whom I put away from before you.
And your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me. Your throne shall be established forever.
In accordance with all these words, and in accordance with all this vision, Natan spoke to Dawid.
Then King Dawid went in and sat before YHWH and said, Who am I, O YHWH Creator, and what is my house, that you have brought me thus far?
And yet this was a small thing in your eyes, O YHWH Creator. You have spoken also of your servant's house for a great while to come, and this is instruction for mankind, O YHWH Creator.
And what more can Dawid say to you? For you know your servant, O YHWH Creator.
Because of your promise, and according to your own heart, you have brought about all this greatness, to make your servant know it.
Therefore you are great, O YHWH Creator. For there is none like you, and there is no Creator besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

And who is like your people Yisra'EL, the one nation on earth whom Creator went to redeem to be his people, making himself a name and doing for them great and awesome things by driving out before your people, whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt, a nation and its gods?
And you established for yourself your people Yisra'EL to be your people forever. And you, O YHWH, became their Creator.
And now, O YHWH Creator, confirm forever the word that you have spoken concerning your servant and concerning his house, and do as you have spoken.
And your name will be magnified forever, saying, YHWH of hosts is Creator over Yisra'EL, and the house of your servant Dawid will be established before you.
For you, O YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL, have made this revelation to your servant, saying, I will build you a house. Therefore your servant has found courage to pray this prayer to you.
And now, O YHWH Creator, you are Creator, and your words are true, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.

Now therefore may it please you to bless the house of your servant, so that it may continue forever before you. For you, O YHWH Creator, have spoken, and with your blessing shall the house of your servant be blessed forever.
After this Dawid defeated the Pelishtim and subdued them, and Dawid took Meteg-ha-Ammah out of the hand of the Pelishtim.

And he defeated Moav and he measured them with a line, making them lie down on the ground. Two lines he measured to be put to death, and one full line to be kept alive. And Moav became servants to Dawid and brought tribute.
Dawid also defeated Hadadezer the son of Rekhov, king of Tzovah, as he went to restore his power at the river Euphrates.
And Dawid took from him one thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers. And Dawid hamstrung all the chariot horses but left enough for a hundred chariots.
And when the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Tzovah, Dawid struck down twenty-two thousand men of the Syrians.
Then Dawid put garrisons in Aram-Damascus, and the Syrians became servants to Dawid and brought tribute. And YHWH gave victory to Dawid wherever he went.
And Dawid took the shields of gold that were carried by the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Yerushalayim.
And from Betakh and from Berotai, cities of Hadadezer, King Dawid took very much bronze.
When Toi king of Khamath heard that Dawid had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer,

Toi sent his son Yoram to King Dawid, to ask about his health and to bless him because he had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him — for Hadadezer had often been at war with Toi. And Yoram brought with him articles of silver, of gold, and of bronze.
These also King Dawid dedicated to YHWH, together with the silver and gold that he dedicated from all the nations he subdued,
From Edom, Moav, the Ammonites, the Pelishtim, Amalek, and from the spoil of Hadadezer the son of Rekhov, king of Tzovah.
And Dawid made a name for himself when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
Then he put garrisons in Edom — throughout all Edom he put garrisons — and all the Edomites became Dawid's servants. And YHWH gave victory to Dawid wherever he went.
So Dawid reigned over all Yisra'EL. And Dawid administered justice and equity to all his people.
Yoav the son of Tzeruya was over the army, and Yehoshafat the son of Akhilud was recorder,
And Tzadok the son of Akhituv and Akhimelekh the son of Evyatar were priests, and Seraya was secretary,
And Benaya the son of Yehoyada was over the Kerethites and the Pelethites, and Dawid's sons were priests.
And Dawid said, Is there still anyone left of the house of Sha'ul, that I may show him kindness for Yonatan's sake?
Now there was a servant of the house of Sha'ul whose name was Tziva. And when they called him to Dawid, the king said to him, Are you Tziva? And he said, I am your servant.

And the king said, Is there not still someone of the house of Sha'ul, that I may show the kindness of Creator to him? Tziva said to the king, There is still a son of Yonatan — he is crippled in his feet.
The king said to him, Where is he? And Tziva said to the king, He is in the house of Makhir the son of Ammiel, at Lo-Devar.
Then King Dawid sent and brought him from the house of Makhir the son of Ammiel, at Lo-Devar.
And Mefiboshet the son of Yonatan, son of Sha'ul, came to Dawid and fell on his face and paid homage. And Dawid said, Mefiboshet. And he answered, Behold, I am your servant.

And Dawid said to him, Do not fear, for I will show you kindness for the sake of your father Yonatan, and I will restore to you all the land of Sha'ul your father, and you shall eat at my table always.
And he paid homage and said, What is your servant, that you should show regard for a dead dog such as I?
Then the king called Tziva, Sha'ul's servant, and said to him, All that belonged to Sha'ul and to all his house I have given to your master's grandson.

And you and your sons and your servants shall till the land for him and shall bring in the produce, that your master's grandson may have bread to eat. But Mefiboshet your master's grandson shall always eat at my table. Now Tziva had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
Then Tziva said to the king, According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so will your servant do. So Mefiboshet ate at Dawid's table, like one of the king's sons.
And Mefiboshet had a young son, whose name was Mikha. And all who lived in Tziva's house became Mefiboshet's servants.
So Mefiboshet lived in Yerushalayim, for he ate always at the king's table. Now he was lame in both his feet.
After this the king of the Ammonites died, and Khanun his son reigned in his place.

And Dawid said, I will deal loyally with Khanun the son of Nakhash, as his father dealt loyally with me. So Dawid sent by his servants to console him concerning his father. And Dawid's servants came into the land of the Ammonites.

But the princes of the Ammonites said to Khanun their lord, Do you think, because Dawid has sent comforters to you, that he is honoring your father? Has not Dawid sent his servants to you to search the city and to spy it out and to overthrow it?
So Khanun took Dawid's servants and shaved off half the beard of each and cut off their garments in the middle, at their hips, and sent them away.
When it was told Dawid, he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, Remain at Yerikho until your beards have grown and then return.

When the Ammonites saw that they had become a stench to Dawid, the Ammonites sent and hired the Syrians of Beit-Rekhov and the Syrians of Tzovah, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and the king of Ma'akhah with one thousand men, and the men of Tov, twelve thousand men.
And when Dawid heard of it, he sent Yoav and all the host of the mighty men.
And the Ammonites came out and drew up in battle array at the entrance of the gate, and the Syrians of Tzovah and of Rekhov and the men of Tov and Ma'akhah were by themselves in the open country.
When Yoav saw that the battle was set against him both in front and in the rear, he chose some of the best men of Yisra'EL and arrayed them against the Syrians.
The rest of his men he put in the charge of Avishai his brother, and he arrayed them against the Ammonites.
And he said, If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you shall help me, but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come and help you.
Be of good courage, and let us be courageous for our people, and for the cities of our Creator, and may YHWH do what seems good to him.
So Yoav and the people who were with him drew near to battle against the Syrians, and they fled before him.
And when the Ammonites saw that the Syrians fled, they also fled before Avishai and entered the city. Then Yoav returned from fighting against the Ammonites and came to Yerushalayim.
But when the Syrians saw that they had been defeated by Yisra'EL, they gathered themselves together.
And Hadadezer sent and brought out the Syrians who were beyond the Euphrates. They came to Khelam, with Shovakh the commander of the army of Hadadezer at their head.
And when it was told Dawid, he gathered all Yisra'EL together and crossed the Yarden and came to Khelam. The Syrians arrayed themselves against Dawid and fought with him.

And the Syrians fled before Yisra'EL, and Dawid killed of the Syrians the men of seven hundred chariots, and forty thousand horsemen, and wounded Shovakh the commander of their army, so that he died there.

And when all the kings who were servants of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Yisra'EL, they made peace with Yisra'EL and became subject to them. So the Syrians were afraid to save the Ammonites anymore.

In the spring of the year, the time when kings go out to battle, Dawid sent Yoav, and his servants with him, and all Yisra'EL. And they ravaged the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah. But Dawid remained at Yerushalayim.
It happened, late one afternoon, when Dawid arose from his couch and was walking on the roof of the king's house, that he saw from the roof a woman bathing. And the woman was very beautiful.
And Dawid sent and inquired about the woman. And one said, Is not this Bathsheva, the daughter of Eli'am, the wife of Uriyah the Khittite?
So Dawid sent messengers and took her, and she came to him, and he lay with her. Now she had been purifying herself from her uncleanness. Then she returned to her house.
And the woman conceived, and she sent and told Dawid, I am pregnant.
So Dawid sent word to Yoav, Send me Uriyah the Khittite. And Yoav sent Uriyah to Dawid.
When Uriyah came to him, Dawid asked how Yoav was doing and how the people were doing and how the war was going.
And Dawid said to Uriyah, Go down to your house and wash your feet. And Uriyah went out of the king's house, and there followed him a present from the king.
But Uriyah slept at the door of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and did not go down to his house.
When they told Dawid, Uriyah did not go down to his house, Dawid said to Uriyah, Have you not come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?

Uriyah said to Dawid, The Ark and Yisra'EL and Yehudah dwell in booths, and my lord Yoav and the servants of my lord are camping in the open field. Shall I then go to my house, to eat and to drink and to lie with my wife? As you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do this thing.
Then Dawid said to Uriyah, Remain here today also, and tomorrow I will send you back. So Uriyah remained in Yerushalayim that day and the next.

And Dawid invited him, and he ate in his presence and drank, so that he made him drunk. And in the evening he went out to lie on his couch with the servants of his lord, but he did not go down to his house.
In the morning Dawid wrote a letter to Yoav and sent it by the hand of Uriyah.
In the letter he wrote, Set Uriyah in the forefront of the hardest fighting, and then draw back from him, that he may be struck down, and die.
And as Yoav was besieging the city, he assigned Uriyah to the place where he knew there were valiant men.
And the men of the city came out and fought with Yoav, and some of the servants of Dawid among the people fell. Uriyah the Khittite also died.
Then Yoav sent and told Dawid all the news about the fighting.
And he instructed the messenger, When you have finished telling all the news about the fighting to the king,
Then, if the king's anger rises, and if he says to you, Why did you go so near the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot from the wall?

Who killed Avimelekh the son of Yeruba'al? Did not a woman cast an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died at Tevetz? Why did you go so near the wall? then you shall say, Your servant Uriyah the Khittite is dead also.
So the messenger went and came and told Dawid all that Yoav had sent him to tell.
The messenger said to Dawid, The men gained an advantage over us and came out against us in the field, but we drove them back to the entrance of the gate.
Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall. Some of the king's servants are dead, and your servant Uriyah the Khittite is dead also.

Dawid said to the messenger, Thus shall you say to Yoav, Do not let this matter trouble you, for the sword devours now one and now another. Strengthen your attack against the city and overthrow it. And encourage him.
When the wife of Uriyah heard that Uriyah her husband was dead, she lamented over her husband.
And when the mourning was over, Dawid sent and brought her to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that Dawid had done displeased YHWH.
And YHWH sent Natan to Dawid. He came to him and said to him, There were two men in a certain city, the one rich and the other poor.
The rich man had very many flocks and herds,

But the poor man had nothing but one little ewe lamb, which he had bought. And he brought it up, and it grew up with him and with his children. It used to eat of his morsel and drink from his cup and lie in his arms, and it was like a daughter to him.

Now there came a traveler to the rich man, and he was unwilling to take one of his own flock or herd to prepare for the guest who had come to him, but he took the poor man's lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him.
Then Dawid's anger was greatly kindled against the man, and he said to Natan, As YHWH lives, the man who has done this deserves to die,
And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
Natan said to Dawid, You are the man. Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, I anointed you king over Yisra'EL, and I delivered you out of the hand of Sha'ul.
And I gave you your master's house and your master's wives into your arms and gave you the house of Yisra'EL and of Yehudah. And if this were too little, I would add to you as much more.

Why have you despised the word of YHWH, to do what is evil in his sight? You have struck down Uriyah the Khittite with the sword and have taken his wife to be your wife and have killed him with the sword of the Ammonites.
Now therefore the sword shall never depart from your house, because you have despised me and have taken the wife of Uriyah the Khittite to be your wife.

Thus says YHWH, Behold, I will raise up evil against you out of your own house. And I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he shall lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.
For you did it secretly, but I will do this thing before all Yisra'EL and before the sun.
Dawid said to Natan, I have sinned against YHWH. And Natan said to Dawid, YHWH also has put away your sin — you shall not die.
Nevertheless, because by this deed you have utterly scorned YHWH, the child who is born to you shall die.
Then Natan went to his house. And YHWH afflicted the child that Uriyah's wife bore to Dawid, and he became sick.
Dawid therefore sought Creator on behalf of the child. And Dawid fasted and went in and lay all night on the ground.
And the elders of his house stood beside him, to raise him from the ground, but he would not, nor did he eat food with them.

On the seventh day the child died. And the servants of Dawid were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spoke to him, and he did not listen to us. How then can we say to him the child is dead? He may do himself some harm.
But when Dawid saw that his servants were whispering together, Dawid understood that the child was dead. And Dawid said to his servants, Is the child dead? They said, He is dead.

Then Dawid arose from the earth and washed and anointed himself and changed his clothes. And he went into the house of YHWH and worshiped. He then went to his own house. And when he asked, they set food before him, and he ate.
Then his servants said to him, What is this thing that you have done? You fasted and wept for the child while it was alive, but when the child died, you arose and ate food.
He said, While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept, for I said, Who knows whether YHWH will be gracious to me, that the child may live?
But now he is dead. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he will not return to me.
Then Dawid comforted his wife Bathsheva, and went in to her and lay with her, and she bore a son, and he called his name Shelomoh. And YHWH loved him
And sent a message by Natan the prophet. So he called his name Yedidyah, because of YHWH.
Now Yoav fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and took the royal city.
And Yoav sent messengers to Dawid and said, I have fought against Rabbah — moreover, I have taken the city of waters.
Now then gather the rest of the people together and encamp against the city and take it, lest I take the city and it be called by my name.
So Dawid gathered all the people together and went to Rabbah and fought against it and took it.

And he took the crown of their king from his head. The weight of it was a talent of gold, and in it was a precious stone, and it was placed on Dawid's head. And he brought out the spoil of the city, a very great amount.

And he brought out the people who were in it and set them to labor with saws and iron picks and iron axes and made them toil at the brick kilns. And thus he did to all the cities of the Ammonites. Then Dawid and all the people returned to Yerushalayim.
Afterward this happened: Dawid's son Avshalom had a beautiful sister, whose name was Tamar. And Amnon, Dawid's son, loved her.
And Amnon was so tormented that he made himself ill because of his sister Tamar, for she was a virgin, and it seemed impossible to Amnon to do anything to her.
But Amnon had a friend, whose name was Yonadav, the son of Shim'ah, Dawid's brother. And Yonadav was a very crafty man.
And he said to him, O son of the king, why are you so haggard morning after morning? Will you not tell me? Amnon said to him, I love Tamar, my brother Avshalom's sister.

Yonadav said to him, Lie down on your bed and pretend to be ill. And when your father comes to see you, say to him, Let my sister Tamar come and give me bread to eat, and prepare the food in my sight, that I may see it and eat it from her hand.

So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill. And when the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand.
Then Dawid sent home to Tamar, saying, Go to your brother Amnon's house and prepare food for him.
So Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house, where he was lying down. And she took dough and kneaded it and made cakes in his sight and baked the cakes.
And she took the pan and emptied it out before him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Send out everyone from me. So everyone went out from him.
Then Amnon said to Tamar, Bring the food into the chamber, that I may eat from your hand. And Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them into the chamber to Amnon her brother.
But when she brought them near him to eat, he took hold of her and said to her, Come, lie with me, my sister.
She answered him, No, my brother, do not violate me, for such a thing is not done in Yisra'EL — do not do this outrageous thing.
As for me, where could I carry my shame? And as for you, you would be as one of the outrageous fools in Yisra'EL. Now therefore, please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you.
But he would not listen to her, and being stronger than she, he violated her and lay with her.
Then Amnon hated her with very great hatred, so that the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, Get up and go.
But she said to him, No, my brother, for this wrong in sending me away is greater than the other that you did to me. But he would not listen to her.
He called the young man who served him and said, Put this woman out of my presence and bolt the door after her.
Now she was wearing a long robe with sleeves, for thus were the virgin daughters of the king dressed. So his servant put her out and bolted the door after her.
And Tamar put ashes on her head and tore the long robe that she wore. And she laid her hand on her head and went away, crying aloud as she went.

And her brother Avshalom said to her, Has Amnon your brother been with you? Now hold your peace, my sister. He is your brother — do not take this to heart. So Tamar lived, a desolate woman, in her brother Avshalom's house.
When King Dawid heard of all these things, he was very angry.
But Avshalom spoke to Amnon neither good nor bad, for Avshalom hated Amnon, because he had violated his sister Tamar.
After two full years Avshalom had sheepshearers at Ba'al-Khatzor, which is near Efrayim, and Avshalom invited all the king's sons.
And Avshalom came to the king and said, Behold, your servant has sheepshearers. Please let the king and his servants go with your servant.
But the king said to Avshalom, No, my son, let us not all go, lest we be burdensome to you. He pressed him, but he would not go but gave him his blessing.
Then Avshalom said, If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us. And the king said to him, Why should he go with you?
But Avshalom pressed him until he let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him.

Then Avshalom commanded his servants, Mark when Amnon's heart is merry with wine, and when I say to you, Strike Amnon, then kill him. Do not fear — have I not commanded you? Be courageous and be valiant.
So the servants of Avshalom did to Amnon as Avshalom had commanded. Then all the king's sons arose, and each mounted his mule and fled.
While they were on the way, news came to Dawid, Avshalom has struck down all the king's sons, and not one of them is left.
Then the king arose and tore his garments and lay on the earth. And all his servants who were standing by tore their garments.

But Yonadav, the son of Shim'ah, Dawid's brother, said, Let not my lord suppose that they have killed all the young men, the king's sons, for Amnon alone is dead. For by the command of Avshalom this has been determined from the day he violated his sister Tamar.
Now therefore let not my lord the king take it to heart as if all the king's sons are dead, for Amnon alone is dead.
But Avshalom fled. And the young man who kept the watch lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, many people were coming from the road behind him by the side of the mountain.
And Yonadav said to the king, Behold, the king's sons have come — as your servant said, so it has come about.
And as soon as he had finished speaking, behold, the king's sons came and lifted up their voice and wept. And the king also and all his servants wept very bitterly.
But Avshalom fled and went to Talmai the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And Dawid mourned for his son day after day.
So Avshalom fled and went to Geshur, and was there three years.
And the spirit of the king longed to go out to Avshalom, because he was comforted about Amnon, since he was dead.
Now Yoav the son of Tzeruya knew that the king's heart went out to Avshalom.

And Yoav sent to Teko'a and brought from there a wise woman and said to her, Please pretend to be a mourner and put on mourning garments. Do not anoint yourself with oil, but behave like a woman who has been mourning many days for the dead.
Go to the king and speak thus to him. So Yoav put the words in her mouth.
When the woman of Teko'a came to the king, she fell on her face to the ground and paid homage and said, Help, O king.
And the king said to her, What is your trouble? She answered, Alas, I am a widow — my husband is dead.
And your servant had two sons, and they quarreled with one another in the field. There was no one to separate them, and one struck the other and killed him.

And now the whole clan has risen against your servant, and they say, Give up the man who struck his brother, that we may put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed. And so they would destroy the heir also. Thus they would quench my coal that is left and leave to my husband neither name nor remnant on the face of the earth.
Then the king said to the woman, Go to your house, and I will give orders concerning you.
And the woman of Teko'a said to the king, On me be the guilt, my lord the king, and on my father's house — let the king and his throne be guiltless.
The king said, If anyone says anything to you, bring him to me, and he shall never touch you again.

Then she said, Please let the king invoke YHWH your Creator, that the avenger of blood kill no more, and my son not be destroyed. He said, As YHWH lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground.
Then the woman said, Please let your servant speak a word to my lord the king. He said, Speak.

The woman said, Why then have you planned such a thing against the people of Creator? For in giving this decision the king convicts himself, inasmuch as the king does not bring his banished one home again.

We must all die — we are like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. But Creator will not take away life, and he devises means so that the banished one will not remain an outcast.

Now I have come to say this to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid, and your servant thought, I will speak to the king. It may be that the king will perform the request of his servant.
For the king will hear and deliver his servant from the hand of the man who would destroy me and my son together from the heritage of Creator.
And your servant thought, The word of my lord the king will set me at rest, for my lord the king is like the angel of Creator to discern good and evil. May YHWH your Creator be with you.
Then the king answered the woman, Do not hide from me anything I ask you. And the woman said, Let my lord the king speak.

The king said, Is the hand of Yoav with you in all this? The woman answered and said, As your soul lives, my lord the king, one cannot turn to the right hand or to the left from anything that my lord the king has said. It was your servant Yoav who commanded me — it was he who put all these words in the mouth of your servant.
In order to change the course of things your servant Yoav did this. But my lord has wisdom like the wisdom of the angel of Creator to know all things that are on earth.
Then the king said to Yoav, Behold now, I do this thing. Go, bring back the young man Avshalom.

And Yoav fell on his face to the ground and paid homage and blessed the king. And Yoav said, Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord the king, in that the king has granted the request of his servant.
So Yoav arose and went to Geshur and brought Avshalom to Yerushalayim.
And the king said, Let him dwell apart in his own house — he is not to come into my presence. So Avshalom lived apart in his own house and did not come into the king's presence.
Now in all Yisra'EL there was no one so much to be praised for his handsome appearance as Avshalom. From the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
And when he cut the hair of his head — he cut it at the end of every year, because it was heavy on him, and when he cut it he weighed the hair of his head, two hundred shekels by the king's weight —
There were born to Avshalom three sons, and one daughter whose name was Tamar. She was a beautiful woman.
So Avshalom lived two full years in Yerushalayim without coming into the king's presence.
Then Avshalom sent for Yoav, to send him to the king, but Yoav would not come to him. And he sent a second time, but Yoav would not come.
Then he said to his servants, See, Yoav's field is next to mine, and he has barley there — go and set it on fire. So Avshalom's servants set the field on fire.
Then Yoav arose and went to Avshalom at his house and said to him, Why have your servants set my field on fire?

Avshalom answered Yoav, Behold, I sent word to you, Come here, that I may send you to the king, to ask, Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to be there still. Now therefore let me go into the presence of the king, and if there is guilt in me, let him put me to death.
Then Yoav went to the king and told him, and he summoned Avshalom. So he came to the king and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king, and the king kissed Avshalom.
After this Avshalom got himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

And Avshalom used to rise early and stand beside the way of the gate. And when any man had a dispute to come before the king for judgment, Avshalom would call to him and say, From what city are you? And when he said, Your servant is of such and such a tribe in Yisra'EL,
Avshalom would say to him, See, your claims are good and right, but there is no man designated by the king to hear you.
Then Avshalom would say, Oh that I were judge in the land. Then every man with a dispute or cause might come to me, and I would give him justice.
And whenever a man came near to pay homage to him, he would put out his hand and take hold of him and kiss him.
Thus Avshalom did to all of Yisra'EL who came to the king for judgment. So Avshalom stole the hearts of the men of Yisra'EL.
And at the end of four years Avshalom said to the king, Please let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed to YHWH, in Khevron.
For your servant vowed a vow while I lived at Geshur in Aram, saying, If YHWH will indeed bring me back to Yerushalayim, then I will offer worship to YHWH.
The king said to him, Go in peace. So he arose and went to Khevron.
But Avshalom sent secret messengers throughout all the tribes of Yisra'EL, saying, As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then say, Avshalom is king at Khevron.
With Avshalom went two hundred men from Yerushalayim who were invited guests, and they went in their innocence and knew nothing.

And while Avshalom was offering the sacrifices, he sent for Akhitofel the Gilonite, Dawid's counselor, from his city Gilo. And the conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Avshalom kept increasing.
And a messenger came to Dawid, saying, The hearts of the men of Yisra'EL have gone after Avshalom.

Then Dawid said to all his servants who were with him at Yerushalayim, Arise, and let us flee, or else there will be no escape for us from Avshalom. Go quickly, lest he overtake us quickly and bring down ruin on us and strike the city with the edge of the sword.
And the king's servants said to the king, Behold, your servants are ready to do whatever my lord the king decides.
So the king went out, and all his household after him. And the king left ten concubines to keep the house.
And the king went out, and all the people after him. And they halted at the last house.
And all his servants passed by him, and all the Kerethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gat, passed before the king.
Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, Why do you also go with us? Go back and stay with the king, for you are a foreigner and also an exile from your home.
You came only yesterday, and shall I today make you wander with us, since I go I know not where? Go back and take your brothers with you, and may YHWH show steadfast love and faithfulness to you.
But Ittai answered the king, As YHWH lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will your servant be.
And Dawid said to Ittai, Go then, pass on. So Ittai the Gittite passed on with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.
And all the land wept aloud as all the people passed by, and the king crossed the brook Kidron, and all the people passed on toward the wilderness.

And Zadok came also with all the Levites, bearing the Ark of the Covenant of Creator. And they set down the Ark of Creator until the people had all passed out of the city. And Evyatar offered sacrifices until the people had all passed out of the city.
Then the king said to Tzadok, Carry the Ark of Creator back into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of YHWH, he will bring me back and let me see both it and his dwelling place.
But if he says, I have no pleasure in you, behold, here I am — let him do to me what seems good to him.
The king also said to Tzadok the priest, Are you not a seer? Go back to the city in peace, with your two sons, Akhima'atz your son, and Yehonatan the son of Evyatar.
See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.
So Tzadok and Evyatar carried the Ark of Creator back to Yerushalayim, and they remained there.

But Dawid went up the ascent of the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went, barefoot and with his head covered. And all the people who were with him covered their heads, and they went up, weeping as they went.
And it was told Dawid, Akhitofel is among the conspirators with Avshalom. And Dawid said, O YHWH, please turn the counsel of Akhitofel into foolishness.
When Dawid came to the summit, where Creator was worshiped, behold, Khushai the Arkite came to meet him with his coat torn and dirt on his head.
Dawid said to him, If you go on with me, you will be a burden to me.

But if you return to the city and say to Avshalom, I will be your servant, O king — as I have been your father's servant in time past, so now I will be your servant — then you will defeat for me the counsel of Akhitofel.
Are not Tzadok and Evyatar the priests with you there? So whatever you hear from the king's house, tell it to Tzadok and Evyatar the priests.
Behold, their two sons are with them there, Akhima'atz, Tzadok's son, and Yehonatan, Evyatar's son, and by them you shall send to me everything you hear.
So Khushai, Dawid's friend, came into the city, just as Avshalom was entering Yerushalayim.

When Dawid had passed a little beyond the summit, Tziva the servant of Mefiboshet met him, with a couple of donkeys saddled, bearing two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred of summer fruits, and a skin of wine.

And the king said to Tziva, Why have you brought these? Tziva answered, The donkeys are for the king's household to ride on, the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat, and the wine for those who faint in the wilderness to drink.
And the king said, And where is your master's son? Tziva said to the king, Behold, he remains in Yerushalayim, for he said, Today the house of Yisra'EL will give me back the kingdom of my father.
Then the king said to Tziva, Behold, all that belonged to Mefiboshet is now yours. And Tziva said, I pay homage — let me ever find favor in your sight, my lord the king.
When King Dawid came to Bakhurim, there came out a man of the family of the house of Sha'ul, whose name was Shim'i, the son of Gera, and as he came he cursed continually.
And he threw stones at Dawid and at all the servants of King Dawid, and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.
And Shim'i said as he cursed, Get out, get out, you man of blood, you worthless man.

YHWH has avenged on you all the blood of the house of Sha'ul, in whose place you have reigned, and YHWH has given the kingdom into the hand of your son Avshalom. See, your evil is on you, for you are a man of blood.
Then Avishai the son of Tzeruya said to the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and take off his head.
But the king said, What have I to do with you, you sons of Tzeruya? If he is cursing because YHWH said to him, Curse Dawid, who then shall say, Why have you done so?

And Dawid said to Avishai and to all his servants, Behold, my son who came from my own body seeks my life — how much more now may this Binyaminite. Leave him alone, and let him curse, for YHWH has told him to.
It may be that YHWH will look on the wrong done to me, and that YHWH will repay me with good for his cursing today.
So Dawid and his men went on the road, while Shim'i went along on the hillside opposite him and cursed as he went and threw stones at him and flung dust.
And the king, and all the people who were with him, arrived weary at the Jordan. And there he refreshed himself.
Now Avshalom and all the people, the men of Yisra'EL, came to Yerushalayim, and Akhitofel with him.
And when Khushai the Arkite, Dawid's friend, came to Avshalom, Khushai said to Avshalom, Long live the king. Long live the king.
And Avshalom said to Khushai, Is this your loyalty to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?
And Khushai said to Avshalom, No, for whom YHWH and this people and all the men of Yisra'EL have chosen, his I will be, and with him I will remain.
And again, whom should I serve? Should it not be his son? As I have served your father, so I will serve you.
Then Avshalom said to Akhitofel, Give your counsel. What shall we do?

Akhitofel said to Avshalom, Go in to your father's concubines, whom he has left to keep the house, and all Yisra'EL will hear that you have made yourself a stench to your father, and the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened.
So they pitched a tent for Avshalom on the roof. And Avshalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Yisra'EL.
Now in those days the counsel that Akhitofel gave was as if one consulted the word of Creator — so was all the counsel of Akhitofel esteemed, both by Dawid and by Avshalom.
Moreover, Akhitofel said to Avshalom, Let me choose twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue Dawid tonight.
I will come upon him while he is weary and discouraged and throw him into a panic, and all the people who are with him will flee. I will strike down only the king,
And will bring all the people back to you as a bride comes home to her husband. You seek the life of only one man, and all the people will be at peace.
And the advice seemed right in the eyes of Avshalom and all the elders of Yisra'EL.
Then Avshalom said, Call Khushai the Arkite also, and let us hear what he has to say.
And when Khushai came to Avshalom, Avshalom said to him, Thus has Akhitofel spoken. Shall we do as he says? If not, you speak.
Then Khushai said to Avshalom, This time the counsel that Akhitofel has given is not good.

Khushai said, You know that your father and his men are mighty men, and that they are enraged, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. Besides, your father is expert in war — he will not spend the night with the people.

Behold, even now he has hidden himself in one of the pits or in some other place. And as soon as some of the people fall at the first attack, whoever hears it will say, There has been a defeat among the people who follow Avshalom.

Then even the valiant man, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will utterly melt with fear, for all Yisra'EL knows that your father is a mighty man, and that those who are with him are valiant men.
But my counsel is that all Yisra'EL be gathered to you, from Dan to Be'er-Sheva, as the sand by the sea for multitude, and that you go to battle in person.
So we shall come upon him in some place where he is to be found, and we shall light on him as the dew falls on the ground, and of him and all the men with him not one will be left.
If he withdraws into a city, then all Yisra'EL shall bring ropes to that city, and we shall drag it into the valley, until not even a pebble is to be found there.

And Avshalom and all the men of Yisra'EL said, The counsel of Khushai the Arkite is better than the counsel of Akhitofel. For YHWH had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Akhitofel, so that YHWH might bring harm upon Avshalom.
Then Khushai said to Tzadok and Evyatar the priests, Thus and so did Akhitofel counsel Avshalom and the elders of Yisra'EL, and thus and so have I counseled.
Now therefore send quickly and tell Dawid, Do not stay tonight at the fords of the wilderness, but by all means pass over, lest the king and all the people who are with him be swallowed up.
Now Yehonatan and Akhima'atz were waiting at En-Rogel. A female servant was to go and tell them, and they were to go and tell King Dawid, for they were not to be seen entering the city.
But a young man saw them and told Avshalom. So both of them went away quickly and came to the house of a man at Bakhurim, who had a well in his courtyard. And they went down into it.
And the woman took and spread a covering over the well's mouth and scattered grain on it, and nothing was known of it.

When Avshalom's servants came to the woman at the house, they said, Where are Akhima'atz and Yehonatan? And the woman said to them, They have gone over the brook of water. And when they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Yerushalayim.
After they had gone, the men came up out of the well, and went and told King Dawid. They said to Dawid, Arise, and go quickly over the water, for thus and so has Akhitofel counseled against you.
Then Dawid arose, and all the people who were with him, and they crossed the Yarden. By daybreak not one was left who had not crossed the Yarden.

When Akhitofel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his donkey and went off home to his own city. He set his house in order and hanged himself, and he died and was buried in the tomb of his father.
Then Dawid came to Makhanayim. And Avshalom crossed the Yarden with all the men of Yisra'EL.
Now Avshalom had set Amasa over the army instead of Yoav. Amasa was the son of a man named Yitra the Ishmaelite, who had married Avigal the daughter of Nakash, sister of Tzeruya, Yoav's mother.
And Yisra'EL and Avshalom encamped in the land of Gil'ad.
When Dawid came to Makhanayim, Shobi the son of Nakhash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, and Makhir the son of Ammiel from Lo-Devar, and Barzillai the Gil'adite from Rogelim,
Brought beds, basins, and earthen vessels, wheat, barley, flour, parched grain, beans and lentils,
Honey and curds and sheep and cheese from the herd, for Dawid and the people with him to eat, for they said, The people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness.
Then Dawid mustered the men who were with him and set over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

And Dawid sent out the army, one third under the command of Yoav, one third under the command of Avishai the son of Tzeruya, Yoav's brother, and one third under the command of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the men, I myself will also go out with you.

But the men said, You shall not go out. For if we flee, they will not care about us. If half of us die, they will not care about us. But you are worth ten thousand of us. Therefore it is better that you send us help from the city.
The king said to them, Whatever seems best to you I will do. So the king stood at the side of the gate, while all the army marched out by hundreds and by thousands.
And the king commanded Yoav and Avishai and Ittai, Deal gently for my sake with the young man Avshalom. And all the people heard when the king gave orders to all the commanders about Avshalom.
So the army went out into the field against Yisra'EL, and the battle was fought in the forest of Efrayim.
And the men of Yisra'EL were defeated there before the servants of Dawid, and the loss there was great on that day — twenty thousand men.
The battle spread over the face of all the country, and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword.

And Avshalom happened to meet the servants of Dawid. Avshalom was riding on his mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of a great oak, and his head caught fast in the oak, and he was suspended between heaven and earth, while the mule that was under him went on.
And a certain man saw it and told Yoav, Behold, I saw Avshalom hanging in an oak.
Yoav said to the man who told him, What, you saw him? Why then did you not strike him there to the ground? I would have been glad to give you ten pieces of silver and a belt.

But the man said to Yoav, Even if I felt in my hand the weight of a thousand pieces of silver, I would not reach out my hand against the king's son, for in our hearing the king commanded you and Avishai and Ittai, saying, For my sake protect the young man Avshalom.
On the other hand, if I had dealt treacherously against his life — and there is nothing hidden from the king — then you yourself would have stood aloof.
Yoav said, I will not waste time like this with you. And he took three javelins in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Avshalom while he was still alive in the oak.
And ten young men, Yoav's armor-bearers, surrounded Avshalom and struck him and killed him.
Then Yoav blew the trumpet, and the troops came back from pursuing Yisra'EL, for Yoav restrained the troops.
And they took Avshalom and threw him into a great pit in the forest and raised over him a very great heap of stones. And all Yisra'EL fled every one to his own home.

Now Avshalom in his lifetime had taken and set up for himself the pillar that is in the King's Valley, for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance. He called the pillar after his own name, and it is called Avshalom's monument to this day.
Then Akhima'atz the son of Tzadok said, Let me run and carry news to the king that YHWH has delivered him from the hand of his enemies.
And Yoav said to him, You are not to carry news today. You may carry news another day, but today you shall carry no news, because the king's son is dead.
Then Yoav said to the Kushite, Go, tell the king what you have seen. The Kushite bowed before Yoav and ran.
Then Akhima'atz the son of Tzadok said again to Yoav, Come what may, let me also run after the Kushite. And Yoav said, Why will you run, my son, seeing that you will have no reward for the news?
Come what may, I will run. And he said to him, Run. Then Akhima'atz ran by the way of the plain and outran the Kushite.
Now Dawid was sitting between the two gates. And the watchman went up to the roof of the gate by the wall and lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man running alone.
And the watchman called out and told the king. And the king said, If he is alone, there is news in his mouth. And he came rapidly and drew near.
And the watchman saw another man running and called to the gatekeeper, Behold, another man running alone. The king said, He also brings news.
And the watchman said, I think the running of the first is like the running of Akhima'atz the son of Tzadok. And the king said, He is a good man and comes with good news.

And Akhima'atz called out to the king, All is well. And he bowed before the king with his face to the earth and said, Blessed be YHWH your Creator, who has delivered up the men who raised their hand against my lord the king.
And the king said, Is it well with the young man Avshalom? Akhima'atz answered, When Yoav sent the king's servant, your servant, I saw a great commotion, but I do not know what it was.
And the king said, Turn aside and stand here. So he turned aside and stood still.
And behold, the Kushite came, and the Kushite said, Good news for my lord the king. For YHWH has delivered you this day from the hand of all who rose up against you.
The king said to the Kushite, Is it well with the young man Avshalom? And the Kushite answered, May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up against you for evil be like that young man.

And the king was deeply moved and went up to the chamber over the gate and wept. And as he went, he said, O my son Avshalom, my son, my son Avshalom. Would I had died instead of you, O Avshalom, my son, my son.
It was told Yoav, Behold, the king is weeping and mourning for Avshalom.
So the victory that day was turned into mourning for all the people, for the people heard that day, The king is grieving for his son.
And the people stole into the city that day as people who are ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
The king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, O my son Avshalom, O Avshalom, my son, my son.

Then Yoav came into the house to the king and said, You have today covered with shame the faces of all your servants, who have this day saved your life and the lives of your sons and your daughters and the lives of your wives and your concubines,

Because you love those who hate you and hate those who love you. For you have made it clear today that commanders and servants are nothing to you, for today I know that if Avshalom were alive and all of us were dead today, then you would be pleased.

Now therefore arise, go out and speak kindly to your servants, for I swear by YHWH, if you do not go, not a man will stay with you this night, and this will be worse for you than all the evil that has come upon you from your youth until now.

Then the king arose and took his seat in the gate. And the people were all told, Behold, the king is sitting in the gate. And all the people came before the king. Now Yisra'EL had fled every man to his own home.

And all the people were arguing throughout all the tribes of Yisra'EL, saying, The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies and saved us from the hand of the Pelishtim, and now he has fled out of the land from Avshalom.
But Avshalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. Now therefore why do you say nothing about bringing the king back?

And King Dawid sent this message to Tzadok and Evyatar the priests, Say to the elders of Yehudah, Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his house, when the word of all Yisra'EL has come to the king?
You are my brothers — you are my bone and my flesh. Why then should you be the last to bring back the king?
And say to Amasa, Are you not my bone and my flesh? Creator do so to me, and more also, if you are not commander of my army from now on in place of Yoav.
And he swayed the heart of all the men of Yehudah as one man, so that they sent word to the king, Return, both you and all your servants.
So the king came back to the Yarden, and Yehudah came to Gilgal to meet the king and to bring the king over the Yarden.
And Shim'i the son of Gera, the Binyaminite, from Bakhurim, hurried to come down with the men of Yehudah to meet King Dawid.
And with him were a thousand men from Binyamin. And Tziva the servant of the house of Sha'ul, with his fifteen sons and his twenty servants, rushed down to the Yarden before the king,
And they crossed the ford to bring over the king's household and to do his pleasure. And Shim'i the son of Gera fell down before the king, as he was about to cross at the Yarden.
And he said to the king, Let not my lord hold me guilty or remember how your servant did wrong on the day my lord the king left Yerushalayim. Let not the king take it to heart.
For your servant knows that I have sinned. Therefore, behold, I have come this day, the first of all the house of Yosef to come down to meet my lord the king.
Avishai the son of Tzeruya answered, Shall not Shim'i be put to death for this, because he cursed YHWH's anointed?

But Dawid said, What have I to do with you, you sons of Tzeruya, that you should this day be as an adversary to me? Shall anyone be put to death in Yisra'EL this day? For do I not know that I am this day king over Yisra'EL?
And the king said to Shim'i, You shall not die. And the king gave him his oath.

And Mefiboshet the son of Sha'ul came down to meet the king. He had neither taken care of his feet nor trimmed his beard nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came back in safety.
And when he came to Yerushalayim to meet the king, the king said to him, Why did you not go with me, Mefiboshet?
He answered, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me, for your servant said, I will saddle a donkey for myself, that I may ride on it and go with the king. For your servant is lame.
He has slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like the angel of Creator — do therefore what is good in your eyes.
For all my father's house were but men doomed to death before my lord the king, but you set your servant among those who eat at your table. What further right have I, then, to cry to the king?
And the king said to him, Why speak any more of your affairs? I have decided: you and Tziva shall divide the land.
And Mefiboshet said to the king, Oh, let him take it all, since my lord the king has come safely home.
Now Barzillai the Gil'adite had come down from Rogelim, and he went on with the king to the Yarden, to escort him over the Yarden.
Barzillai was a very aged man, eighty years old. He had provided the king with food while he stayed at Makhanayim, for he was a very wealthy man.
And the king said to Barzillai, Come over with me, and I will provide for you with me in Yerushalayim.
But Barzillai said to the king, How many years have I still to live, that I should go up with the king to Yerushalayim?
