Then he went up and lay on the child, putting his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. And as he stretched himself upon him, the flesh of the child became warm.
Then he got up again and walked once back and forth in the house, and went up and stretched himself upon him. The child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
Then he summoned Gekhazi and said, Call this Shunammite. So he called her. And when she came to him, he said, Pick up your son.
She came and fell at his feet, bowing to the ground. Then she picked up her son and went out.

And Elisha came again to Gilgal when there was a famine in the land. And as the sons of the prophets were sitting before him, he said to his servant, Set on the large pot, and boil stew for the sons of the prophets.
One of them went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine and gathered from it his lap full of wild gourds, and came and cut them up into the pot of stew, not knowing what they were.
And they poured it out for the men to eat. But while they were eating of the stew, they cried out, O man of Creator, there is death in the pot. And they could not eat it.
He said, Then bring flour. And he threw it into the pot and said, Pour some out for the men, that they may eat. And there was nothing harmful in the pot.
A man came from Ba'al-Shalishah, bringing the man of Creator bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. And Elisha said, Give to the men that they may eat.
But his servant said, How can I set this before a hundred men? So he repeated, Give them to the men, that they may eat, for thus says YHWH, They shall eat and have some left.
So he set it before them. And they ate and had some left, according to the word of YHWH.
Na'aman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man with his master and in high favor, because by him YHWH had given victory to Aram. He was a mighty man of valor, but he was a leper.
Now the Arameans on one of their raids had carried off a little girl from the land of Yisra'EL, and she worked in the service of Na'aman's wife.
She said to her mistress, Would that my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria — he would cure him of his leprosy.
So Na'aman went in and told his lord, Thus and so spoke the girl from the land of Yisra'EL.
And the king of Aram said, Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Yisra'EL. So he went, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten changes of clothing.
And he brought the letter to the king of Yisra'EL, which read, When this letter reaches you, know that I have sent to you Na'aman my servant, that you may cure him of his leprosy.

And when the king of Yisra'EL read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, Am I Creator, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends word to me to cure a man of his leprosy? Only consider, and see how he is seeking a quarrel with me.

But when Elisha the man of Creator heard that the king of Yisra'EL had torn his clothes, he sent to the king, saying, Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come now to me, that he may know there is a prophet in Yisra'EL.
So Na'aman came with his horses and chariots and stood at the door of Elisha's house.
And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, Go and wash in the Yarden seven times, and your flesh shall be restored, and you shall be clean.

But Na'aman was angry and went away, saying, Behold, I thought that he would surely come out to me and stand and call upon the name of YHWH his Creator, and wave his hand over the place and cure the leper.
Are not Avana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Yisra'EL? Could I not wash in them and be clean? So he turned and went away in a rage.
But his servants came near and said to him, My father, it is a great word the prophet has spoken to you — will you not do it? Has he actually said to you, Wash, and be clean?
So he went down and dipped himself seven times in the Yarden, according to the word of the man of Creator, and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

Then he returned to the man of Creator, he and all his company, and he came and stood before him. And he said, Behold, I know that there is no Creator in all the earth but in Yisra'EL. So accept now a present from your servant.
But he said, As YHWH lives, before whom I stand, I will receive none. And he urged him to take it, but he refused.
Then Na'aman said, If not, please let there be given to your servant two mule loads of earth, for from now on your servant will not offer burnt offering or sacrifice to any god but YHWH.

In this matter may YHWH pardon your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship there, leaning on my arm, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon, when I bow myself in the house of Rimmon, YHWH pardon your servant in this matter.
He said to him, Go in peace. So he departed from him a little way.

But Gekhazi, the servant of Elisha the man of Creator, said, See, my master has spared this Na'aman the Aramean, in not accepting from his hand what he brought. As YHWH lives, I will run after him and get something from him.
So Gekhazi followed Na'aman. And when Na'aman saw someone running after him, he got down from the chariot to meet him and said, Is all well?

And he said, All is well. My master has sent me to say, There have just come to me from the hill country of Efrayim two young men of the sons of the prophets. Please give them a talent of silver and two festal garments.

And Na'aman said, Be pleased to accept two talents. And he urged him and tied up two talents of silver in two bags, with two festal garments, and laid them on two of his servants. And they carried them before Gekhazi.
And when he came to the hill, he took them from their hand and put them in the house, and he sent the men away, and they departed.
He went in and stood before his master, and Elisha said to him, Where have you been, Gekhazi? And he said, Your servant went nowhere.

But he said to him, Did not my heart go when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Was it a time to accept money and garments, olive orchards and vineyards, sheep and oxen, male servants and female servants?
Therefore the leprosy of Na'aman shall cling to you and to your descendants forever. So he went out from his presence a leper, like snow.
Now the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, See, the place where we dwell under your charge is too small for us.
Let us go to the Yarden and each of us get there a log, and let us make a place for us to dwell there. And he answered, Go.
Then one of them said, Be pleased to go with your servants. And he answered, I will go.
So he went with them. And when they came to the Yarden, they cut down trees.
But as one was felling a log, his axe head fell into the water, and he cried out, Alas, my master — it was borrowed.
Then the man of Creator said, Where did it fall? When he showed him the place, he cut off a stick and threw it in there and made the iron float.
And he said, Take it up. So he reached out his hand and took it.
Once when the king of Aram was warring against Yisra'EL, he took counsel with his servants, saying, At such and such a place shall be my camp.
But the man of Creator sent word to the king of Yisra'EL, Beware that you do not pass this place, for the Arameans are going down there.
And the king of Yisra'EL sent to the place about which the man of Creator told him. Thus he used to warn him, so that he saved himself there more than once or twice.
And the mind of the king of Aram was greatly troubled because of this thing, and he called his servants and said to them, Will you not show me who of us is for the king of Yisra'EL?
And one of his servants said, None, my lord, O king — but Elisha, the prophet who is in Yisra'EL, tells the king of Yisra'EL the words that you speak in your bedroom.
And he said, Go and see where he is, that I may send and seize him. It was told him, Behold, he is in Dotan.
So he sent there horses and chariots and a great army, and they came by night and surrounded the city.

When the servant of the man of Creator rose early in the morning and went out, behold, an army with horses and chariots was all around the city. And the servant said, Alas, my master — what shall we do?
He said, Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.

Then Elisha prayed and said, O YHWH, please open his eyes that he may see. So YHWH opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw, and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
And when the Arameans came down against him, Elisha prayed to YHWH and said, Please strike this people with blindness. So he struck them with blindness in accordance with the prayer of Elisha.
And Elisha said to them, This is not the way, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will bring you to the man whom you seek. And he led them to Samaria.
As soon as they entered Samaria, Elisha said, O YHWH, open the eyes of these men, that they may see. So YHWH opened their eyes, and they saw, and behold, they were in the midst of Samaria.
As soon as the king of Yisra'EL saw them, he said to Elisha, My father, shall I strike them down? Shall I strike them down?

He answered, You shall not strike them down. Would you strike down those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow? Set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink and go to their master.
So he prepared for them a great feast, and when they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they went to their master. And the Arameans did not come again on raids into the land of Yisra'EL.
Afterward Ben-Hadad king of Aram mustered his entire army and went up and besieged Samaria.
And there was a great famine in Samaria, as they besieged it, until a donkey's head was sold for eighty shekels of silver, and the fourth part of a kab of dove's dung for five shekels of silver.
Now as the king of Yisra'EL was passing by on the wall, a woman cried out to him, Help, my lord, O king.
And he said, If YHWH will not help you, how shall I help you? From the threshing floor, or from the winepress?
And the king asked her, What is your trouble? She answered, This woman said to me, Give your son, that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.
So we boiled my son and ate him. And on the next day I said to her, Give your son, that we may eat him. But she has hidden her son.
When the king heard the words of the woman, he tore his clothes — now he was passing by on the wall — and the people looked, and behold, he had sackcloth beneath on his body.
And he said, May Creator do so to me and more also, if the head of Elisha the son of Shafat remains on his shoulders today.

Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. Now the king had dispatched a man from his presence, but before the messenger arrived Elisha said to the elders, Do you see how this murderer has sent to take off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold the door fast against him. Is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?
And while he was still speaking with them, the messenger came down to him and said, This trouble is from YHWH — why should I wait for YHWH any longer?
But Elisha said, Hear the word of YHWH: thus says YHWH, Tomorrow about this time a seah of fine flour shall be sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria.

Then the captain on whose hand the king leaned said to the man of Creator, If YHWH himself should make windows in heaven, could this thing be? But he said, You shall see it with your own eyes, but you shall not eat of it.
Now there were four men who were lepers at the entrance to the gate. And they said to one another, Why are we sitting here until we die?

If we say, Let us enter the city, the famine is in the city, and we shall die there. And if we sit here, we also die. So now come, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they spare our lives we shall live, and if they kill us we shall but die.
So they arose at twilight to go to the camp of the Arameans. But when they came to the edge of the Aramean camp, behold, there was no one there.

For YHWH had made the army of the Arameans hear the sound of chariots and of horses, the sound of a great army, so that they said to one another, Behold, the king of Yisra'EL has hired against us the kings of the Khittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us.
So they fled away in the twilight and abandoned their tents, their horses, and their donkeys, leaving the camp as it was, and fled for their lives.

And when these lepers came to the edge of the camp, they went into a tent and ate and drank and carried off silver and gold and clothing and went and hid them. Then they came back and entered another tent and carried off things from it and went and hid them.

Then they said to one another, We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news. If we are silent and wait until the morning light, punishment will overtake us. Now therefore come — let us go and tell the king's household.

So they came and called to the gatekeepers of the city and told them, We went to the camp of the Arameans, and behold, there was no one to be seen or heard there — nothing but the horses tied and the donkeys tied, and the tents as they were.
Then the gatekeepers called out, and it was told within the king's household.

And the king rose in the night and said to his servants, I will tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are hungry. Therefore they have gone out of the camp to hide themselves in the open country, thinking, When they come out of the city, we shall take them alive and get into the city.

And one of his servants said, Let some men take five of the remaining horses, seeing that those who are left here will fare like the whole multitude of Yisra'EL who have already perished. Let us send and see.
So they took two horsemen, and the king sent them after the army of the Arameans, saying, Go and see.

So they went after them as far as the Yarden, and behold, all the way was littered with garments and equipment that the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. And the messengers returned and told the king.
Then the people went out and plundered the camp of the Arameans. So a seah of fine flour was sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, according to the word of YHWH.

Now the king had appointed the captain on whose hand he leaned to have charge of the gate. And the people trampled him in the gate, so that he died, as the man of Creator had said when the king came down to him.
For when the man of Creator had said to the king, Two seahs of barley shall be sold for a shekel and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, about this time tomorrow in the gate of Samaria,
The captain had answered the man of Creator, If YHWH himself should make windows in heaven, could such a thing be? And he had said, You shall see it with your own eyes, but you shall not eat of it.
And so it happened to him, for the people trampled him in the gate and he died.

Now Elisha had said to the woman whose son he had restored to life, Arise, and depart with your household, and sojourn wherever you can, for YHWH has called for a famine, and it will come upon the land for seven years.
So the woman arose and did according to the word of the man of Creator. She went with her household and sojourned in the land of the Pelishtim seven years.
And at the end of the seven years, when the woman returned from the land of the Pelishtim, she went to appeal to the king for her house and her land.
Now the king was talking with Gekhazi the servant of the man of Creator, saying, Tell me all the great things that Elisha has done.

And while he was telling the king how Elisha had restored the dead to life, behold, the woman whose son he had restored to life appealed to the king for her house and her land. And Gekhazi said, My lord, O king, here is the woman, and here is her son whom Elisha restored to life.

And when the king asked the woman, she told him. So the king appointed an official for her, saying, Restore all that was hers, together with all the produce of the fields from the day that she left the land until now.
Now Elisha came to Damascus. Ben-Hadad the king of Aram was sick. And when it was told him, The man of Creator has come here,
The king said to Khaza'el, Take a present with you and go to meet the man of Creator, and inquire of YHWH through him, saying, Shall I recover from this sickness?

So Khaza'el went to meet him, and took a present with him, all kinds of goods of Damascus, forty camel loads. When he came and stood before him, he said, Your son Ben-Hadad king of Aram has sent me to you, saying, Shall I recover from this sickness?
And Elisha said to him, Go, say to him, You shall certainly recover, but YHWH has shown me that he shall certainly die.
And he fixed his gaze and stared at him, until he was embarrassed. And the man of Creator wept.

And Khaza'el said, Why does my lord weep? He answered, Because I know the evil that you will do to the people of Yisra'EL. You will set on fire their fortresses, and you will kill their young men with the sword and dash in pieces their little ones and rip open their pregnant women.
And Khaza'el said, What is your servant, who is but a dog, that he should do this great thing? Elisha answered, YHWH has shown me that you are to be king over Aram.
Then he departed from Elisha and came to his master, who said to him, What did Elisha say to you? And he answered, He told me that you would certainly recover.
But the next day he took the bed cloth and dipped it in water and spread it over his face, till he died. And Khaza'el became king in his place.
In the fifth year of Yehoram the son of Akhav, king of Yisra'EL, when Yehoshafat was king of Yehudah, Yehoram the son of Yehoshafat king of Yehudah began to reign.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Yerushalayim.
And he walked in the way of the kings of Yisra'EL, as the house of Akhav had done, for the daughter of Akhav was his wife. And he did what was evil in the sight of YHWH.
Yet YHWH was not willing to destroy Yehudah, for the sake of Dawid his servant, since he promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons forever.
In his days Edom revolted from the rule of Yehudah and set up a king of their own.
Then Yehoram passed over to Tza'ir with all his chariots and rose by night, and he and his chariot commanders struck the Edomites who had surrounded him, but his army fled home.
So Edom revolted from the rule of Yehudah to this day. Then Livnah revolted at the same time.
Now the rest of the acts of Yehoram, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yehudah?
And Yehoram slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of Dawid. And Akhazyahu his son reigned in his place.
In the twelfth year of Yehoram the son of Akhav, king of Yisra'EL, Akhazyahu the son of Yehoram, king of Yehudah, began to reign.
Akhazyahu was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Athalyahu, the granddaughter of Omri king of Yisra'EL.
He also walked in the way of the house of Akhav and did what was evil in the sight of YHWH, as the house of Akhav had done, for he was son-in-law to the house of Akhav.
He went with Yehoram the son of Akhav to make war against Khaza'el king of Aram at Ramot-Gil'ad. And the Arameans wounded Yehoram.

And King Yehoram returned to be healed in Yizre'el of the wounds that the Arameans had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Khaza'el king of Aram. And Akhazyahu the son of Yehoram king of Yehudah went down to see Yehoram the son of Akhav in Yizre'el, because he was sick.
Then Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, Tie up your garment, and take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramot-Gil'ad.
And when you arrive, look there for Yehu the son of Yehoshafat, son of Nimshi. And go in and have him rise from among his brothers, and lead him to an inner chamber.
Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head and say, Thus says YHWH, I anoint you king over Yisra'EL. Then open the door and flee — do not linger.
So the young man, the servant of the prophet, went to Ramot-Gil'ad.
And when he arrived, behold, the commanders of the army were in council. And he said, I have a word for you, O commander. And Yehu said, To which of us all? And he said, To you, O commander.
So he arose and went into the house. And the young man poured the oil on his head, saying to him, Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, I anoint you king over the people of YHWH, over Yisra'EL.
And you shall strike down the house of Akhav your master, so that I may avenge on Izevel the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of YHWH.
For the whole house of Akhav shall perish, and I will cut off from Akhav every male, bond or free, in Yisra'EL.
And I will make the house of Akhav like the house of Yarovam the son of Nevat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Akhiyah.
And the dogs shall eat Izevel in the territory of Yizre'el, and none shall bury her. Then he opened the door and fled.
When Yehu came out to the servants of his master, they said to him, Is all well? Why did this mad fellow come to you? And he said to them, You know the fellow and his talk.
And they said, That is not true — tell us. And he said, Thus and so he spoke to me, saying, Thus says YHWH, I anoint you king over Yisra'EL.
Then in haste every man of them took his garment and put it under him on the bare steps, and they blew the trumpet and proclaimed, Yehu is king.
Thus Yehu the son of Yehoshafat the son of Nimshi conspired against Yehoram. Now Yehoram with all Yisra'EL had been on guard at Ramot-Gil'ad against Khaza'el king of Aram.

But King Yehoram had returned to be healed in Yizre'el of the wounds that the Arameans had given him, when he fought with Khaza'el king of Aram. So Yehu said, If this is your decision, let no one slip out of the city to go and tell the news in Yizre'el.
Then Yehu mounted his chariot and went to Yizre'el, for Yehoram lay there. And Akhazyahu king of Yehudah had come down to visit Yehoram.

Now the watchman was standing on the tower in Yizre'el, and he saw the company of Yehu as he came, and said, I see a company. And Yehoram said, Take a horseman and send to meet them, and let him ask, Is it peace?

So a man on horseback went to meet him and said, Thus says the king, Is it peace? And Yehu said, What do you have to do with peace? Turn around and ride behind me. And the watchman reported, The messenger reached them, but he is not coming back.
Then he sent out a second horseman, who came to them and said, Thus the king says, Is it peace? And Yehu answered, What do you have to do with peace? Turn around and ride behind me.
Again the watchman reported, He reached them, but he is not coming back. And the driving is like the driving of Yehu the son of Nimshi, for he drives furiously.

Yehoram said, Make ready. And his chariot was made ready. Then Yehoram king of Yisra'EL and Akhazyahu king of Yehudah set out, each in his chariot, and went to meet Yehu, and met him at the property of Navot the Yizreelite.
And when Yehoram saw Yehu, he said, Is it peace, Yehu? He answered, What peace can there be, so long as the whorings and the sorceries of your mother Izevel are so many?
Then Yehoram reined about and fled, saying to Akhazyahu, Treachery, O Akhazyahu.
And Yehu drew his bow with his full strength, and shot Yehoram between the shoulders, so that the arrow pierced his heart, and he sank in his chariot.

Yehu said to Bidkar his aide, Take him up and throw him on the plot of ground belonging to Navot the Yizreelite. For remember, when you and I rode side by side behind Akhav his father, how YHWH uttered this oracle against him:

As surely as I saw yesterday the blood of Navot and the blood of his sons — declares YHWH — I will repay you on this plot of ground. Now therefore take him up and throw him on the plot of ground, in accordance with the word of YHWH.

When Akhazyahu the king of Yehudah saw this, he fled in the direction of Beit-Haggan. And Yehu pursued him and said, Shoot him also. And they shot him in the chariot at the ascent of Gur, which is by Yivle'am. And he fled to Megiddo and died there.
His servants carried him in a chariot to Yerushalayim, and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in the city of Dawid.
In the eleventh year of Yehoram the son of Akhav, Akhazyahu had become king over Yehudah.
When Yehu came to Yizre'el, Izevel heard of it. And she painted her eyes and adorned her head and looked out of the window.
And as Yehu entered the gate, she said, Is it peace, you Zimri, murderer of your master?
And he lifted up his face to the window and said, Who is on my side? Who? Two or three eunuchs looked out at him.
He said, Throw her down. So they threw her down. And some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled over her.
Then he went in and ate and drank. And he said, See now to this cursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter.
But when they went to bury her, they found no more of her than the skull and the feet and the palms of her hands.
When they came back and told him, he said, This is the word of YHWH, which he spoke by his servant Eliyahu the Tishbite: In the territory of Yizre'el the dogs shall eat the flesh of Izevel,
And the corpse of Izevel shall be as dung on the face of the field in the territory of Yizre'el, so that no one can say, This is Izevel.
Now Akhav had seventy sons in Samaria. So Yehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the rulers of the city, to the elders, and to the guardians of the sons of Akhav, saying,
Now then, as soon as this letter comes to you, seeing your master's sons are with you, and there are with you chariots and horses, fortified cities also, and weapons,
Select the best and most upright of your master's sons and set him on his father's throne and fight for your master's house.
But they were exceedingly afraid and said, Behold, the two kings could not stand before him. How then can we stand?

So he who was over the palace, and he who was over the city, together with the elders and the guardians, sent to Yehu, saying, We are your servants, and we will do all that you tell us. We will not make anyone king — do whatever is good in your eyes.

Then he wrote to them a second letter, saying, If you are on my side, and if you are ready to obey me, take the heads of your master's sons and come to me at Yizre'el tomorrow at this time. Now the king's sons, seventy persons, were with the great men of the city, who were bringing them up.
And as soon as the letter came to them, they took the king's sons and slaughtered them, seventy persons, and put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Yizre'el.
When the messenger came and told him, Behold, they have brought the heads of the king's sons, he said, Lay them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until the morning.
Then in the morning, when he went out, he stood and said to all the people, You are innocent. It was I who conspired against my master and killed him, but who struck down all these?
Know then that there shall fall to the earth nothing of the word of YHWH, which YHWH spoke concerning the house of Akhav, for YHWH has done what he said by his servant Eliyahu.
So Yehu struck down all who remained of the house of Akhav in Yizre'el, all his great men and his close friends and his priests, until he left him none remaining.
Then he set out and went to Samaria. On the way, when he was at Beit-Eked of the Shepherds,

Yehu met the relatives of Akhazyahu king of Yehudah, and he said, Who are you? And they answered, We are the relatives of Akhazyahu, and we came down to visit the royal princes and the sons of the queen mother.
He said, Take them alive. And they took them alive and slaughtered them at the pit of Beit-Eked, forty-two persons, and he left none of them.

And when he departed from there, he met Yehonadav the son of Rekhav coming to meet him. And he greeted him and said to him, Is your heart true to my heart as mine is to yours? And Yehonadav answered, It is. Yehu said, If it is, give me your hand. So he gave him his hand. And Yehu took him up with him into the chariot.
And he said, Come with me, and see my zeal for YHWH. So he had him ride in his chariot.
And when he came to Samaria, he struck down all who remained to Akhav in Samaria, till he had wiped them out, according to the word of YHWH that he spoke to Eliyahu.
Then Yehu assembled all the people and said to them, Akhav served Ba'al a little, but Yehu will serve him much.

Now therefore call to me all the prophets of Ba'al, all his worshipers and all his priests. Let none be missing, for I have a great sacrifice to offer to Ba'al. Whoever is missing shall not live. But Yehu did it with cunning in order to destroy the worshipers of Ba'al.
And Yehu ordered, Sanctify a solemn assembly for Ba'al. So they proclaimed it.

And Yehu sent throughout all Yisra'EL, and all the worshipers of Ba'al came, so that there was not a man left who did not come. And they entered the house of Ba'al, and the house of Ba'al was filled from one end to the other.
He said to him who was in charge of the wardrobe, Bring out the vestments for all the worshipers of Ba'al. So he brought out the vestments for them.

Then Yehu went into the house of Ba'al with Yehonadav the son of Rekhav, and he said to the worshipers of Ba'al, Search, and see that there is no servant of YHWH here among you, but only the worshipers of Ba'al.

Then they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Yehu had stationed eighty men outside and said, The man who allows any of the men whom I give into your hands to escape shall forfeit his life.

As soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, Yehu commanded the guard and the officers, Go in and strike them down — let not a man escape. So when they put them to the sword, the guard and the officers cast them out. And they went into the inner room of the house of Ba'al
And they brought out the pillar that was in the house of Ba'al and burned it.
And they demolished the pillar of Ba'al, and demolished the house of Ba'al, and made it a latrine to this day.
Thus Yehu wiped out Ba'al from Yisra'EL.
But Yehu did not turn aside from the sins of Yarovam the son of Nevat, which he made Yisra'EL to sin — that is, the golden calves that were in Beit-El and in Dan.

And YHWH said to Yehu, Because you have done well in carrying out what is right in my eyes, and have done to the house of Akhav according to all that was in my heart, your sons of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Yisra'EL.
But Yehu was not careful to walk in the Torah of YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, with all his heart. He did not turn from the sins of Yarovam, which he made Yisra'EL to sin.
In those days YHWH began to cut off parts of Yisra'EL. Khaza'el defeated them throughout the territory of Yisra'EL:
From the Yarden eastward, all the land of Gil'ad, the Gadites, and the Reuvenites, and the Menashehites, from Aro'er, which is by the Valley of the Arnon, that is, Gil'ad and Bashan.
Now the rest of the acts of Yehu and all that he did, and all his might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yisra'EL?
So Yehu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria. And Yeho'ahaz his son reigned in his place.
The time that Yehu reigned over Yisra'EL in Samaria was twenty-eight years.
Now when Atalyahu the mother of Akhazyahu saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal family.

But Yehosheva, the daughter of King Yehoram, sister of Akhazyahu, took Yo'ash the son of Akhazyahu and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death, and she put him and his nurse in a bedroom. Thus they hid him from Atalyahu, so that he was not put to death.
And he remained with her six years, hidden in the house of YHWH, while Atalyahu reigned over the land.

But in the seventh year Yehoyada sent and brought the captains of the Carites and of the guards, and had them come to him in the house of YHWH. And he made a covenant with them and put them under oath in the house of YHWH, and he showed them the king's son.
And he commanded them, This is the thing that you shall do: one third of you, those who come off duty on the Sabbath and guard the king's house
— Another third being at the gate Sur and a third at the gate behind the guards — shall guard the palace.
And the two divisions of you, which come on duty in force on the Sabbath and guard the house of YHWH,
Shall surround the king, each with his weapons in his hand. And whoever approaches the ranks is to be put to death. Be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in.

The captains did according to all that Yehoyada the priest commanded, and they each brought his men who were to come on duty on the Sabbath, with those who were to go off duty on the Sabbath, and came to Yehoyada the priest.
And the priest gave to the captains the spears and shields that had been King Dawid's, which were in the house of YHWH.
And the guards stood, every man with his weapons in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, around the altar and the house, to guard the king on every side.
Then he brought out the king's son and put the crown on him and gave him the testimony. And they proclaimed him king and anointed him, and they clapped their hands and said, Long live the king.
When Atalyahu heard the noise of the guard and of the people, she went into the house of YHWH to the people.

And when she looked, there was the king standing by the pillar, according to the custom, with the captains and the trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets. And Atalyahu tore her clothes and cried, Treason, treason.

Then Yehoyada the priest commanded the captains who were set over the army, Bring her out between the ranks, and put to the sword anyone who follows her. For the priest said, Let her not be put to death in the house of YHWH.
So they laid hands on her and she went through the horses' entrance to the king's house, and there she was put to death.
And Yehoyada made a covenant between YHWH and the king and people, that they should be YHWH's people, and also between the king and the people.

Then all the people of the land went to the house of Ba'al and tore it down. His altars and his images they broke in pieces, and they killed Mattan the priest of Ba'al before the altars. And the priest posted watchmen over the house of YHWH.

And he took the captains, the Carites, the guards, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of YHWH, marching through the gate of the guards to the king's house. And he took his seat on the throne of the kings.
So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet after Atalyahu had been put to death with the sword at the king's house.
Yo'ash was seven years old when he began to reign.
In the seventh year of Yehu, Yo'ash began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Tzivyah of Be'er-Sheva.
And Yo'ash did what was right in the eyes of YHWH all his days, because Yehoyada the priest instructed him.
Nevertheless, the high places were not taken away — the people continued to sacrifice and make offerings on the high places.

Yo'ash said to the priests, All the money of the holy things that is brought into the house of YHWH, the money for which each man is assessed — the money from the assessment of persons — and the money that a man's heart prompts him to bring into the house of YHWH,
Let the priests take, each from his donor, and let them repair the house wherever any need of repairs is discovered.
But by the twenty-third year of King Yo'ash, the priests had made no repairs on the house.

Therefore King Yo'ash summoned Yehoyada the priest and the other priests and said to them, Why are you not repairing the house? Now therefore take no more money from your donors, but hand it over for the repair of the house.
So the priests agreed that they would neither accept money from the people nor repair the house.

Then Yehoyada the priest took a chest and bored a hole in the lid of it and set it beside the altar on the right side as one entered the house of YHWH. And the priests who guarded the threshold put in it all the money that was brought into the house of YHWH.
And whenever they saw that there was much money in the chest, the king's secretary and the high priest came up and they bagged and counted the money that was found in the house of YHWH.

Then they would give the money that was weighed out to the hands of the workmen who had the oversight of the house of YHWH. And they paid it out to the carpenters and the builders who worked on the house of YHWH,
And to the masons and the stonecutters, as well as to buy timber and quarried stone for making repairs on the house of YHWH, and for any outlay for the repairs of the house.
But there were not made for the house of YHWH basins of silver, snuffers, bowls, trumpets, or any vessels of gold, or of silver, from the money that was brought into the house of YHWH,
For that was given to the workmen who were repairing the house of YHWH with it.
And they did not ask an accounting from the men into whose hand they gave the money to pay out to the workmen, for they dealt honestly.
The money from the guilt offerings and the money from the sin offerings was not brought into the house of YHWH — it belonged to the priests.
At that time Khaza'el king of Aram went up and fought against Gat and took it. But when Khaza'el set his face to go up against Yerushalayim,

Yo'ash king of Yehudah took all the sacred gifts that Yehoshafat and Yehoram and Akhazyahu his fathers, the kings of Yehudah, had dedicated, and his own sacred gifts, and all the gold that was found in the treasuries of the house of YHWH and of the king's house, and sent these to Khaza'el king of Aram. Then Khaza'el went away from Yerushalayim.
Now the rest of the acts of Yo'ash and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yehudah?
His servants arose and made a conspiracy and struck down Yo'ash in the house of Millo, on the way that goes down to Silla.

It was Yozakar the son of Shim'at and Yehozavad the son of Shomer, his servants, who struck him down, so that he died. And they buried him with his fathers in the city of Dawid, and Amazyahu his son reigned in his place.
In the twenty-third year of Yo'ash the son of Akhazyahu, king of Yehudah, Yeho'ahaz the son of Yehu began to reign over Yisra'EL in Samaria, and he reigned seventeen years.
He did what was evil in the sight of YHWH and followed the sins of Yarovam the son of Nevat, which he made Yisra'EL to sin — he did not depart from them.
And the anger of YHWH was kindled against Yisra'EL, and he gave them continually into the hand of Khaza'el king of Aram and into the hand of Ben-Hadad the son of Khaza'el.
Then Yeho'ahaz sought the favor of YHWH, and YHWH listened to him, for he saw the oppression of Yisra'EL, how the king of Aram oppressed them.
Therefore YHWH gave Yisra'EL a savior, so that they escaped from the hand of the Arameans, and the people of Yisra'EL lived in their homes as formerly.
Nevertheless, they did not depart from the sins of the house of Yarovam, which he made Yisra'EL to sin, but walked in them — and the Asherah also remained in Samaria.

For there was not left to Yeho'ahaz an army of more than fifty horsemen and ten chariots and ten thousand foot soldiers, for the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like the dust at threshing.
Now the rest of the acts of Yeho'ahaz and all that he did, and his might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yisra'EL?
So Yeho'ahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria, and Yo'ash his son reigned in his place.
In the thirty-seventh year of Yo'ash king of Yehudah, Yo'ash the son of Yeho'ahaz began to reign over Yisra'EL in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.
He also did what was evil in the sight of YHWH. He did not depart from all the sins of Yarovam the son of Nevat, which he made Yisra'EL to sin, but he walked in them.

Now the rest of the acts of Yo'ash and all that he did, and the might with which he fought against Amazyahu king of Yehudah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yisra'EL?
So Yo'ash slept with his fathers, and Yarovam sat on his throne. And Yo'ash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Yisra'EL.

Now when Elisha had fallen sick with the illness of which he was to die, Yo'ash king of Yisra'EL went down to him and wept before him, crying, My father, my father. The chariots of Yisra'EL and its horsemen.
And Elisha said to him, Take a bow and arrows. So he took a bow and arrows.
Then he said to the king of Yisra'EL, Draw the bow. And he drew it. And Elisha laid his hands on the king's hands.

And he said, Open the window eastward. And he opened it. Then Elisha said, Shoot. And he shot. And he said, YHWH's arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram, for you shall fight the Arameans in Afek until you have made an end of them.
And he said, Take the arrows. And he took them. And he said to the king of Yisra'EL, Strike the ground with them. And he struck three times and stopped.

Then the man of Creator was angry with him and said, You should have struck five or six times — then you would have struck down Aram until you had made an end of it, but now you will strike down Aram only three times.
So Elisha died, and they buried him. Now bands of Moavites used to invade the land in the spring of the year.
And as a man was being buried, behold, a marauding band was seen and the man was thrown into the grave of Elisha, and as soon as the man touched the bones of Elisha, he revived and stood on his feet.
Now Khaza'el king of Aram oppressed Yisra'EL all the days of Yeho'ahaz.

But YHWH was gracious to them and had compassion on them, and he turned toward them, because of his covenant with Avraham, Yitzhak, and Yaakov, and would not destroy them, nor has he cast them from his presence until now.
When Khaza'el king of Aram died, Ben-Hadad his son became king in his place.

Then Yo'ash the son of Yeho'ahaz took again from Ben-Hadad the son of Khaza'el the cities that he had taken from Yeho'ahaz his father in war. Three times Yo'ash defeated him and recovered the cities of Yisra'EL.
In the second year of Yo'ash the son of Yeho'ahaz, king of Yisra'EL, Amazyahu the son of Yo'ash, king of Yehudah, began to reign.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Yehoaddan of Yerushalayim.
And he did what was right in the eyes of YHWH, yet not like Dawid his father. He did in all things as Yo'ash his father had done.
But the high places were not removed — the people still sacrificed and made offerings on the high places.
And as soon as the royal power was firmly in his hand, he struck down his servants who had struck down the king his father.

But he did not put to death the children of the murderers, according to what is written in the Book of the Torah of Moshe, where YHWH commanded, Fathers shall not be put to death because of their children, nor shall children be put to death because of their fathers. But every person shall be put to death for his own sin.
He struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and took Sela by storm, and called it Yokte'el, which is its name to this day.
Then Amazyahu sent messengers to Yo'ash the son of Yeho'ahaz, son of Yehu, king of Yisra'EL, saying, Come, let us look one another in the face.

And Yo'ash the king of Yisra'EL sent word to Amazyahu king of Yehudah, A thistle on Lebanon sent to a cedar on Lebanon, saying, Give your daughter to my son for a wife. And a wild beast of Lebanon passed by and trampled down the thistle.
You have indeed struck down Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Be content with your glory, and stay at home, for why should you provoke trouble so that you fall, you and Yehudah with you?
But Amazyahu would not listen. So Yo'ash king of Yisra'EL went up, and he and Amazyahu king of Yehudah faced one another in battle at Beit-Shemesh, which belongs to Yehudah.
And Yehudah was defeated by Yisra'EL, and every man fled to his home.

And Yo'ash king of Yisra'EL captured Amazyahu king of Yehudah, the son of Yo'ash, son of Akhazyahu, at Beit-Shemesh, and came to Yerushalayim and broke down the wall of Yerushalayim for four hundred cubits, from the Gate of Efrayim to the Corner Gate.
And he seized all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of YHWH and in the treasuries of the king's house, also hostages, and he returned to Samaria.
Now the rest of the acts of Yo'ash that he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amazyahu king of Yehudah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yisra'EL?
And Yo'ash slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Yisra'EL, and Yarovam his son reigned in his place.
And Amazyahu the son of Yo'ash, king of Yehudah, lived fifteen years after the death of Yo'ash the son of Yeho'ahaz, king of Yisra'EL.
Now the rest of the deeds of Amazyahu, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yehudah?
And they made a conspiracy against him in Yerushalayim, and he fled to Lakhish. But they sent after him to Lakhish and put him to death there.
And they brought him on horses, and he was buried in Yerushalayim with his fathers in the city of Dawid.
And all the people of Yehudah took Azaryahu, who was sixteen years old, and made him king instead of his father Amazyahu.
He built Elat and restored it to Yehudah, after the king slept with his fathers.
In the fifteenth year of Amazyahu the son of Yo'ash, king of Yehudah, Yarovam the son of Yo'ash, king of Yisra'EL, began to reign in Samaria, and he reigned forty-one years.
And he did what was evil in the sight of YHWH. He did not depart from all the sins of Yarovam the son of Nevat, which he made Yisra'EL to sin.

He restored the border of Yisra'EL from Lebo-Khamath as far as the Sea of the Aravah, according to the word of YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, which he spoke by his servant Yonah the son of Amittai, the prophet, who was from Gat-Khefer.
For YHWH saw that the affliction of Yisra'EL was very bitter, for there was none left, bond or free, and there was none to help Yisra'EL.
But YHWH had not said that he would blot out the name of Yisra'EL from under heaven, so he saved them by the hand of Yarovam the son of Yo'ash.

Now the rest of the acts of Yarovam and all that he did, and his might, how he fought, and how he restored Damascus and Khamath to Yehudah in Yisra'EL, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yisra'EL?
And Yarovam slept with his fathers, the kings of Yisra'EL, and Zekhariah his son reigned in his place.
In the twenty-seventh year of Yarovam king of Yisra'EL, Azaryahu the son of Amazyahu, king of Yehudah, began to reign.
He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Yekholyahu of Yerushalayim.
And he did what was right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that his father Amazyahu had done.
Nevertheless, the high places were not taken away — the people still sacrificed and made offerings on the high places.
And YHWH touched the king, so that he was a leper to the day of his death, and he lived in a separate house. And Yotam the king's son was over the household, governing the people of the land.
Now the rest of the acts of Azaryahu, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yehudah?
And Azaryahu slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the city of Dawid, and Yotam his son reigned in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Azaryahu king of Yehudah, Zekhariah the son of Yarovam reigned over Yisra'EL in Samaria six months.
And he did what was evil in the sight of YHWH, as his fathers had done. He did not depart from the sins of Yarovam the son of Nevat, which he made Yisra'EL to sin.
Shallum the son of Yavesh conspired against him and struck him down before the people and killed him and reigned in his place.
Now the rest of the deeds of Zekhariah, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yisra'EL.
This was the promise of YHWH that he gave to Yehu, Your sons of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Yisra'EL. And so it came to pass.
Shallum the son of Yavesh began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziyahu king of Yehudah, and he reigned one month in Samaria.
Then Menakhem the son of Gadi came up from Tirtzah and came to Samaria, and he struck down Shallum the son of Yavesh in Samaria and killed him and reigned in his place.
Now the rest of the deeds of Shallum, and the conspiracy that he made, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yisra'EL.

At that time Menakhem destroyed Tifsakha and all who were in it and its territory from Tirtzah, because they did not open it to him. Therefore he destroyed it, and he ripped open all the pregnant women in it.
In the thirty-ninth year of Azaryahu king of Yehudah, Menakhem the son of Gadi began to reign over Yisra'EL, and he reigned ten years in Samaria.
And he did what was evil in the sight of YHWH. He did not depart all his days from all the sins of Yarovam the son of Nevat, which he made Yisra'EL to sin.
Pul the king of Assyria came against the land, and Menakhem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, that his hand might be with him to confirm his hold on the royal power.

Menakhem exacted the money from Yisra'EL, that is, from all the wealthy men, fifty shekels of silver from every man, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back and did not stay there in the land.
Now the rest of the deeds of Menakhem and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yisra'EL?
And Menakhem slept with his fathers, and Pekakhyahu his son reigned in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azaryahu king of Yehudah, Pekakhyahu the son of Menakhem began to reign over Yisra'EL in Samaria, and he reigned two years.
And he did what was evil in the sight of YHWH. He did not turn away from the sins of Yarovam the son of Nevat, which he made Yisra'EL to sin.

And Pekakh the son of Remaliyahu, his captain, conspired against him with fifty men of the Gil'adites, and struck him down in Samaria, in the citadel of the king's house, also Argov and Arye — he killed him and reigned in his place.
Now the rest of the deeds of Pekakhyahu and all that he did, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yisra'EL.
In the fifty-second year of Azaryahu king of Yehudah, Pekakh the son of Remaliyahu began to reign over Yisra'EL in Samaria, and he reigned twenty years.
And he did what was evil in the sight of YHWH. He did not depart from the sins of Yarovam the son of Nevat, which he made Yisra'EL to sin.

In the days of Pekakh king of Yisra'EL, Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria came and captured Iyon, Avel-Beit-Ma'akhah, Yanoakh, Kedesh, Khattzor, Gil'ad, and Galil, all the land of Naftali, and he carried the people captive to Assyria.
Then Hoshea the son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekakh the son of Remaliyahu and struck him down and killed him and reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Yotam the son of Uzziyahu.
Now the rest of the deeds of Pekakh and all that he did, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yisra'EL.
In the second year of Pekakh the son of Remaliyahu, king of Yisra'EL, Yotam the son of Uzziyahu, king of Yehudah, began to reign.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Yerushah the daughter of Tzadok.
And he did what was right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that his father Uzziyahu had done.
Nevertheless, the high places were not removed — the people still sacrificed and made offerings on the high places. He built the upper gate of the house of YHWH.
Now the rest of the acts of Yotam and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yehudah?
In those days YHWH began to send Retzin the king of Aram and Pekakh the son of Remaliyahu against Yehudah.
And Yotam slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of Dawid his father, and Akhaz his son reigned in his place.
In the seventeenth year of Pekakh the son of Remaliyahu, Akhaz the son of Yotam, king of Yehudah, began to reign.
Akhaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim. And he did not do what was right in the eyes of YHWH his Creator, as his father Dawid had done,
But he walked in the way of the kings of Yisra'EL. He even burned his son as an offering, according to the despicable practices of the nations whom YHWH drove out before the people of Yisra'EL.
And he sacrificed and made offerings on the high places and on the hills and under every green tree.
Then Retzin the king of Aram and Pekakh the son of Remaliyahu, king of Yisra'EL, came up to wage war on Yerushalayim, and they besieged Akhaz but could not conquer him.
At that time Retzin the king of Aram recovered Elat for Aram and drove the men of Yehudah from Elat, and the Edomites came to Elat, where they dwell to this day.

So Akhaz sent messengers to Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria, saying, I am your servant and your son. Come up and rescue me from the hand of the king of Aram and from the hand of the king of Yisra'EL, who are attacking me.
Akhaz also took the silver and gold that was found in the house of YHWH and in the treasures of the king's house and sent a present to the king of Assyria.
And the king of Assyria listened to him. The king of Assyria marched up against Damascus and took it, carrying its people captive to Kir, and he killed Retzin.

When King Akhaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria, he saw the altar that was at Damascus. And King Akhaz sent to Uriyah the priest a model of the altar, and its pattern, exact in all its details.
And Uriyah the priest built the altar — in accordance with all that King Akhaz had sent from Damascus, so Uriyah the priest made it, before King Akhaz arrived from Damascus.
And when the king came from Damascus, the king viewed the altar. Then the king drew near to the altar and went up on it
And burned his burnt offering and his grain offering and poured his drink offering and threw the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.
And the bronze altar that was before YHWH he removed from the front of the house, from the place between his altar and the house of YHWH, and put it on the north side of his new altar.

And King Akhaz commanded Uriyah the priest, saying, On the great altar burn the morning burnt offering and the evening grain offering and the king's burnt offering and his grain offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, and their grain offering and their drink offering. And throw on it all the blood of the burnt offering and all the blood of the sacrifice, but the bronze altar shall be for me to inquire by.
Uriyah the priest did all this, as King Akhaz commanded.
And King Akhaz cut off the frames of the stands and removed the basin from them, and he took down the sea from off the bronze oxen that were under it and put it on a stone pedestal.
And the covered way for the Sabbath that had been built inside the house, and the outer entrance for the king, he removed from the house of YHWH, because of the king of Assyria.
Now the rest of the acts of Akhaz that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yehudah?
And Akhaz slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of Dawid, and Khizkiyahu his son reigned in his place.
In the twelfth year of Akhaz king of Yehudah, Hoshea the son of Elah began to reign in Samaria over Yisra'EL, and he reigned nine years.
And he did what was evil in the sight of YHWH, yet not as the kings of Yisra'EL who were before him.
Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria. And Hoshea became his vassal and paid him tribute.

But the king of Assyria found treachery in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So, king of Egypt, and offered no tribute to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year. Therefore the king of Assyria shut him up and bound him in prison.
Then the king of Assyria invaded all the land and came to Samaria, and for three years he besieged it.

In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria, and he carried Yisra'EL away to Assyria and placed them in Khala, and on the Khavor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

And this occurred because the people of Yisra'EL had sinned against YHWH their Creator, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods
And walked in the customs of the nations whom YHWH drove out before the people of Yisra'EL, and in the customs that the kings of Yisra'EL had practiced.
And the people of Yisra'EL did secretly against YHWH their Creator things that were not right. They built for themselves high places in all their towns, from watchtower to fortified city.
They set up for themselves pillars and Asherim on every high hill and under every green tree,
And there they made offerings on all the high places, as the nations did whom YHWH carried away before them. And they did wicked things, provoking YHWH to anger,
And they served idols, of which YHWH had said to them, You shall not do this.

Yet YHWH warned Yisra'EL and Yehudah by every prophet and every seer, saying, Turn from your evil ways and keep my commandments and my statutes, in accordance with all the Torah that I commanded your fathers, and that I sent to you by my servants the prophets.
But they would not listen, but were stubborn, as their fathers had been, who did not believe in YHWH their Creator.

They despised his statutes and his covenant that he made with their fathers and the warnings that he gave them. They went after false idols and became false, and they followed the nations that were around them, concerning whom YHWH had commanded them that they should not do like them.
And they abandoned all the commandments of YHWH their Creator, and made for themselves metal images of two calves — and they made an Asherah and worshiped all the host of heaven and served Ba'al.
And they burned their sons and their daughters as offerings and used divination and omens and sold themselves to do evil in the sight of YHWH, provoking him to anger.
Therefore YHWH was very angry with Yisra'EL and removed them out of his sight. None was left but the tribe of Yehudah only.
Yehudah also did not keep the commandments of YHWH their Creator, but walked in the customs that Yisra'EL had introduced.
And YHWH rejected all the descendants of Yisra'EL and afflicted them and gave them into the hand of plunderers, until he had cast them out of his sight.
When he had torn Yisra'EL from the house of Dawid, they made Yarovam the son of Nevat king. And Yarovam drove Yisra'EL from following YHWH and made them commit great sin.
The people of Yisra'EL walked in all the sins that Yarovam did. They did not depart from them,
Until YHWH removed Yisra'EL out of his sight, as he had spoken by all his servants the prophets. So Yisra'EL was exiled from their own land to Assyria until this day.

And the king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Kutah, Avva, Khamath, and Sefarvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the people of Yisra'EL. And they took possession of Samaria and lived in its cities.
And at the beginning of their dwelling there, they did not fear YHWH. Therefore YHWH sent lions among them, which killed some of them.

So the king of Assyria was told, The nations that you have carried away and placed in the cities of Samaria do not know the law of the god of the land. Therefore he has sent lions among them, and behold, they are killing them, because they do not know the law of the god of the land.
Then the king of Assyria commanded, Send there one of the priests whom you carried away from there, and let him go and dwell there and teach them the law of the god of the land.
So one of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria came and lived in Beit-El and taught them how they should fear YHWH.
But every nation still made gods of its own and put them in the shrines of the high places that the Samaritans had made, every nation in the cities in which they lived.
The men of Babylon made Sukkot-Benot, the men of Kut made Nergal, the men of Khamath made Ashima,
The Avvites made Nivkhaz and Tartaq — and the Sefarvites burned their children in the fire to Adrammelekh and Anammelekh, the gods of Sefarvaim.
They also feared YHWH and appointed from among themselves all sorts of people as priests of the high places, who sacrificed for them in the shrines of the high places.
So they feared YHWH but also served their own gods, after the manner of the nations from among whom they had been carried away.

To this day they do according to the former manner. They do not fear YHWH, and they do not follow the statutes or the rules or the Torah or the commandment that YHWH commanded the children of Yaakov, whom he named Yisra'EL.
YHWH made a covenant with them and commanded them, You shall not fear other gods or bow yourselves to them or serve them or sacrifice to them,
But you shall fear YHWH, who brought you out of the land of Egypt with great power and with an outstretched arm. You shall bow yourselves to him, and to him you shall sacrifice.
And the statutes and the rules and the Torah and the commandment that he wrote for you, you shall always be careful to do. You shall not fear other gods,
And you shall not forget the covenant that I have made with you. You shall not fear other gods,
But you shall fear YHWH your Creator, and he will deliver you out of the hand of all your enemies.
However, they would not listen, but they did according to their former manner.
So these nations feared YHWH and also served their carved images. Their children did likewise, and their children's children — as their fathers did, so they do to this day.
In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Yisra'EL, Khizkiyahu the son of Akhaz, king of Yehudah, began to reign.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Avi the daughter of Zekhariah.
And he did what was right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that Dawid his father had done.

He removed the high places and broke the pillars and cut down the Asherah. And he broke in pieces the bronze serpent that Moshe had made, for until those days the people of Yisra'EL had made offerings to it — it was called Nakhushtan.
He trusted in YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, so that there was none like him among all the kings of Yehudah after him, nor among those who were before him.
For he held fast to YHWH. He did not depart from following him, but kept the commandments that YHWH commanded Moshe.
And YHWH was with him — wherever he went out, he prospered. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and would not serve him.
He struck down the Pelishtim as far as Azzah and its territory, from watchtower to fortified city.
In the fourth year of King Khizkiyahu, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Yisra'EL, Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it,
And at the end of three years he took it. In the sixth year of Khizkiyahu, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Yisra'EL, Samaria was taken.
The king of Assyria carried Yisra'EL away to Assyria and put them in Khala, and on the Khavor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes,
Because they did not obey the voice of YHWH their Creator but transgressed his covenant, even all that Moshe the servant of YHWH commanded. They neither listened nor obeyed.
In the fourteenth year of King Khizkiyahu, Sanheriv king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Yehudah and took them.

And Khizkiyahu king of Yehudah sent to the king of Assyria at Lakhish, saying, I have done wrong — withdraw from me. Whatever you impose on me I will bear. And the king of Assyria required of Khizkiyahu king of Yehudah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
And Khizkiyahu gave him all the silver that was found in the house of YHWH and in the treasuries of the king's house.
At that time Khizkiyahu stripped the gold from the doors of the temple of YHWH and from the doorposts that Khizkiyahu king of Yehudah had overlaid and gave it to the king of Assyria.

And the king of Assyria sent the Tartan, the Rav-Saris, and the Rabshakeh with a great army from Lakhish to King Khizkiyahu at Yerushalayim. And they went up and came to Yerushalayim. When they arrived, they came and stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is on the highway to the Washer's Field.
And when they called for the king, there came out to them Elyakim the son of Khilkiyahu, who was over the household, and Shevna the secretary, and Yo'akh the son of Asaf, the recorder.
And the Rabshakeh said to them, Say to Khizkiyahu, Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: On what do you rest this trust of yours?
Do you think that mere words are strategy and power for war? In whom do you now trust, that you have rebelled against me?
Behold, you are trusting now in Egypt, that broken reed of a staff, which will pierce the hand of any man who leans on it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.

But if you say to me, We trust in YHWH our Creator, is it not he whose high places and altars Khizkiyahu has removed, telling Yehudah and Yerushalayim, You shall worship before this altar in Yerushalayim?
Come now, make a wager with my master the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to set riders on them.
How then can you repulse a single captain among the least of my master's servants, when you trust in Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
Moreover, is it without YHWH that I have come up against this place to destroy it? YHWH said to me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.

Then Elyakim the son of Khilkiyahu, and Shevna, and Yo'akh said to the Rabshakeh, Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in the language of Yehudah within the hearing of the people who are on the wall.

But the Rabshakeh said to them, Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are doomed with you to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?
Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out in a loud voice in the language of Yehudah: Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria.
Thus says the king, Do not let Khizkiyahu deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver you out of his hand.
Do not let Khizkiyahu make you trust in YHWH by saying, YHWH will surely deliver us, and this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.

Do not listen to Khizkiyahu, for thus says the king of Assyria: Make your peace with me and come out to me. Then each one of you will eat of his own vine, and each one of his own fig tree, and each one of you will drink the water of his own cistern,

Until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and honey, that you may live, and not die. And do not listen to Khizkiyahu when he misleads you by saying, YHWH will deliver us.
Has any of the gods of the nations ever delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Khamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sefarvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?
Who among all the gods of the lands have delivered their lands out of my hand, that YHWH should deliver Yerushalayim out of my hand?
But the people were silent and answered him not a word, for the king's command was, Do not answer him.

Then Elyakim the son of Khilkiyahu, who was over the household, and Shevna the secretary, and Yo'akh the son of Asaf, the recorder, came to Khizkiyahu with their clothes torn and told him the words of the Rabshakeh.
As soon as King Khizkiyahu heard it, he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of YHWH.
And he sent Elyakim, who was over the household, and Shevna the secretary, and the senior priests, covered with sackcloth, to the prophet Yesha'yahu the son of Amoz.
They said to him, Thus says Khizkiyahu, This day is a day of distress, of rebuke, and of disgrace — children have come to the point of birth, and there is no strength to bring them forth.

It may be that YHWH your Creator will hear all the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to mock the living Creator, and will rebuke the words that YHWH your Creator has heard. Therefore lift up your prayer for the remnant that is left.
When the servants of King Khizkiyahu came to Yesha'yahu,
Yesha'yahu said to them, Say to your master, Thus says YHWH: Do not be afraid because of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have reviled me.
Behold, I will put a spirit in him, so that he shall hear a rumor and return to his own land, and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.
The Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of Assyria fighting against Livnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lakhish.
And when the king heard concerning Tirhakah king of Kush, Behold, he has set out to fight against you, he sent messengers again to Khizkiyahu, saying,
Thus shall you speak to Khizkiyahu king of Yehudah: Do not let your Creator in whom you trust deceive you by saying, Yerushalayim will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.
Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, devoting them to destruction. And shall you be delivered?
Have the gods of the nations delivered them, the nations that my fathers destroyed, Gozan, Kharan, Retzef, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Khamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sefarvaim, the king of Hena, or the king of Ivvah?
Khizkiyahu received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. And Khizkiyahu went up to the house of YHWH and spread it before YHWH.

And Khizkiyahu prayed before YHWH and said, O YHWH, Creator of Yisra'EL, enthroned above the cherubim, you are the Creator, you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth — you have made heaven and earth.
Incline your ear, O YHWH, and hear — open your eyes, O YHWH, and see — and hear the words of Sanheriv, which he has sent to mock the living Creator.
Truly, O YHWH, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands
And have cast their gods into the fire, for they were not gods, but the work of men's hands, wood and stone. Therefore they were destroyed.
So now, O YHWH our Creator, save us, please, from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, O YHWH, are Creator alone.
Then Yesha'yahu the son of Amoz sent to Khizkiyahu, saying, Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Your prayer to me about Sanheriv king of Assyria I have heard.
This is the word that YHWH has spoken concerning him: She despises you, she scorns you — the virgin daughter of Tziyon — she wags her head behind you, the daughter of Yerushalayim.
Whom have you mocked and reviled? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes to the heights? Against the Holy One of Yisra'EL.

By your messengers you have mocked YHWH, and you have said, With my many chariots I have gone up the heights of the mountains, to the far recesses of Lebanon, to cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest cypresses — I entered its farthest lodging place, its most fruitful forest.
I dug wells and drank the waters, and I dried up with the sole of my foot all the streams of Egypt.
Have you not heard that I determined it long ago? I planned from days of old what now I bring to pass, that you should make fortified cities crash into heaps of ruins,
While their inhabitants, shorn of strength, are dismayed and confounded, and have become like plants of the field and like tender grass, like grass on the housetops, blighted before it is grown.
But I know your sitting down and your going out and coming in, and your raging against me.
Because you have raged against me and your complacency has come to my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth, and I will turn you back on the way by which you came.

And this shall be the sign for you: this year you shall eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs of the same. Then in the third year sow and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.
And the surviving remnant of the house of Yehudah shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
For out of Yerushalayim shall go a remnant, and out of Mount Tziyon a band of survivors. The zeal of YHWH of hosts will do this.
Therefore thus says YHWH concerning the king of Assyria: He shall not come into this city or shoot an arrow there, or come before it with a shield or cast up a siege mound against it.
By the way that he came, by the same he shall return, and he shall not come into this city, declares YHWH.
For I will defend this city to save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant Dawid.

And that night the angel of YHWH went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians. And when people arose early in the morning, behold, these were all dead bodies.
Then Sanheriv king of Assyria departed and went home and lived at Nineveh.

And as he was worshiping in the house of Nisrokh his god, Adrammelekh and Sharetzer, his sons, struck him down with the sword and escaped into the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.

In those days Khizkiyahu became sick and was at the point of death. And Yesha'yahu the prophet the son of Amoz came to him and said to him, Thus says YHWH, Set your house in order, for you shall die — you shall not recover from this illness.
Then Khizkiyahu turned his face to the wall and prayed to YHWH, saying,
Now, O YHWH, please remember how I have walked before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in your sight. And Khizkiyahu wept bitterly.
And before Yesha'yahu had gone out of the middle court, the word of YHWH came to him:

Turn back, and say to Khizkiyahu the leader of my people, Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Dawid your father, I have heard your prayer — I have seen your tears. Behold, I will heal you. On the third day you shall go up to the house of YHWH.
And I will add fifteen years to your life. I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city for my own sake and for my servant Dawid's sake.
And Yesha'yahu said, Bring a cake of figs. And let them take and lay it on the boil, that he may recover.
And Khizkiyahu said to Yesha'yahu, What shall be the sign that YHWH will heal me, and that I shall go up to the house of YHWH on the third day?
And Yesha'yahu said, This shall be the sign to you from YHWH, that YHWH will do the thing that he has promised: shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or go back ten steps?
And Khizkiyahu answered, It is an easy thing for the shadow to lengthen ten steps. Rather let the shadow go back ten steps.
And Yesha'yahu the prophet called to YHWH, and he brought the shadow back ten steps, by which it had gone down on the steps of Akhaz.
At that time Merodakh-Baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent envoys with letters and a present to Khizkiyahu, for he heard that Khizkiyahu had been sick.

And Khizkiyahu welcomed them, and he showed them all his treasure house, the silver, the gold, the spices, the precious oil, his armory, all that was found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his house or in all his realm that Khizkiyahu did not show them.
Then Yesha'yahu the prophet came to King Khizkiyahu, and said to him, What did these men say? And from where did they come to you? Khizkiyahu said, They have come from a far country, from Babylon.
He said, What have they seen in your house? And Khizkiyahu answered, They have seen all that is in my house — there is nothing in my storehouses that I did not show them.
Then Yesha'yahu said to Khizkiyahu, Hear the word of YHWH:
Behold, the days are coming, when all that is in your house, and that which your fathers have stored up till this day, shall be carried to Babylon. Nothing shall be left, says YHWH.
And some of your own sons, who will come from you, whom you will father, shall be taken away, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
Then Khizkiyahu said to Yesha'yahu, The word of YHWH that you have spoken is good. For he thought, Why not, if there will be peace and security in my days?

The rest of the deeds of Khizkiyahu and all his might, and how he made the pool and the conduit and brought water into the city, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Yehudah?
And Khizkiyahu slept with his fathers, and Menasheh his son reigned in his place.
Menasheh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Kheftzivah.
And he did what was evil in the sight of YHWH, according to the despicable practices of the nations whom YHWH drove out before the people of Yisra'EL.

For he rebuilt the high places that Khizkiyahu his father had destroyed, and he erected altars for Ba'al and made an Asherah, as Akhav king of Yisra'EL had done, and worshiped all the host of heaven and served them.
And he built altars in the house of YHWH, of which YHWH had said, In Yerushalayim will I put my name.
And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of YHWH.
And he burned his son as an offering and used fortune-telling and omens and dealt with mediums and with necromancers. He did much evil in the sight of YHWH, provoking him to anger.

And the carved image of Asherah that he had made he set in the house of which YHWH said to Dawid and to Shelomoh his son, In this house, and in Yerushalayim, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Yisra'EL, I will put my name forever.

And I will not cause the feet of Yisra'EL to wander anymore out of the land that I gave to their fathers, if only they will be careful to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the Torah that my servant Moshe commanded them.
But they did not listen, and Menasheh led them astray to do more evil than the nations had done whom YHWH destroyed before the people of Yisra'EL.
And YHWH said by his servants the prophets,
Because Menasheh king of Yehudah has committed these abominations and has done things more evil than all that the Amorites did, who were before him, and has made Yehudah also to sin with his idols,
