In those days they shall no longer say, The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.
But everyone shall die for his own iniquity. Each man who eats sour grapes, his teeth shall be set on edge.
Behold, the days are coming, declares YHWH, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Yisra'EL and the house of Yehudah,

Not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, my covenant that they broke, though I was their husband, declares YHWH.

For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Yisra'EL after those days, declares YHWH: I will put my Torah within them, and I will write it on their hearts. And I will be their Creator, and they shall be my people.

And no longer shall each one teach his neighbor and each his brother, saying, Know YHWH, for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares YHWH. For I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.
Thus says YHWH, who gives the sun for light by day and the fixed order of the moon and the stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar — YHWH of hosts is his name:
If this fixed order departs from before me, declares YHWH, then shall the offspring of Yisra'EL cease from being a nation before me forever.

Thus says YHWH: If the heavens above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth below can be explored, then I will cast off all the offspring of Yisra'EL for all that they have done, declares YHWH.
Behold, the days are coming, declares YHWH, when the city shall be rebuilt for YHWH from the Tower of Hanan'el to the Corner Gate.
And the measuring line shall go out farther, straight to the hill Garev, and shall then turn to Go'ah.

The whole valley of the dead bodies and the ashes, and all the fields as far as the brook Kidron, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, shall be sacred to YHWH. It shall not be uprooted or overthrown anymore forever.
The word that came to Yirmeyahu from YHWH in the tenth year of Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah, which was the eighteenth year of Nevukhadnetzar.
At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Yerushalayim, and Yirmeyahu the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard that was in the palace of the king of Yehudah.
For Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah had imprisoned him, saying, Why do you prophesy and say, Thus says YHWH: Behold, I am giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall capture it;

Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah shall not escape out of the hand of the Chaldeans, but shall surely be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and shall speak with him face to face and see him eye to eye.
And he shall take Tzidkiyahu to Babylon, and there he shall remain until I visit him, declares YHWH. Though you fight against the Chaldeans, you shall not succeed?
Yirmeyahu said, The word of YHWH came to me:
Behold, Khanamel the son of Shallum your uncle will come to you and say, Buy my field that is at Anatot, for the right of redemption by purchase is yours.

Then Khanamel my cousin came to me in the court of the guard, in accordance with the word of YHWH, and said to me, Buy my field that is at Anatot in the land of Binyamin, for the right of possession and redemption is yours. Buy it for yourself. Then I knew that this was the word of YHWH.
And I bought the field at Anatot from Khanamel my cousin, and weighed out the money to him, seventeen shekels of silver.
I signed the deed, sealed it, got witnesses, and weighed the money on scales.
Then I took the sealed deed of purchase, containing the terms and conditions, and the open copy.

And I gave the deed of purchase to Barukh the son of Neriyahu son of Makhseiyahu, in the presence of Khanamel my cousin, in the presence of the witnesses who signed the deed of purchase, and in the presence of all the Yehudim who were sitting in the court of the guard.
I charged Barukh in their presence, saying,
Thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Take these deeds, both this sealed deed of purchase and this open deed, and put them in an earthenware vessel, that they may last for a long time.
For thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Houses and fields and vineyards shall again be bought in this land.
After I had given the deed of purchase to Barukh the son of Neriyahu, I prayed to YHWH, saying:
Ah, YHWH my Creator — it is you who have made the heavens and the earth by your great power and by your outstretched arm. Nothing is too hard for you.
You show steadfast love to thousands, but you repay the guilt of fathers to their children after them, O great and mighty Creator, whose name is YHWH of hosts,
Great in counsel and mighty in deed, whose eyes are open to all the ways of the children of man, rewarding each one according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.
You have shown signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and to this day in Yisra'EL and among all mankind, and have made a name for yourself, as at this day.
You brought your people Yisra'EL out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and outstretched arm, and with great terror.
And you gave them this land, which you swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.

And they entered and took possession of it. But they did not obey your voice or walk in your Torah. They did nothing of all you commanded them to do. Therefore you have made all this disaster come upon them.

Behold, the siege mounds have come up to the city to take it, and because of sword and famine and pestilence the city is given into the hands of the Chaldeans who are fighting against it. What you spoke has come to pass, and behold, you see it.
Yet you, O YHWH my Creator, have said to me, Buy the field for money and get witnesses — though the city is given into the hands of the Chaldeans.
The word of YHWH came to Yirmeyahu:
Behold, I am YHWH, the Creator of all flesh. Is anything too hard for me?
Therefore, thus says YHWH: Behold, I am giving this city into the hands of the Chaldeans and into the hand of Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon, and he shall capture it.

The Chaldeans who are fighting against this city shall come and set this city on fire and burn it, with the houses on whose roofs offerings have been made to Ba'al and drink offerings have been poured out to other gods, to provoke me to anger.

For the children of Yisra'EL and the children of Yehudah have done nothing but evil in my sight from their youth. The children of Yisra'EL have done nothing but provoke me to anger by the work of their hands, declares YHWH.
This city has aroused my anger and wrath, from the day it was built to this day, so that I will remove it from my sight

Because of all the evil of the children of Yisra'EL and the children of Yehudah that they did to provoke me to anger — their kings and their officials, their priests and their prophets, the men of Yehudah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.
They have turned their back to me and not their face. And though I have taught them persistently, they have not listened to receive instruction.
They set up their abominations in the house that is called by my name, to defile it.

They built the high places of Ba'al in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, to offer up their sons and daughters to Molekh, though I did not command them, nor did it enter into my mind, that they should do this abomination, to cause Yehudah to sin.
Now therefore thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, concerning this city of which you say, It is given into the hand of the king of Babylon by sword, by famine, and by pestilence:
Behold, I will gather them from all the countries to which I drove them in my anger and my wrath and in great indignation. I will bring them back to this place, and I will make them dwell in safety.
And they shall be my people, and I will be their Creator.
I will give them one heart and one way, that they may fear me forever, for their own good and the good of their children after them.
I will make with them an everlasting covenant, that I will not turn away from doing good to them. And I will put the fear of me in their hearts, that they may not turn from me.
I will rejoice in doing them good, and I will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all my heart and all my soul.
For thus says YHWH: Just as I have brought all this great disaster upon this people, so I will bring upon them all the good that I promise them.
Fields shall be bought in this land of which you are saying, It is a desolation, without man or beast — it is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.

Fields shall be bought for money, and deeds shall be signed and sealed and witnessed, in the land of Binyamin, in the places around Yerushalayim, and in the cities of Yehudah, in the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the Shephelah, and in the cities of the Negev. For I will restore their fortunes, declares YHWH.
The word of YHWH came to Yirmeyahu a second time, while he was still shut up in the court of the guard:
Thus says YHWH who made the earth, YHWH who formed it to establish it — YHWH is his name:
Call to me and I will answer you, and will tell you great and hidden things that you have not known.

For thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, concerning the houses of this city and the houses of the kings of Yehudah that were torn down to make a defense against the siege mounds and against the sword:

They are coming in to fight against the Chaldeans and to fill them with the dead bodies of men whom I shall strike down in my anger and my wrath, for I have hidden my face from this city because of all their evil.
Behold, I will bring to it health and healing, and I will heal them and reveal to them abundance of prosperity and security.
I will restore the fortunes of Yehudah and the fortunes of Yisra'EL, and rebuild them as they were at first.
I will cleanse them from all the guilt of their sin against me, and I will forgive all the guilt of their sin and rebellion against me.

And this city shall be to me a name of joy, a praise and a glory before all the nations of the earth who shall hear of all the good that I do for them. They shall fear and tremble because of all the good and all the prosperity I provide for it.

Thus says YHWH: In this place of which you say, It is a waste without man or beast, in the cities of Yehudah and the streets of Yerushalayim that are desolate, without man or inhabitant or beast, there shall be heard again

The voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voices of those who sing, as they bring thank offerings to the house of YHWH: Give thanks to YHWH of hosts, for YHWH is good, for his steadfast love endures forever. For I will restore the fortunes of the land as at first, says YHWH.
Thus says YHWH of hosts: In this place that is waste, without man or beast, and in all of its cities, there shall again be habitations of shepherds resting their flocks.

In the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the Shephelah, and in the cities of the Negev, in the land of Binyamin, the places about Yerushalayim, and in the cities of Yehudah, flocks shall again pass under the hands of the one who counts them, says YHWH.
Behold, the days are coming, declares YHWH, when I will fulfill the promise I made to the house of Yisra'EL and the house of Yehudah.
In those days and at that time I will cause a righteous Branch to spring up for Dawid, and he shall execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Yehudah will be saved, and Yerushalayim will dwell securely. And this is the name by which it will be called: YHWH Is Our Righteousness.
For thus says YHWH: Dawid shall never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Yisra'EL,
And the Levitical priests shall never lack a man in my presence to offer burnt offerings, to burn grain offerings, and to make sacrifices forever.
Thus says YHWH: If you can break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night, so that day and night will not come at their appointed time,
Then also my covenant with Dawid my servant may be broken, so that he shall not have a son to reign on his throne, and my covenant with the Levitical priests my ministers.
As the host of heaven cannot be numbered and the sands of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the offspring of Dawid my servant, and the Levitical priests who minister to me.
Have you not observed that these people are saying, YHWH has rejected the two clans that he chose? Thus they have despised my people so that they are no longer a nation in their sight.
Thus says YHWH: If I have not established my covenant with day and night and the fixed order of heaven and earth,

Then I will reject the offspring of Yaakov and Dawid my servant and will not choose one of his offspring to rule over the offspring of Avraham, Yitzkhak, and Yaakov. For I will restore their fortunes and will have mercy on them.

The word that came to Yirmeyahu from YHWH, when Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon and all his army and all the kingdoms of the earth under his dominion and all the peoples were fighting against Yerushalayim and all of its cities:

Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Go and speak to Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah and say to him, Thus says YHWH: Behold, I am giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn it with fire.
You shall not escape from his hand but shall surely be captured and delivered into his hand. You shall see the king of Babylon eye to eye and speak with him face to face. And you shall go to Babylon.
Yet hear the word of YHWH, O Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah. Thus says YHWH concerning you: You shall not die by the sword.

You shall die in peace. And as spices were burned for your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so people shall burn spices for you and lament for you, saying, Ah, lord — for I have spoken the word, declares YHWH.
Then Yirmeyahu the prophet spoke all these words to Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah, in Yerushalayim,

When the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Yerushalayim and against all the cities of Yehudah that were left, Lakhish and Azekah, for these were the only fortified cities of Yehudah that remained.
The word that came to Yirmeyahu from YHWH, after King Tzidkiyahu had made a covenant with all the people in Yerushalayim to make a proclamation of liberty to them,
That everyone should set free his Hebrew slaves, male and female, so that no one should enslave a Yehudi, his brother.

And they obeyed, all the officials and all the people who had entered into the covenant that everyone would set free his slave, male or female, so that they would not be enslaved again. They obeyed and set them free.
But afterward they turned around and took back the male and female slaves they had set free, and brought them into subjection as slaves.
The word of YHWH came to Yirmeyahu from YHWH:
Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL: I myself made a covenant with your fathers when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, saying,

At the end of seven years each of you must set free the fellow Hebrew who has been sold to you and has served you six years. You must set him free from your service. But your fathers did not listen to me or incline their ears to me.
You recently repented and did what was right in my eyes by proclaiming liberty, each to his neighbor, and you made a covenant before me in the house that is called by my name.

But then you turned around and profaned my name when each of you took back his male and female slaves, whom you had set free according to their desire, and you brought them into subjection to be your slaves.

Therefore, thus says YHWH: You have not obeyed me by proclaiming liberty, every one to his brother and to his neighbor. Behold, I proclaim to you liberty to the sword, to pestilence, and to famine, declares YHWH. I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
And the men who transgressed my covenant and did not keep the terms of the covenant that they made before me, I will make them like the calf that they cut in two and passed between its parts —
The officials of Yehudah, the officials of Yerushalayim, the eunuchs, the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the parts of the calf.
And I will give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their lives. Their dead bodies shall be food for the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth.

And Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah and his officials I will give into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their lives, into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon which has withdrawn from you.

Behold, I will command, declares YHWH, and will bring them back to this city, and they will fight against it and take it and burn it with fire. I will make the cities of Yehudah a desolation without inhabitant.
The word that came to Yirmeyahu from YHWH in the days of Yeho'yakim the son of Yoshiyahu, king of Yehudah:
Go to the house of the Rekhabites and speak with them and bring them to the house of YHWH, into one of the chambers, and offer them wine to drink.
So I took Yaazanyahu the son of Yirmeyahu, son of Khabatzinyahu, and his brothers and all his sons and the whole house of the Rekhabites.

I brought them to the house of YHWH, into the chamber of the sons of Khanan the son of Yigdalyahu, the man of Creator, which was near the chamber of the officials, above the chamber of Ma'aseiyahu the son of Shallum, keeper of the threshold.
Then I set before the sons of the house of the Rekhabites pitchers full of wine, and cups, and I said to them, Drink wine.
But they answered, We will drink no wine, for Yonadav the son of Rekhav, our father, commanded us, You shall not drink wine, neither you nor your sons forever.
You shall not build a house. You shall not sow seed. You shall not plant or have a vineyard, but you shall live in tents all your days, that you may live many days in the land where you sojourn.
We have obeyed the voice of Yonadav the son of Rekhav, our father, in all that he commanded us, to drink no wine all our days, ourselves, our wives, our sons, or our daughters,
And not to build houses to dwell in. We have no vineyard or field or seed,
But we have lived in tents and have obeyed and done all that Yonadav our father commanded us.

But when Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon came up against the land, we said, Come, and let us go to Yerushalayim for fear of the army of the Chaldeans and the army of the Arameans. So we are living in Yerushalayim.
Then the word of YHWH came to Yirmeyahu:
Thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Go and say to the people of Yehudah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, Will you not receive instruction and listen to my words? declares YHWH.

The command that Yonadav the son of Rekhav gave to his sons, to drink no wine, has been kept, and they drink none to this day, for they have obeyed their father's command. I have spoken to you persistently, but you have not listened to me.

I have sent to you all my servants the prophets, sending them persistently, saying, Turn now every one of you from his evil way, and amend your deeds, and do not go after other gods to serve them, and then you shall dwell in the land that I gave to you and your fathers. But you did not incline your ear or listen to me.
The sons of Yonadav the son of Rekhav have kept the command that their father gave them, but this people has not obeyed me.

Therefore, thus says YHWH, the Creator of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Behold, I am bringing upon Yehudah and all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim all the disaster that I have pronounced against them, because I have spoken to them and they have not listened, I have called to them and they have not answered.

But to the house of the Rekhabites Yirmeyahu said, Thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Because you have obeyed the command of Yonadav your father and kept all his precepts and done all that he commanded you,
Therefore thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Yonadav the son of Rekhav shall never lack a man to stand before me.
In the fourth year of Yeho'yakim the son of Yoshiyahu, king of Yehudah, this word came to Yirmeyahu from YHWH:
Take a scroll and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you against Yisra'EL and Yehudah and all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Yoshiyahu until today.
It may be that the house of Yehudah will hear all the disaster that I intend to do to them, so that every one may turn from his evil way, and that I may forgive their iniquity and their sin.
Then Yirmeyahu called Barukh the son of Neriyahu, and Barukh wrote on a scroll at the dictation of Yirmeyahu all the words of YHWH that he had spoken to him.
And Yirmeyahu ordered Barukh, saying, I am banned from going to the house of YHWH,

So you are to go, and on a day of fasting in the hearing of all the people in YHWH's house you shall read the words of YHWH from the scroll that you have written at my dictation. You shall read them also in the hearing of all the people of Yehudah who come out of their cities.
It may be that their plea for mercy will come before YHWH, and that every one will turn from his evil way, for great is the anger and wrath that YHWH has pronounced against this people.
And Barukh the son of Neriyahu did all that Yirmeyahu the prophet ordered him about reading from the scroll the words of YHWH in YHWH's house.

In the fifth year of Yeho'yakim the son of Yoshiyahu, king of Yehudah, in the ninth month, all the people in Yerushalayim and all the people who came from the cities of Yehudah to Yerushalayim proclaimed a fast before YHWH.

Then, in the hearing of all the people, Barukh read the words of Yirmeyahu from the scroll, in the house of YHWH, in the chamber of Gemaryahu the son of Shafan the secretary, which was in the upper court, at the entry of the New Gate of YHWH's house.
When Mikhayahu the son of Gemaryahu, son of Shafan, heard all the words of YHWH from the scroll,

He went down to the king's house, into the secretary's chamber, and all the officials were sitting there: Elishama the secretary, Delayahu the son of Shemayahu, Elnatan the son of Akhbor, Gemaryahu the son of Shafan, Tzidkiyahu the son of Hananyahu, and all the officials.
And Mikhayahu told them all the words that he had heard, when Barukh read the scroll in the hearing of the people.

Then all the officials sent Yehudi the son of Netanyahu, son of Shelemyahu, son of Khushi, to say to Barukh, Take in your hand the scroll that you read in the hearing of the people, and come. So Barukh the son of Neriyahu took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
And they said to him, Sit down and read it to us. So Barukh read it to them.
When they heard all the words, they turned one to another in fear. And they said to Barukh, We must report all these words to the king.
Then they asked Barukh, Tell us, how did you write all these words? Was it at his dictation?
Barukh answered them, He dictated all these words to me, while I wrote them with ink on the scroll.
Then the officials said to Barukh, Go and hide, you and Yirmeyahu, and let no one know where you are.
So they went into the court to the king, having put the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the secretary, and they reported all the words to the king.
Then the king sent Yehudi to get the scroll, and he took it from the chamber of Elishama the secretary. And Yehudi read it to the king and all the officials who stood beside the king.
It was the ninth month, and the king was sitting in the winter house, and there was a fire burning in the fire pot before him.
As Yehudi read three or four columns, the king would cut them off with a knife and throw them into the fire in the fire pot, until the entire scroll was consumed in the fire that was in the fire pot.
Yet neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words was afraid, nor did they tear their garments.
Even when Elnatan and Delayahu and Gemaryahu urged the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them.
And the king commanded Yerakhmeel the king's son and Serayahu the son of Azri'el and Shelemyahu the son of Avde'el to seize Barukh the secretary and Yirmeyahu the prophet, but YHWH hid them.
Now after the king had burned the scroll with the words that Barukh wrote at Yirmeyahu's dictation, the word of YHWH came to Yirmeyahu:
Take another scroll and write on it all the former words that were in the first scroll, which Yeho'yakim the king of Yehudah has burned.

And concerning Yeho'yakim king of Yehudah you shall say, Thus says YHWH: You have burned this scroll, saying, Why have you written in it that the king of Babylon will certainly come and destroy this land, and will cut off from it man and beast?
Therefore thus says YHWH concerning Yeho'yakim king of Yehudah: He shall have none to sit on the throne of Dawid, and his dead body shall be cast out to the heat by day and the frost by night.

And I will punish him and his offspring and his servants for their iniquity. I will bring upon them and upon the inhabitants of Yerushalayim and upon the people of Yehudah all the disaster that I have pronounced against them, but they would not hear.

Then Yirmeyahu took another scroll and gave it to Barukh the son of Neriyahu, the secretary, who wrote on it at the dictation of Yirmeyahu all the words of the scroll that Yeho'yakim king of Yehudah had burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to them.
Tzidkiyahu the son of Yoshiyahu, whom Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Yehudah, reigned instead of Coniyahu the son of Yeho'yakim.
But neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of YHWH that he spoke through Yirmeyahu the prophet.
King Tzidkiyahu sent Yukhal the son of Shelemyahu, and Tzefanyahu the priest, the son of Ma'aseiyahu, to Yirmeyahu the prophet, saying, Please pray for us to YHWH our Creator.
Now Yirmeyahu was still going in and out among the people, for he had not yet been put in prison.
The army of Pharaoh had come out of Egypt, and when the Chaldeans who were besieging Yerushalayim heard news about them, they withdrew from Yerushalayim.
Then the word of YHWH came to Yirmeyahu the prophet:

Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Thus shall you say to the king of Yehudah who sent you to me to inquire of me: Behold, Pharaoh's army that came to help you is about to return to Egypt, to its own land.
And the Chaldeans shall come back and fight against this city. They shall capture it and burn it with fire.
Thus says YHWH: Do not deceive yourselves, saying, The Chaldeans will surely go away from us, for they will not go away.

For even if you had struck down the whole army of Chaldeans who are fighting against you, and there remained of them only wounded men, every man in his tent, they would rise up and burn this city with fire.
Now when the Chaldean army had withdrawn from Yerushalayim at the approach of Pharaoh's army,
Yirmeyahu set out from Yerushalayim to go to the land of Binyamin to receive his portion there among the people.
When he was at the Benjamin Gate, a sentry there named Yiriyahu the son of Shelemyahu, son of Khananiyahu, seized Yirmeyahu the prophet, saying, You are deserting to the Chaldeans.
And Yirmeyahu said, It is a lie — I am not deserting to the Chaldeans. But Yiriyahu would not listen to him, and seized Yirmeyahu and brought him to the officials.
And the officials were enraged at Yirmeyahu, and they beat him and imprisoned him in the house of Yehonatan the secretary, for it had been made a prison.
When Yirmeyahu had come into the dungeon house and the cells, Yirmeyahu remained there many days.

Then King Tzidkiyahu sent for him and received him. The king questioned him secretly in his house and said, Is there any word from YHWH? Yirmeyahu said, There is. Then he said, You shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.
Yirmeyahu also said to King Tzidkiyahu, What wrong have I done to you or your servants or this people, that you have put me in prison?
Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, The king of Babylon will not come against you and against this land?
Now hear, please, O my lord the king: let my humble plea come before you, and do not send me back to the house of Yehonatan the secretary, lest I die there.

So King Tzidkiyahu gave orders, and they committed Yirmeyahu to the court of the guard. And a loaf of bread was given him daily from the bakers' street, until all the bread of the city was gone. So Yirmeyahu remained in the court of the guard.
Now Shefatyahu the son of Matan, Gedalyahu the son of Pashkhur, Yukhal the son of Shelemyahu, and Pashkhur the son of Malkiyahu heard the words that Yirmeyahu was saying to all the people,
Thus says YHWH: He who stays in this city shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence, but he who goes out to the Chaldeans shall live. He shall have his life as a prize of war, and live.
Thus says YHWH: This city shall surely be given into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon and be captured.

Then the officials said to the king, Let this man be put to death, for he is weakening the hands of the soldiers who are left in this city, and the hands of all the people, by speaking such words to them. For this man is not seeking the welfare of this people, but their harm.
King Tzidkiyahu said, Behold, he is in your hands, for the king can do nothing against you.

So they took Yirmeyahu and cast him into the cistern of Malkiyahu, the king's son, which was in the court of the guard, letting Yirmeyahu down by ropes. And there was no water in the cistern, but only mud, and Yirmeyahu sank in the mud.
When Eved-Melekh the Kushite, a eunuch who was in the king's house, heard that they had put Yirmeyahu into the cistern — the king was sitting in the Benjamin Gate —
Eved-Melekh went from the king's house and said to the king,
My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they did to Yirmeyahu the prophet by casting him into the cistern, and he will die there of hunger, for there is no bread left in the city.
Then the king commanded Eved-Melekh the Kushite, Take thirty men with you from here, and lift Yirmeyahu the prophet out of the cistern before he dies.

So Eved-Melekh took the men with him and went to the house of the king, to a wardrobe in the storehouse, and took from there old rags and worn-out clothes, which he let down to Yirmeyahu in the cistern by ropes.
Then Eved-Melekh the Kushite said to Yirmeyahu, Put the rags and clothes between your armpits and the ropes. Yirmeyahu did so.
Then they drew Yirmeyahu up with ropes and lifted him out of the cistern. And Yirmeyahu remained in the court of the guard.
King Tzidkiyahu sent for Yirmeyahu the prophet and received him at the third entrance of the temple of YHWH. The king said to Yirmeyahu, I will ask you a question — hide nothing from me.
Yirmeyahu said to Tzidkiyahu, If I tell you, will you not surely put me to death? And if I give you counsel, you will not listen to me.
Then King Tzidkiyahu swore secretly to Yirmeyahu, As YHWH lives, who made our souls, I will not put you to death or deliver you into the hand of these men who seek your life.

Then Yirmeyahu said to Tzidkiyahu, Thus says YHWH, the Creator of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: If you will surrender to the officials of the king of Babylon, then your life shall be spared, and this city shall not be burned with fire, and you and your house shall live.

But if you do not surrender to the officials of the king of Babylon, then this city shall be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and you shall not escape from their hand.
King Tzidkiyahu said to Yirmeyahu, I am afraid of the Yehudim who have deserted to the Chaldeans, lest I be handed over to them and they deal cruelly with me.
Yirmeyahu said, You shall not be given to them. Obey now the voice of YHWH in what I say to you, and it shall be well with you, and your life shall be spared.
But if you refuse to surrender, this is the vision that YHWH has shown to me:

Behold, all the women left in the house of the king of Yehudah were being led out to the officials of the king of Babylon and were saying, Your trusted friends have deceived you and prevailed against you. Now that your feet are sunk in the mud, they have turned away from you.
All your wives and your sons shall be led out to the Chaldeans, and you yourself shall not escape from their hand, but shall be seized by the king of Babylon, and this city shall be burned with fire.
Then Tzidkiyahu said to Yirmeyahu, Let no one know of these words, and you shall not die.

If the officials hear that I have spoken with you and come to you and say to you, Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you — hide nothing from us and we will not put you to death —
Then you shall say to them, I made a humble plea to the king that he would not send me back to the house of Yehonatan to die there.
Then all the officials came to Yirmeyahu and asked him, and he answered them as the king had instructed him. So they stopped speaking with him, for the conversation had not been overheard.
And Yirmeyahu remained in the court of the guard until the day that Yerushalayim was taken. And he was there when Yerushalayim was taken.
In the ninth year of Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah, in the tenth month, Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon and all his army came against Yerushalayim and besieged it.
In the eleventh year of Tzidkiyahu, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, a breach was made in the city.

Then all the officials of the king of Babylon came and sat in the middle gate: Nergal-Sar-Etzer, Samgar, Nevu-Sar-Sekhim the chief officer, Nergal-Sar-Etzer the chief officer, and all the rest of the officials of the king of Babylon.

When Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah and all the soldiers saw them, they fled, going out of the city at night by way of the king's garden through the gate between the two walls, and they went toward the Arabah.

But the army of the Chaldeans pursued them and overtook Tzidkiyahu in the plains of Yericho. And when they had taken him, they brought him up to Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon, at Rivlah, in the land of Khamat, and he pronounced judgment on him.
The king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Tzidkiyahu at Rivlah before his eyes, and the king of Babylon slaughtered all the nobles of Yehudah.
He put out the eyes of Tzidkiyahu and bound him in chains to take him to Babylon.
The Chaldeans burned the king's house and the house of the people, and broke down the walls of Yerushalayim.
Then Nevuzaradan, the captain of the guard, carried into exile to Babylon the rest of the people who were left in the city, those who had deserted to him, and the people who remained.
Nevuzaradan, the captain of the guard, left in the land of Yehudah some of the poor people who owned nothing, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time.
Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon gave command concerning Yirmeyahu through Nevuzaradan, the captain of the guard, saying,
Take him, look after him well, and do him no harm, but deal with him as he tells you.
So Nevuzaradan the captain of the guard, Nevu-Shasban the chief officer, Nergal-Sar-Etzer the chief officer, and all the chief officers of the king of Babylon sent
And took Yirmeyahu from the court of the guard. They entrusted him to Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam, son of Shafan, that he should take him home. So he lived among the people.
The word of YHWH came to Yirmeyahu while he was shut up in the court of the guard:

Go, and say to Eved-Melekh the Kushite, Thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Behold, I will fulfill my words against this city for harm and not for good, and they shall be accomplished before you on that day.
But I will deliver you on that day, declares YHWH, and you shall not be given into the hand of the men of whom you are afraid.
For I will surely save you, and you shall not fall by the sword, but you shall have your life as a prize of war, because you have put your trust in me, declares YHWH.

The word that came to Yirmeyahu from YHWH after Nevuzaradan the captain of the guard had let him go from Ramah, when he took him bound in chains along with all the captives of Yerushalayim and Yehudah who were being exiled to Babylon.
The captain of the guard took Yirmeyahu and said to him, YHWH your Creator pronounced this disaster against this place.
YHWH has brought it about, and has done as he said. Because you sinned against YHWH and did not obey his voice, this thing has come upon you.

Now behold, I release you today from the chains on your hands. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you well. But if it seems wrong to you to come with me to Babylon, remain here. See, the whole land is before you — go wherever you think it good and right to go.

If you remain, then return to Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam, son of Shafan, whom the king of Babylon appointed governor of the cities of Yehudah, and dwell with him among the people. Or go wherever you think it right to go. So the captain of the guard gave him an allowance of food and a present, and let him go.
Then Yirmeyahu went to Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam, at Mitzpah, and lived with him among the people who were left in the land.

When all the captains of the forces in the open country and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam governor in the land and had committed to him men, women, and children, those of the poorest of the land who had not been taken into exile to Babylon,

They went to Gedalyahu at Mitzpah — Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu, Yokhanan and Yonatan the sons of Kare'akh, Serayahu the son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Efai the Netofathite, and Yezanyahu the son of the Ma'akhathite, they and their men.

Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam, son of Shafan, swore to them and their men, saying, Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.

As for me, I will dwell at Mitzpah, to stand before the Chaldeans who will come to us. But as for you, gather wine and summer fruits and oil, and store them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have taken.

Likewise, when all the Yehudim who were in Moav and among the Ammonites and in Edom and in other lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Yehudah and had appointed over them Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam, son of Shafan,
Then all the Yehudim returned from all the places to which they had been driven and came to the land of Yehudah, to Gedalyahu at Mitzpah. And they gathered wine and summer fruits in great abundance.
Now Yokhanan the son of Kare'akh and all the leaders of the forces in the open country came to Gedalyahu at Mitzpah
And said to him, Do you know that Ba'alis the king of the Ammonites has sent Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu to take your life? But Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam would not believe them.

Then Yokhanan the son of Kare'akh spoke secretly to Gedalyahu at Mitzpah, saying, Please let me go and strike down Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu — no one will know it. Why should he take your life, so that all the Yehudim who are gathered around you would be scattered, and the remnant of Yehudah would perish?
But Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam said to Yokhanan the son of Kare'akh, You shall not do this thing, for you are speaking falsely of Yishma'el.

In the seventh month, Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu, son of Elishama, of the royal family, one of the chief officers of the king, came with ten men to Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam, at Mitzpah. As they ate bread together there at Mitzpah,

Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu and the ten men with him rose up and struck down Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam, son of Shafan, with the sword, and killed him, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor in the land.
Yishma'el also struck down all the Yehudim who were with Gedalyahu at Mitzpah, and the Chaldean soldiers who happened to be there.
On the day after the murder of Gedalyahu, before anyone knew of it,
Eighty men arrived from Shekhem and Shiloh and Samaria, with their beards shaved and their clothes torn, and their bodies gashed, bringing grain offerings and incense to present at the house of YHWH.
And Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu came out from Mitzpah to meet them, weeping as he came. As he met them, he said to them, Come in to Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam.
When they came into the city, Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu and the men with him slaughtered them and cast them into a cistern.

But there were ten men among them who said to Yishma'el, Do not put us to death, for we have stores of wheat, barley, oil, and honey hidden in the fields. So he refrained and did not put them to death with their companions.

Now the cistern into which Yishma'el had thrown all the bodies of the men whom he had struck down because of Gedalyahu was the large cistern that King Asa had made for defense against Baasha king of Yisra'EL. Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu filled it with the slain.

Then Yishma'el took captive all the rest of the people who were in Mitzpah, the king's daughters and all the people who were left at Mitzpah, whom Nevuzaradan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam. Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu took them captive and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.
But when Yokhanan the son of Kare'akh and all the leaders of the forces with him heard of all the evil that Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu had done,
They took all their men and went to fight against Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu. They came upon him at the great pool that is in Givon.
And when all the people who were with Yishma'el saw Yokhanan the son of Kare'akh and all the leaders of the forces with him, they were glad.
So all the people whom Yishma'el had taken captive from Mitzpah turned around and came back, and went to Yokhanan the son of Kare'akh.
But Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu escaped from Yokhanan with eight men, and went to the Ammonites.

Then Yokhanan the son of Kare'akh and all the leaders of the forces with him took all the remnant of the people whom Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu had taken captive from Mitzpah, after he had struck down Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam — soldiers, women, children, and eunuchs, whom Yokhanan brought back from Givon.
And they went and stayed at Gerut Kimham near Beit-Lekhem, intending to go to Egypt

Because of the Chaldeans. For they were afraid of them, because Yishma'el the son of Netanyahu had struck down Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor over the land.
Then all the commanders of the forces, and Yokhanan the son of Kare'akh and Yezanyahu the son of Hoshayahu, and all the people from the least to the greatest, came near
And said to Yirmeyahu the prophet, Let our plea for mercy come before you, and pray to YHWH your Creator for us, for all this remnant — for we are left with but a few, as your eyes see us —
That YHWH your Creator may tell us the way we should go, and the thing that we should do.

Yirmeyahu the prophet said to them, I have heard you. Behold, I will pray to YHWH your Creator according to your request, and whatever YHWH answers you I will tell you. I will keep nothing back from you.
Then they said to Yirmeyahu, May YHWH be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act according to all the word with which YHWH your Creator sends you to us.
Whether it is good or evil, we will obey the voice of YHWH our Creator to whom we are sending you, that it may be well with us when we obey the voice of YHWH our Creator.
At the end of ten days the word of YHWH came to Yirmeyahu.
Then he summoned Yokhanan the son of Kare'akh and all the commanders of the forces who were with him, and all the people from the least to the greatest.
And he said to them, Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, to whom you sent me to present your plea for mercy before him:
If you will remain in this land, then I will build you up and not pull you down, and I will plant you and not pluck you up. For I relent of the disaster that I did to you.
Do not fear the king of Babylon, of whom you are afraid. Do not fear him, declares YHWH, for I am with you, to save you and to deliver you from his hand.
I will grant you mercy, that he may have mercy on you and let you remain in your own land.
But if you say, We will not remain in this land, disobeying the voice of YHWH your Creator
And saying, No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we shall not see war or hear the sound of the trumpet or be hungry for bread, and we will dwell there,
Then hear the word of YHWH, O remnant of Yehudah. Thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: If you set your faces to enter Egypt and go to live there,
Then the sword that you fear shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine of which you are afraid shall follow close after you to Egypt, and there you shall die.

All the men who set their faces to go to Egypt to live there shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence. They shall have no remnant or survivor from the disaster that I will bring upon them.

For thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: As my anger and my wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, so my wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You shall become an execration, a horror, a curse, and a taunt. You shall see this place no more.
YHWH has said to you, O remnant of Yehudah, Do not go to Egypt. Know for a certainty that I have warned you this day
That you have gone astray at the cost of your lives. For you sent me to YHWH your Creator, saying, Pray for us to YHWH our Creator, and whatever YHWH our Creator says, tell us and we will do it.
And I have this day told you, but you have not obeyed the voice of YHWH your Creator in anything that he sent me to tell you.
Now therefore know for a certainty that you shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence in the place where you desire to go to live.
When Yirmeyahu finished speaking to all the people all these words of YHWH their Creator, with which YHWH their Creator had sent him to them,

Azaryahu the son of Hoshayahu and Yokhanan the son of Kare'akh and all the insolent men said to Yirmeyahu, You are telling a lie. YHWH our Creator did not send you to say, Do not go to Egypt to live there,
But Barukh the son of Neriyahu has set you against us, to deliver us into the hand of the Chaldeans, that they may kill us or take us into exile to Babylon.
So Yokhanan the son of Kare'akh and all the commanders of the forces and all the people did not obey the voice of YHWH, to remain in the land of Yehudah.

But Yokhanan the son of Kare'akh and all the commanders of the forces took all the remnant of Yehudah who had returned to live in the land of Yehudah from all the nations to which they had been driven —

Men, women, children, the king's daughters, and every person whom Nevuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with Gedalyahu the son of Akhikam, son of Shafan, and Yirmeyahu the prophet and Barukh the son of Neriyahu —
And they came into the land of Egypt, for they did not obey the voice of YHWH. And they arrived at Takhpanes.
Then the word of YHWH came to Yirmeyahu in Takhpanes:
Take in your hands large stones and hide them in the mortar in the pavement that is at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace in Takhpanes, in the sight of the men of Yehudah,

And say to them, Thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Behold, I will send and take Nevukhadnetzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and I will set his throne above these stones that I have hidden, and he will spread his royal canopy over them.

He shall come and strike the land of Egypt, giving over to pestilence those who are doomed to pestilence, to captivity those who are doomed to captivity, and to the sword those who are doomed to the sword.

He shall kindle a fire in the temples of the gods of Egypt, and he shall burn them and carry them away captive. And he shall clean the land of Egypt as a shepherd cleans his cloak of vermin, and he shall go away from there in peace.
He shall break the obelisks of Heliopolis, which is in the land of Egypt, and the temples of the gods of Egypt he shall burn with fire.
The word that came to Yirmeyahu concerning all the Yehudim who lived in the land of Egypt, at Migdol, at Takhpanes, at Nof, and in the land of Patros:

Thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: You have seen all the disaster that I brought upon Yerushalayim and upon all the cities of Yehudah. Behold, this day they are a desolation, and no one dwells in them,
Because of the evil that they committed, provoking me to anger, in that they went to make offerings and serve other gods that they knew not, neither they, nor you, nor your fathers.
Yet I persistently sent to you all my servants the prophets, saying, Oh, do not do this abomination that I hate.
But they did not listen or incline their ear, to turn from their evil and make no offerings to other gods.
Therefore my wrath and my anger were poured out and kindled in the cities of Yehudah and in the streets of Yerushalayim, and they became a waste and a desolation, as at this day.

And now thus says YHWH, the Creator of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Why do you commit this great evil against yourselves, to cut off from you man and woman, infant and child, from the midst of Yehudah, leaving you no remnant?

You provoke me to anger with the works of your hands, making offerings to other gods in the land of Egypt where you have come to live, so that you may be cut off and become a curse and a taunt among all the nations of the earth.

Have you forgotten the evil of your fathers, the evil of the kings of Yehudah, the evil of their wives, your own evil, and the evil of your wives, which they committed in the land of Yehudah and in the streets of Yerushalayim?
They have not humbled themselves even to this day, nor have they feared, nor walked in my Torah and my statutes that I set before you and before your fathers.
Therefore thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Behold, I will set my face against you for harm, to cut off all Yehudah.

I will take the remnant of Yehudah who have set their faces to come to the land of Egypt to live, and they shall all be consumed. In the land of Egypt they shall fall. By the sword and by famine they shall be consumed, from the least to the greatest. They shall die by the sword and by famine, and they shall become an oath, a horror, a curse, and a taunt.
I will punish those who dwell in the land of Egypt, as I have punished Yerushalayim, with the sword, with famine, and with pestilence,

So that none of the remnant of Yehudah who have come to live in the land of Egypt shall escape or survive or return to the land of Yehudah, to which they lift up their hearts to return to dwell there. For they shall not return, except some fugitives.

Then all the men who knew that their wives had made offerings to other gods, and all the women who stood by, a great assembly, all the people who lived in Patros in the land of Egypt, answered Yirmeyahu:
As for the word that you have spoken to us in the name of YHWH, we will not listen to you.

But we will do everything that we have vowed, make offerings to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, as we did, both we and our fathers, our kings and our officials, in the cities of Yehudah and in the streets of Yerushalayim. For then we had plenty of food, and prospered, and saw no disaster.
But since we left off making offerings to the queen of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been consumed by the sword and by famine.

And the women said, When we made offerings to the queen of heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, was it without our husbands' approval that we made cakes for her bearing her image and poured out drink offerings to her?
Then Yirmeyahu said to all the people, men and women, all the people who had answered him:

The offerings that you made in the cities of Yehudah and in the streets of Yerushalayim, you and your fathers, your kings and your officials, and the people of the land — did not YHWH remember them? Did it not come into his mind?
YHWH could no longer bear your evil deeds and the abominations that you committed. Therefore your land has become a desolation and a waste and a curse, without inhabitant, as it is this day.

It is because you made offerings and because you sinned against YHWH and did not obey the voice of YHWH or walk in his Torah and in his statutes and in his testimonies that this disaster has happened to you, as at this day.
Yirmeyahu said to all the people and all the women: Hear the word of YHWH, all you of Yehudah who are in the land of Egypt.

Thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: You and your wives have declared with your mouths, and have fulfilled it with your hands, saying, We will surely perform our vows that we have made, to make offerings to the queen of heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her. Then confirm your vows and perform your vows.

Therefore hear the word of YHWH, all you of Yehudah who dwell in the land of Egypt: Behold, I have sworn by my great name, says YHWH, that my name shall no more be invoked by the mouth of any man of Yehudah in all the land of Egypt, saying, As the Creator YHWH lives.
Behold, I am watching over them for harm and not for good, and all the men of Yehudah who are in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by the sword and by famine, until there is an end of them.

And those who escape the sword shall return from the land of Egypt to the land of Yehudah, few in number. And all the remnant of Yehudah, who came to the land of Egypt to live, shall know whose word will stand, mine or theirs.
This shall be the sign to you, declares YHWH, that I will punish you in this place, in order that you may know that my words will surely stand against you for harm:

Thus says YHWH, Behold, I will give Pharaoh Khofra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those who seek his life, as I gave Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah into the hand of Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon, who was his enemy and sought his life.

The word that Yirmeyahu the prophet spoke to Barukh the son of Neriyahu, when he wrote these words in a book at the dictation of Yirmeyahu, in the fourth year of Yeho'yakim the son of Yoshiyahu, king of Yehudah:
Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, to you, O Barukh:
You said, Woe is me, for YHWH has added sorrow to my pain. I am weary with my groaning, and I find no rest.
Thus shall you say to him: Thus says YHWH — Behold, what I have built I am breaking down, and what I have planted I am plucking up — that is, the whole land.

And do you seek great things for yourself? Seek them not, for behold, I am bringing disaster upon all flesh, declares YHWH. But I will give you your life as a prize of war in all places to which you may go.
The word of YHWH that came to Yirmeyahu the prophet concerning the nations.

Concerning Egypt: about the army of Pharaoh Nekho, king of Egypt, which was by the Euphrates River at Karkemish and which Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon defeated in the fourth year of Yeho'yakim the son of Yoshiyahu, king of Yehudah:
Prepare buckler and shield, and advance for battle.
Harness the horses — mount, O horsemen. Take your stations with your helmets, polish your spears, put on your armor.
Why have I seen it? They are dismayed and have turned backward. Their warriors are beaten down and have fled in haste. They look not back — terror on every side, declares YHWH.
The swift cannot flee away, nor the warrior escape. In the north by the river Euphrates they have stumbled and fallen.
Who is this, rising like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge?
Egypt rises like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge. He said, I will rise — I will cover the earth — I will destroy cities and their inhabitants.
Advance, O horses, and rage, O chariots. Let the warriors go out: men of Kush and Put who handle the shield, men of Lud, skilled in handling and bending the bow.

That day is the day of YHWH of hosts, a day of vengeance, to avenge himself on his foes. The sword shall devour and be sated and drink its fill of their blood. For YHWH of hosts holds a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.
Go up to Gil'ad, and take balm, O virgin daughter of Egypt. In vain you have used many medicines — there is no healing for you.
The nations have heard of your shame, and the earth is full of your cry. For warrior has stumbled against warrior — they have both fallen together.
The word that YHWH spoke to Yirmeyahu the prophet about the coming of Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:
Declare in Egypt, and proclaim in Migdol — proclaim in Nof and Takhpanes. Say: Stand ready and be prepared, for the sword shall devour around you.
Why are your mighty ones face down? They do not stand because YHWH thrust them down.
He made many stumble, and they fell, and they said one to another: Arise, and let us go back to our own people and to the land of our birth, because of the sword of the oppressor.
Call the name of Pharaoh, king of Egypt: Noisy one who lets the hour go by.
As I live, declares the King, whose name is YHWH of hosts, like Tabor among the mountains and like Karmel by the sea, shall one come.
Prepare yourselves baggage for exile, O inhabitants of Egypt. For Nof shall become a waste and desolate, without inhabitant.
Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a biting fly from the north has come upon her.

Even her hired soldiers in her midst are like fattened calves. They too have turned and fled together — they did not stand, for the day of their calamity has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
Her sound is like a fleeing serpent, for her enemies march in force and come against her with axes, like those who fell trees.
They shall cut down her forest, declares YHWH, though it is impenetrable, because they are more numerous than locusts — they are without number.
The daughter of Egypt shall be put to shame. She shall be delivered into the hand of a people from the north.
YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL, said: Behold, I am bringing punishment upon Amon of No, and Pharaoh and Egypt and her gods and her kings, upon Pharaoh and those who trust in him.

I will deliver them into the hand of those who seek their lives, into the hand of Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon and his officers. Afterward Egypt shall be inhabited as in the days of old, declares YHWH.

But fear not, O Yaakov my servant, nor be dismayed, O Yisra'EL. For behold, I will save you from far away, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Yaakov shall return and have quiet and ease, and none shall make him afraid.

Fear not, O Yaakov my servant, declares YHWH, for I am with you. I will make a full end of all the nations to which I have driven you, but of you I will not make a full end. I will discipline you in just measure, and I will by no means leave you unpunished.
The word of YHWH that came to Yirmeyahu the prophet concerning the Pelishtim, before Pharaoh struck down Aza.

Thus says YHWH: Behold, waters are rising out of the north, and shall become an overflowing torrent. They shall overflow the land and all that fills it, the city and those who dwell in it. People shall cry out, and every inhabitant of the land shall wail.
At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his stallions, at the rushing of his chariots, at the rumbling of their wheels, the fathers look not back to their children, so feeble are their hands,

Because of the day that is coming to destroy all the Pelishtim, to cut off from Tzor and Tzidon every helper that remains. For YHWH is destroying the Pelishtim, the remnant of the coastland of Kaftor.
Baldness has come upon Aza — Ashkelon has perished. O remnant of their valley, how long will you gash yourselves?
Ah, sword of YHWH, how long till you are quiet? Put yourself into your scabbard — rest and be still.
How can it be quiet when YHWH has given it a charge? Against Ashkelon and against the seashore he has appointed it.
Concerning Moav. Thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Woe to Nebo, for it is laid waste. Kiriyatayim is put to shame, it is taken. The fortress is put to shame and broken down.
The renown of Moav is no more. In Heshbon they planned disaster against her: Come, let us cut her off from being a nation. You also, O Madmen, shall be brought to silence. The sword shall pursue you.
A voice — a cry from Horonayim, desolation and great destruction.
Moav is destroyed. Her little ones have made a cry.
For at the ascent of Luhit they go up weeping. For at the descent of Horonayim they have heard the distressed cry of destruction.
Flee. Save yourselves. You shall be like a juniper in the desert.
For because you trusted in your works and your treasures, you also shall be taken. And Kemosh shall go into exile with his priests and his officials.
The destroyer shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape. The valley shall perish, and the plain shall be destroyed, as YHWH has spoken.
Give wings to Moav, for she would fly away. Her cities shall become a desolation, with no inhabitant in them.
Cursed is he who does the work of YHWH with slackness, and cursed is he who keeps back his sword from bloodshed.

Moav has been at ease from his youth and has settled on his dregs. He has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, nor has he gone into exile. So his taste remains in him, and his scent is not changed.
Therefore, behold, the days are coming, declares YHWH, when I shall send to him pourers who will pour him, and empty his vessels and break his jars in pieces.
Then Moav shall be ashamed of Kemosh, as the house of Yisra'EL was ashamed of Beit-El, their confidence.
How do you say, We are heroes and mighty men of war?
The destroyer of Moav and his cities has come up, and the choicest of his young men have gone down to slaughter, declares the King, whose name is YHWH of hosts.
The calamity of Moav is near at hand, and his affliction hastens swiftly.
Grieve for him, all you who are around him, and all who know his name. Say, How the mighty scepter is broken, the glorious staff.
Come down from your glory, and sit on the parched ground, O inhabitant of Dibon. For the destroyer of Moav has come up against you. He has destroyed your strongholds.
Stand by the way and watch, O inhabitant of Aro'er. Ask him who flees and her who escapes. Say: What has happened?
Moav is put to shame, for it is broken. Wail and cry. Tell it by the Arnon, that Moav is laid waste.
Judgment has come upon the tableland, upon Holon, and Yahtzah, and Meifaat,
And Divon, and Nebo, and Beit-Divlatayim,
And Kiryatayim, and Beit-Gamul, and Beit-Me'on,
And Keriyot, and Botzrah, and all the cities of the land of Moav, far and near.
The horn of Moav is cut off, and his arm is broken, declares YHWH.
Make him drunk, because he magnified himself against YHWH, so that Moav shall wallow in his vomit, and he too shall be held in derision.
Was not Yisra'EL a derision to you? Was he found among thieves, that whenever you spoke of him you wagged your head?
Leave the cities and dwell in the rock, O inhabitants of Moav. Be like the dove that nests in the sides of the mouth of a gorge.
We have heard of the pride of Moav — he is very proud — of his loftiness, his pride, and his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart.
I know his insolence, declares YHWH. His boasts are false — his deeds are false.
Therefore I wail for Moav. I cry out for all Moav. For the men of Kir-Heres I mourn.
More than for Yazer I weep for you, O vine of Sivmah. Your branches passed over the sea — they reached to the sea of Yazer. On your summer fruits and your grape harvest the destroyer has fallen.
Gladness and joy have been taken away from the fruitful land of Moav. I have made the wine cease from the winepresses — no one treads them with shouts of joy. The shouting is not the shout of joy.
From the cry of Heshbon to El'aleh, as far as Yahatz they utter their voice, from Tzo'ar to Horonayim and Eglat-Shelishiyah. For the waters of Nimrim also have become desolate.
And I will bring to an end in Moav, declares YHWH, him who offers sacrifice at the high place and makes offerings to his god.
Therefore my heart moans for Moav like flutes, and my heart moans like flutes for the men of Kir-Heres. Therefore the riches they gained have perished.
For every head is shaved and every beard cut off. On all the hands are gashes, and around the waist is sackcloth.
On all the housetops of Moav and in the squares there is nothing but lamentation, for I have broken Moav like a vessel for which no one cares, declares YHWH.
How it is broken. How they wail. How Moav has turned his back in shame. So Moav has become a derision and a horror to all that are around him.
For thus says YHWH: Behold, one shall fly swiftly like an eagle and spread his wings against Moav.
The cities shall be taken and the strongholds seized. The heart of the warriors of Moav shall be in that day like the heart of a woman in her birth pains.
Moav shall be destroyed and be no longer a people, because he magnified himself against YHWH.
Terror, pit, and snare are before you, O inhabitant of Moav, declares YHWH.

He who flees from the terror shall fall into the pit, and he who climbs out of the pit shall be caught in the snare. For I will bring these things upon Moav, the year of their punishment, declares YHWH.

In the shadow of Heshbon fugitives stop without strength, for fire came out from Heshbon, flame from the house of Sikhon. It has destroyed the forehead of Moav and the crown of the head of the sons of tumult.
Woe to you, O Moav. The people of Kemosh are undone, for your sons have been taken captive and your daughters into captivity.
Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moav in the latter days, declares YHWH. Thus far is the judgment on Moav.
Concerning the Ammonites. Thus says YHWH: Has Yisra'EL no sons? Has he no heir? Why then has Malkam dispossessed Gad, and his people settled in its cities?

Therefore, behold, the days are coming, declares YHWH, when I will cause the battle cry to be heard against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It shall become a desolate mound, and its villages shall be burned with fire. Then Yisra'EL shall dispossess those who dispossessed him, says YHWH.

Wail, O Heshbon, for Ai is laid waste. Cry out, O daughters of Rabbah. Put on sackcloth, lament, and run to and fro among the hedges, for Malkam shall go into exile, with his priests and his officials.
Why do you boast in your valleys, O faithless daughter, who trusted in her treasures, saying, Who will come against me?
Behold, I will bring terror upon you, declares YHWH of hosts, from all who are around you, and you shall be driven out, every man straight before him, with none to gather the fugitives.
But afterward I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites, declares YHWH.
Concerning Edom. Thus says YHWH of hosts: Is wisdom no more in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom vanished?
Flee, turn back, dwell in the depths, O inhabitants of Dedan. For I will bring the calamity of Esav upon him, the time when I punish him.
If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings? If thieves came by night, would they not destroy only enough for themselves?
But I have stripped Esav bare. I have uncovered his hiding places, and he is not able to conceal himself. His children are destroyed, and his brothers, and his neighbors. And he is no more.
Leave your fatherless children. I will keep them alive. And let your widows trust in me.
For thus says YHWH: If those who did not deserve to drink the cup must drink it, will you go unpunished? You shall not go unpunished, but you must drink.
For I have sworn by myself, declares YHWH, that Botzrah shall become a horror, a taunt, a waste, and a curse, and all her cities shall be perpetual wastes.
I have heard a message from YHWH, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: Gather yourselves together and come against her, and rise up for battle.
For behold, I will make you small among the nations, despised among mankind.

The horror you inspire has deceived you, and the pride of your heart, you who live in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill. Though you make your nest as high as the eagle's, I will bring you down from there, declares YHWH.
Edom shall become a horror. Everyone who passes by it will be horrified and will hiss because of all its wounds.
As when Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighboring cities were overthrown, says YHWH, no man shall dwell there, no man shall sojourn in her.

Behold, like a lion coming up from the jungle of the Yarden against a perennial pasture, I will suddenly make him run away from her. And I will appoint over her whomever I choose. For who is like me? Who will summon me? What shepherd can stand before me?

Therefore hear the plan that YHWH has made against Edom and the purposes that he has formed against the inhabitants of Teman: Even the little ones of the flock shall be dragged away. Surely their fold shall be appalled at their fate.
At the sound of their fall the earth shall tremble. The sound of their cry shall be heard at the Sea of Reeds.
Behold, one shall mount up and fly swiftly like an eagle and spread his wings against Botzrah, and the heart of the warriors of Edom shall be in that day like the heart of a woman in her birth pains.
Concerning Damascus: Hamat and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard bad news. They melt in fear. There is anguish on the sea — it cannot be quiet.
Damascus has become feeble. She turned to flee, and panic seized her. Anguish and sorrows have taken hold of her, as of a woman in labor.
How is the famous city not forsaken, the city of my joy?
Therefore her young men shall fall in her squares, and all her soldiers shall be destroyed in that day, declares YHWH of hosts.
And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it shall devour the strongholds of Ben-Hadad.
Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hatzor that Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon struck down. Thus says YHWH: Rise up, advance against Kedar. Destroy the people of the east.
Their tents and their flocks shall be taken, their curtains and all their goods. Their camels shall be led away from them, and men shall cry to them: Terror on every side.
Flee, wander far away, dwell in the depths, O inhabitants of Hatzor, declares YHWH. For Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon has made a plan against you and formed a purpose against you.
Rise up, advance against a nation at ease, that dwells securely, declares YHWH, that has no gates or bars, that dwells alone.

Their camels shall become plunder, their herds of livestock a spoil. I will scatter to every wind those who cut the corners of their hair, and I will bring their calamity from every side of them, declares YHWH.
Hatzor shall become a haunt of jackals, an everlasting waste. No man shall dwell there. No man shall sojourn in her.
The word of YHWH that came to Yirmeyahu the prophet concerning Eilam, in the beginning of the reign of Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah:
Thus says YHWH of hosts: Behold, I will break the bow of Eilam, the mainstay of their might.

And I will bring upon Eilam the four winds from the four quarters of heaven. And I will scatter them to all those winds, and there shall be no nation to which those driven out of Eilam shall not come.

I will terrify Eilam before their enemies and before those who seek their life. I will bring disaster upon them, my fierce anger, declares YHWH. I will send the sword after them, until I have consumed them.
And I will set my throne in Eilam and destroy their king and officials, declares YHWH.
But in the latter days I will restore the fortunes of Eilam, declares YHWH.
The word that YHWH spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by Yirmeyahu the prophet:

Declare among the nations and proclaim, set up a banner and proclaim, conceal it not, and say: Babylon is taken, Bel is put to shame, Merodach is dismayed. Her images are put to shame, her idols are dismayed.
For out of the north a nation has come up against her, which shall make her land a desolation, and none shall dwell in it. Both man and beast shall flee away.
In those days and in that time, declares YHWH, the people of Yisra'EL and the people of Yehudah shall come together, weeping as they come, and they shall seek YHWH their Creator.
They shall ask the way to Tziyon, with faces turned toward it, saying, Come, let us join ourselves to YHWH in an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten.
My people have been lost sheep. Their shepherds have led them astray, turning them away on the mountains. From mountain to hill they have gone. They have forgotten their fold.
All who found them have devoured them, and their enemies have said, We are not guilty, for they have sinned against YHWH, their true habitation, YHWH, the hope of their fathers.
Flee from the midst of Babylon, and go out of the land of the Chaldeans, and be as male goats before the flock.

For behold, I am stirring up and bringing against Babylon a gathering of great nations, from the north country. And they shall array themselves against her. From there she shall be taken. Their arrows are like a skilled warrior who does not return empty-handed.
Chaldea shall be plundered. All who plunder her shall be sated, declares YHWH.
Though you rejoice, though you exult, O plunderers of my heritage, though you frolic like a heifer in the grass and neigh like stallions,
Your mother shall be utterly shamed, and she who bore you shall be disgraced. Behold, she shall be the last of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.
Because of the wrath of YHWH she shall not be inhabited but shall be an utter desolation. Everyone who passes by Babylon shall be appalled, and hiss because of all her wounds.
Set yourselves in array against Babylon all around, all you who bend the bow. Shoot at her, spare no arrows, for she has sinned against YHWH.
Raise a shout against her all around. She has surrendered. Her bulwarks have fallen. Her walls are thrown down. For this is the vengeance of YHWH: take vengeance on her. Do to her as she has done.

Cut off from Babylon the sower, and the one who handles the sickle in time of harvest. Because of the sword of the oppressor, every one shall turn to his own people, and every one shall flee to his own land.
Yisra'EL is a hunted sheep driven away by lions. First the king of Assyria devoured him, and now at last Nevukhadnetzar king of Babylon has gnawed his bones.
Therefore, thus says YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL: Behold, I am bringing punishment on the king of Babylon and his land, as I punished the king of Assyria.
I will restore Yisra'EL to his pasture, and he shall feed on Karmel and in Bashan, and his desire shall be satisfied on the hills of Efrayim and in Gil'ad.

In those days and in that time, declares YHWH, iniquity shall be sought in Yisra'EL, and there shall be none. And sin in Yehudah, and none shall be found, for I will pardon those whom I leave as a remnant.
Go up against the land of Meratayim, and against the inhabitants of Pekod. Kill, and devote them to destruction, declares YHWH, and do all that I have commanded you.
The noise of battle is in the land, and great destruction.
How the hammer of the whole earth is cut down and broken. How Babylon has become a horror among the nations.
I set a snare for you and you were taken, O Babylon, and you did not know it. You were found and caught, because you opposed YHWH.
YHWH has opened his armory and brought out the weapons of his wrath, for YHWH of hosts has a work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come against her from every quarter. Open her granaries. Pile her up like heaps of grain, and devote her to destruction. Let nothing be left of her.
Kill all her bulls. Let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their punishment.
A voice. Fugitives and refugees from the land of Babylon, declaring in Tziyon the vengeance of YHWH our Creator, vengeance for his temple.

Summon archers against Babylon, all those who bend the bow. Encamp around her. Let no one escape. Repay her according to her deeds. Do to her according to all that she has done. For she has proudly defied YHWH, the Holy One of Yisra'EL.
Therefore her young men shall fall in her squares, and all her soldiers shall be destroyed on that day, declares YHWH.
Behold, I am against you, O proud one, declares YHWH of hosts, for your day has come, the time when I will punish you.
The proud one shall stumble and fall, with none to raise him up. And I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it will devour all that is around him.
Thus says YHWH of hosts: The people of Yisra'EL are oppressed, and the people of Yehudah with them. All who took them captive have held them fast. They refuse to let them go.
Their Redeemer is strong — YHWH of hosts is his name. He will surely plead their cause, that he may give rest to the earth, but unrest to the inhabitants of Babylon.
A sword against the Chaldeans, declares YHWH, and against the inhabitants of Babylon, and against her officials and her wise men.
A sword against the diviners, that they may become fools. A sword against her warriors, that they may be destroyed.
A sword against her horses and against her chariots, and against all the foreign troops in her midst, that they may become women. A sword against all her treasures, that they may be plundered.
A drought against her waters, that they may be dried up. For it is a land of images, and they are mad over idols.
Therefore wild beasts shall dwell with hyenas in Babylon, and ostriches shall dwell in her. She shall never again have people, nor be inhabited for all generations.
As when Creator overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighboring cities, declares YHWH, so no man shall dwell there, and no son of man shall sojourn in her.
Behold, a people comes from the north. A great nation and many kings are stirring from the farthest parts of the earth.

They lay hold of bow and spear. They are cruel and have no mercy. The sound of them is like the roaring of the sea. They ride on horses, arrayed as a man for battle against you, O daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon heard the report of them, and his hands fell helpless. Anguish seized him, pain as of a woman in labor.

Behold, like a lion coming up from the thicket of the Yarden against a perennial pasture, I will suddenly make them run away from her, and I will appoint over her whomever I choose. For who is like me? Who will summon me? What shepherd can stand before me?

Therefore hear the plan that YHWH has made against Babylon, and the purposes that he has formed against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely the little ones of their flock shall be dragged away. Surely their fold shall be appalled at their fate.
At the sound of the capture of Babylon the earth shall tremble, and her cry shall be heard among the nations.
Thus says YHWH: Behold, I will stir up the spirit of a destroyer against Babylon, against the inhabitants of Lev-Kamai.
And I will send to Babylon winnowers who shall winnow her, and they shall empty her land, when they come against her from every side on the day of trouble.
