So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Yisra'EL lived in their towns. And when the seventh month had come, the people of Yisra'EL were in their towns.
And all the people gathered as one man into the square before the Water Gate. And they told Ezra the scribe to bring the Book of the Torah of Mosheh that YHWH had commanded Yisra'EL.
So Ezra the priest brought the Torah before the assembly, both men and women and all who could understand what they heard, on the first day of the seventh month.

And he read from it facing the square before the Water Gate from early morning until midday, in the presence of the men and the women and those who could understand. And the ears of all the people were attentive to the Book of the Torah.

And Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform that they had made for the purpose. And beside him stood Mattityahu, Shema, Anayahu, Uriyahu, Hilkiyahu, and Ma'aseiyahu on his right hand, and Pedayahu, Misha'el, Malkiyahu, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zekhariyahu, and Meshullam on his left hand.
And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people, for he was above all the people, and as he opened it all the people stood.
And Ezra blessed YHWH, the great Creator, and all the people answered, Amen, Amen, lifting up their hands. And they bowed their heads and worshiped YHWH with their faces to the ground.

Also Yeshua, Bani, Sherevyahu, Yamin, Akkuv, Shabbetai, Hodiyahu, Ma'aseiyahu, Kelita, Azaryahu, Yozavad, Hanan, Pelayahu, the Levites, helped the people to understand the Torah, while the people remained in their places.
They read from the book, from the Torah of Creator, clearly, and they gave the sense, so that the people understood the reading.

And Nekhemyah, who was the governor, and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people said to all the people, This day is holy to YHWH your Creator. Do not mourn or weep. For all the people wept as they heard the words of the Torah.

Then he said to them, Go your way. Eat the fat and drink sweet wine and send portions to anyone who has nothing ready, for this day is holy to our Creator. And do not be grieved, for the joy of YHWH is your strength.
So the Levites calmed all the people, saying, Be quiet, for this day is holy. Do not be grieved.
And all the people went their way to eat and drink and to send portions and to make great rejoicing, because they had understood the words that were declared to them.
On the second day the heads of fathers' houses of all the people, with the priests and the Levites, came together to Ezra the scribe in order to study the words of the Torah.
And they found it written in the Torah that YHWH had commanded by Mosheh that the people of Yisra'EL should dwell in booths during the feast of the seventh month,

And that they should proclaim it and publish it in all their towns and in Yerushalayim, Go out to the hills and bring branches of olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm, and other leafy trees to make booths, as it is written.

So the people went out and brought them and made booths for themselves, each on his roof, and in their courts and in the courts of the house of Creator, and in the square at the Water Gate and in the square at the Gate of Efrayim.

And all the assembly of those who had returned from the captivity made booths and lived in the booths, for from the days of Yeshua the son of Nun to that day the people of Yisra'EL had not done so. And there was very great rejoicing.

And day by day, from the first day to the last day, he read from the Book of the Torah of Creator. They kept the feast seven days, and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly, according to the rule.
Now on the twenty-fourth day of this month the people of Yisra'EL were assembled with fasting and in sackcloth, and with earth on their heads.
And the Israelites separated themselves from all foreigners and stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
And they stood up in their place and read from the Book of the Torah of YHWH their Creator for a quarter of the day. For another quarter of it they made confession and worshiped YHWH their Creator.
On the stairs of the Levites stood Yeshua, Bani, Kadmi'el, Shevanyahu, Bunni, Sherevyahu, Bani, and Kenani, and they cried with a loud voice to YHWH their Creator.

Then the Levites, Yeshua, Kadmi'el, Bani, Hashabneyahu, Sherevyahu, Hodiyahu, Shevanyahu, and Petakhyahu, said, Stand up and bless YHWH your Creator from everlasting to everlasting. Blessed be your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise.

You are YHWH, you alone. You have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them, and you preserve all of them, and the host of heaven worships you.
You are YHWH, the Creator who chose Avram and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and gave him the name Avraham.

You found his heart faithful before you, and made with him the covenant to give to his offspring the land of the Kena'ani, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Yevusite, and the Girgashite. And you have kept your promise, for you are righteous.
And you saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt and heard their cry at the Sea of Reeds,

And performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh and all his servants and all the people of his land, for you knew that they acted arrogantly against our fathers. And you made a name for yourself, as it is to this day.
And you divided the sea before them, so that they went through the midst of the sea on dry land, and you cast their pursuers into the depths, as a stone into mighty waters.
By a pillar of cloud you led them in the day, and by a pillar of fire in the night to light for them the way in which they should go.
You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven and gave them right rules and true laws, good statutes and commandments.
And you made known to them your holy Shabbat and commanded them commandments and statutes and a law by Mosheh your servant.
You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger and brought water for them out of the rock for their thirst, and you told them to go in to possess the land that you had sworn to give them.
But they and our fathers acted presumptuously and stiffened their neck and did not obey your commandments.

They refused to obey and were not mindful of the wonders that you performed among them, but they stiffened their neck and appointed a leader to return to their slavery in Egypt. But you are a Creator ready to forgive, gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and did not forsake them.
Even when they had made for themselves a golden calf and said, This is your Creator who brought you up out of Egypt, and had committed great blasphemies,

You in your great mercies did not forsake them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud to lead them in the way did not depart from them by day, nor the pillar of fire by night to light for them the way in which they should go.
You gave your good Spirit to instruct them and did not withhold your manna from their mouth and gave them water for their thirst.
Forty years you sustained them in the wilderness, and they lacked nothing. Their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell.
And you gave them kingdoms and peoples and allotted to them every corner. So they took possession of the land of Sikhon king of Heshbon and the land of Og king of Bashan.
You multiplied their children as the stars of heaven, and you brought them into the land that you had told their fathers to enter and possess.

So the descendants went in and possessed the land, and you subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, the Kena'anim, and gave them into their hand, with their kings and the peoples of the land, that they might do with them as they would.

And they captured fortified cities and a rich land, and took possession of houses full of all good things, cisterns already hewn, vineyards, olive orchards, and fruit trees in abundance. So they ate and were filled and became fat and delighted themselves in your great goodness.

Nevertheless, they were disobedient and rebelled against you and cast your Torah behind their back and killed your prophets, who had warned them in order to turn them back to you, and they committed great blasphemies.

Therefore you gave them into the hand of their enemies, who made them suffer. And in the time of their suffering they cried out to you and you heard them from heaven, and according to your great mercies you gave them saviors who saved them from the hand of their enemies.

But after they had rest they did evil again before you, and you abandoned them to the hand of their enemies, so that they had dominion over them. Yet when they turned and cried to you, you heard from heaven, and many times you delivered them according to your mercies.

And you warned them in order to turn them back to your Torah. Yet they acted presumptuously and did not obey your commandments, but sinned against your rules, which if a person does them, he shall live by them, and they turned a stubborn shoulder and stiffened their neck and would not obey.
Many years you bore with them and warned them by your Spirit through your prophets. Yet they would not give ear. Therefore you gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
Nevertheless, in your great mercies you did not make an end of them or forsake them, for you are a gracious and merciful Creator.

Now, therefore, our Creator, the great, the mighty, and the awesome Creator, who keeps covenant and steadfast love, let not all the hardship seem little to you that has come upon us, upon our kings, our princes, our priests, our prophets, our fathers, and all your people, since the time of the kings of Assyria until this day.
Yet you have been just in all that has come upon us, for you have dealt faithfully and we have acted wickedly.
Our kings, our princes, our priests, and our fathers have not kept your Torah or paid attention to your commandments and your warnings that you gave them.
Even in their own kingdom, and amid your great goodness that you gave them, and in the large and rich land that you set before them, they did not serve you or turn from their wicked works.
Behold, we are slaves this day. In the land that you gave to our fathers to enjoy its fruit and its good gifts, behold, we are slaves.
And its rich yield goes to the kings whom you have set over us because of our sins. They rule over our bodies and over our livestock as they please, and we are in great distress.

Join with their brothers, their nobles, and enter into a curse and an oath to walk in Creator's Torah that was given by Mosheh the servant of Creator, and to observe and do all the commandments of YHWH our Creator and his rules and his statutes.
We will not give our daughters to the peoples of the land or take their daughters for our sons.

And if the peoples of the land bring in goods or any grain on the Shabbat day to sell, we will not buy from them on the Shabbat or on a holy day. And we will forego the crops of the seventh year and the exaction of every debt.
We also take on ourselves the obligation to give yearly a third part of a shekel for the service of the house of our Creator:

For the showbread, the regular grain offering, the regular burnt offering, the Shabbatot, the new moons, the appointed feasts, the holy things, and the sin offerings to make atonement for Yisra'EL, and for all the work of the house of our Creator.

We, the priests, the Levites, and the people, have likewise cast lots for the wood offering, to bring it into the house of our Creator, according to our fathers' houses, at times appointed, year by year, to burn on the altar of YHWH our Creator, as it is written in the Torah.
We obligate ourselves to bring the firstfruits of our ground and the firstfruits of all fruit of every tree, year by year, to the house of YHWH.

Also to bring to the house of our Creator, to the priests who minister in the house of our Creator, the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as it is written in the Torah, and the firstborn of our herds and of our flocks.

And to bring the first of our dough, and our contributions, the fruit of every tree, the wine and the oil, to the priests, to the chambers of the house of our Creator, and to bring to the Levites the tithes from our ground, for it is the Levites who collect the tithes in all our towns where we labor.

And the priest, the son of Aharon, shall be with the Levites when the Levites receive the tithes. And the Levites shall bring up the tithe of the tithes to the house of our Creator, to the chambers of the storehouse.

For the people of Yisra'EL and the sons of Levi shall bring the contribution of grain, wine, and oil to the chambers where the vessels of the sanctuary are, as well as the priests who minister, the gatekeepers and the singers. We will not neglect the house of our Creator.

Mattanyahu, Bakbukiyahu, Ovadyahu, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers standing guard at the storerooms of the gates.
These were in the days of Yoyakim the son of Yeshua, son of Yotzadak, and in the days of Nekhemyah the governor and of Ezra the priest and scribe.

And at the dedication of the wall of Yerushalayim they sought the Levites in all their places, to bring them to Yerushalayim to celebrate the dedication with gladness, with thanksgivings and with singing, with cymbals, harps, and lyres.
And the sons of the singers gathered together from the district surrounding Yerushalayim and from the villages of the Netofathites,
Also from Beit-Haggilgal and from the region of Geva and Azmaveth, for the singers had built villages for themselves around Yerushalayim.
And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gates and the wall.
Then I brought the leaders of Yehudah up onto the wall and appointed two great choirs that gave thanks. One went to the south on the wall to the Dung Gate.
And after them went Hoshayahu and half of the leaders of Yehudah,
And Azaryahu, Ezra, Meshullam,
Yehudah, Binyamin, Shemayahu, and Yirmeyahu,
And certain of the priests' sons with trumpets: Zekhariyahu the son of Yonatan, son of Shemayahu, son of Mattanyahu, son of Mikha'yahu, son of Zakkur, son of Asaf,
And his relatives, Shemayahu, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Ma'ai, Netane'el, Yehudah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of Dawid the man of Creator. And Ezra the scribe went before them.
And at the Fountain Gate they went straight up by the stairs of the city of Dawid, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of Dawid, to the Water Gate on the east.
The other choir of those who gave thanks went to the north, and I followed them with half of the people, on the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens, to the Broad Wall,

And above the Gate of Efrayim, and by the Gate of Yeshanah, and by the Fish Gate and the Tower of Hanan'el and the Tower of the Hundred, to the Sheep Gate. And they came to a halt at the Gate of the Guard.
So both choirs of those who gave thanks stood in the house of Creator, and I and half of the officials with me.
And the priests Elyakim, Ma'aseiyahu, Minyamin, Mikha'yahu, Ely o'enai, Zekhariyahu, and Hananyahu, with trumpets,
And Ma'aseiyahu, Shemayahu, El'azar, Uzzi, Yehohanan, Malkiyahu, Eilam, and Ezer. And the singers sang with Yizrakhyahu as their leader.
And they offered great sacrifices that day and rejoiced, for Creator had made them rejoice with great joy. The women and children also rejoiced. And the joy of Yerushalayim was heard far away.

On that day men were appointed over the storerooms, the contributions, the firstfruits, and the tithes, to gather into them the portions required by the Torah for the priests and for the Levites from the fields of the towns, for Yehudah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who ministered.
And they performed the service of their Creator and the service of purification, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of Dawid and his son Shelomoh.
For long ago in the days of Dawid and Asaf there were directors of the singers, and there were songs of praise and thanksgiving to Creator.

And all Yisra'EL in the days of Zerubbavel and in the days of Nekhemyah gave the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers. They also set apart that which was for the Levites, and the Levites set apart that which was for the sons of Aharon.
On that day they read from the Book of Mosheh in the hearing of the people. And in it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of Creator,
For they did not meet the people of Yisra'EL with bread and water, but hired Bil'am against them to curse them — yet our Creator turned the curse into a blessing.
As soon as the people heard the Torah, they separated from Yisra'EL all those of foreign descent.
Now before this, Elyashiv the priest, who was appointed over the chambers of the house of our Creator, and who was related to Toviyahu,

Had prepared for Toviyahu a large chamber where they had previously put the grain offering, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of grain, wine, and oil, which were given by commandment to the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests.
While all this was taking place, I was not in Yerushalayim, for in the thirty-second year of Artakhshasta king of Babylon I had gone to the king. And after some time I asked leave of the king
And came to Yerushalayim, and I then discovered the evil that Elyashiv had done for Toviyahu, in preparing for him a chamber in the courts of the house of Creator.
And I was very angry, and I threw all the household furniture of Toviyahu out of the chamber.
Then I gave orders, and they cleansed the chambers, and I brought back there the vessels of the house of Creator, with the grain offering and the frankincense.
I also found out that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them, so that the Levites and the singers, who did the work, had fled each to his field.
So I rebuked the officials and said, Why is the house of Creator forsaken? And I gathered them together and set them in their stations.
Then all Yehudah brought the tithe of the grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses.

And I appointed as treasurers over the storehouses Shelemyahu the priest, Tzadok the scribe, and Pedayahu of the Levites, and as their assistant Hanan the son of Zakkur, son of Mattanyahu, for they were considered reliable, and their duty was to distribute to their brothers.
Remember me, O my Creator, concerning this, and do not wipe out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my Creator and for his service.

In those days I saw in Yehudah people treading winepresses on the Shabbat, and bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of loads, which they brought into Yerushalayim on the Shabbat day. And I warned them on the day when they sold food.
Tyrians also, who lived in the city, brought in fish and all kinds of goods and sold them on the Shabbat to the people of Yehudah, in Yerushalayim itself.
Then I rebuked the nobles of Yehudah and said to them, What is this evil thing that you are doing, profaning the Shabbat day?
Did not your fathers act in this way, and did not our Creator bring all this disaster on us and on this city? Now you are bringing more wrath on Yisra'EL by profaning the Shabbat.

As soon as it began to grow dark at the gates of Yerushalayim before the Shabbat, I commanded that the doors should be shut and gave orders that they should not be opened until after the Shabbat. And I stationed some of my servants at the gates, so that no load might be brought in on the Shabbat day.
Then the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares spent the night outside Yerushalayim once or twice.
But I warned them and said to them, Why do you spend the night outside the wall? If you do so again, I will lay hands on you. From that time on they did not come on the Shabbat.

Then I commanded the Levites that they should purify themselves and come and guard the gates, to keep the Shabbat day holy. Remember this also in my favor, O my Creator, and spare me according to the greatness of your steadfast love.
In those days also I saw the Yehudim who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moav.
And half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and they could not speak the language of Yehudah, but only the language of each people.

And I contended with them and cursed them and beat some of them and pulled out their hair. And I made them take an oath in the name of Creator, saying, You shall not give your daughters to their sons, or take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.

Did not Shelomoh king of Yisra'EL sin on account of such women? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was beloved by his Creator, and Creator made him king over all Yisra'EL. Nevertheless, foreign women made even him to sin.
Shall we then listen to you and do all this great evil and act treacherously against our Creator by marrying foreign women?
And one of the sons of Yoyada, the son of Elyashiv the high priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite. Therefore I chased him from me.
Remember them, O my Creator, because they have desecrated the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.
Thus I cleansed them from everything foreign, and I established the duties of the priests and Levites, each in his work,
And I provided for the wood offering at appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my Creator, for good.
Adam, Shet, Enosh,
Kenan, Mahalal'el, Yered,
Khanokh, Metushelakh, Lamekh,
Noakh, Shem, Kham, and Yefet.
The sons of Yefet: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Yavan, Tuval, Meshekh, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Rifat, and Togarmah.
The sons of Yavan: Elisha, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
The sons of Kham: Kush, Mitzrayim, Put, and Kena'an.
The sons of Kush: Seva, Havilah, Savta, Ra'ma, and Savtekha. The sons of Ra'ma: Sheva and Dedan.
Kush fathered Nimrod. He was the first on earth to be a mighty man.
Mitzrayim fathered the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehavim, the Naftuhim,
The Patrusim, the Kasluhim — from whom the Pelishtim came — and the Kaftorim.
Kena'an fathered Tzidon his firstborn and Khet,
And the Yevusite, the Amorite, the Girgashite,
The Hivite, the Arkite, the Sinite,
The Arvadite, the Tzemarite, and the Khamathite.
The sons of Shem: Eilam, Assyria, Arpakhshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshekh.
Arpakhshad fathered Shelakh, and Shelakh fathered Ever.
To Ever were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg — for in his days the earth was divided — and his brother's name was Yoktan.
Yoktan fathered Almodad, Shelef, Hatzarmaveth, Yerakh,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Eval, Avima'el, Sheva,
Ofir, Havilah, and Yovav. All these were the sons of Yoktan.
Shem, Arpakhshad, Shelakh,
Ever, Peleg, Re'u,
Serug, Nakhor, Terakh,
Avram, that is Avraham.
The sons of Avraham: Yitzkhak and Yishma'el.
These are their genealogies: the firstborn of Yishma'el, Nevayot, then Kedar, Adve'el, Mivsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,
Yetur, Nafish, and Kedmah. These are the sons of Yishma'el.
The sons of Keturah, Avraham's concubine: she bore Zimran, Yokshan, Medan, Midyan, Yishbak, and Shuakh. The sons of Yokshan: Sheva and Dedan.
The sons of Midyan: Efah, Efer, Khanokh, Avida, and Elda'ah. All these were the sons of Keturah.
Avraham fathered Yitzkhak. The sons of Yitzkhak: Esav and Yisra'EL.
The sons of Esav: Elifaz, Re'uel, Ye'ush, Ya'lam, and Korakh.
The sons of Elifaz: Teman, Omar, Tzfei, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
The sons of Re'uel: Nakhat, Zerakh, Shammah, and Mizzah.
The sons of Se'ir: Lotan, Shoval, Tziv'on, Anah, Dishon, Etzer, and Dishan.
The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam. And Lotan's sister was Timna.
The sons of Shoval: Alyan, Manakhat, Eval, Shfei, and Onam. The sons of Tziv'on: Ayah and Anah.
The son of Anah: Dishon. The sons of Dishon: Hamran, Eshban, Yitran, and Keran.
The sons of Etzer: Bilhan, Za'avan, and Ya'akan. The sons of Dishan: Utz and Aran.
These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the people of Yisra'EL: Bela the son of Be'or, the name of his city being Dinhabah.
Bela died, and Yovav the son of Zerakh of Botzrah reigned in his place.
Yovav died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who defeated Midyan in the country of Moav, reigned in his place, the name of his city being Avit.
Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.
Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehovot on the Euphrates reigned in his place.
Shaul died, and Ba'al-Khanan the son of Akhbor reigned in his place.
Ba'al-Khanan died, and Hadad reigned in his place, the name of his city being Pa'i, and his wife's name Mehetavel the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mei-Zahav.
And Hadad died. The chiefs of Edom were: chief Timna, chief Alyah, chief Yetet,
Chief Oholivamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
Chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mivtzar,
Chief Magdi'el, and chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom.
These are the sons of Yisra'EL: Re'uven, Shim'on, Levi, Yehudah, Yissachar, Zevulun,
Dan, Yosef, Binyamin, Naftali, Gad, and Asher.
The sons of Yehudah: Er, Onan, and Shelah. These three were born to him by Bat-Shua the Kena'anite. And Er, Yehudah's firstborn, was evil in the sight of YHWH, and he put him to death.
And Tamar his daughter-in-law bore him Peretz and Zerakh. All the sons of Yehudah were five.
The sons of Peretz: Khetzron and Hamul.
The sons of Zerakh: Zimri, Eitan, Heman, Kalkol, and Dara, five in all.
The son of Karmi: Akhar, the troubler of Yisra'EL, who broke faith in the matter of the devoted thing.
The son of Eitan: Azaryahu.
The sons of Khetzron that were born to him: Yerakhmeel, Ram, and Keluvai.
Ram fathered Amminadav, and Amminadav fathered Nakhshon, prince of the sons of Yehudah.
Nakhshon fathered Salma, and Salma fathered Bo'az,
Bo'az fathered Oved, and Oved fathered Yishai.
Yishai fathered Eliav his firstborn, Avinadav the second, Shim'a the third,
Netanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
Otzzem the sixth, Dawid the seventh.
And their sisters were Tzeruyah and Avigayil. The sons of Tzeruyah: Avishai, Yo'av, and Asahel, three.
Avigayil bore Amasa, and the father of Amasa was Yeter the Yishma'elite.
Kalev the son of Khetzron fathered children by his wife Azuvah, and by Yeriot. And these were her sons: Yesher, Shovav, and Ardon.
When Azuvah died, Kalev married Efrat, who bore him Hur.
Hur fathered Uri, and Uri fathered Bezalel.
Afterward Khetzron went in to the daughter of Makhir the father of Gil'ad, whom he married when he was sixty years old, and she bore him Seguv.
And Seguv fathered Yair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gil'ad.
But Geshur and Aram took from them Havot-Yair, Kenat, and its villages — sixty towns. All these were the sons of Makhir the father of Gil'ad.
After the death of Khetzron, Kalev went in to Efratah, the wife of Khetzron his father, and she bore him Ashkhur, the father of Tekoa.
The sons of Yerakhmeel the firstborn of Khetzron: Ram, his firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Otzzem, and Akhiyah.
Yerakhmeel had another wife, whose name was Atarah. She was the mother of Onam.
The sons of Ram, the firstborn of Yerakhmeel: Ma'atz, Yamin, and Eker.
The sons of Onam: Shammai and Yada. The sons of Shammai: Nadav and Avishur.
The name of Avishur's wife was Avikha'il, and she bore him Akhvan and Molid.
The sons of Nadav: Seled and Apayim. And Seled died without children.
The son of Apayim: Yishi. The son of Yishi: Sheshan. The son of Sheshan: Akhlai.
The sons of Yada, Shammai's brother: Yeter and Yonatan. And Yeter died without children.
The sons of Yonatan: Pelet and Zaza. These were the sons of Yerakhmeel.
Now Sheshan had no sons, only daughters, but Sheshan had an Egyptian slave whose name was Yarkha.
So Sheshan gave his daughter in marriage to Yarkha his slave, and she bore him Attai.
Attai fathered Natan, and Natan fathered Zavad.
Zavad fathered Eflal, and Eflal fathered Oved.
Oved fathered Yehu, and Yehu fathered Azaryahu.
Azaryahu fathered Khaletz, and Khaletz fathered El'asah.
El'asah fathered Sismai, and Sismai fathered Shallum.
Shallum fathered Yekamiahu, and Yekamiahu fathered Elishama.
The sons of Kalev the brother of Yerakhmeel: Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Zif, and his son Mareshah the father of Khevron.
The sons of Khevron: Korakh, Tappuakh, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema fathered Rakham, the father of Yorke'am, and Rekem fathered Shammai.
The son of Shammai: Ma'on, and Ma'on was the father of Beit-Tzur.
Efah also, Kalev's concubine, bore Kharan, Moza, and Gazez. Kharan fathered Gazez.
The sons of Yahdai: Regem, Yotam, Geshan, Pelet, Efah, and Sha'af.
Ma'akha, Kalev's concubine, bore Shever and Tirkhana.
She also bore Sha'af the father of Madmannah, Sheva the father of Makhvena and the father of Givea. And the daughter of Kalev was Akhsah.
These were the descendants of Kalev. The sons of Hur the firstborn of Efratah: Shoval the father of Kiryat-Ye'arim,
Salma the father of Beit-Lekhem, and Kharef the father of Beit-Gader.
Shoval the father of Kiryat-Ye'arim had sons: Haro'eh, half of the Menukhotites.
And the clans of Kiryat-Ye'arim: the Yitrites, the Putites, the Shumatites, and the Mishraites. From these came the Tzorathites and the Eshtaolites.
The sons of Salma: Beit-Lekhem, the Netofathites, Atrot-Beit-Yo'av, and half of the Manakhtites, the Tzori'ites.
The clans also of the scribes who lived at Yavetz: the Tirathites, the Shim'athites, and the Sukathites. These are the Kenites who came from Khamat, the father of the house of Rekhav.
These are the sons of Dawid who were born to him in Khevron: the firstborn, Amnon, by Akhinoam the Yizre'elite; the second, Dani'el, by Avigayil the Karmelite;
The third, Avshalom, the son of Ma'akha the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth, Adoniyahu, the son of Haggit;
The fifth, Shefatyahu, by Avital; the sixth, Yitream, by his wife Eglah.
Six were born to him in Khevron, where he reigned for seven years and six months. And he reigned thirty-three years in Yerushalayim.
These were born to him in Yerushalayim: Shim'a, Shovav, Natan, and Shelomoh, four by Bat-Shu'a the daughter of Ammi'el.
And Yivkhar, Elishama, Elifelet,
Nogah, Nefeg, Yafia,
Elishama, Elyada, and Elifelet, nine.
All these were Dawid's sons, besides the sons of the concubines, and Tamar was their sister.
The son of Shelomoh: Rekhavam, Aviyah his son, Asa his son, Yehoshafat his son,
Yoram his son, Akhaziyahu his son, Yo'ash his son,
Amatziyahu his son, Azaryahu his son, Yotam his son,
Akhaz his son, Khizkiyahu his son, Menasheh his son,
Amon his son, Yoshiyahu his son.
The sons of Yoshiyahu: Yokhanan the firstborn, the second Yehoiakim, the third Tzidkiyahu, the fourth Shallum.
The descendants of Yehoiakim: Yekhonyahu his son, Tzidkiyahu his son.
The sons of Yekhonyahu, the captive: She'altiel his son,
Malkiram, Pedayahu, Shenazzar, Yekamyah, Hoshama, and Nedavyah.
The sons of Pedayahu: Zerubavel and Shim'i. The son of Zerubavel: Meshullam and Hananyahu, and Shelomit was their sister.
And Hashuvah, Ohel, Berekhyahu, Khasadyahu, and Yushav-Khesed, five.
The sons of Hananyahu: Pelatyahu and Yeshayahu, his son Refayahu, his son Arnan, his son Ovadyahu, his son Shekhanyahu.
The son of Shekhanyahu: Shemayahu. And the sons of Shemayahu: Khattush, Yig'al, Bariyakh, Ne'aryahu, and Shafat, six.
The son of Ne'aryahu: Elyoe'nai, Hizkiyahu, and Azrikam, three.
The sons of Elyoe'nai: Hodavyahu, Elyashiv, Pelatyahu, Akkuv, Yohanan, Delayahu, and Anani, seven.
The sons of Yehudah: Peretz, Khetzron, Karmi, Hur, and Shoval.
Reayah the son of Shoval fathered Yakhat, and Yakhat fathered Akhumai and Lahad. These were the clans of the Tzorathites.
These were the sons of Etam: Yizre'el, Yishma, and Yivdash, and the name of their sister was Hatzlelponi.
And Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah. These were the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Efratah, the father of Beit-Lekhem.
Ashkhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives, Khe'lah and Na'arah.
Na'arah bore him Akhuzzam, Khefer, Temeni, and Haashtari. These were the sons of Na'arah.
The sons of Khe'lah: Tzeret, Yitzhar, and Etnan.
Koz fathered Anuv, Hatzovevah, and the clans of Akharkhel the son of Harum.
Yavetz was more honorable than his brothers, and his mother called his name Yavetz, saying, Because I bore him in pain.

Yavetz called upon the Creator of Yisra'EL, saying, Oh that you would bless me and enlarge my border, and that your hand might be with me, and that you would keep me from harm so that it might not bring me pain. And Creator granted what he asked.
Kelub, the brother of Shukha, fathered Mehir, who was the father of Eshton.
Eshton fathered Beit-Rafa, Paseakh, and Tehinnah the father of Ir-Nakhash. These are the men of Rekhah.
The sons of Kenaz: Otni'el and Serayahu. The sons of Otni'el: Khatat and Me'onotai.
Me'onotai fathered Ofrah. Serayahu fathered Yo'av, the father of Ge-Kharashim, so called because they were craftsmen.
The sons of Kalev the son of Yefunneh: Iru, Elah, and Na'am. And the son of Elah: Kenaz.
The sons of Yehallelel: Zif, Zifah, Tirya, and Asarel.
The sons of Ezra: Yeter, Mered, Efer, and Yalon. She conceived and bore Miriam, Shammai, and Yishvakh the father of Eshtemoa.
And his Jewish wife bore Yered the father of Gedor, Khever the father of Sokho, and Yekuti'el the father of Zanoakh. These were the sons of Bitya the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered married.
The sons of the wife of Hodiyah, the sister of Nakham: the father of Ke'ilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Ma'akhathite.
The sons of Shim'on: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-Khanan, and Tilon. The sons of Yishi: Zokhet and Ben-Zokhet.
The sons of Shelah the son of Yehudah: Er the father of Lekha, and La'adah the father of Mareshah, and the clans of the house of the linen workers at Beit-Ashvea,
And Yokim, and the men of Kozeva, and Yo'ash, and Saraf, who ruled in Moav and returned to Lekhem — these are ancient records.
These were the potters and inhabitants of Neta'im and Gederah. They lived there in the king's service.
The sons of Shim'on: Nemuel, Yamin, Yariv, Zerakh, Shaul.
Shallum was his son, Mivsam his son, Mishma his son.
The sons of Mishma: Khammuel his son, Zakkur his son, Shim'i his son.
Shim'i had sixteen sons and six daughters. But his brothers did not have many children, nor did all their clan multiply like the people of Yehudah.
They lived in Be'er-Sheva, Moladah, Hatsar-Shu'al,
Bilhah, Etzem, Tolad,
Betu'el, Khormah, Ziklag,
Beit-Markavot, Hatsar-Susim, Beit-Bir'i, and Sha'arayim. These were their cities until Dawid became king.
And their villages were Etam, Ayin, Rimmon, Tokhen, and Ashan, five cities,
Along with all their villages that were around these cities as far as Ba'al. These were their settlements, and they kept a genealogical record.
And Meshobav, Yamlekh, Yoshah the son of Amatziyahu,
Yo'el, Yehu the son of Yoshivyahu, son of Serayahu, son of Asi'el,
Elyoe'nai, Ya'akova, Yeshokhayah, Asayahu, Adi'el, Yesimiel, Benayah,
Ziza the son of Shifi, son of Allon, son of Yedayah, son of Shimri, son of Shemayah —
These mentioned by name were princes in their clans, and their fathers' houses increased greatly.
They journeyed to the entrance of Gedor, to the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks.
Where they found rich, good pasture, and the land was very broad, quiet, and peaceful, for the former inhabitants there belonged to Kham.

These, registered by name, came in the days of Khizkiyahu king of Yehudah and attacked their tents and the Me'unites who were found there and destroyed them utterly to this day and settled in their place, because there was pasture there for their flocks.
And some of them, five hundred men of the Shim'onites, went to Mount Se'ir, having as their leaders Pelatyahu, Ne'aryahu, Refayahu, and Uzzi'el, the sons of Yishi.
And they defeated the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped, and they have lived there to this day.

The sons of Re'uven the firstborn of Yisra'EL. He was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Yosef the son of Yisra'EL, so that he is not enrolled in the genealogy according to the birthright.
Though Yehudah became strong among his brothers and a prince was from him, yet the birthright belonged to Yosef.
The sons of Re'uven the firstborn of Yisra'EL: Khanokh, Pallu, Khetzron, and Karmi.
The sons of Yo'el: Shemayah his son, Gog his son, Shim'i his son,
Mikha his son, Re'ayah his son, Ba'al his son,
Be'erah his son, whom Tilgat-Piln'eser king of Assyria carried away into exile. He was a chief of the Re'uvenites.
And his kinsmen by their clans, when the genealogy of their generations was recorded: the chief, Ye'i'el, and Zekhariah,
And Bela the son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Yo'el, who lived in Aro'er, as far as Nevo and Ba'al-Me'on.
He also lived to the east as far as the entrance of the desert this side of the Euphrates, because their livestock had multiplied in the land of Gil'ad.
And in the days of Sha'ul they waged war against the Hagarites, who fell into their hand. And they lived in their tents throughout all the region east of Gil'ad.
The sons of Gad lived over against them in the land of Bashan as far as Salkhah:
Yo'el the chief, Shafam the second, Yanai, and Shafat in Bashan.
And their kinsmen according to their fathers' houses: Mikha'el, Meshullam, Sheva, Yorai, Yakhan, Zia, and Ever, seven.
These were the sons of Avikha'il the son of Khuri, son of Yaro'akh, son of Gil'ad, son of Mikha'el, son of Yeshishai, son of Yakhdo, son of Buz.
Akhi the son of Avdi'el, son of Guni, was chief of their fathers' houses.
And they lived in Gil'ad, in Bashan and its villages, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon to their limits.
All of these were recorded in genealogies in the days of Yotam king of Yehudah and in the days of Yarov'am king of Yisra'EL.
The Re'uvenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Menasheh had valiant men who carried shield and sword, and drew the bow, expert in war, 44,760, able to go to war.
They waged war against the Hagarites, Yetur, Nafish, and Nodav.

And when they prevailed over them, the Hagarites and all who were with them were given into their hands, for they cried out to Creator in the battle, and he granted their urgent plea because they trusted in him.
They carried off their livestock: 50,000 of their camels, 250,000 sheep, 2,000 donkeys, and 100,000 men alive.
For many fell slain, because the war was from Creator. And they lived in their place until the exile.
The members of the half-tribe of Menasheh lived in the land. They were very numerous from Bashan to Ba'al-Hermon, Senir, and Mount Khermon.
These were the heads of their fathers' houses: Efer, Yishi, Eli'el, Azri'el, Yirmeyahu, Hodavyah, and Yakhdi'el, mighty warriors, famous men, heads of their fathers' houses.
But they broke faith with the Creator of their fathers and whored after the gods of the peoples of the land, whom Creator had destroyed before them.

So the Creator of Yisra'EL stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, the spirit of Tilgat-Pilneser king of Assyria, and he took them into exile, namely, the Re'uvenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Menasheh, and brought them to Halakh, Khavor, Hara, and the river Gozan, to this day.
The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Yitzhar, Khevron, and Uzzi'el.
The children of Amram: Aharon, Mosheh, and Miryam. The sons of Aharon: Nadav, Avihu, El'azar, and Itamar.
El'azar fathered Pinkhas, Pinkhas fathered Avishua,
Avishua fathered Bukki, Bukki fathered Uzzi,
Uzzi fathered Zerakhy ahu, Zerakhy ahu fathered Meraioth,
Meraioth fathered Amaryahu, Amaryahu fathered Akhituv,
Akhituv fathered Tzadok, Tzadok fathered Akhima'atz,
Akhima'atz fathered Azaryahu, Azaryahu fathered Yohanan,
Yohanan fathered Azaryahu — it was he who served as priest in the house that Shelomoh built in Yerushalayim.
Azaryahu fathered Amaryahu, Amaryahu fathered Akhituv,
Akhituv fathered Tzadok, Tzadok fathered Shallum,
Shallum fathered Khilkiyahu, Khilkiyahu fathered Azaryahu,
Azaryahu fathered Serayahu, Serayahu fathered Yehotzadak.
And Yehotzadak went into exile when YHWH sent Yehudah and Yerushalayim into exile by the hand of Nevukhadnetzar.
And these are the names of the sons of Gershom: Livni and Shim'i.
The sons of Merari: Makhli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites according to their fathers.
Of Gershom: Livni his son, Yakhat his son, Zimmah his son,
Yo'akh his son, Iddo his son, Zerakh his son, Yeat'rai his son.
The sons of Kohath: Amminadav his son, Korakh his son, Assir his son,
Elkanah his son, Evyasaf his son, Assir his son,
Takhat his son, Uriel his son, Uziyahu his son, and Sha'ul his son.
The sons of Elkanah: Amasai and Akhimot.
As for Elkanah, the sons of Elkanah: Tzofai his son, Nakhat his son,
Eliav his son, Yeroham his son, Elkanah his son.
The sons of Shemu'el: Yo'el his firstborn, the second Aviyah.
The sons of Merari: Makhli, Livni his son, Shim'i his son, Uzza his son,
Shim'a his son, Khaggiyah his son, Asayahu his son.
These are the men whom Dawid put in charge of the service of song in the house of YHWH after the ark rested there.
They ministered with song before the tabernacle of the tent of meeting until Shelomoh built the house of YHWH in Yerushalayim, and they performed their service according to their order.
These are the men who served, and their sons. Of the sons of the Kohathites: Heman the singer, the son of Yo'el, son of Shemu'el,
Son of Elkanah, son of Yeroham, son of Eli'el, son of Toakh,
Son of Tzuf, son of Elkanah, son of Makhat, son of Amasai,
Son of Elkanah, son of Yo'el, son of Azaryahu, son of Tzefanyahu,
Son of Takhat, son of Assir, son of Evyasaf, son of Korakh,
Son of Yitzhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Yisra'EL.
And his brother Asaf, who stood on his right hand, namely Asaf the son of Berekhyahu, son of Shim'a,
Son of Mikha'el, son of Ba'aseiyahu, son of Malkiyahu,
Son of Etni, son of Zerakh, son of Adayahu,
Son of Eitan, son of Zimmah, son of Shim'i,
Son of Yakhat, son of Gershom, son of Levi.
On the left hand were their brothers the sons of Merari: Eitan the son of Kishi, son of Avdi, son of Mallukh,
Son of Khashavyahu, son of Amatzyahu, son of Khilkiyahu,
Son of Amtzi, son of Bani, son of Shemer,
Son of Makhli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.
And their brothers the Levites were appointed for all the service of the tabernacle of the house of Creator.

But Aharon and his sons made offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense for all the work of the most holy place, and to make atonement for Yisra'EL, according to all that Mosheh the servant of Creator had commanded.
These are the sons of Aharon: El'azar his son, Pinkhas his son, Avishua his son,
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerakhy ahu his son,
Meraioth his son, Amaryahu his son, Akhituv his son,
Tzadok his son, Akhima'atz his son.
Now these are their dwelling places according to their settlements within their borders: to the sons of Aharon of the clans of Kohathites, for the lot fell to them,
To them they gave Khevron in the land of Yehudah and its surrounding pasturelands,
But the fields of the city and its villages they gave to Kalev the son of Yefunneh.
To the sons of Aharon they gave the cities of refuge: Khevron, Livnah with its pasturelands, Yattir, Eshtemoa with its pasturelands,
Khilen with its pasturelands, Devir with its pasturelands,
Ashan with its pasturelands, and Beit-Shemesh with its pasturelands.
And from the tribe of Binyamin: Geva with its pasturelands, Alemeth with its pasturelands, and Anatot with its pasturelands. All their cities throughout their clans were thirteen.
To the rest of the Kohathites were given by lot out of the clan of the tribe, out of the half-tribe, the half of Menasheh, ten cities.
To the Gershomites according to their clans were allotted thirteen cities out of the tribes of Yissachar, Asher, Naftali, and Menasheh in Bashan.
To the Merarites according to their clans were allotted twelve cities out of the tribes of Re'uven, Gad, and Zevulun.
So the people of Yisra'EL gave the Levites the cities with their pasturelands.
They gave by lot out of the tribes of Yehudah, Shim'on, and Binyamin these cities that are mentioned by name.
And some of the clans of the sons of Kohath had cities of their territory out of the tribe of Efrayim.
They were given the cities of refuge: Shekhem with its pasturelands in the hill country of Efrayim, Gezer with its pasturelands,
Yokmeam with its pasturelands, Beit-Khoron with its pasturelands,
Ayalon with its pasturelands, and Gat-Rimmon with its pasturelands.
And out of the half-tribe of Menasheh: Aner with its pasturelands, and Vileam with its pasturelands, for the rest of the clans of the Kohathites.
To the Gershomites were given out of the clan of the half-tribe of Menasheh: Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands and Ashtarot with its pasturelands.
And out of the tribe of Yissachar: Kedesh with its pasturelands, Davrat with its pasturelands,
Ramot with its pasturelands, and Anem with its pasturelands.
Out of the tribe of Asher: Mashal with its pasturelands, Avdon with its pasturelands,
Khukok with its pasturelands, and Rekhov with its pasturelands.
And out of the tribe of Naftali: Kedesh in Galil with its pasturelands, Khamon with its pasturelands, and Kiryataim with its pasturelands.
To the rest of the Merarites were allotted out of the tribe of Zevulun: Rimono with its pasturelands, Tabor with its pasturelands.
And beyond the Yarden at Yericho, on the east side of the Yarden, were given out of the tribe of Re'uven: Betzer in the wilderness with its pasturelands, Yahtzah with its pasturelands,
Kedemot with its pasturelands, and Mefaat with its pasturelands.
And out of the tribe of Gad: Ramot in Gil'ad with its pasturelands, Makhanayim with its pasturelands,
Kheshbon with its pasturelands, and Yazer with its pasturelands.
The sons of Yissachar: Tola, Puah, Yashuv, and Shimron, four.

The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Refayahu, Yeri'el, Yakhmai, Yivsam, and Shemu'el, heads of their fathers' houses. The sons of Tola were mighty warriors of their generations. Their number in the days of Dawid was 22,600.
The son of Uzzi: Yizrakhyahu. And the sons of Yizrakhyahu: Mikha'el, Ovadyahu, Yo'el, and Yishshiyahu, five, all of them chief men.
And along with them, by their generations, according to their fathers' houses, were 36,000 troops ready for war, for they had many wives and sons.
Their kinsmen belonging to all the clans of Yissachar were in all 87,000 mighty warriors, enrolled by genealogy.
The sons of Binyamin: Bela, Bekher, and Yedia'el, three.
The sons of Bela: Etzbon, Uzzi, Uzzi'el, Yerimot, and Iri, five, heads of fathers' houses, mighty warriors. And their enrollment by genealogy was 22,034.
The sons of Bekher: Zemira, Yo'ash, Eli'ezer, Elyoe'nai, Omri, Yeremot, Aviyah, Anatot, and Alemet. All these were the sons of Bekher.
And their enrollment by genealogy, according to their generations, as heads of their fathers' houses, mighty warriors, was 20,200.
The son of Yedia'el: Bilhan. And the sons of Bilhan: Ye'ush, Binyamin, Ehud, Khena'anah, Zeitan, Tarshish, and Akhishahar.
All these were the sons of Yedia'el according to the heads of their fathers' houses, mighty warriors, 17,200, fit for service in war.
And Shuppim and Khuppim were the sons of Ir, and Khushim the son of Akher.
The sons of Naftali: Yakhtze'el, Guni, Yetzer, and Shallum, the sons of Bilhah.
The sons of Menasheh: Asri'el, whom his Aramean concubine bore. She bore Makhir the father of Gil'ad.
And Makhir took a wife for Khuppim and Shuppim. The name of his sister was Ma'akhah. And the name of the second was Tzlofkhad, and Tzlofkhad had daughters.
And Ma'akhah the wife of Makhir bore a son, and she called his name Peresh. And the name of his brother was Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rekem.
The son of Ulam: Bedan. These were the sons of Gil'ad the son of Makhir, son of Menasheh.
And his sister Molechet bore Ishhod, Avi'ezer, and Makhla.
The sons of Shemida were Akhyan, Shekhem, Likhi, and Aniam.
The sons of Efrayim: Shuthelakh, and Bered his son, Takhat his son, El'adah his son, Takhat his son,
Zavad his son, Shuthelakh his son, and Ezer and El'ad, whom the men of Gat who were born in that land killed, because they came down to raid their livestock.
And Efrayim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
And Efrayim went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son. And he called his name Beri'ah, because disaster had befallen his house.
His daughter was She'erah, who built both lower and upper Beit-Khoron, and Uzzen-She'erah.
Refakh was his son, Reshef his son, Telakh his son, Takhan his son,
La'adan his son, Ammikhud his son, Elishama his son,
Nun his son, Yehoshua his son.
Their possessions and settlements were Beit-El and its towns, and to the east Na'aran, and to the west Gezer and its towns, Shekhem and its towns, and Ayah and its towns.
And along the borders of Menasheh, Beit-She'an and its towns, Ta'anakh and its towns, Megiddo and its towns, Dor and its towns. In these lived the sons of Yosef the son of Yisra'EL.
The sons of Asher: Yimnah, Yishvah, Yishvi, and Beriah, and their sister Serakh.
The sons of Beriah: Khever and Malki'el, who was the father of Birzaith.
Khever fathered Yaflet, Shomer, Khotam, and their sister Shua.
The sons of Yaflet: Pasakh, Vimhal, and Ashvat. These are the sons of Yaflet.
The sons of Shemer: Akhi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
The sons of his brother Khotem: Tzofakh, Yimna, Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Tzofakh: Suakh, Kharnefer, Shu'al, Beri, Yimrah,
Betzer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Yitran, and Be'era.
The sons of Yeter: Yefunneh, Pispah, and Ara.
The sons of Ulla: Arakh, Khanni'el, and Ritzya.
All of these were the sons of Asher, heads of fathers' houses, approved, mighty warriors, chief of the princes. Their number enrolled by genealogy for service in war was 26,000.
Binyamin fathered Bela his firstborn, Ashvel the second, Akharakh the third,
Nokha the fourth, and Rafa the fifth.
And Bela had sons: Addar, Gera, Avihud,
Avishua, Na'aman, Acho'akh,
Gera, Shefufan, and Khuram.
These are the sons of Ehud — these were the heads of fathers' houses of the inhabitants of Geva, and they were carried into exile to Manakhat:
Na'aman, Akhiyah, and Gera — that is, Heglam — who fathered Uzza and Akhikhud.
And Shaharayim fathered sons in the country of Moav after he had sent away Khushim and Ba'ara his wives.
He fathered sons by his wife Khodesh: Yovav, Tzivya, Mesha, Malkam,
Ye'utz, Sakhyah, and Mirmah. These were his sons, heads of fathers' houses.
He also fathered sons by Khushim: Avituv and Elpaal.
The sons of Elpaal: Ever, Mish'am, and Shemed, who built Ono and Lod with its towns,
And Beriah and Shema, who were heads of fathers' houses of the inhabitants of Ayalon, who drove away the inhabitants of Gat.
And Akhyo, Shashak, and Yeremot.
Zevadyahu, Arad, Ader,
Mikha'el, Yishpah, and Yokha were sons of Beriah.
Zevadyahu, Meshullam, Khizki, Khever,
Yishmerai, Yizliah, and Yovav were the sons of Elpaal.
Yakim, Zikhri, Zavdi,
Eli'enai, Tzillethai, Eli'el,
Adayahu, Berayahu, and Shimrat were the sons of Shim'i.
Yishpan, Ever, Eli'el,
Avdon, Zikhri, Khanan,
Hananyahu, Eilam, Antotiyah,
Yifdeyahu, and Penuel were the sons of Shashak.
Shamsherai, Shekharya, Atalyah,
Ya'areshyah, Eliyahu, and Zikhri were the sons of Yeroham.
These were the heads of fathers' houses, according to their generations, chief men. These lived in Yerushalayim.
Ye'iel the father of Giv'on lived in Giv'on, and the name of his wife was Ma'akhah.
His firstborn son: Avdon, then Tzur, Kish, Ba'al, Ner, Nadav,
Gedor, Akhyo, Zekher,
And Miklot, who fathered Shim'ah. Now these also lived opposite their kinsmen in Yerushalayim, with their kinsmen.
Ner fathered Kish, Kish fathered Sha'ul, Sha'ul fathered Yonatan, Malkishua, Avinadav, and Eshba'al.
The son of Yonatan: Meriv-Ba'al, and Meriv-Ba'al fathered Mikha.
The sons of Mikha: Piton, Melekh, Tare'a, and Akaz.
Akaz fathered Ye'hora, Ye'hora fathered Alemet, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri fathered Motza.
Motza fathered Bin'a. Refayah was his son, El'asah his son, Atzel his son.
Atzel had six sons, and these are their names: Azrikam, Bokhru, Yishma'el, She'aryah, Ovadyahu, and Khanan. All these were the sons of Atzel.
The sons of his brother Eshek: Ulam his firstborn, Ye'ush the second, and Elifelet the third.
The sons of Ulam were mighty warriors, bowmen, having many sons and grandsons, 150. All these were Benjaminites.
So all Yisra'EL was enrolled by genealogies, and these are written in the Book of the Kings of Yisra'EL. And Yehudah was taken into exile in Babylon because of their breach of faith.
Now the first to dwell again in their possessions in their cities were Yisra'EL, the priests, the Levites, and the temple servants.
And some of the people of Yehudah, Binyamin, Efrayim, and Menasheh lived in Yerushalayim:
Utai the son of Ammikhud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani, from the sons of Peretz the son of Yehudah.
And of the Shilonites: Asayah the firstborn and his sons.
Of the sons of Zerakh: Ye'uel and their kinsmen, 690.
Of the Binyaminites: Sallu the son of Meshullam, son of Hodavyah, son of Hassenuah.
Yivneyah the son of Yeroham, Elah the son of Uzzi, son of Mikri, and Meshullam the son of Shefatyahu, son of Re'uel, son of Yivniyah.
And their kinsmen according to their generations, 956. All these were heads of fathers' houses according to their fathers' houses.
Of the priests: Yedayah, Yehoyariv, Yakhin,
And Azaryahu the son of Khilkiyahu, son of Meshullam, son of Tzadok, son of Meraioth, son of Akhituv, the chief officer of the house of Creator.
And Adayah the son of Yeroham, son of Paskhur, son of Malkiyah, and Ma'asai the son of Adi'el, son of Yakhzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemit, son of Immer.
And their kinsmen, heads of their fathers' houses, 1,760, mighty men for the work of the service of the house of Creator.
Of the Levites: Shemayah the son of Khashuv, son of Azrikam, son of Khashavyahu, of the sons of Merari.
And Vakbakkar, Kheres, Galal, and Mattanyah the son of Mikha, son of Zikhri, son of Asaf.
And Ovadyah the son of Shemayah, son of Galal, son of Yedutun, and Berekhyahu the son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netofathites.
The gatekeepers were: Shallum, Akkuv, Talmon, and Akhiman, and their kinsmen — Shallum was the chief.
Until then they were in the king's gate on the east side. These were the gatekeepers of the camps of the Levites.

Shallum the son of Kore, son of Evyasaf, son of Korakh, and his kinsmen of his fathers' house, the Korahites, were in charge of the work of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent, as their fathers had been in charge of the camp of YHWH, keepers of the entrance.
And Pinkhas the son of El'azar was the chief over them in former times. YHWH was with him.
Zekhariyahu the son of Meshelemyahu was gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
All these, who were chosen as gatekeepers at the thresholds, were 212. They were enrolled by genealogies in their villages. Dawid and Shemu'el the seer established them in their office of trust.
So they and their sons were in charge of the gates of the house of YHWH, that is, the house of the tent, as guards.
The gatekeepers were on the four sides, east, west, north, and south.
And their kinsmen who were in their villages were obligated to come in every seven days, in turn, to be with these.
For the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were in charge of the chambers and the treasuries of the house of Creator.
And they lodged around the house of Creator, for on them lay the duty of watching, and they had charge of opening it every morning.
Some of them had charge of the utensils of service, for they were counted when they were brought in and when they were taken out.
Some of them were appointed over the furniture and over all the holy utensils, also over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.
Others, the sons of the priests, prepared the mixing of the spices.
Mattityahu, one of the Levites, the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with making the flat cakes.
Also some of their kinsmen of the Kohathites had charge of the showbread, to prepare it every Shabbat.
Now these, the singers, the heads of fathers' houses of the Levites, were in the chambers of the temple free from other service, for they were on duty day and night.
These were heads of fathers' houses of the Levites, according to their generations, chiefs. These lived in Yerushalayim.
In Giv'on lived the father of Giv'on, Ye'uel, and the name of his wife was Ma'akhah.
Gedor, Akhyo, Zekhariah, and Miklot.
And Miklot was the father of Shim'am. And these also lived opposite their kinsmen in Yerushalayim, with their kinsmen.
Ner was the father of Kish, Kish was the father of Sha'ul, Sha'ul was the father of Yonatan, Malkishua, Avinadav, and Eshba'al.
And the son of Yonatan was Meriv-Ba'al, and Meriv-Ba'al was the father of Mikha.
The sons of Mikha: Piton, Melekh, Tahrea, and Akaz.
And Akaz was the father of Yarah, and Yarah was the father of Alemet, Azmaveth, and Zimri. And Zimri was the father of Motza.
Motza was the father of Bin'a, and Refayah was his son, El'asah his son, Atzel his son.
Atzel had six sons and these are their names: Azrikam, Bokru, Yishma'el, She'aryah, Ovadyahu, and Khanan. These were the sons of Atzel.
Now the Pelishtim fought against Yisra'EL, and the men of Yisra'EL fled before the Pelishtim and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
And the Pelishtim overtook Sha'ul and his sons, and the Pelishtim struck down Yonatan and Avinadav and Malkishua, the sons of Sha'ul.
The battle pressed hard against Sha'ul, and the archers found him, and he was wounded by the archers.

Then Sha'ul said to his armor-bearer, Draw your sword and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and mistreat me. But his armor-bearer would not, for he feared greatly. Therefore Sha'ul took his own sword and fell upon it.
And when his armor-bearer saw that Sha'ul was dead, he also fell upon his sword and died.
Thus Sha'ul died. He and his three sons and all his house died together.

And when all the men of Yisra'EL who were in the valley saw that the army had fled and that Sha'ul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and fled, and the Pelishtim came and lived in them.
The next day, when the Pelishtim came to strip the slain, they found Sha'ul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
And they stripped him and took his head and his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Pelishtim to carry the good news to their idols and to the people.
And they put his armor in the house of their gods and fastened his head in the house of Dagon.
But when all Yavesh-Gil'ad heard all that the Pelishtim had done to Sha'ul,
All the valiant men arose and took away the body of Sha'ul and the bodies of his sons, and brought them to Yavesh. And they buried their bones under the oak in Yavesh and fasted seven days.
So Sha'ul died for his breach of faith. He broke faith with YHWH in that he did not keep the command of YHWH, and also consulted a medium, seeking guidance.
He did not seek guidance from YHWH. Therefore YHWH put him to death and turned the kingdom over to Dawid the son of Yishai.
Then all Yisra'EL gathered together to Dawid at Khevron and said, Behold, we are your bone and flesh.

In times past, even when Sha'ul was king, it was you who led out and brought in Yisra'EL. And YHWH your Creator said to you, You shall be shepherd of my people Yisra'EL, and you shall be prince over my people Yisra'EL.

So all the elders of Yisra'EL came to the king at Khevron, and Dawid made a covenant with them at Khevron before YHWH. And they anointed Dawid king over Yisra'EL, according to the word of YHWH by Shemu'el.
And Dawid and all Yisra'EL went to Yerushalayim, that is Yevus, where the Yevusites were, the inhabitants of the land.
The inhabitants of Yevus said to Dawid, You will not come in here. Nevertheless, Dawid took the stronghold of Tziyon, that is, the city of Dawid.
Dawid said, Whoever strikes the Yevusites first shall be chief and commander. And Yo'av the son of Tzeruyah went up first, so he became chief.
And Dawid lived in the stronghold. Therefore it was called the city of Dawid.
And he built the city all around from the Millo in complete circuit, and Yo'av repaired the rest of the city.
And Dawid became greater and greater, for YHWH of hosts was with him.
Now these are the chiefs of Dawid's mighty warriors, who gave him strong support in his kingdom, together with all Yisra'EL, to make him king, according to the word of YHWH concerning Yisra'EL.
This is an account of Dawid's mighty warriors: Yashobeam, a Hakhmonite, was chief of the three. He wielded his spear against 300, whom he killed at one time.
And next to him among the three mighty warriors was El'azar the son of Dodo, the Ahohite.
He was with Dawid at Pas-Dammim when the Pelishtim were gathered there for battle. There was a plot of ground full of barley, and the men fled from the Pelishtim.
But he took his stand in the midst of the plot and defended it and killed the Pelishtim. And YHWH saved them by a great victory.
Three of the thirty chiefs went down to the rock to Dawid at the cave of Adullam, when the army of Pelishtim was encamped in the Valley of Refa'im.
Dawid was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Pelishtim was then at Beit-Lekhem.
And Dawid said longingly, Oh that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Beit-Lekhem that is by the gate.

Then the three broke through the camp of the Pelishtim and drew water out of the well of Beit-Lekhem that was by the gate and took it and brought it to Dawid. But Dawid would not drink it. He poured it out to YHWH

And said, Far be it from me before my Creator that I should do this. Shall I drink the lifeblood of these men? For at the risk of their lives they brought it. Therefore he would not drink it. These things did the three mighty men.
Now Avishai, the brother of Yo'av, was chief of the thirty. And he wielded his spear against 300 and killed them and won a name beside the three.
He was the most renowned of the thirty and became their commander, but he did not attain to the three.

And Benayahu the son of Yehoyada was a valiant man of Kavtze'el, a doer of great deeds. He struck down two heroes of Moav. He also went down and struck down a lion in a pit on a day when snow had fallen.

And he struck down an Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits tall. The Egyptian had in his hand a spear like a weaver's beam, but Benayahu went down to him with a staff and snatched the spear out of the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.
These things did Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, and won a name beside the three mighty men.
He was renowned among the thirty, but he did not attain to the three. And Dawid set him over his bodyguard.
The mighty warriors of the armies: Asahel the brother of Yo'av, Elkhanah of Beit-Lekhem,
Shammot the Harorite, Kheletz the Pelonite,
Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Aviezer the Antothite,
Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,
Maharai the Netofathite, Kheled the son of Ba'anah the Netofathite,
Itai the son of Rivai of Giv'ah of the Binyaminites, Benayahu of Pir'aton,
Hurai of the brooks of Ga'ash, Avi'el the Arvathite,
Azmaveth the Bakharumite, Elyakhba the Sha'albonite,
The sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Yonatan the son of Shage the Hararite,
Akhiam the son of Sakar the Hararite, Elifal the son of Ur,
Khefer the Mekherathite, Akhiyah the Pelonite,
Khetzro the Karmelite, Na'arai the son of Ezbai,
Yo'el the brother of Natan, Mivkhar the son of Hagri,
Tzelek the Ammonite, Nakhrai the Berothite, the armor-bearer of Yo'av the son of Tzeruyah,
Ira the Yitrite, Garev the Yitrite,
Uriyah the Hittite, Zavad the son of Akhlai,
Adina the son of Shiza the Reubenite, a chief of the Reubenites, and thirty with him,
Hanan the son of Ma'akha, and Yoshafat the Mithnite,
Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Ye'iel the sons of Khotam the Aroerith,
Yedia'el the son of Shimri, and Yokha his brother, the Titzite,
Eliel the Makhavite, and Yerivai and Yoshavyah the sons of Elnaam, and Yitmah the Moabite,
Eliel, and Oved, and Ya'asi'el the Mezobaite.
Now these are the men who came to Dawid at Tziklag, while he could not move about freely because of Sha'ul the son of Kish. And they were among the mighty men who helped him in war.
They were bowmen and could shoot arrows and sling stones with either the right or the left hand. They were Binyaminites, Sha'ul's kinsmen.
The chief was Akhiezer, then Yo'ash, both sons of Shemah of Giv'ah. And Yeziel and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth, Berakha, Yehu of Anatot,
Yishma'yahu of Giv'on, a mighty man among the thirty and a leader over the thirty, Yirmeyahu, Yakhazi'el, Yokhanan, Yozavad of Gederah,
Eluzai, Yerimot, Be'alyah, Shemaryahu, Shefatyahu the Haruphite,
Elkanah, Yishshiyahu, Azarel, Yo'ezer, and Yashobeam, the Korahites,
And Yo'elah and Zevadyahu, the sons of Yeroham of Gedor.

From the Gadites there went over to Dawid at the stronghold in the wilderness mighty and experienced warriors, expert with shield and spear, whose faces were like the faces of lions and who were swift as gazelles upon the mountains:
Ezer the chief, Ovadyahu second, Eliav third,
Mishmannah fourth, Yirmeyahu fifth,
Attai sixth, Eliel seventh,
Yokhanan eighth, Elzabad ninth,
Yirmeyahu tenth, Makhvannai eleventh.
These Gadites were officers of the army. The least was a match for a hundred men and the greatest for a thousand.
These are the men who crossed the Yarden in the first month, when it was overflowing all its banks, and put to flight all those in the valleys, to the east and to the west.
And some of the men of Binyamin and Yehudah came to the stronghold to Dawid.

Dawid went out to meet them and said to them, If you have come to me in friendship to help me, my heart will be joined to you, but if to betray me to my adversaries, although there is no wrong in my hands, then may the Creator of our fathers see and rebuke you.

Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the thirty, and he said, We are yours, O Dawid, and with you, O son of Yishai. Peace, peace to you, and peace to your helpers. For your Creator helps you. Then Dawid received them and made them officers of his troops.

Some of the men of Menasheh deserted to Dawid when he came with the Pelishtim for the battle against Sha'ul. Yet he did not help them, for the rulers of the Pelishtim took counsel and sent him away, saying, At peril of our heads he will desert to his master Sha'ul.
As he went to Tziklag, these men of Menasheh deserted to him: Adnakh, Yozavad, Yediael, Mikha'el, Yozavad, Elihu, and Tziltai, chiefs of thousands in Menasheh.
They helped Dawid against the band of raiders, for they were all mighty men of valor and were commanders in the army.
For from day to day men kept coming to Dawid to help him, until there was a great army, like an army of Creator.
These are the numbers of the divisions of the armed troops who came to Dawid in Khevron, to turn the kingdom of Sha'ul over to him, according to the word of YHWH.
The men of Yehudah bearing shield and spear were 6,800 armed troops.
Of the Shim'onites, mighty men of valor for war, 7,100.
Of the Levites, 4,600.
The prince Yehoyada, of the house of Aharon, and with him 3,700.
Tzadok, a young man mighty in valor, and twenty-two commanders from his father's house.
Of the Binyaminites, the kinsmen of Sha'ul, 3,000, of whom the majority had to that point kept their allegiance to the house of Sha'ul.
Of the Efrayimites, 20,800 mighty men of valor, famous men in their fathers' houses.
Of the half-tribe of Menasheh, 18,000, who were expressly named to come and make Dawid king.
Of Yissachar, men who had understanding of the times, to know what Yisra'EL ought to do, 200 chiefs, and all their kinsmen under their command.
Of Zevulun, 50,000 seasoned troops, equipped for battle with all the weapons of war, to help Dawid with singleness of purpose.
Of Naftali, 1,000 commanders with whom were 37,000 men armed with shield and spear.
Of the Danites, 28,600 men equipped for battle.
Of Asher, 40,000 seasoned troops ready for battle.
Of the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Menasheh from beyond the Yarden, 120,000 men armed with all the weapons of war.
All these, men of war, arrayed in battle order, came to Khevron with full intent to make Dawid king over all Yisra'EL. Likewise, all the rest of Yisra'EL were of a single mind to make Dawid king.
And they were there with Dawid for three days, eating and drinking, for their brothers had made preparation for them.

And also their relatives, from as far as Yissachar, Zevulun, and Naftali, came bringing food on donkeys and on camels and on mules and on oxen, abundant provisions of flour, cakes of figs, clusters of raisins, and wine and oil and oxen and sheep, for there was joy in Yisra'EL.
Dawid consulted with the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with every leader.

And Dawid said to all the assembly of Yisra'EL, If it seems good to you and from YHWH our Creator, let us send abroad to our brothers who remain in all the lands of Yisra'EL, as well as to the priests and Levites in the cities that have pasturelands, that they may be gathered to us.
Then let us bring again the ark of our Creator to us, for we did not seek it in the days of Sha'ul.
All the assembly agreed to do so, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.
So Dawid assembled all Yisra'EL from the Shihor of Egypt to Levo-Hamat, to bring the ark of Creator from Kiryat-Ye'arim.

And Dawid and all Yisra'EL went up to Ba'alah, that is, to Kiryat-Ye'arim that belongs to Yehudah, to bring up from there the ark of Creator, who is enthroned above the cherubim, which is called by his name.
And they carried the ark of Creator on a new cart, from the house of Avinadav, and Uzza and Akhyo were driving the cart.
And Dawid and all Yisra'EL were celebrating before Creator with all their might, with song and lyres and harps and tambourines and cymbals and trumpets.
And when they came to the threshing floor of Kidon, Uzza put out his hand to take hold of the ark, for the oxen stumbled.
And the anger of YHWH was kindled against Uzza, and he struck him down because he put out his hand to the ark, and he died there before Creator.
And Dawid was angry because YHWH had burst out against Uzza. And that place is called Peretz-Uzza to this day.
And Dawid was afraid of Creator that day, and he said, How can I bring the ark of Creator home to me?
So Dawid did not take the ark home into the city of Dawid, but took it aside to the house of Oved-Edom the Gittite.
And the ark of Creator remained with the household of Oved-Edom in his house three months. And YHWH blessed the household of Oved-Edom and all that he had.
And Khiram king of Tzor sent messengers to Dawid, and cedar trees, also masons and carpenters to build a house for him.
And Dawid knew that YHWH had established him as king over Yisra'EL, and that his kingdom was highly exalted for the sake of his people Yisra'EL.
And Dawid took more wives in Yerushalayim, and Dawid fathered more sons and daughters.
These are the names of the children born to him in Yerushalayim: Shammua, Shovav, Natan, Shelomoh,
Yivkhar, Elishua, Elpelet,
Nogah, Nefeg, Yafia,
Elishama, Ba'alyada, and Elifelet.
When the Pelishtim heard that Dawid had been anointed king over all Yisra'EL, all the Pelishtim went up to seek Dawid. And Dawid heard of it and went out against them.
Now the Pelishtim had come and made a raid in the Valley of Refa'im.
And Dawid inquired of Creator, Shall I go up against the Pelishtim? Will you give them into my hand? And YHWH said to him, Go up, and I will give them into your hand.

And he went up to Ba'al-Peratzim, and Dawid struck them down there. And Dawid said, Creator has broken through my enemies by my hand, like a bursting flood. Therefore the name of that place is called Ba'al-Peratzim.
And they left their gods there, and Dawid gave command, and they were burned.
And the Pelishtim yet again made a raid in the valley.
And Dawid again inquired of Creator, and Creator said to him, You shall not go up after them. Go around and come against them opposite the balsam trees.
And when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then go out to battle, for Creator has gone out before you to strike down the army of the Pelishtim.
And Dawid did as Creator commanded him, and they struck down the Pelishtim from Givon to Gezer.
And the fame of Dawid went out into all lands, and YHWH brought the fear of him upon all nations.
Dawid built houses for himself in the city of Dawid. And he prepared a place for the ark of Creator and pitched a tent for it.
Then Dawid said, No one but the Levites may carry the ark of Creator, for YHWH chose them to carry the ark of Creator and to minister to him forever.
And Dawid assembled all Yisra'EL at Yerushalayim to bring up the ark of YHWH to its place, which he had prepared for it.
And Dawid gathered together the sons of Aharon and the Levites:
Of the sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief, with 120 of his brothers.
Of the sons of Merari, Asayah the chief, with 220 of his brothers.
Of the sons of Gershom, Yo'el the chief, with 130 of his brothers.
Of the sons of Elitzafan, Shemayah the chief, with 200 of his brothers.
Of the sons of Khevron, Eliel the chief, with 80 of his brothers.
Of the sons of Uzzi'el, Amminadav the chief, with 112 of his brothers.
Dawid summoned the priests Tzadok and Evyatar, and the Levites Uriel, Asayah, Yo'el, Shemayah, Eliel, and Amminadav,

And said to them, You are the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites. Consecrate yourselves, you and your brothers, so that you may bring up the ark of YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, to the place that I have prepared for it.
Because you did not carry it the first time, YHWH our Creator broke out against us, because we did not seek him according to the rule.
So the priests and the Levites consecrated themselves to bring up the ark of YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL.
And the Levites carried the ark of Creator on their shoulders with the poles, as Mosheh had commanded according to the word of YHWH.
Dawid also commanded the chiefs of the Levites to appoint their brothers as the singers who should play loudly on musical instruments, on harps and lyres and cymbals, to raise sounds of joy.
So the Levites appointed Heman the son of Yo'el, and of his brothers Asaf the son of Berekhyahu, and of the sons of Merari, their brothers, Eitan the son of Kushayahu.

And with them their brothers of the second order: Zekhariyah, Ya'azi'el, Shemiramot, Yekhiel, Unni, Eli'av, Benayahu, Ma'aseiyahu, Mattityahu, Elifelehu, and Mikneyahu, and Oved-Edom and Ye'iel, the gatekeepers.
The singers, Heman, Asaf, and Eitan, were to sound bronze cymbals.
Zekhariyah, Azi'el, Shemiramot, Yekhiel, Unni, Eli'av, Ma'aseiyahu, and Benayahu were to play harps according to Alamot.
But Mattityahu, Elifelehu, Mikneyahu, Oved-Edom, Ye'iel, and Azazyahu were to lead with lyres according to the Sheminit.
Kenanyahu, the chief of the Levites, was in charge of the music, for he was skilled in it.
Berekhyahu and Elkanah were to be gatekeepers for the ark.

Shevanyahu, Yoshafat, Netane'el, Amasai, Zekhariyahu, Benayahu, and Eli'ezer, the priests, were to blow the trumpets before the ark of Creator. Oved-Edom and Yekhiyahu were also to be gatekeepers for the ark.
So Dawid and the elders of Yisra'EL and the commanders of thousands went to bring up the ark of the covenant of YHWH from the house of Oved-Edom with rejoicing.
And because Creator helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the covenant of YHWH, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.

Dawid was clothed with a robe of fine linen, as also were all the Levites who were carrying the ark, and the singers and Kenanyahu the leader of the music of the singers. And Dawid wore a linen ephod.
So all Yisra'EL brought up the ark of the covenant of YHWH with shouting, to the sound of the horn, trumpets, and cymbals, and made loud music on harps and lyres.
And as the ark of the covenant of YHWH came to the city of Dawid, Mikhal the daughter of Sha'ul looked out of the window and saw King Dawid dancing and celebrating, and she despised him in her heart.
And they brought in the ark of Creator and set it inside the tent that Dawid had pitched for it, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before Creator.
And when Dawid had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of YHWH
And distributed to all Yisra'EL, both men and women, to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins.
Then he appointed some of the Levites as ministers before the ark of YHWH, to invoke, to thank, and to praise YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL.

Asaf was the chief, and second to him Zekhariah, then Ye'iel, Shemiramot, Yekhiel, Mattityahu, Eli'av, Benayahu, Oved-Edom, and Ye'iel, who were to play harps and lyres. Asaf was to sound the cymbals.
And Benayahu and Yakhazi'el the priests were to blow trumpets regularly before the ark of the covenant of Creator.
Then on that day Dawid first appointed that thanksgiving be sung to YHWH by Asaf and his brothers.
Oh give thanks to YHWH. Call upon his name. Make known his deeds among the peoples.
Sing to him, sing praises to him, tell of all his wondrous works.
Glory in his holy name. Let the hearts of those who seek YHWH rejoice.
Seek YHWH and his strength. Seek his presence continually.
Remember the wondrous works that he has done, his miracles and the judgments he uttered,
O offspring of Yisra'EL his servant, children of Yaakov, his chosen ones.
He is YHWH our Creator. His judgments are in all the earth.
Remember his covenant forever, the word that he commanded, for a thousand generations,
The covenant that he made with Avraham, his sworn promise to Yitzkhak,
Which he confirmed as a statute to Yaakov, as an everlasting covenant to Yisra'EL,
Saying, To you I will give the land of Kena'an as your portion for an inheritance.
When you were few in number, of little account, and sojourners in it,
Wandering from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people,
He allowed no one to oppress them. He rebuked kings on their account,
Saying, Touch not my anointed ones, do my prophets no harm.
Sing to YHWH, all the earth. Tell of his salvation from day to day.
Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples.
For great is YHWH, and greatly to be praised, and he is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but YHWH made the heavens.
Splendor and majesty are before him. Strength and joy are in his place.
Ascribe to YHWH, O clans of the peoples, ascribe to YHWH glory and strength.
Ascribe to YHWH the glory due his name. Bring an offering and come before him. Worship YHWH in the splendor of holiness.
Tremble before him, all the earth. Yes, the world is established. It shall never be moved.
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice, and let them say among the nations, YHWH is king.
Let the sea roar, and all that fills it. Let the field exult, and everything in it.
Then shall the trees of the forest sing for joy before YHWH, for he comes to judge the earth.
