Oh give thanks to YHWH, for he is good. For his steadfast love endures forever.
Say also, Save us, O Creator of our salvation, and gather and deliver us from among the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name, and glory in your praise.
Blessed be YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, from everlasting to everlasting. Then all the people said, Amen, and praised YHWH.
So Dawid left Asaf and his brothers there before the ark of the covenant of YHWH to minister regularly before the ark as each day required,
And also Oved-Edom and his sixty-eight brothers, while Oved-Edom, the son of Yedutun, and Khosah were to be gatekeepers.
And he left Tzadok the priest and his brothers the priests before the tabernacle of YHWH in the high place that was at Givon,
To offer burnt offerings to YHWH on the altar of burnt offering regularly morning and evening, to do all that is written in the Torah of YHWH that he commanded Yisra'EL.
With them were Heman and Yedutun and the rest of those chosen and expressly named to give thanks to YHWH, for his steadfast love endures forever.
Heman and Yedutun had trumpets and cymbals for the music and instruments for sacred song. The sons of Yedutun were appointed to the gate.
Then all the people departed each to his house, and Dawid went home to bless his household.
Now when Dawid lived in his house, Dawid said to Natan the prophet, Behold, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of YHWH is under a tent.
And Natan said to Dawid, Do all that is in your heart, for Creator is with you.
But that same night the word of Creator came to Natan,
Go and tell my servant Dawid, Thus says YHWH: You shall not build me a house to dwell in.
For I have not lived in a house since the day I led up Yisra'EL to this day, but I have gone from tent to tent and from dwelling to dwelling.
In all places where I have moved with all Yisra'EL, did I speak a word with any of the judges of Yisra'EL, whom I commanded to shepherd my people, saying, Why have you not built me a house of cedar?
Now therefore thus shall you say to my servant Dawid, Thus says YHWH of hosts, I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be leader over my people Yisra'EL.
And I have been with you wherever you went and have cut off all your enemies from before you. And I will make for you a name, like the name of the great ones of the earth.
And I will appoint a place for my people Yisra'EL and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more. And violent men shall waste them no more, as formerly,
From the time that I appointed judges over my people Yisra'EL. And I will subdue all your enemies. Moreover, I declare to you that YHWH will build you a house.
When your days are fulfilled to walk with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, one of your own sons, and I will establish his kingdom.
He shall build a house for me, and I will establish his throne forever.
I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son. I will not take my steadfast love from him, as I took it from him who was before you,
But I will confirm him in my house and in my kingdom forever, and his throne shall be established forever.
In accordance with all these words, and in accordance with all this vision, Natan spoke to Dawid.
Then King Dawid went in and sat before YHWH and said, Who am I, O YHWH Creator, and what is my house, that you have brought me thus far?
And this was a small thing in your eyes, O Creator. You have also spoken of your servant's house for a great while to come, and have shown me future generations, O YHWH Creator.
And what more can Dawid say to you for honoring your servant? For you know your servant.
For your servant's sake, O YHWH, and according to your own heart, you have done all this greatness, in making known all these great things.
There is none like you, O YHWH, and there is no Creator besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

And who is like your people Yisra'EL, the one nation on earth whom Creator went to redeem to be his people, making for yourself a name for great and awesome things, in driving out nations before your people whom you redeemed from Egypt?
And you made your people Yisra'EL to be your people forever, and you, O YHWH, became their Creator.
And now, O YHWH, let the word that you have spoken concerning your servant and concerning his house be established forever, and do as you have spoken.
And let your name be established and magnified forever, saying, YHWH of hosts, the Creator of Yisra'EL, is Yisra'EL's Creator, and the house of your servant Dawid will be established before you.
For you, my Creator, have revealed to your servant that you will build a house for him. Therefore your servant has found courage to pray before you.
And now, O YHWH, you are Creator, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.
Now you have been pleased to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you, for it is you, O YHWH, who have blessed, and it is blessed forever.
After this Dawid defeated the Pelishtim and subdued them, and he took Gat and its villages out of the hand of the Pelishtim.
And he defeated Moav, and the Moabites became servants to Dawid and brought tribute.
Dawid also defeated Hadadezer king of Tzovar-Tzovah toward Hamat, as he went to set up his monument at the river Euphrates.
And Dawid took from him 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen, and 20,000 foot soldiers. And Dawid hamstrung all the chariot horses, but left enough for 100 chariots.
And when the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Tzovar-Tzovah, Dawid struck down 22,000 men of the Syrians.
Then Dawid put garrisons in Syria of Damascus, and the Syrians became servants to Dawid and brought tribute. And YHWH gave Dawid victory wherever he went.
And Dawid took the shields of gold that were carried by the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Yerushalayim.
And from Tivchat and from Kun, cities of Hadadezer, Dawid took a large amount of bronze. With it Shelomoh made the bronze sea and the pillars and the vessels of bronze.
When To'u king of Hamat heard that Dawid had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer king of Tzovar-Tzovah,

He sent his son Hadoram to King Dawid to greet him and to congratulate him because he had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him — for Hadadezer had often been at war with To'u — and he sent all sorts of articles of gold, of silver, and of bronze.
These also King Dawid dedicated to YHWH, together with the silver and gold that he had carried off from all the nations, from Edom, Moav, the Ammonites, the Pelishtim, and Amalek.
And Avishai the son of Tzeruyah defeated 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
And he put garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became servants to Dawid. And YHWH gave Dawid victory wherever he went.
So Dawid reigned over all Yisra'EL, and he administered justice and equity to all his people.
Yo'av the son of Tzeruyah was over the army. Yehoshafat the son of Akhilud was recorder.
Tzadok the son of Akhituv and Avimelekh the son of Evyatar were priests. Shavsha was secretary.
Benayahu the son of Yehoyada was over the Kerethites and the Pelethites. And Dawid's sons were the chief officials in the service of the king.
After this Nakhash the king of the Ammonites died, and his son Khanum reigned in his place.

And Dawid said, I will deal kindly with Khanum the son of Nakhash, for his father dealt kindly with me. So Dawid sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. And Dawid's servants came to the land of the Ammonites to Khanum to comfort him.

But the princes of the Ammonites said to Khanum, Do you think, because Dawid has sent comforters to you, that he is honoring your father? Have not his servants come to you to search and to overthrow and to spy out the land?
So Khanum took Dawid's servants and shaved them and cut off their garments in the middle, at their hips, and sent them away.
And Dawid was told concerning the men. And he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, Remain at Yericho until your beards have grown, and then return.

When the Ammonites saw that they had become a stench to Dawid, Khanum and the Ammonites sent 1,000 talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Mesopotamia, from Aram-Ma'akhah, and from Tzovar-Tzovah.
They hired 32,000 chariots and the king of Ma'akhah with his army, who came and encamped before Medeva. And the Ammonites were mustered from their cities and came to battle.
When Dawid heard of it, he sent Yo'av and all the army of the mighty men.
And the Ammonites came out and drew up in battle array at the entrance of the city, and the kings who had come were by themselves in the open country.
When Yo'av saw that the battle was set against him both in front and in the rear, he chose some of the best men of Yisra'EL and arrayed them against the Syrians.
The rest of his men he put in the charge of Avishai his brother, and they were arrayed against the Ammonites.
And he said, If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you shall help me, but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will help you.
Be strong, and let us use our strength for our people and for the cities of our Creator, and may YHWH do what seems good to him.
So Yo'av and the people who were with him drew near before the Syrians for battle, and they fled before him.
And when the Ammonites saw that the Syrians fled, they also fled before Avishai his brother and entered the city. Then Yo'av came to Yerushalayim.

But when the Syrians saw that they had been defeated by Yisra'EL, they sent messengers and brought out the Syrians who were beyond the Euphrates, with Shofakh the commander of the army of Hadadezer at their head.

And when it was told to Dawid, he gathered all Yisra'EL together and crossed the Yarden and came to them and drew up his forces against them. And Dawid set the battle in array against the Syrians, and they fought with him.
And the Syrians fled before Yisra'EL, and Dawid killed of the Syrians the men of 7,000 chariots and 40,000 foot soldiers, and put to death also Shofakh the commander of their army.
And when the servants of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Yisra'EL, they made peace with Dawid and became subject to him. So the Syrians were not willing to save the Ammonites anymore.

In the spring of the year, the time when kings go out to battle, Yo'av led out the army and ravaged the country of the Ammonites and came and besieged Rabbah. But Dawid remained at Yerushalayim. And Yo'av struck Rabbah and overthrew it.

And Dawid took the crown of their king from his head. He found that it weighed a talent of gold, and in it was a precious stone. And it was placed on Dawid's head. And he brought out the spoil of the city, a very great amount.

And he brought out the people who were in it and set them to labor with saws and iron picks and axes. And thus Dawid did to all the cities of the Ammonites. Then Dawid and all the people returned to Yerushalayim.
And after this there arose war with the Pelishtim at Gezer. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Sippai, who was one of the descendants of the giants, and the Pelishtim were subdued.
And there was again war with the Pelishtim, and Elkhanah the son of Yair struck down Lakhmi the brother of Golyat the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.
And there was again war at Gat, where there was a man of great stature, who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number, and he also was descended from the giants.
And when he taunted Yisra'EL, Yonatan the son of Shim'a, Dawid's brother, struck him down.
These were descended from the giants in Gat, and they fell by the hand of Dawid and by the hand of his servants.
Then Satan stood against Yisra'EL and incited Dawid to number Yisra'EL.
So Dawid said to Yo'av and the commanders of the people, Go, number Yisra'EL, from Beersheba to Dan, and bring me a report, that I may know their number.

But Yo'av said, May YHWH add to his people a hundred times as many as they are. Are they not, my lord the king, all of them my lord's servants? Why then should my lord require this? Why should it be a cause of guilt for Yisra'EL?
But the king's word prevailed against Yo'av. So Yo'av departed and went throughout all Yisra'EL and came back to Yerushalayim.
And Yo'av gave the sum of the numbering of the people to Dawid. In all Yisra'EL there were 1,100,000 men who drew the sword, and in Yehudah 470,000 who drew the sword.
But he did not include Levi and Binyamin in the numbering, for the king's command was abhorrent to Yo'av.
But Creator was displeased with this thing, and he struck Yisra'EL.
And Dawid said to Creator, I have sinned greatly in that I have done this thing. But now, please take away the iniquity of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.
And YHWH spoke to Gad, Dawid's seer, saying,
Go and say to Dawid, Thus says YHWH, Three things I offer you. Choose one of them, that I may do it to you.
So Gad came to Dawid and said to him, Thus says YHWH, Choose what you will:

Either three years of famine, or three months of devastation by your foes while the sword of your enemies overtakes you, or else three days of the sword of YHWH, pestilence on the land, with the angel of YHWH destroying throughout all the territory of Yisra'EL. Now decide what answer I shall return to him who sent me.
Then Dawid said to Gad, I am in great distress. Let me fall into the hand of YHWH, for his mercy is very great, but do not let me fall into the hand of man.
So YHWH sent a pestilence on Yisra'EL, and 70,000 men of Yisra'EL fell.

And Creator sent the angel to Yerushalayim to destroy it, but as he was about to destroy it, YHWH saw, and he relented from the calamity. And he said to the angel who was destroying, It is enough. Now stay your hand. And the angel of YHWH was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Yevusite.

And Dawid lifted his eyes and saw the angel of YHWH standing between earth and heaven, and in his hand a drawn sword stretched out over Yerushalayim. Then Dawid and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell upon their faces.

And Dawid said to Creator, Was it not I who gave command to number the people? It is I who have sinned and done great evil. But these sheep, what have they done? Please let your hand, O YHWH my Creator, be against me and against my father's house. But do not let the plague be on your people.
Now the angel of YHWH had commanded Gad to say to Dawid that Dawid should go up and raise an altar to YHWH on the threshing floor of Ornan the Yevusite.
So Dawid went up at Gad's word, which he had spoken in the name of YHWH.
Now Ornan had turned and saw the angel, and his four sons who were with him hid themselves. As Ornan was threshing wheat,
Dawid came to Ornan. And when Ornan looked and saw Dawid, he went out from the threshing floor and paid homage to Dawid with his face to the ground.
And Dawid said to Ornan, Give me the site of the threshing floor so that I may build on it an altar to YHWH — give it to me at its full price — that the plague may be averted from the people.

Then Ornan said to Dawid, Take it, and let my lord the king do what seems good to him. See, I give the oxen for burnt offerings and the threshing sledges for the wood and the wheat for a grain offering. I give it all.
But King Dawid said to Ornan, No, but I will buy them for the full price. I will not take for YHWH what is yours, nor offer burnt offerings that cost me nothing.
So Dawid paid Ornan 600 shekels of gold by weight for the site.
And Dawid built there an altar to YHWH and presented burnt offerings and peace offerings and called on YHWH, and YHWH answered him with fire from heaven upon the altar of burnt offering.
Then YHWH commanded the angel, and he put his sword back into its sheath.
At that time, when Dawid saw that YHWH had answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Yevusite, he sacrificed there.
For the tabernacle of YHWH, which Mosheh had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering were at that time in the high place at Givon.
But Dawid could not go before it to inquire of Creator, for he was afraid of the sword of the angel of YHWH.
Then Dawid said, Here shall be the house of YHWH Creator and here the altar of burnt offering for Yisra'EL.
Dawid commanded to gather together the sojourners who were in the land of Yisra'EL, and he set stonecutters to cut dressed stones for building the house of Creator.
Dawid also provided great quantities of iron for nails for the doors of the gates and for clamps, as well as bronze in quantities beyond weighing,
And cedar timbers without number, for the Sidonians and Tyrians brought great quantities of cedar to Dawid.

For Dawid said, Shelomoh my son is young and inexperienced, and the house that is to be built for YHWH must be exceedingly magnificent, of fame and glory throughout all lands. I will therefore make preparation for it. So Dawid made ample preparations before his death.
Then he called for Shelomoh his son and charged him to build a house for YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL.
Dawid said to Shelomoh, My son, I had it in my heart to build a house to the name of YHWH my Creator.
But the word of YHWH came to me, saying, You have shed much blood and have waged great wars. You shall not build a house to my name, because you have shed so much blood before me on the earth.

Behold, a son shall be born to you who shall be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all his surrounding enemies. For his name shall be Shelomoh, and I will give peace and quiet to Yisra'EL in his days.
He shall build a house for my name. He shall be my son, and I will be his father, and I will establish his royal throne over Yisra'EL forever.
Now, my son, YHWH be with you, so that you may succeed in building the house of YHWH your Creator, as he has spoken concerning you.
Only, may YHWH grant you discretion and understanding, that when he gives you charge over Yisra'EL you may keep the Torah of YHWH your Creator.
Then you will prosper if you are careful to observe the statutes and the rules that YHWH commanded Mosheh for Yisra'EL. Be strong and courageous. Fear not. Do not be dismayed.

With great pains I have provided for the house of YHWH 100,000 talents of gold, 1,000,000 talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weighing, for there is so much of it. Timber and stone too I have provided. To these you must add more.
You have an abundance of workmen: stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and all kinds of craftsmen without number, skilled in working
Gold, silver, bronze, and iron. Arise and work. YHWH be with you.
Dawid also commanded all the leaders of Yisra'EL to help Shelomoh his son, saying,
Is not YHWH your Creator with you? And has he not given you peace on every side? For he has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land is subdued before YHWH and his people.

Now set your mind and heart to seek YHWH your Creator. Arise and build the sanctuary of YHWH Creator, so that the ark of the covenant of YHWH and the holy vessels of Creator may be brought into a house built for the name of YHWH.
When Dawid was old and full of days, he made Shelomoh his son king over Yisra'EL.
Dawid assembled all the leaders of Yisra'EL and the priests and the Levites.
The Levites, thirty years old and upward, were numbered, and the total was 38,000 men.
Twenty-four thousand of these, said Dawid, shall have oversight of the work in the house of YHWH, 6,000 shall be officers and judges,
4,000 gatekeepers, and 4,000 shall offer praises to YHWH with the instruments that I have made for praise.
And Dawid organized them in divisions corresponding to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Gershon: La'dan and Shim'i.
The sons of La'dan: Yekhiel the chief, and Zetam and Yo'el, three.
The sons of Shim'i: Shelomit, Hazi'el, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the fathers' houses of La'dan.
And the sons of Shim'i: Yakhat, Zina, and Ye'ush and Beri'ah. These four were the sons of Shim'i.
Yakhat was the chief, and Zizah the second. But Ye'ush and Beri'ah did not have many sons, so they became a single fathers' house.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Yitzhar, Khevron, and Uzzi'el, four.

The sons of Amram: Aharon and Mosheh. Aharon was set apart to dedicate the most holy things, that he and his sons forever should make offerings before YHWH, minister to him and pronounce blessings in his name forever.
But the sons of Mosheh the man of Creator were named among the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Mosheh: Gershom and Eli'ezer.
The sons of Gershom: Shevuel the chief.
The sons of Eli'ezer: Rekhavyahu the chief. Eli'ezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rekhavyahu were very many.
The sons of Yitzhar: Shelomit the chief.
The sons of Khevron: Yeriyahu the chief, Amaryahu the second, Yakhazi'el the third, and Yekame'am the fourth.
The sons of Uzzi'el: Mikha the chief and Yishshiyahu the second.
The sons of Merari: Makhli and Mushi. The sons of Makhli: El'azar and Kish.
El'azar died having no sons, but only daughters. Their kinsmen, the sons of Kish, married them.
The sons of Mushi: Makhli, Eder, and Yeremot, three.

These were the sons of Levi by their fathers' houses, the heads of the fathers' houses as they were listed according to the number of the names of the individuals from twenty years old and upward who did the work for the service of the house of YHWH.
For Dawid said, YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, has given rest to his people, and he dwells in Yerushalayim forever.
And so the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the things for its service.
For by the last words of Dawid the sons of Levi were numbered from twenty years old and upward.

For their duty was to assist the sons of Aharon for service in the house of YHWH, having the care of the courts and the chambers, the cleansing of all that is holy, and any work for the service of the house of Creator.

Their duty was also to assist with the showbread, the flour for the grain offering, the wafers of unleavened bread, the baked offering, the offering mixed with oil, and all measures of quantity and size.
And they were to stand every morning, thanking and praising YHWH, and likewise at evening,
And whenever burnt offerings were offered to YHWH on Shabbatot, new moons, and feast days, according to the number required of them, regularly before YHWH.
Thus they were to keep charge of the tent of meeting and the sanctuary, and to attend the sons of Aharon, their brothers, for the service of the house of YHWH.
The divisions of the sons of Aharon were these. The sons of Aharon: Nadav, Avihu, El'azar, and Itamar.
But Nadav and Avihu died before their father and had no children, so El'azar and Itamar became the priests.
With the help of Tzadok of the sons of El'azar and Akhimelekh of the sons of Itamar, Dawid organized them according to the appointed duties in their service.

Since more chief men were found among the sons of El'azar than among the sons of Itamar, they organized them under sixteen heads of fathers' houses of the sons of El'azar and eight of the sons of Itamar.
They divided them by lot, all alike, for there were sacred officers and officers of Creator among both the sons of El'azar and the sons of Itamar.

And the scribe Shemayah the son of Netanel, a Levite, recorded them in the presence of the king and the officials and Tzadok the priest and Akhimelekh the son of Evyatar and the heads of the fathers' houses of the priests and of the Levites, one father's house being chosen for El'azar and one chosen for Itamar.
The first lot fell to Yehoyariv, the second to Yedayah,
The third to Harim, the fourth to Se'orim,
The fifth to Malkiyah, the sixth to Miyamin,
The seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Aviyah,
The ninth to Yeshua, the tenth to Shekhanyahu,
The eleventh to Elyashiv, the twelfth to Yakim,
The thirteenth to Khuppah, the fourteenth to Yeshevav,
The fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
The seventeenth to Khezir, the eighteenth to Happitstetz,
The nineteenth to Petakhyah, the twentieth to Yekhezkel,
The twenty-first to Yakhin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
The twenty-third to Delayahu, the twenty-fourth to Ma'azyahu.

These had as their appointed duty in their service to come into the house of YHWH according to the procedure established for them by Aharon their father, as YHWH Creator of Yisra'EL had commanded him.
And of the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shuvael. Of the sons of Shuvael, Yakhdeyahu.
Of Rekhavyahu: of the sons of Rekhavyahu, Yishshiyahu the chief.
Of the Yitzharites, Shelomot. Of the sons of Shelomot, Yakhat.
The sons of Khevron: Yeriyahu the chief, Amaryahu the second, Yakhazi'el the third, Yekame'am the fourth.
The son of Uzzi'el, Mikha. Of the sons of Mikha, Shamir.
The brother of Mikha, Yishshiyahu. Of the sons of Yishshiyahu, Zekhariah.
The sons of Merari: Makhli and Mushi. The sons of Ya'aziyahu: Beno.
The sons of Merari: of Ya'aziyahu, Beno, Shoham, Zakkur, and Ivri.
Of Makhli: El'azar, who had no sons.
Of Kish, the son of Kish: Yerakhmeel.
The sons of Mushi: Makhli, Eder, and Yerimot. These were the sons of the Levites according to their fathers' houses.

These also, the heads of their fathers' houses and their younger brothers alike, cast lots, just as their brothers the sons of Aharon, in the presence of King Dawid and Tzadok and Akhimelekh and the heads of fathers' houses of the priests and the Levites.

Dawid and the commanders of the army set apart for the service the sons of Asaf, and of Heman, and of Yedutun, who prophesied with lyres, with harps, and with cymbals. The list of those who did the work and their service was:
Of the sons of Asaf: Zakkur, Yosef, Netanyah, and Asarel'ah, sons of Asaf, under the direction of Asaf, who prophesied under the direction of the king.

Of Yedutun, the sons of Yedutun: Gedaiyahu, Tzeri, Yeshayahu, Shimei, Khashabyahu, and Mattityahu, six, under the direction of their father Yedutun, who prophesied with the lyre in thanksgiving and praise to YHWH.
Of Heman, the sons of Heman: Bukkiyahu, Mattanyahu, Uzzi'el, Shevuel, Yerimot, Hananyahu, Khannani, Eli'ata, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Yoshbekashah, Malloti, Hotir, and Makhazioth.
All these were the sons of Heman the king's seer, according to the promise of Creator to exalt him, for Creator had given Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

They were all under the direction of their father for music in the house of YHWH with cymbals, harps, and lyres for the service of the house of Creator. Asaf, Yedutun, and Heman were under the order of the king.
The number of them along with their brothers, who were trained in singing to YHWH, all who were skillful, was 288.
And they cast lots for their duties, small and great, teacher and pupil alike.
The first lot fell for Asaf to Yosef. The second to Gedaiyahu, to him and his brothers and his sons, twelve.
The third to Zakkur, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The fourth to Yitzri, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The fifth to Netanyahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The sixth to Bukkiyahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The seventh to Yesarelah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The eighth to Yeshayahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The ninth to Mattanyahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The tenth to Shim'i, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The eleventh to Azarel, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twelfth to Khashabyahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The thirteenth to Shuvael, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The fourteenth to Mattityahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The fifteenth to Yeremot, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The sixteenth to Hananyahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The seventeenth to Yoshbekashah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The eighteenth to Khannani, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The nineteenth to Malloti, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twentieth to Elyatah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twenty-first to Hotir, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twenty-third to Makhazioth, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twenty-fourth to Romamti-Ezer, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
As for the divisions of the gatekeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemyahu the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaf.
And Meshelemyahu had sons: Zekhariyahu the firstborn, Yedia'el the second, Zevadyahu the third, Yatni'el the fourth,
Eilam the fifth, Yehohanan the sixth, Ely o'enai the seventh.
And Oved-Edom had sons: Shemayahu the firstborn, Yehozavad the second, Yo'akh the third, Sakar the fourth, Netanel the fifth,
Ammi'el the sixth, Yissachar the seventh, Pe'ultai the eighth, for Creator blessed him.
Also to his son Shemayahu were born sons who were rulers in their fathers' houses, for they were men of great ability.
The sons of Shemayahu: Otni, Refael, Oved, and Elzavad, whose brothers were able men, Elihu and Semakhyahu.
All these were of the sons of Oved-Edom with their sons and brothers, able men qualified for the service, sixty-two of Oved-Edom.
And Meshelemyahu had sons and brothers, able men, eighteen.
And Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief — for though he was not the firstborn, his father made him chief —
Khilkiyahu the second, Tevalyahu the third, Zekhariyahu the fourth. All the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen.
These divisions of the gatekeepers, corresponding to their chief men, had duties, just as their brothers did, ministering in the house of YHWH.
And they cast lots by fathers' houses, small and great alike, for their gates.
The lot for the east fell to Shelemyahu. They cast lots also for his son Zekhariyahu, a shrewd counselor, and his lot came out for the north.
Oved-Edom's lot came out for the south, and to his sons fell the gatehouse.
For Shuppim and Hosah it came out for the west, at the gate of Shallekheth on the road that goes up. Watch corresponded to watch.
On the east there were six Levites, on the north four a day, on the south four a day, as well as two and two at the storehouse.
For the colonnade on the west there were four at the road and two at the colonnade.
These were the divisions of the gatekeepers among the Korahites and the sons of Merari.
And of the Levites, Akhiyah had charge of the treasuries of the house of Creator and the treasuries of the dedicated gifts.
The sons of La'dan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to La'dan, the heads of the fathers' houses of La'dan the Gershonite: Yekhi'eli.
The sons of Yekhi'eli, Zetam, and Yo'el his brother, were in charge of the treasuries of the house of YHWH.
Of the Amramites, the Yitzharites, the Khevronites, and the Uzzi'elites —
And Shevuel the son of Gershom, son of Mosheh, was chief officer in charge of the treasuries.
His brothers: from Eli'ezer were his son Rekhavyahu, and his son Yeshayahu, and his son Yoram, and his son Zikhri, and his son Shelomot.

This Shelomot and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated gifts that Dawid the king and the heads of the fathers' houses and the officers of the thousands and the hundreds and the commanders of the army had dedicated.
From spoil won in battles they dedicated gifts for the maintenance of the house of YHWH.
Also all that Shemu'el the seer and Sha'ul the son of Kish and Avner the son of Ner and Yo'av the son of Tzeruyah had dedicated — all dedicated gifts were in the care of Shelomot and his brothers.
Of the Yitzharites, Kenanyahu and his sons were appointed to outside duties for Yisra'EL, as officers and judges.
Of the Khevronites, Khashabyahu and his brothers, 1,700 men of ability, had the oversight of Yisra'EL westward of the Yarden for all the work of YHWH and for the service of the king.

Of the Khevronites, Yeriyah was chief of the Khevronites of whatever genealogy or fathers' houses. In the fortieth year of Dawid's reign search was made and men of great ability among them were found at Yazer of Gil'ad.

King Dawid appointed him and his brothers, 2,700 men of ability, heads of fathers' houses, to have the oversight of the Re'uvenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Menasheh for everything pertaining to Creator and for the affairs of the king.

This is the list of the people of Yisra'EL, the heads of fathers' houses, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and their officers who served the king in all matters concerning the divisions that came and went, month after month throughout the year, each division numbering 24,000:
Yashov'am the son of Zavdi'el was in charge of the first division in the first month. In his division were 24,000.
He was a descendant of Peretz and was chief of all the commanders. He served in the first month.
Dodai the Ahohite was in charge of the division of the second month. Miklot was the chief officer of his division. In his division were 24,000.
The third commander, for the third month, was Benayahu the son of Yehoyada the chief priest. In his division were 24,000.
This is the Benayahu who was a mighty man of the thirty and in command of the thirty. His son Ammizavad was in charge of his division.
Asahel the brother of Yo'av was fourth, for the fourth month, and his son Zevadyahu after him. In his division were 24,000.
The fifth commander, for the fifth month, was Shamhut the Yizrahite. In his division were 24,000.
Sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. In his division were 24,000.
Seventh, for the seventh month, was Kheletz the Pelonite, of the sons of Efrayim. In his division were 24,000.
Eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites. In his division were 24,000.
Ninth, for the ninth month, was Avi'ezer the Antathite, of the Binyaminites. In his division were 24,000.
Tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netofathite, of the Zerahites. In his division were 24,000.
Eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benayahu the Piratonite, of the sons of Efrayim. In his division were 24,000.
Twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Kheldai the Netofathite, of Otni'el. In his division were 24,000.
Over the tribes of Yisra'EL: for the Re'uvenites, Eliezer the son of Zikhri was chief officer. For the Shim'onites, Shefatyahu the son of Ma'akhah.
For Levi, Khashabyahu the son of Kemu'el. For Aharon, Tzadok.
For Yehudah, Elihu, one of Dawid's brothers. For Yissachar, Omri the son of Mikha'el.
For Zevulun, Yishma'yahu the son of Ovadyahu. For Naftali, Yerimot the son of Azri'el.
For the sons of Efrayim, Hoshe'a the son of Azazyahu. For the half-tribe of Menasheh, Yo'el the son of Pedayahu.
For the half of Menasheh in Gil'ad, Iddo the son of Zekhariyahu. For Binyamin, Ya'asi'el the son of Avner.
For Dan, Azar'el the son of Yerokham. These were the commanders of the tribes of Yisra'EL.
Dawid did not number those below twenty years of age, for YHWH had promised to make Yisra'EL as many as the stars of heaven.
Yo'av the son of Tzeruyah began to count, but did not finish. Yet wrath came upon Yisra'EL for this, and the number was not entered in the chronicles of King Dawid.
Over the king's treasuries was Azmaveth the son of Adi'el. Over the treasuries in the country, in the cities, in the villages, and in the towers was Yehonatan the son of Uziyahu.
Over those who did the work of the field, tilling the soil, was Ezri the son of Kelub.
Over the vineyards was Shim'i the Ramathite. Over the produce of the vineyards for the wine cellars was Zavdi the Shafamite.
Over the olive trees and the sycamore trees in the Shephelah was Ba'al-Khanan the Gederite. Over the stores of oil was Yo'ash.
Over the herds that pastured in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite. Over the herds in the valleys was Shafat the son of Adlai.
Over the camels was Ovil the Yishmaelite. Over the donkeys was Yekhdeiyahu the Meronothite.
Over the flocks was Yaziz the Hagarite. All these were stewards of King Dawid's property.
Yonatan, Dawid's uncle, was a counselor, being a man of understanding and a scribe. He and Yekhiel the son of Khakhmoni attended the king's sons.
Akhitofel was the king's counselor. Khushai the Arkhite was the king's friend.
After Akhitofel came Yehoyada the son of Benayahu, and Evyatar. Yo'av was the commander of the king's army.

Dawid assembled at Yerushalayim all the officials of Yisra'EL, the officials of the tribes, the commanders of the divisions that served the king, the commanders of thousands, the commanders of hundreds, the stewards of all the property and livestock of the king and his sons, together with the palace officials, the mighty men and all the seasoned warriors.

Then King Dawid rose to his feet and said, Hear me, my brothers and my people. I had it in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of YHWH and for the footstool of our Creator, and I made preparations for building.
But Creator said to me, You may not build a house for my name, for you are a man of war and have shed blood.

Yet YHWH Creator of Yisra'EL chose me from all my father's house to be king over Yisra'EL forever. For he chose Yehudah as leader, and in the house of Yehudah my father's house, and among my father's sons he took pleasure in me to make me king over all Yisra'EL.
And of all my sons — for YHWH has given me many sons — he has chosen Shelomoh my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of YHWH over Yisra'EL.
He said to me, It is Shelomoh your son who shall build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.
I will establish his kingdom forever if he continues steadfast in keeping my commandments and my rules, as he is today.

Now therefore in the sight of all Yisra'EL, the assembly of YHWH, and in the hearing of our Creator, observe and seek out all the commandments of YHWH your Creator, that you may possess this good land and leave it for an inheritance to your children after you forever.

And you, Shelomoh my son, know the Creator of your father and serve him with a whole heart and with a willing mind, for YHWH searches all hearts and understands every plan and thought. If you seek him, he will be found by you, but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever.
Be careful now, for YHWH has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and do it.
Then Dawid gave Shelomoh his son the plan of the vestibule of the temple, and of its houses, its treasuries, its upper rooms, and its inner chambers, and of the room for the mercy seat.
And the plan of all that he had in mind for the courts of the house of YHWH, all the surrounding chambers, the treasuries of the house of Creator, and the treasuries for dedicated gifts.
For the divisions of the priests and of the Levites, and all the work of the service in the house of YHWH, for all the vessels for the service in the house of YHWH,
The weight of gold for all golden vessels for each service, the weight of silver vessels for each service,

The weight of the golden lampstands and their lamps, the weight of gold for each lampstand and its lamps, the weight of silver for a lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand in the service,
The weight of gold for each table for the showbread, the weight of silver for the silver tables,
And pure gold for the forks, the basins, and the cups, the weight of gold for each golden bowl, the weight of silver for each silver bowl,
The weight of refined gold for the altar of incense, and the plan of the golden chariot of the cherubim that spread their wings and covered the ark of the covenant of YHWH.
All this he made clear to me in writing from the hand of YHWH, all the work to be done according to the plan.

Then Dawid said to Shelomoh his son, Be strong and courageous and do it. Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed, for YHWH Creator, my Creator, is with you. He will not leave you or forsake you, until all the work for the service of the house of YHWH is finished.

And here are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of the house of Creator. There will be with you for all the work, for all the service, every willing man who has skill for any kind of service. Also the officers and all the people will be wholly at your command.
And King Dawid said to all the assembly, Shelomoh my son, whom alone Creator has chosen, is young and inexperienced, and the work is great, for the palace will not be for man but for YHWH Creator.

So I have provided for the house of my Creator, so far as I was able, the gold for the things of gold, the silver for the things of silver, and the bronze for the things of bronze, the iron for the things of iron, and wood for the things of wood, besides great quantities of onyx and stones for setting, antimony, colored stones, all sorts of precious stones, and marble.

Moreover, in addition to all that I have provided for the holy house, I have a treasure of my own of gold and silver, and because of my devotion to the house of my Creator I give it to the house of my Creator:
Three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ofir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, for overlaying the walls of the house.
The gold for the things of gold and the silver for the things of silver and for all the work to be done by craftsmen. Who then will offer willingly, consecrating himself today to YHWH?
Then the leaders of fathers' houses made their freewill offerings, as did also the leaders of the tribes, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officers over the king's work.
They gave for the service of the house of Creator 5,000 talents and 10,000 darics of gold, 10,000 talents of silver, 18,000 talents of bronze, and 100,000 talents of iron.
And whoever had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the house of YHWH, in the care of Yekhiel the Gershonite.
Then the people rejoiced because they had given willingly, for with a whole heart they had offered freely to YHWH. Dawid the king also rejoiced greatly.
Therefore Dawid blessed YHWH in the presence of all the assembly. And Dawid said, Blessed are you, O YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL our father, forever and ever.

Yours, O YHWH, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the victory and the majesty, for all that is in the heavens and in the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, O YHWH, and you are exalted as head above all.
Both riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all. In your hand are power and might, and in your hand it is to make great and to give strength to all.
And now we thank you, our Creator, and praise your glorious name.
But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able thus to offer willingly? For all things come from you, and of your own have we given you.
For we are strangers before you and sojourners, as all our fathers were. Our days on the earth are like a shadow, and there is no abiding.
O YHWH our Creator, all this abundance that we have provided for building you a house for your holy name comes from your hand and is all your own.

I know, my Creator, that you test the heart and have pleasure in uprightness. In the uprightness of my heart I have freely offered all these things, and now I have seen your people, who are present here, offering freely and joyously to you.
O YHWH, the Creator of Avraham, Yitzkhak, and Yisra'EL, our fathers, keep forever such purposes and thoughts in the hearts of your people, and direct their hearts toward you.
Grant to Shelomoh my son a whole heart that he may keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your statutes, performing all, and that he may build the palace for which I have made provision.
Then Dawid said to all the assembly, Bless YHWH your Creator. And all the assembly blessed YHWH, the Creator of their fathers, and bowed their heads and paid homage to YHWH and to the king.

And they offered sacrifices to YHWH, and on the next day offered burnt offerings to YHWH, 1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, and 1,000 lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Yisra'EL.
And they ate and drank before YHWH on that day with great gladness. And they made Shelomoh the son of Dawid king the second time, and anointed him as prince for YHWH, and Tzadok as priest.
Then Shelomoh sat on the throne of YHWH as king in place of Dawid his father. And he prospered, and all Yisra'EL obeyed him.
All the leaders and the mighty men, and also all the sons of King Dawid, pledged their allegiance to King Shelomoh.
And YHWH made Shelomoh very great in the sight of all Yisra'EL and bestowed on him such royal majesty as had not been on any king before him in Yisra'EL.
Thus Dawid the son of Yishai reigned over all Yisra'EL.
The time that he reigned over Yisra'EL was forty years. He reigned seven years in Khevron and thirty-three years in Yerushalayim.
Then he died in a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor. And Shelomoh his son reigned in his place.
Now the acts of King Dawid, from first to last, are written in the Chronicles of Shemu'el the seer, and in the Chronicles of Natan the prophet, and in the Chronicles of Gad the seer,
With accounts of all his rule and his might and of the circumstances that came upon him and upon Yisra'EL and upon all the kingdoms of the countries.
Shelomoh the son of Dawid established himself in his kingdom, and YHWH his Creator was with him and made him exceedingly great.
Shelomoh spoke to all Yisra'EL, to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader in all Yisra'EL, the heads of fathers' houses.
And Shelomoh, and all the assembly with him, went to the high place that was at Givon, for the tent of meeting of Creator, which Mosheh the servant of YHWH had made in the wilderness, was there.
But Dawid had brought up the ark of Creator from Kiryat-Ye'arim to the place that Dawid had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Yerushalayim.
Moreover, the bronze altar that Betzalel the son of Uri, son of Khur, had made, was there before the tabernacle of YHWH. And Shelomoh and the assembly sought it out.
And Shelomoh went up there to the bronze altar before YHWH, which was at the tent of meeting, and offered a thousand burnt offerings on it.
In that night Creator appeared to Shelomoh, and said to him, Ask what I shall give you.
And Shelomoh said to Creator, You have shown great and steadfast love to Dawid my father, and have made me king in his place.
O YHWH Creator, let your word to Dawid my father be now fulfilled, for you have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
Give me now wisdom and knowledge to go out and come in before this people, for who can govern this people of yours, which is so great?

Creator said to Shelomoh, Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked for possessions, wealth, honor, or the life of those who hate you, and have not even asked for long life, but have asked for wisdom and knowledge for yourself that you may govern my people over whom I have made you king,
Wisdom and knowledge are granted to you. I will also give you riches, possessions, and honor, such as none of the kings had who were before you, and none after you shall have the like.
So Shelomoh came from the high place at Givon, from before the tent of meeting, to Yerushalayim. And he reigned over Yisra'EL.
Shelomoh gathered together chariots and horsemen. He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Yerushalayim.
And the king made silver and gold as common in Yerushalayim as stone, and he made cedar as plentiful as the sycamore of the Shephelah.
And Shelomoh's import of horses was from Egypt and Kue, and the king's traders received them from Kue at a price.
They imported a chariot from Egypt for 600 shekels of silver, and a horse for 150. Likewise through them these were exported to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Syria.
Now Shelomoh purposed to build a house for the name of YHWH, and a royal palace for himself.
And Shelomoh assigned 70,000 men to bear burdens and 80,000 to quarry in the hill country, and 3,600 to oversee them.
And Shelomoh sent word to Khuram the king of Tzor: As you dealt with Dawid my father and sent him cedar to build himself a house to dwell in, so deal with me.

Behold, I am about to build a house for the name of YHWH my Creator and dedicate it to him for the burning of incense of sweet spices before him, and for the regular showbread, and for burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Shabbatot and the new moons and the appointed feasts of YHWH our Creator, as ordained forever for Yisra'EL.
The house that I am to build will be great, for our Creator is greater than all gods.
But who is able to build him a house, since heaven, even highest heaven, cannot contain him? Who am I to build a house for him, except as a place to make offerings before him?

So now send me a man skilled to work in gold, silver, bronze, and iron, and in purple, crimson, and blue fabrics, trained also in engraving, to be with the skilled workers who are with me in Yehudah and Yerushalayim, whom Dawid my father provided.
Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut timber in Lebanon. And my servants will be with your servants,
To prepare timber for me in abundance, for the house I am to build will be great and wonderful.
I will give for your servants, the woodcutters who cut timber, 20,000 cors of crushed wheat, 20,000 cors of barley, 20,000 baths of wine, and 20,000 baths of oil.
Then Khuram the king of Tzor answered in a letter that he sent to Shelomoh, Because YHWH loves his people, he has made you king over them.

Khuram also said, Blessed be YHWH Creator of Yisra'EL, who made heaven and earth, who has given King Dawid a wise son, who has discretion and understanding, who will build a temple for YHWH and a royal palace for himself.
Now I have sent a skilled man, endowed with understanding, Khuram-Avi,

The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tzor. He is trained to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, and in purple, blue, and crimson fabrics and fine linen, and to do all sorts of engraving and execute any design that may be assigned him, with your craftsmen, the craftsmen of my lord, Dawid your father.
Now therefore the wheat and barley, oil and wine, of which my lord has spoken, let him send to his servants.
And we will cut whatever timber you need from Lebanon and bring it to you in rafts by sea to Yapho, so that you may take it up to Yerushalayim.
Then Shelomoh counted all the resident aliens who were in the land of Yisra'EL, after the census of them that Dawid his father had taken, and there were found 153,600.
Seventy thousand of them he assigned to bear burdens, 80,000 to quarry in the hill country, and 3,600 as overseers to make the people work.

Then Shelomoh began to build the house of YHWH in Yerushalayim on Mount Moriyah, where YHWH had appeared to Dawid his father, at the place that Dawid had appointed, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Yevusite.
He began to build in the second month of the fourth year of his reign.
These are Solomon's measurements for building the house of Creator: the length, in cubits of the old standard, was sixty cubits, and the breadth twenty cubits.
The vestibule in front of the nave of the house was twenty cubits long, equal to the width of the house, and its height was 120 cubits. He overlaid it on the inside with pure gold.
The nave he lined with cypress and covered it with fine gold and made palms and chains on it.
He adorned the house with settings of precious stones. The gold was gold of Parvaim.
So he lined the house with gold — its beams, its thresholds, its walls, and its doors — and he carved cherubim on the walls.
And he made the Most Holy Place. Its length, corresponding to the breadth of the house, was twenty cubits, and its breadth was twenty cubits. He overlaid it with 600 talents of fine gold.
The weight of gold for the nails was fifty shekels. And he overlaid the upper chambers with gold.
In the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of wood and overlaid them with gold.

The wings of the cherubim together extended twenty cubits: one wing of the one, of five cubits, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, of five cubits, touched the wing of the other cherub.
And of this cherub, one wing, of five cubits, touched the wall of the house, and the other wing, also of five cubits, was joined to the wing of the first cherub.
The wings of these cherubim extended twenty cubits. The cherubim stood on their feet, facing the nave.
And he made the veil of blue and purple and crimson fabrics and fine linen, and he worked cherubim on it.
In front of the house he made two pillars thirty-five cubits high, with a capital of five cubits on the top of each.
He made chains like a necklace and put them on the tops of the pillars, and he made a hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.
He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the south, the other on the north. The one on the south he called Yakhin, and the one on the north Bo'az.
He made an altar of bronze, twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide and ten cubits high.
Then he made the sea of cast metal. It was round, ten cubits from brim to brim, and five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference.
Under it were figures of gourds, for ten cubits, compassing the sea all around. The gourds were in two rows, cast with it when it was cast.
It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The sea was set on them, and all their rear parts were inward.
Its thickness was a handbreadth. And its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It held 3,000 baths.

He also made ten lavers in which to wash, and set five on the south side, and five on the north side. In these they were to rinse off what was used for the burnt offering, and the sea was for the priests to wash in.
And he made ten golden lampstands as prescribed, and set them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north.
He also made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north. And he made a hundred basins of gold.
He made the court of the priests and the great court and doors for the court and overlaid their doors with bronze.
And he set the sea at the southeast corner of the house.
Khuram also made the pots, the shovels, and the basins. So Khuram finished the work that he did for King Shelomoh on the house of Creator:
The two pillars, the bowls, and the two capitals on the top of the pillars, and the two latticeworks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars,
And the 400 pomegranates for the two latticeworks, two rows of pomegranates for each latticework, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the pillars.
He made the stands also, and the lavers on the stands,
And the one sea, and the twelve oxen underneath it.
The pots, the shovels, the forks, and all the equipment for these Khuram-Avi made of burnished bronze for King Shelomoh for the house of YHWH.
In the plain of the Yarden the king cast them, in the clay ground between Sukkot and Tzeredah.
Shelomoh made all these things in great quantities, so that the weight of the bronze was not determined.
So Shelomoh made all the vessels that were in the house of Creator: the golden altar, the tables for the showbread,
The lampstands and their lamps of pure gold to burn before the inner sanctuary, as prescribed,
The flowers, the lamps, and the tongs, of purest gold,

The snuffers, basins, dishes for incense, and fire pans, of pure gold, and the sockets of the temple, for the inner doors to the Most Holy Place and for the doors of the nave of the temple were of gold.

Thus all the work that Shelomoh did for the house of YHWH was finished. And Shelomoh brought in the things that Dawid his father had dedicated, and stored the silver, the gold, and all the vessels in the treasuries of the house of Creator.

Then Shelomoh assembled the elders of Yisra'EL and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers' houses of the people of Yisra'EL, in Yerushalayim, to bring up the ark of the covenant of YHWH out of the city of Dawid, which is Tziyon.
And all the men of Yisra'EL assembled before the king at the feast that is in the seventh month.
And all the elders of Yisra'EL came, and the Levites took up the ark.
And they brought up the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent. The Levitical priests brought them up.
And King Shelomoh and all the congregation of Yisra'EL, who had assembled before him, were before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
So the priests brought the ark of the covenant of YHWH to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, to the Most Holy Place, underneath the wings of the cherubim.
The cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, so that the cherubim made a covering above the ark and its poles.
And the poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the Holy Place before the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen from outside. And they are there to this day.
There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Mosheh put there at Khoreiv, where YHWH made a covenant with the people of Yisra'EL, when they came out of Egypt.
And when the priests came out of the Holy Place — for all the priests who were present had consecrated themselves, without regard to their divisions —
And all the Levitical singers, Asaf, Heman, and Yedutun, their sons and kinsmen, arrayed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, stood east of the altar with 120 priests who were trumpeters,

And it was the duty of the trumpeters and singers to make themselves heard in unison in praise and thanksgiving to YHWH — and when the song was raised, with trumpets and cymbals and other musical instruments, in praise to YHWH, For he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever — the house, the house of YHWH, was filled with a cloud,
So that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of YHWH filled the house of Creator.
Then Shelomoh said, YHWH has said that he would dwell in thick darkness.
But I have built you an exalted house, a place for you to dwell in forever.
Then the king turned around and blessed all the assembly of Yisra'EL, while all the assembly of Yisra'EL stood.
And he said, Blessed be YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, who with his hand has fulfilled what he promised with his mouth to Dawid my father, saying,

Since the day that I brought my people out of the land of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Yisra'EL in which to build a house, that my name might be there, and I chose no man as leader over my people Yisra'EL.
But I have chosen Yerushalayim that my name may be there, and I have chosen Dawid to be over my people Yisra'EL.
Now it was in the heart of Dawid my father to build a house for the name of YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL.
But YHWH said to Dawid my father, Whereas it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart.
Nevertheless, it is not you who shall build the house, but your son who shall be born to you shall build the house for my name.

Now YHWH has fulfilled his promise that he made. For I have risen in the place of Dawid my father and sit on the throne of Yisra'EL, as YHWH promised, and I have built the house for the name of YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL.
And there I have set the ark, in which is the covenant of YHWH that he made with the people of Yisra'EL.
Then Shelomoh stood before the altar of YHWH in the presence of all the assembly of Yisra'EL and spread out his hands.

Shelomoh had made a bronze platform five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high, and had set it in the court, and he stood on it. Then he knelt on his knees in the presence of all the assembly of Yisra'EL, and spread out his hands toward heaven.
And said, O YHWH, Creator of Yisra'EL, there is no Creator like you, in heaven or on earth, keeping covenant and showing steadfast love to your servants who walk before you with all their heart.
You have kept with your servant Dawid my father what you declared to him. You spoke with your mouth, and with your hand have fulfilled it this day.

Now therefore, O YHWH, Creator of Yisra'EL, keep for your servant Dawid my father what you have promised him, saying, You shall not lack a man to sit before me on the throne of Yisra'EL, if only your sons pay close attention to their way, to walk in my Torah as you have walked before me.
Now therefore, O YHWH, Creator of Yisra'EL, let your word be confirmed, which you have spoken to your servant Dawid.
But will Creator indeed dwell with man on the earth? Behold, heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you. How much less this house that I have built.
Yet have regard to the prayer of your servant and to his plea, O YHWH my Creator, listening to the cry and to the prayer that your servant prays before you,
That your eyes may be open day and night toward this house, the place where you have promised to set your name, that you may listen to the prayer that your servant offers toward this place.
And listen to the pleas of your servant and of your people Yisra'EL, when they pray toward this place. And listen from heaven your dwelling place, and when you hear, forgive.
If a man sins against his neighbor and is made to take an oath and comes and swears his oath before your altar in this house,
Then hear from heaven and act and judge your servants, repaying the guilty by bringing his conduct on his own head, and vindicating the righteous by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
If your people Yisra'EL are defeated before the enemy because they have sinned against you, and they turn again and acknowledge your name and pray and plead with you in this house,
Then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your people Yisra'EL and bring them back to the land that you gave to them and to their fathers.
When heaven is shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, if they pray toward this place and acknowledge your name and turn from their sin, when you afflict them,

Then hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Yisra'EL, when you teach them the good way in which they should walk, and grant rain upon your land, which you have given to your people as an inheritance.

If there is famine in the land, if there is pestilence or blight or mildew or locust or caterpillar, if their enemies besiege them in the land at their gates, whatever plague, whatever sickness there is,
Whatever prayer, whatever plea is made by any man or by all your people Yisra'EL, each knowing his own affliction and his own sorrow and stretching out his hands toward this house,
Then hear from heaven your dwelling place and forgive and render to each whose heart you know, according to all his ways, for you, you only, know the hearts of the children of mankind,
That they may fear you and walk in your ways all the days that they live in the land that you gave to our fathers.

Likewise, when a foreigner, who is not of your people Yisra'EL, comes from a far country for the sake of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm, when he comes and prays toward this house,

Hear from heaven your dwelling place and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to you, in order that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as do your people Yisra'EL, and that they may know that this house that I have built is called by your name.
If your people go out to battle against their enemies, by whatever way you shall send them, and they pray to you toward this city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,
Then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and maintain their cause.
If they sin against you — for there is no one who does not sin — and you are angry with them and give them to an enemy, so that they are carried away captive to a land far or near,

Yet if they turn their heart in the land to which they have been carried captive, and repent and plead with you in the land of their captivity, saying, We have sinned and have acted perversely and wickedly,

If they repent with all their mind and with all their heart in the land of their captivity to which they were carried captive, and pray toward their land, which you gave to their fathers, the city that you have chosen, and the house that I have built for your name,
Then hear from heaven your dwelling place their prayer and their pleas, and maintain their cause and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
Now, O my Creator, let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
And now arise, O YHWH Creator, and go to your resting place, you and the ark of your might. Let your priests, O YHWH Creator, be clothed with salvation, and let your saints rejoice in your goodness.
O YHWH Creator, do not turn away the face of your anointed one. Remember your steadfast love for Dawid your servant.
As soon as Shelomoh finished his prayer, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of YHWH filled the temple.
And the priests could not enter the house of YHWH, because the glory of YHWH filled YHWH's house.

When all the people of Yisra'EL saw the fire come down and the glory of YHWH on the temple, they bowed down with their faces to the ground on the pavement and worshiped and gave thanks to YHWH, saying, For he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever.
Then the king and all the people offered sacrifice before YHWH.
King Shelomoh offered as a sacrifice 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated the house of Creator.

The priests stood at their posts; the Levites also, with the instruments for music to YHWH that King Dawid had made for giving thanks to YHWH — for his steadfast love endures forever — whenever Dawid offered praises by their ministry. Opposite them the priests sounded trumpets, and all Yisra'EL stood.

And Shelomoh consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of YHWH, for there he offered the burnt offering and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that Shelomoh had made could not hold the burnt offering and the grain offering and the fat.
At that time Shelomoh held the feast for seven days, and all Yisra'EL with him, a very great assembly, from Levo-Hamat to the Brook of Egypt.
And on the eighth day they held a solemn assembly, for they had kept the dedication of the altar seven days and the feast seven days.

On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their homes, joyful and glad of heart for the prosperity that YHWH had granted to Dawid and to Shelomoh and to Yisra'EL his people.
Thus Shelomoh finished the house of YHWH and the king's house. All that Shelomoh had planned to do in the house of YHWH and in his own house he successfully accomplished.
Then YHWH appeared to Shelomoh in the night and said to him, I have heard your prayer and have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.
When I shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, or command the locust to devour the land, or send pestilence among my people,
If my people who are called by my name humble themselves, and pray and seek my face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven and will forgive their sin and heal their land.
Now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayer that is made in this place.
For now I have chosen and consecrated this house that my name may be there forever. My eyes and my heart will be there for all time.
And as for you, if you walk before me as Dawid your father walked, doing according to all that I have commanded you and keeping my statutes and my rules,
Then I will establish your royal throne, as I covenanted with Dawid your father, saying, You shall not lack a man to rule Yisra'EL.
But if you turn aside and forsake my statutes and my commandments that I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and worship them,

Then I will pluck you up from my land that I have given you, and this house that I have consecrated for my name, I will cast out of my sight, and I will make it a proverb and a byword among all peoples.
And at this house, which was exalted, everyone passing by will be astonished and say, Why has YHWH done thus to this land and to this house?

Then they will say, Because they abandoned YHWH, the Creator of their fathers who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold on other gods and worshiped them and served them. Therefore he has brought all this disaster on them.
At the end of twenty years, in which Shelomoh had built the house of YHWH and his own house,
Shelomoh rebuilt the cities that Khuram had given to him, and settled the people of Yisra'EL in them.
And Shelomoh went to Hamat-Tzovah and took it.
He built Tadmor in the wilderness and all the store cities that he built in Hamat.
He also built Upper Beit-Khoron and Lower Beit-Khoron, fortified cities with walls, gates, and bars,

And Ba'alat and all the store cities that Shelomoh had and all the cities for his chariots and the cities for his horsemen, and whatever Shelomoh desired to build in Yerushalayim, in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.
All the people who were left of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Yevusites, who were not of Yisra'EL,
From their descendants who were left after them in the land, whom the people of Yisra'EL had not destroyed — these Shelomoh drafted as forced labor, and so they are to this day.
But of the people of Yisra'EL Shelomoh made no slaves for his work; they were soldiers, and his officers, the commanders of his chariots, and his horsemen.
And these were the chief officers of King Shelomoh, 250, who exercised authority over the people.

Shelomoh brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the city of Dawid to the house that he had built for her, for he said, My wife shall not live in the house of Dawid king of Yisra'EL, for the places to which the ark of YHWH has come are holy.
Then Shelomoh offered up burnt offerings to YHWH on the altar of YHWH that he had built before the vestibule,

As the duty of each day required, offering according to the commandment of Mosheh for the Shabbatot, the new moons, and the three annual feasts — the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Booths.

According to the ruling of Dawid his father, he appointed the divisions of the priests for their service, and the Levites for their offices of praise and ministry before the priests as the duty of each day required, and the gatekeepers in their divisions at each gate, for so Dawid the man of Creator had commanded.
And they did not turn aside from what the king had commanded the priests and Levites concerning any matter and concerning the treasuries.
Thus was accomplished all the work of Shelomoh from the day the foundation of the house of YHWH was laid until it was finished. So the house of YHWH was completed.
Then Shelomoh went to Etzyon-Gever and Elot on the shore of the sea, in the land of Edom.

And Khuram sent to him by the hand of his servants ships and servants familiar with the sea, and they went to Ofir together with the servants of Shelomoh and brought from there 450 talents of gold and brought it to King Shelomoh.

Now when the queen of Sheva heard of the fame of Shelomoh, she came to Yerushalayim to test him with hard questions, having a very great retinue and camels bearing spices and very much gold and precious stones. And when she came to Shelomoh, she told him all that was on her mind.
And Shelomoh answered all her questions. There was nothing hidden from Shelomoh that he could not explain to her.
And when the queen of Sheva had seen the wisdom of Shelomoh, the house that he had built,

The food of his table, the seating of his officials, and the attendance of his servants, and their clothing, his cupbearers, and their clothing, and his burnt offerings that he offered at the house of YHWH, there was no more breath in her.
And she said to the king, The report was true that I heard in my own land of your words and of your wisdom,
But I did not believe the reports until I came and my own eyes had seen it. And behold, half the greatness of your wisdom was not told me. You surpass the report that I heard.
Happy are your men. Happy are your servants, who continually stand before you and hear your wisdom.

Blessed be YHWH your Creator, who has delighted in you and set you on his throne as king for YHWH your Creator. Because your Creator loved Yisra'EL and would establish them forever, he has made you king over them, that you may execute justice and righteousness.
Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, and a very great quantity of spices, and precious stones. There were no spices such as those that the queen of Sheva gave to King Shelomoh.
Moreover, the servants of Khuram and the servants of Shelomoh, who brought gold from Ofir, also brought algum wood and precious stones.
And the king made from the algum wood steps for the house of YHWH and for the king's house, lyres also and harps for the singers. There were none such as these seen before in the land of Yehudah.
And King Shelomoh gave to the queen of Sheva all that she desired, whatever she asked besides what she had brought to the king. So she turned and went back to her own land with her servants.
Now the weight of gold that came to Shelomoh in one year was 666 talents of gold,
Besides that which the explorers and merchants brought. And all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land brought gold and silver to Shelomoh.
King Shelomoh made 200 large shields of beaten gold. Six hundred shekels of beaten gold went into each shield.
And he made 300 shields of beaten gold. Three hundred shekels of gold went into each shield, and the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king also made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with pure gold.
The throne had six steps and a footstool of gold, which were attached to the throne, and on each side of the seat were armrests and two lions standing beside the armrests,
While twelve lions stood there, one on each end of a step on the six steps. The like of it was never made in any kingdom.
All King Shelomoh's drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold. Silver was not considered as anything in the days of Shelomoh.
For the king's ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Khuram. Once every three years the ships of Tarshish used to come bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
Thus King Shelomoh excelled all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.
And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Shelomoh to hear his wisdom, which Creator had put into his mind.
Every one of them brought his present, articles of silver and of gold, garments, myrrh, spices, horses, and mules, so much year by year.
And Shelomoh had 4,000 stalls for horses and chariots, and 12,000 horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Yerushalayim.
And he ruled over all the kings from the Euphrates to the land of the Pelishtim and to the border of Egypt.
The king made silver as common in Yerushalayim as stone, and he made cedar as plentiful as the sycamore of the Shephelah.
And horses were imported for Shelomoh from Egypt and from all lands.

Now the rest of the acts of Shelomoh, from first to last, are they not written in the history of Natan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahiyah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Yarov'am the son of Nevat?
Shelomoh reigned in Yerushalayim over all Yisra'EL forty years.
And Shelomoh slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of Dawid his father, and Rekhavam his son reigned in his place.
Rekhavam went to Shekhem, for all Yisra'EL had come to Shekhem to make him king.
And as soon as Yarov'am the son of Nevat heard of it — for he was in Egypt, where he had fled from King Shelomoh — Yarov'am returned from Egypt.
And they sent and called him. And Yarov'am and all Yisra'EL came and said to Rekhavam,
Your father made our yoke heavy. Now therefore lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke on us, and we will serve you.
He said to them, Come to me again in three days. So the people went away.
Then King Rekhavam took counsel with the old men, who had stood before Shelomoh his father while he was yet alive, saying, How do you advise me to answer this people?
And they said to him, If you will be good to this people and please them and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants forever.
But he abandoned the counsel that the old men gave him, and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him and stood before him.
And he said to them, What do you advise that we answer this people who have said to me, Lighten the yoke that your father put on us?

And the young men who had grown up with him said to him, Thus shall you speak to the people who said to you, Your father made our yoke heavy, but you lighten it for us. Thus shall you say to them, My little finger is thicker than my father's thigh.
And now, whereas my father laid on you a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.
So Yarov'am and all the people came to Rekhavam the third day, as the king had said, Come to me again the third day.
And the king answered them harshly. And King Rekhavam abandoned the counsel of the old men

And spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.
So the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turn of affairs brought about by Creator that YHWH might fulfill his word, which he spoke by Ahiyah the Shilonite to Yarov'am the son of Nevat.

And when all Yisra'EL saw that the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king, What portion have we in Dawid? We have no inheritance in the son of Yishai. Each of you to your tents, O Yisra'EL. Look now to your own house, Dawid. So all Yisra'EL went to their tents.
But Rekhavam reigned over the people of Yisra'EL who lived in the cities of Yehudah.

Then King Rekhavam sent Hadoram, who was taskmaster over the forced labor, and the people of Yisra'EL stoned him to death with stones. And King Rekhavam quickly mounted his chariot to flee to Yerushalayim.
So Yisra'EL has been in rebellion against the house of Dawid to this day.
When Rekhavam came to Yerushalayim, he assembled the house of Yehudah and Binyamin, 180,000 chosen warriors, to fight against Yisra'EL, to restore the kingdom to Rekhavam.
But the word of YHWH came to Shemayah the man of Creator:
Say to Rekhavam the son of Shelomoh, king of Yehudah, and to all Yisra'EL in Yehudah and Binyamin,

Thus says YHWH, You shall not go up or fight against your relatives. Return every man to his home, for this thing is from me. So they listened to the word of YHWH and returned and did not go against Yarov'am.
Rekhavam lived in Yerushalayim, and he built cities for defense in Yehudah.
He built Beit-Lekhem, Etam, Tekoa,
Beit-Tzur, Sokho, Adullam,
Gat, Mareshah, Ziph,
Adorayim, Lakhish, Azekah,
Tzorah, Ayalon, and Khevron, fortified cities that are in Yehudah and in Binyamin.
