He made the fortresses strong and put commanders in them and stores of food, oil, and wine.
And he put shields and spears in all the cities and made them very strong. So he held Yehudah and Binyamin.
And the priests and the Levites who were in all Yisra'EL presented themselves to him from all their territories.
For the Levites left their common lands and their holdings and came to Yehudah and Yerushalayim, because Yarov'am and his sons cast them out from serving as priests to YHWH,
And he appointed his own priests for the high places and for the goat idols and for the calves that he had made.
And those who had set their hearts to seek YHWH Creator of Yisra'EL came after them from all the tribes of Yisra'EL to Yerushalayim to sacrifice to YHWH, the Creator of their fathers.
They strengthened the kingdom of Yehudah, and for three years they made Rekhavam the son of Shelomoh secure, for they walked for three years in the way of Dawid and Shelomoh.
Rekhavam took as wife Makhalat the daughter of Yerimot the son of Dawid and of Avikha'il the daughter of Eli'av the son of Yishai.
And she bore him sons: Ye'ush, Shemaryahu, and Zaham.
After her he took Ma'akhah the daughter of Avshalom, who bore him Aviyah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomit.
Rekhavam loved Ma'akhah the daughter of Avshalom above all his wives and concubines — he took eighteen wives and sixty concubines and fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
And Rekhavam appointed Aviyah the son of Ma'akhah as chief prince among his brothers, for he intended to make him king.
And he dealt wisely and distributed some of his sons through all the districts of Yehudah and Binyamin, in all the fortified cities, and he gave them abundant provisions and procured wives for them.
When the rule of Rekhavam was established and he was strong, he abandoned the Torah of YHWH, and all Yisra'EL with him.
In the fifth year of King Rekhavam, because they had been unfaithful to YHWH, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Yerushalayim
With 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen. And the people were without number who came with him from Egypt — Lubim, Sukkiim, and Kushim.
And he took the fortified cities of Yehudah and came as far as Yerushalayim.

Then Shemayah the prophet came to Rekhavam and to the princes of Yehudah, who had gathered at Yerushalayim because of Shishak, and said to them, Thus says YHWH, You abandoned me, so I have abandoned you to the hand of Shishak.
Then the princes of Yisra'EL and the king humbled themselves and said, YHWH is righteous.

When YHWH saw that they humbled themselves, the word of YHWH came to Shemayah, They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance, and my wrath shall not be poured out on Yerushalayim by the hand of Shishak.
Nevertheless, they shall be servants to him, so that they may know the difference between serving me and serving the kingdoms of the countries.

So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Yerushalayim. He took away the treasures of the house of YHWH and the treasures of the king's house. He took away everything. He also took away the shields of gold that Shelomoh had made.
And King Rekhavam made in their place shields of bronze and committed them to the hands of the officers of the guard, who kept the door of the king's house.
And as often as the king went into the house of YHWH, the guard came and carried them and brought them back to the guardroom.
And when he humbled himself the wrath of YHWH turned from him, so as not to make a complete destruction. Moreover, conditions were good in Yehudah.

So King Rekhavam grew strong in Yerushalayim and reigned. Rekhavam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Yerushalayim, the city that YHWH had chosen out of all the tribes of Yisra'EL to put his name there. His mother's name was Na'amah the Ammonite.
And he did evil, for he did not set his heart to seek YHWH.
Now the acts of Rekhavam, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Shemayah the prophet and of Iddo the seer? There were continual wars between Rekhavam and Yarov'am.
And Rekhavam slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of Dawid, and Aviyah his son reigned in his place.
In the eighteenth year of King Yarov'am, Aviyah began to reign over Yehudah.
He reigned for three years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Mikha'yahu the daughter of Uri'el of Givah. Now there was war between Aviyah and Yarov'am.
Aviyah went out to battle having an army of valiant men of war, 400,000 chosen men. And Yarov'am drew up his forces against him with 800,000 chosen mighty warriors.
Then Aviyah stood up on Mount Tzemarayim, which is in the hill country of Efrayim, and said, Hear me, O Yarov'am and all Yisra'EL.
Ought you not to know that YHWH Creator of Yisra'EL gave the kingship over Yisra'EL forever to Dawid and his sons by a covenant of salt?
Yet Yarov'am the son of Nevat, a servant of Shelomoh the son of Dawid, rose up and rebelled against his lord,
And certain worthless scoundrels gathered about him and defied Rekhavam the son of Shelomoh, when Rekhavam was young and irresolute and could not withstand them.
And now you think to withstand the kingdom of YHWH in the hand of the sons of Dawid, because you are a great multitude and have with you the golden calves that Yarov'am made you for gods.

Have you not driven out the priests of YHWH, the sons of Aharon, and the Levites, and made priests for yourselves like the peoples of other lands? Whoever comes for ordination with a young bull or seven rams becomes a priest of what are not gods.
But as for us, YHWH is our Creator, and we have not forsaken him. We have priests ministering to YHWH who are sons of Aharon, and Levites for their service.

They offer to YHWH every morning and every evening burnt offerings and incense of sweet spices, set out the showbread on the table of pure gold, and care for the golden lampstand so that its lamps burn every evening. For we keep the charge of YHWH our Creator, but you have forsaken him.

Behold, Creator is with us at our head, and his priests with their battle trumpets to sound the call to battle against you. O people of Yisra'EL, do not fight against YHWH, the Creator of your fathers, for you cannot succeed.
Yarov'am had sent an ambush around to come upon them from behind. Thus his troops were in front of Yehudah, and the ambush was behind them.
And when Yehudah looked, behold, the battle was in front of and behind them. And they cried to YHWH, and the priests blew the trumpets.
Then the men of Yehudah raised the battle shout. And when the men of Yehudah shouted, Creator defeated Yarov'am and all Yisra'EL before Aviyah and Yehudah.
The men of Yisra'EL fled before Yehudah, and Creator gave them into their hand.
Aviyah and his people struck them with great force, so there fell slain of Yisra'EL 500,000 chosen men.
Thus the people of Yisra'EL were subdued at that time, and the people of Yehudah prevailed, because they relied on YHWH, the Creator of their fathers.
And Aviyah pursued Yarov'am and took cities from him, Beit-El with its villages and Yeshanah with its villages and Efron with its villages.
Yarov'am did not recover his power in the days of Aviyah. And YHWH struck him down, and he died.
But Aviyah grew mighty. And he took fourteen wives and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
The rest of the acts of Aviyah, his ways and his sayings, are written in the story of the prophet Iddo.
Aviyah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of Dawid. And Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land had rest for ten years.
And Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of YHWH his Creator.
He took away the foreign altars and the high places and broke down the pillars and cut down the Asherim
And commanded Yehudah to seek YHWH, the Creator of their fathers, and to keep the Torah and the commandment.
He also took out of all the cities of Yehudah the high places and the incense altars. And the kingdom had rest under him.
He built fortified cities in Yehudah, for the land had rest. He had no war in those years, for YHWH gave him peace.

And he said to Yehudah, Let us build these cities and surround them with walls and towers, gates and bars. The land is still ours, because we have sought YHWH our Creator. We have sought him, and he has given us peace on every side. So they built and prospered.
And Asa had an army of 300,000 from Yehudah, armed with large shields and spears, and 280,000 men from Binyamin that carried shields and drew bows. All these were mighty men of valor.
Zerah the Kushite came out against them with an army of a million men and 300 chariots, and came as far as Mareshah.
And Asa went out to meet him, and they drew up their lines of battle in the Valley of Tzefatah at Mareshah.

And Asa cried to YHWH his Creator, O YHWH, there is none like you to help, between the mighty and the weak. Help us, O YHWH our Creator, for we rely on you, and in your name we have come against this multitude. O YHWH, you are our Creator. Let not man prevail against you.
So YHWH defeated the Kushites before Asa and before Yehudah, and the Kushites fled.

Asa and the people who were with him pursued them as far as Gerar, and the Kushites fell until none remained alive, for they were broken before YHWH and his army. The men of Yehudah carried away very much spoil.
And they attacked all the cities around Gerar, for the fear of YHWH was upon them. They plundered all the cities, for there was much plunder in them.
And they also attacked the tents of those who had livestock and carried away sheep in abundance and camels. Then they returned to Yerushalayim.
The Spirit of Creator came upon Azaryahu the son of Oded,

And he went out to meet Asa and said to him, Hear me, Asa, and all Yehudah and Binyamin: YHWH is with you while you are with him. If you seek him, he will be found by you, but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.
For a long time Yisra'EL was without the true Creator, and without a teaching priest and without Torah.
But when in their distress they turned to YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, and sought him, he was found by them.
In those times there was no peace to him who went out or to him who came in, for great disturbances afflicted all the inhabitants of the lands.
They were broken in pieces. Nation was crushed by nation and city by city, for Creator troubled them with every sort of distress.
But you, take courage. Do not let your hands be weak, for your work shall be rewarded.

As soon as Asa heard these words, the prophecy of Azaryahu the son of Oded, he took courage and put away the abominable idols from all the land of Yehudah and Binyamin and from the cities that he had taken in the hill country of Efrayim, and he repaired the altar of YHWH that was in front of the vestibule of the house of YHWH.

And he gathered all Yehudah and Binyamin, and those from Efrayim, Menasheh, and Shim'on who were residing with them, for great numbers had deserted to him from Yisra'EL when they saw that YHWH his Creator was with him.
They were gathered at Yerushalayim in the third month of the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.
They sacrificed to YHWH on that day from the spoil that they had brought, 700 oxen and 7,000 sheep.
And they entered into a covenant to seek YHWH, the Creator of their fathers, with all their heart and with all their soul,
But that whoever would not seek YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, should be put to death, whether young or old, man or woman.
They swore an oath to YHWH with a loud voice and with shouting and with trumpets and with horns.
And all Yehudah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and had sought him with their whole desire, and he was found by them, and YHWH gave them rest on every side.
Even Ma'akhah, his mother, King Asa removed from being queen mother because she had made a detestable image for Asherah. Asa cut down her image, crushed it, and burned it at the brook Kidron.
But the high places were not taken out of Yisra'EL. Nevertheless, the heart of Asa was wholly true all his days.
And he brought into the house of Creator the sacred gifts of his father and his own sacred gifts: silver, gold, and vessels.
And there was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.
In the thirty-sixth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha king of Yisra'EL went up against Yehudah and built Ramah, that he might permit no one to go out or come in to Asa king of Yehudah.
Then Asa took silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of YHWH and the king's house and sent them to Ben-Hadad king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, saying,

There is a covenant between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Behold, I am sending to you silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Yisra'EL, that he may withdraw from me.
And Ben-Hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Yisra'EL, and they conquered Iyon, Dan, Abel-mayim, and all the store cities of Naftali.
And when Baasha heard of it, he stopped building Ramah and let his work cease.
Then King Asa took all Yehudah, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber, with which Baasha had been building, and with them he built Geva and Mitzpah.

At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Yehudah and said to him, Because you relied on the king of Syria, and did not rely on YHWH your Creator, the army of the king of Syria has escaped you.
Were not the Kushites and the Lubim a huge army with very many chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on YHWH, he gave them into your hand.
For the eyes of YHWH range throughout the earth, to give strong support to those whose heart is blameless toward him. You have done foolishly in this, for from now on you will have wars.
Then Asa was angry with the seer and put him in the stocks in prison, for he was in a rage with him because of this. And Asa inflicted cruelties upon some of the people at the same time.
The acts of Asa, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Yehudah and Yisra'EL.
In the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa was diseased in his feet, and his disease became severe. Yet even in his disease he did not seek YHWH, but sought help from physicians.
And Asa slept with his fathers, dying in the forty-first year of his reign.

They buried him in the tomb that he had cut for himself in the city of Dawid. They laid him on a bier that had been filled with various kinds of spices prepared by the perfumers' art, and they made a very great fire in his honor.
Yehoshafat his son reigned in his place and strengthened himself against Yisra'EL.
He placed forces in all the fortified cities of Yehudah and set garrisons in the land of Yehudah, and in the cities of Efrayim that Asa his father had captured.
YHWH was with Yehoshafat, because he walked in the earlier ways of his father Dawid. He did not seek the Ba'alim,
But sought the Creator of his father and walked in his commandments, and not according to the practices of Yisra'EL.
Therefore YHWH established the kingdom in his hand. And all Yehudah brought tribute to Yehoshafat, and he had great riches and honor.
His heart was courageous in the ways of YHWH. And furthermore, he took the high places and the Asherim out of Yehudah.
In the third year of his reign he sent his officials, Ben-Khayil, Ovadyahu, Zekhariyahu, Netanel, and Mikha'yahu, to teach in the cities of Yehudah.
And with them the Levites, Shemayahu, Netanyahu, Zevadyahu, Asahel, Shemiramot, Yehonatan, Adoniahu, Toviyahu, and Tov-Adoniyahu; and with these Levites, the priests Elishama and Yehoram.
And they taught in Yehudah, having the Book of the Torah of YHWH with them. They went about through all the cities of Yehudah and taught among the people.
And the fear of YHWH fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were around Yehudah, and they made no war against Yehoshafat.
Some of the Pelishtim brought Yehoshafat presents and silver for tribute, and the Arabians also brought him 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats.
And Yehoshafat grew steadily greater. He built in Yehudah fortresses and store cities.
He had large supplies in the cities of Yehudah. He had soldiers, mighty men of valor, in Yerushalayim.
This was the muster of them by fathers' houses: Of Yehudah, the commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, with 300,000 mighty men of valor.
And next to him Yehohanan the commander, with 280,000.
And next to him Amasiah the son of Zikhri, a volunteer for the service of YHWH, with 200,000 mighty men of valor.
Of Binyamin: Elyada, a mighty man of valor, with 200,000 men armed with bow and shield.
And next to him Yehozavad with 180,000 armed for war.
These were in the service of the king, besides those whom the king had placed in the fortified cities throughout all Yehudah.
Now Yehoshafat had great riches and honor, and he made a marriage alliance with Akhav.
After some years he went down to Akhav in Samaria. And Akhav killed an abundance of sheep and oxen for him and for the people who were with him, and enticed him to go up against Ramot-Gil'ad.
Akhav king of Yisra'EL said to Yehoshafat king of Yehudah, Will you go with me to Ramot-Gil'ad? He answered him, I am as you are, my people as your people. We will be with you in the war.
And Yehoshafat said to the king of Yisra'EL, Inquire first for the word of YHWH.

Then the king of Yisra'EL gathered the prophets together, 400 men, and said to them, Shall we go to battle against Ramot-Gil'ad, or shall I refrain? And they said, Go up, for Creator will give it into the hand of the king.
But Yehoshafat said, Is there not here another prophet of YHWH of whom we may inquire?

And the king of Yisra'EL said to Yehoshafat, There is yet one man by whom we may inquire of YHWH, Mikha'yahu the son of Yimla, but I hate him, for he never prophesies good concerning me, but always evil. And Yehoshafat said, Let not the king say so.
Then the king of Yisra'EL summoned an officer and said, Bring quickly Mikha'yahu the son of Yimla.

Now the king of Yisra'EL and Yehoshafat the king of Yehudah were sitting on their thrones, arrayed in their robes. And they were sitting at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
And Tzidkiyahu the son of Kena'anah made for himself horns of iron and said, Thus says YHWH, With these you shall push the Syrians until they are destroyed.
And all the prophets prophesied so and said, Go up to Ramot-Gil'ad and triumph. YHWH will give it into the hand of the king.

And the messenger who went to summon Mikha'yahu said to him, Behold, the words of the prophets with one accord are favorable to the king. Let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak favorably.
But Mikha'yahu said, As YHWH lives, what my Creator says, that I will speak.
And when he had come to the king, the king said to him, Mikha'yahu, shall we go to Ramot-Gil'ad to battle, or shall I refrain? And he answered, Go up and triumph. They will be given into your hand.
But the king said to him, How many times shall I make you swear that you speak to me nothing but the truth in the name of YHWH?
And he said, I saw all Yisra'EL scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd. And YHWH said, These have no master. Let each return to his home in peace.
And the king of Yisra'EL said to Yehoshafat, Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?
And Mikha'yahu said, Therefore hear the word of YHWH: I saw YHWH sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing on his right hand and on his left.
And YHWH said, Who will entice Akhav the king of Yisra'EL, that he may go up and fall at Ramot-Gil'ad? And one said one thing, and another said another.
Then a spirit came forward and stood before YHWH, saying, I will entice him. And YHWH said to him, By what means?
And he said, I will go out, and will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, You are to entice him, and you shall succeed. Go out and do so.
Now therefore behold, YHWH has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these your prophets. YHWH has declared disaster for you.
Then Tzidkiyahu the son of Kena'anah came near and struck Mikha'yahu on the cheek and said, Which way did the Spirit of YHWH go from me to speak to you?
And Mikha'yahu said, Behold, you shall see on that day when you go into an inner chamber to hide yourself.
And the king of Yisra'EL said, Seize Mikha'yahu and take him back to Amon the governor of the city and to Yo'ash the king's son,
And say, Thus says the king, Put this fellow in prison and feed him with meager rations of bread and water until I return in peace.
And Mikha'yahu said, If you return in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me. Hear, all you peoples.
So the king of Yisra'EL and Yehoshafat the king of Yehudah went up to Ramot-Gil'ad.
And the king of Yisra'EL said to Yehoshafat, I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your robes. So the king of Yisra'EL disguised himself, and they went into battle.
Now the king of Syria had commanded the captains of his chariots, Fight with neither small nor great, but only with the king of Yisra'EL.

And when the captains of the chariots saw Yehoshafat, they said, It is the king of Yisra'EL. So they turned to fight against him. And Yehoshafat cried out, and YHWH helped him. Creator drew them away from him.
For when the captains of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Yisra'EL, they turned back from pursuing him.

But a certain man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Yisra'EL between the scale armor and the breastplate. Therefore he said to the driver of his chariot, Turn around and carry me out of the battle, for I am wounded.
And the battle continued that day, and the king of Yisra'EL was propped up in his chariot facing the Syrians until evening. Then at sunset he died.
Yehoshafat the king of Yehudah returned in safety to his house in Yerushalayim.

But Yehu the son of Khanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Yehoshafat, Should you help the wicked and love those who hate YHWH? Because of this, wrath has gone out against you from YHWH.
Nevertheless, some good is found in you, for you destroyed the Asheroth out of the land, and have set your heart to seek Creator.
Yehoshafat lived at Yerushalayim. And he went out again among the people, from Be'er-Sheva to the hill country of Efrayim, and brought them back to YHWH, the Creator of their fathers.
He appointed judges in the land in all the fortified cities of Yehudah, city by city,
And said to the judges, Consider what you do, for you judge not for man but for YHWH. He is with you in giving judgment.
Now then, let the fear of YHWH be upon you. Be careful what you do, for there is no injustice with YHWH our Creator, or partiality or taking bribes.

Moreover, in Yerushalayim Yehoshafat appointed certain Levites and priests and heads of fathers' houses of Yisra'EL, to give judgment for YHWH and to decide disputed cases. They had their seat at Yerushalayim.
And he charged them, Thus you shall do in the fear of YHWH, in faithfulness, and with your whole heart.

Whenever a case comes to you from your brothers who live in their cities, concerning bloodshed, law or commandment, statutes or rules, you shall warn them, that they may not incur guilt before YHWH and wrath may not come upon you and your brothers. Thus you shall do, and you will not incur guilt.

And behold, Amaryahu the chief priest is over you in all matters of YHWH, and Zevadyahu the son of Yishma'el, the governor of the house of Yehudah, in all the king's matters, and the Levites will serve you as officers. Deal courageously, and may YHWH be with the upright.
After this the Moabites and Ammonites, and with them some of the Me'unites, came against Yehoshafat for battle.
Some men came and told Yehoshafat, A great multitude is coming against you from Edom, from beyond the sea, and, behold, they are in Khatzetzon-Tamar, that is, En-Gedi.
Then Yehoshafat was afraid and set his face to seek YHWH, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Yehudah.
And Yehudah assembled to seek help from YHWH. From all the cities of Yehudah they came to seek YHWH.
And Yehoshafat stood in the assembly of Yehudah and Yerushalayim, in the house of YHWH, before the new court,
And said, O YHWH, Creator of our fathers, are you not Creator in heaven? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. In your hand are power and might, so that none is able to withstand you.
Did you not, our Creator, drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Yisra'EL, and give it forever to the descendants of Avraham your friend?
And they have lived in it and have built for you in it a sanctuary for your name, saying,

If disaster comes upon us, the sword, judgment, or pestilence, or famine, we will stand before this house and before you — for your name is in this house — and cry out to you in our affliction, and you will hear and save.
And now behold, the men of Ammon and Moav and Mount Se'ir, whom you would not let Yisra'EL invade when they came from the land of Egypt, and whom they avoided and did not destroy —
Behold, they reward us by coming to drive us out of your possession, which you have given us to inherit.
O our Creator, will you not execute judgment on them? For we are powerless against this great horde that is coming against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you.
Meanwhile all Yehudah stood before YHWH, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
And the Spirit of YHWH came upon Yakhazi'el the son of Zekhariyahu, son of Benayahu, son of Ye'iel, son of Mattanyahu, a Levite of the sons of Asaf, in the midst of the assembly.

And he said, Listen, all Yehudah and inhabitants of Yerushalayim and King Yehoshafat. Thus says YHWH to you, Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed at this great horde, for the battle is not yours but Creator's.
Tomorrow go down against them. Behold, they will come up by the ascent of Tzitz. You will find them at the end of the valley, east of the wilderness of Yeru'el.

You will not need to fight in this battle. Stand firm, hold your position, and see the salvation of YHWH on your behalf, O Yehudah and Yerushalayim. Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed. Tomorrow go out against them, and YHWH will be with you.
Then Yehoshafat bowed his head with his face to the ground, and all Yehudah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim fell down before YHWH, worshiping YHWH.
And the Levites, of the Kohathites and the Korahites, stood up to praise YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, with a very loud voice.

And they rose early in the morning and went out into the wilderness of Tekoa. And as they went out, Yehoshafat stood and said, Hear me, Yehudah and inhabitants of Yerushalayim. Believe in YHWH your Creator, and you will be established. Believe his prophets, and you will succeed.

And when he had taken counsel with the people, he appointed those who were to sing to YHWH and praise him in holy attire, as they went before the army, and say, Give thanks to YHWH, for his steadfast love endures forever.
And when they began to sing and praise, YHWH set an ambush against the men of Ammon, Moav, and Mount Se'ir, who had come against Yehudah, so that they were routed.

For the men of Ammon and Moav rose against the inhabitants of Mount Se'ir, devoting them to destruction, and when they had made an end of the inhabitants of Se'ir, they all helped to destroy one another.
When Yehudah came to the watchtower of the wilderness, they looked toward the horde, and behold, there were dead bodies lying on the ground. None had escaped.

When Yehoshafat and his people came to take their spoil, they found among them, in great numbers, goods, clothing, and precious things, which they took for themselves until they could carry no more. They were three days in taking the spoil, it was so much.
On the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Berekhah, for there they blessed YHWH. Therefore the name of that place has been called the Valley of Berekhah to this day.
Then all the men of Yehudah and Yerushalayim, with Yehoshafat at their head, returned to Yerushalayim with joy, for YHWH had made them rejoice over their enemies.
They came to Yerushalayim, to the house of YHWH, with harps and lyres and trumpets.
And the fear of Creator came on all the kingdoms of the countries when they heard that YHWH had fought against the enemies of Yisra'EL.
So the realm of Yehoshafat was quiet, for his Creator gave him rest on every side.
Thus Yehoshafat reigned over Yehudah. He was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Azuvah the daughter of Shilkhi.
He walked in the way of his father Asa and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the sight of YHWH.
The high places, however, were not taken away. The people had not yet set their hearts upon the Creator of their fathers.
Now the rest of the acts of Yehoshafat, from first to last, are written in the chronicles of Yehu the son of Khanani, which are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Yisra'EL.
After this Yehoshafat king of Yehudah joined with Akhazyahu king of Yisra'EL, who acted wickedly.
He joined him in building ships to go to Tarshish, and they built the ships in Etzyon-Gever.

Then Eli'ezer the son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Yehoshafat, saying, Because you have joined with Akhazyahu, YHWH will destroy what you have made. And the ships were wrecked and were not able to go to Tarshish.
Yehoshafat slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of Dawid, and Yehoram his son reigned in his place.
He had brothers, the sons of Yehoshafat: Azaryahu, Yekhiel, Zekhariyahu, Azaryahu, Mikha'el, and Shefatyahu. All these were the sons of Yehoshafat king of Yisra'EL.
Their father gave them great gifts of silver, gold, and valuable possessions, together with fortified cities in Yehudah, but he gave the kingdom to Yehoram, because he was the firstborn.
When Yehoram had ascended the throne of his father and was established, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the princes of Yisra'EL.
Yehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Yerushalayim.
And he walked in the way of the kings of Yisra'EL, as the house of Akhav had done, for the daughter of Akhav was his wife. And he did what was evil in the sight of YHWH.
Yet YHWH was not willing to destroy the house of Dawid, because of the covenant that he had made with Dawid, and since he had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons forever.
In his days Edom revolted from the rule of Yehudah and set up a king of their own.
Then Yehoram crossed over with his commanders and all his chariots, and he rose by night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and his chariot commanders.
So Edom revolted from the rule of Yehudah to this day. At that time Livnah also revolted from his rule, because he had forsaken YHWH, the Creator of his fathers.
Moreover, he made high places in the hill country of Yehudah and led the inhabitants of Yerushalayim into whoredom and made Yehudah go astray.

And a letter came to him from Eliyahu the prophet, saying, Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Dawid your father, Because you have not walked in the ways of your father Yehoshafat or in the ways of Asa king of Yehudah,

But have walked in the way of the kings of Yisra'EL and have enticed Yehudah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim into whoredom, as the house of Akhav led Yisra'EL into whoredom, and also you have killed your brothers, of your father's house, who were better than you,
Behold, YHWH will bring a great plague on your people, your children, your wives, and all your possessions,
And you yourself will have a severe sickness with a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the disease, day by day.
And YHWH stirred up against Yehoram the spirit of the Pelishtim and of the Arabians who are near the Kushites.

And they came up against Yehudah and invaded it and carried away all the possessions they found that belonged to the king's house, and also his sons and his wives, so that no son was left to him except Yeho'ahaz, his youngest son.
And after all this YHWH struck him in his bowels with an incurable disease.
In the course of time, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of the disease, and he died in great agony. His people made no fire in his honor, like the fires made for his fathers.

He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Yerushalayim. And he departed with no one's regret. They buried him in the city of Dawid, but not in the tombs of the kings.

And the inhabitants of Yerushalayim made Akhazyahu his youngest son king in his place, for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had killed all the older sons. So Akhazyahu the son of Yehoram king of Yehudah reigned.
Akhazyahu was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Atalyahu the granddaughter of Omri.
He also walked in the ways of the house of Akhav, for his mother was his counselor in doing wickedly.
He did what was evil in the sight of YHWH, as the house of Akhav had done. For after the death of his father they were his counselors, to his undoing.
He even followed their counsel and went with Yehoram the son of Akhav king of Yisra'EL to make war against Khaza'el king of Syria at Ramot-Gil'ad. And the Syrians wounded Yoram.

And he returned to be healed in Yizre'el of the wounds that he had received at Ramah, when he fought against Khaza'el king of Syria. And Azaryahu the son of Yehoram king of Yehudah went down to see Yehoram the son of Akhav in Yizre'el, because he was wounded.

But it was ordained by Creator that the downfall of Akhazyahu should come about through his going to visit Yoram. For when he came there, he went out with Yehoram to meet Yehu the son of Nimshi, whom YHWH had anointed to destroy the house of Akhav.
And when Yehu was executing judgment on the house of Akhav, he met the princes of Yehudah and the sons of Akhazyahu's brothers, who attended Akhazyahu, and he killed them.

He searched for Akhazyahu, and he was captured while hiding in Samaria, and he was brought to Yehu and put to death. They buried him, for they said, He is the grandson of Yehoshafat, who sought YHWH with all his heart. And the house of Akhazyahu had no one able to rule the kingdom.
Now when Atalyahu the mother of Akhazyahu saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal family of the house of Yehudah.

But Yehosheva, the daughter of the king, took Yoash the son of Akhazyahu and stole him away from among the king's sons who were about to be put to death, and she put him and his nurse in a bedroom. Thus Yehosheva, the daughter of King Yehoram and wife of Yehoyada the priest, hid him from Atalyahu, so that she did not put him to death.
And he remained with them six years, hidden in the house of Creator, while Atalyahu reigned over the land.

But in the seventh year Yehoyada took courage and entered into a covenant with the commanders of hundreds, Azaryahu the son of Yerokham, Yishma'el the son of Yehohanan, Azaryahu the son of Oved, Ma'aseiyahu the son of Adayah, and Elishafat the son of Zikhri.
And they went about through Yehudah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Yehudah, and the heads of fathers' houses of Yisra'EL, and they came to Yerushalayim.
And all the assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of Creator. And Yehoyada said to them, Behold, the king's son. Let him reign, as YHWH spoke concerning the sons of Dawid.
This is the thing that you shall do: one third of you, those who come off duty on the Shabbat, of the priests and Levites, shall be gatekeepers of the thresholds.
And one third shall be at the king's house, and one third at the Gate of the Foundation. And all the people shall be in the courts of the house of YHWH.
Let no one enter the house of YHWH except the priests and ministering Levites. They may enter, for they are holy, but all the people shall keep the charge of YHWH.
The Levites shall surround the king, each with his weapons in his hand. And whoever enters the house shall be put to death. Be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out.

The Levites and all Yehudah did according to all that Yehoyada the priest commanded. They each brought his men, who were to come off duty on the Shabbat, with those who were to come on duty on the Shabbat, for Yehoyada the priest did not dismiss the divisions.
And Yehoyada the priest gave to the commanders the spears and the large and small shields that had been King Dawid's, which were in the house of Creator.
And he set all the people as a guard for the king, every man with his weapon in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, around the altar and the house.
Then they brought out the king's son and put the crown on him and gave him the testimony and made him king. And Yehoyada and his sons anointed him and said, Long live the king.
When Atalyahu heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she went into the house of YHWH to the people.

And when she looked, there was the king standing by his pillar at the entrance, and the commanders and the trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with their musical instruments leading in the celebration. And Atalyahu tore her clothes and cried, Treason, treason.

Then Yehoyada the priest brought out the commanders who were set over the army, saying to them, Bring her out between the ranks, and anyone who follows her is to be put to death with the sword. For the priest said, Do not put her to death in the house of YHWH.
And they seized her, and she went into the entrance of the Horse Gate of the king's house, and they put her to death there.
And Yehoyada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king that they should be YHWH's people.
Then all the people went to the house of Ba'al and tore it down. His altars and his images they broke in pieces, and they killed Mattan the priest of Ba'al before the altars.

And Yehoyada posted watchmen for the house of YHWH under the direction of the Levitical priests and the Levites whom Dawid had organized to be in charge of the house of YHWH, to offer burnt offerings to YHWH, as it is written in the Torah of Mosheh, with rejoicing and with singing, according to the order of Dawid.
And he stationed gatekeepers at the gates of the house of YHWH so that no one who was in any way unclean might enter.

And he took the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the governors of the people, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of YHWH, marching through the upper gate to the king's house. And they set the king on the royal throne.
So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet after Atalyahu had been put to death with the sword.
Yoash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Tzivyah of Be'er-Sheva.
And Yoash did what was right in the eyes of YHWH all the days of Yehoyada the priest.
Yehoyada got for him two wives, and he had sons and daughters.
After this Yoash decided to restore the house of YHWH.

And he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, Go out to the cities of Yehudah and gather from all Yisra'EL money to repair the house of your Creator from year to year, and see that you act quickly. But the Levites did not act quickly.

So the king summoned Yehoyada the chief and said to him, Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Yehudah and Yerushalayim the contribution of Mosheh, the servant of YHWH, and of the congregation of Yisra'EL for the tent of testimony?
For the sons of Atalyah, that wicked woman, had broken into the house of Creator, and had also used all the dedicated things of the house of YHWH for the Ba'alim.
So the king commanded, and they made a chest and set it outside the gate of the house of YHWH.
And a proclamation was made throughout Yehudah and Yerushalayim to bring in for YHWH the tax that Mosheh the servant of Creator laid on Yisra'EL in the wilderness.
And all the princes and all the people rejoiced and brought their tax and dropped it into the chest until it was full.

And whenever the chest was brought to the king's officers by the Levites, when they saw that there was much money in it, the king's secretary and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest and take it and return it to its place. Thus they did day after day, and collected money in abundance.

And the king and Yehoyada gave it to those who had charge of the work of the house of YHWH, and they hired masons and carpenters to restore the house of YHWH, and also workers in iron and bronze to repair the house of YHWH.
So those who were engaged in the work labored, and the repairing went forward in their hands, and they restored the house of Creator to its proper condition and strengthened it.

And when they had finished, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Yehoyada, and with it were made vessels for the house of YHWH, both for the service and for the burnt offerings, and dishes for incense and vessels of gold and silver. And they offered burnt offerings in the house of YHWH regularly all the days of Yehoyada.
But Yehoyada grew old and full of days, and died. He was 130 years old at his death.
And they buried him in the city of Dawid among the kings, because he had done good in Yisra'EL, and toward Creator and his house.
Now after the death of Yehoyada the princes of Yehudah came and paid homage to the king. Then the king listened to them.
And they abandoned the house of YHWH, the Creator of their fathers, and served the Asherim and the idols. And wrath came upon Yehudah and Yerushalayim for this guilt of theirs.
Yet he sent prophets among them to bring them back to YHWH. These testified against them, but they would not pay attention.

Then the Spirit of Creator clothed Zekhariyahu the son of Yehoyada the priest, and he stood above the people, and said to them, Thus says Creator: Why do you break the commandments of YHWH, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken YHWH, he has forsaken you.
But they conspired against him, and by command of the king they stoned him with stones in the court of the house of YHWH.
Thus Yoash the king did not remember the kindness that Yehoyada, Zekhariyahu's father, had shown him, but killed his son. And when he died, he said, May YHWH see and avenge.

At the end of the year the army of Syria came up against Yoash. They came to Yehudah and Yerushalayim and destroyed all the princes of the people from among the people and sent all their spoil to the king of Damascus.

Though the army of the Syrians had come with few men, YHWH delivered into their hand a very great army, because Yehudah had forsaken YHWH, the Creator of their fathers. Thus they executed judgment on Yoash.

When they had withdrawn, leaving him severely wounded, his servants conspired against him because of the blood of the son of Yehoyada the priest, and killed him on his bed. So he died, and they buried him in the city of Dawid, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.
Those who conspired against him were Zavad the son of Shim'at the Ammonite and Yehozavad the son of Shimrit the Moabite.

Accounts of his sons and of the many oracles against him and of the rebuilding of the house of Creator are written in the Commentary on the Book of the Kings. And Amatziyahu his son reigned in his place.
Amatziyahu was twenty-five years old when he began to reign and reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Yehoaddan of Yerushalayim.
And he did what was right in the eyes of YHWH, yet not with a whole heart.
And as soon as the royal power was firmly his, he killed his servants who had struck down the king his father.

But he did not put their children to death, according to what is written in the Torah, in the Book of Mosheh, where YHWH commanded, Fathers shall not die because of their children, nor children die because of their fathers, but each one shall die for his own sin.

Then Amatziyahu assembled the men of Yehudah and set them by fathers' houses under commanders of thousands and of hundreds for all Yehudah and Binyamin. He mustered those twenty years old and upward and found that they were 300,000 choice men, fit for war, able to handle spear and shield.
He hired also 100,000 mighty men of valor from Yisra'EL for 100 talents of silver.
But a man of Creator came to him and said, O king, do not let the army of Yisra'EL go with you, for YHWH is not with Yisra'EL, with all these Efrayimites.
But go, act, be strong for the battle. Why should you suppose that Creator will cast you down before the enemy? For Creator has power to help or to cast down.

And Amatziyahu said to the man of Creator, But what shall we do about the 100 talents that I have given to the army of Yisra'EL? The man of Creator answered, YHWH is able to give you much more than this.
Then Amatziyahu discharged the army that had come to him from Efrayim to go home again. And they became very angry with Yehudah and returned home in fierce anger.
But Amatziyahu took courage and led his people out and went to the Valley of Salt and struck down 10,000 men of Se'ir.
The men of Yehudah captured another 10,000 alive and took them to the top of a rock and threw them down from the top of the rock, and they were all dashed to pieces.

But the men of the army whom Amatziyahu had sent back, not letting them go with him to battle, raided the cities of Yehudah, from Samaria to Beit-Khoron, and struck down 3,000 people in them and took much spoil.
After Amatziyahu came from striking down the Edomites, he brought the gods of the men of Se'ir and set them up as his gods and worshiped them, making offerings to them.
Therefore YHWH was angry with Amatziyahu and sent to him a prophet, who said to him, Why have you sought the gods of a people who did not deliver their own people from your hand?

But as he was speaking, the king said to him, Have we made you a royal counselor? Stop. Why should you be struck down? So the prophet stopped, but said, I know that Creator has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel.
Then Amatziyahu king of Yehudah took counsel and sent to Yoash the son of Yeho'ahaz, son of Yehu, king of Yisra'EL, saying, Come, let us look one another in the face.

And Yoash the king of Yisra'EL sent word to Amatziyahu king of Yehudah, The thistle on Lebanon sent to the cedar on Lebanon, saying, Give your daughter to my son for a wife, and a wild beast of Lebanon passed by and trampled down the thistle.
You say, See, you have struck down Edom, and your heart has lifted you up in boastfulness. But now stay at home. Why should you provoke trouble so that you fall, you and Yehudah with you?
But Amatziyahu would not listen, for it was of Creator, in order that he might give them into the hand of their enemies, because they had sought the gods of Edom.
So Yoash king of Yisra'EL went up, and he and Amatziyahu king of Yehudah faced one another in battle at Beit-Shemesh, which belongs to Yehudah.
And Yehudah was defeated by Yisra'EL, and every man fled to his home.

And Yoash king of Yisra'EL captured Amatziyahu king of Yehudah, the son of Yoash, son of Akhazyahu, at Beit-Shemesh, and brought him to Yerushalayim and broke down the wall of Yerushalayim for 400 cubits, from the Gate of Efrayim to the Corner Gate.

And he seized all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of Creator and Oved-Edom, as well as the treasuries of the king's house, also hostages, and he returned to Samaria.
Amatziyahu the son of Yoash, king of Yehudah, lived fifteen years after the death of Yoash the son of Yeho'ahaz, king of Yisra'EL.
Now the rest of the deeds of Amatziyahu, from first to last, are they not written in the Book of the Kings of Yehudah and Yisra'EL?
From the time when Amatziyahu turned away from YHWH they made a conspiracy against him in Yerushalayim, and he fled to Lakhish. But they sent after him to Lakhish and put him to death there.
And they brought him upon horses, and he was buried with his fathers in the city of Yehudah.
And all the people of Yehudah took Uziyahu, who was sixteen years old, and made him king instead of his father Amatziyahu.
He built Elot and restored it to Yehudah, after the king slept with his fathers.
Uziyahu was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Yekholyah of Yerushalayim.
And he did what was right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that his father Amatziyahu had done.
He set himself to seek Creator in the days of Zekhariyahu, who instructed him in the fear of Creator, and as long as he sought YHWH, Creator made him prosper.

He went out and made war against the Pelishtim and broke down the wall of Gat and the wall of Yavneh and the wall of Ashdod, and he built cities in the territory of Ashdod and elsewhere among the Pelishtim.
Creator helped him against the Pelishtim and against the Arabians who lived in Gur-Ba'al and against the Me'unites.
The Ammonites paid tribute to Uziyahu, and his fame spread even to the border of Egypt, for he became very strong.
Moreover, Uziyahu built towers in Yerushalayim at the Corner Gate and at the Valley Gate and at the Angle, and fortified them.

And he built towers in the wilderness and cut out many cisterns, for he had large herds, both in the Shephelah and in the plain, and he had farmers and vine dressers in the hills and in the fertile lands, for he loved the soil.

Moreover, Uziyahu had an army of soldiers, fit for war, in divisions according to the numbers in the muster made by Ye'iel the secretary and Ma'aseiyahu the officer, under the direction of Khananiyahu, one of the king's commanders.
The whole number of the heads of fathers' houses of mighty men of valor was 2,600.
Under their command was an army of 307,500, who could make war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.
And Uziyahu prepared for all the army shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and stones for slinging.

In Yerushalayim he made engines, invented by skillful men, to be on the towers and the corners, to shoot arrows and great stones. And his fame spread far, for he was marvelously helped, till he was strong.
But when he was strong, he grew proud, to his destruction. For he was unfaithful to YHWH his Creator and entered the temple of YHWH to burn incense on the altar of incense.
But Azaryahu the priest went in after him, with eighty priests of YHWH who were men of valor,

And they withstood King Uziyahu and said to him, It is not for you, Uziyahu, to burn incense to YHWH, but for the priests the sons of Aharon who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have done wrong, and it will bring you no honor from YHWH Creator.

Then Uziyahu was angry. Now he had a censer in his hand to burn incense, and when he became angry with the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead in the presence of the priests in the house of YHWH, beside the altar of incense.

And Azaryahu the chief priest and all the priests looked at him, and behold, he was leprous in his forehead. And they rushed him out quickly, and he himself hurried to go out, because YHWH had struck him.

And King Uziyahu was a leper to the day of his death, and being a leper lived in a separate house, for he was excluded from the house of YHWH. And Yotam his son was over the king's house, governing the people of the land.
Now the rest of the acts of Uziyahu, from first to last, Yesha'yahu the son of Amotz the prophet wrote.
And Uziyahu slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, He is a leper. And Yotam his son reigned in his place.
Yotam was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Yerushah the daughter of Tzadok.
And he did what was right in the eyes of YHWH according to all that his father Uziyahu had done — except he did not enter the temple of YHWH. But the people still followed corrupt practices.
He built the upper gate of the house of YHWH and did much building on the wall of Ofel.
Moreover, he built cities in the hill country of Yehudah, and in the forests he built fortresses and towers.

He fought with the king of the Ammonites and prevailed against them. And the Ammonites paid him that year 100 talents of silver, and 10,000 cors of wheat and 10,000 of barley. The Ammonites paid him the same amount in the second and the third years.
So Yotam became mighty, because he ordered his ways before YHWH his Creator.
Now the rest of the acts of Yotam, and all his wars and his ways, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Yisra'EL and Yehudah.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim.
And Yotam slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of Dawid, and Akhaz his son reigned in his place.
Akhaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim. And he did not do what was right in the eyes of YHWH, as his father Dawid had done,
But he walked in the ways of the kings of Yisra'EL. He even made metal images for the Ba'alim,
And he made offerings in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom and burned his sons as an offering, according to the abominations of the nations whom YHWH drove out before the people of Yisra'EL.
And he sacrificed and made offerings on the high places and on the hills and under every green tree.

Therefore YHWH his Creator gave him into the hand of the king of Syria, who defeated him and took captive a great number of his people and brought them to Damascus. He was also given into the hand of the king of Yisra'EL, who struck him with great force.
For Pekakh the son of Remal'yahu killed 120,000 from Yehudah in one day, all of them men of valor, because they had forsaken YHWH, the Creator of their fathers.
And Zikhri, a mighty man of Efrayim, killed Ma'aseiyahu the king's son and Azrikam the commander of the palace and Elkana the next in authority to the king.
The men of Yisra'EL took captive 200,000 of their relatives, women, sons, and daughters. They also took much spoil from them and brought the spoil to Samaria.

But a prophet of YHWH was there, whose name was Oded, and he went out to meet the army that came to Samaria and said to them, Behold, because YHWH, the Creator of your fathers, was angry with Yehudah, he gave them into your hand, but you have killed them in a rage that has reached up to heaven.
And now you intend to subjugate the people of Yehudah and Yerushalayim, male and female, as your slaves. Have you not sins of your own against YHWH your Creator?
Now hear me, and send back the captives from your relatives whom you have taken, for the fierce wrath of YHWH is upon you.

Certain chiefs also of the men of Efrayim, Azaryahu the son of Yehohanan, Berekhiyahu the son of Meshillemot, Yekhizkiyahu the son of Shallum, and Amasa the son of Hadlai, stood up against those who were coming from the war

And said to them, You shall not bring the captives in here, for you propose to bring upon us guilt against YHWH in addition to our sins and our guilt, for our guilt is already great, and there is fierce wrath against Yisra'EL.
So the armed men left the captives and the spoil before the princes and all the assembly.

And the men who have been mentioned by name rose and took the captives, and with the spoil they clothed all who were naked among them. They clothed them, gave them sandals, provided them with food and drink, and anointed them, and carrying all the feeble among them on donkeys, they brought them to their kinsfolk at Yericho, the city of palms. Then they returned to Samaria.
At that time King Akhaz sent to the king of Assyria for help.
For the Edomites had again invaded and defeated Yehudah and carried away captives.

And the Pelishtim had made raids on the cities in the Shephelah and the Negev of Yehudah, and had taken Beit-Shemesh, Ayalon, Gederot, Sokho with its villages, Timnah with its villages, and Gimzo with its villages. And they settled there.
For YHWH humbled Yehudah because of Akhaz king of Yisra'EL, for he had made Yehudah act sinfully and had been very unfaithful to YHWH.
So Tilgat-Pilneser king of Assyria came against him and afflicted him instead of strengthening him.
For Akhaz took a portion from the house of YHWH and the house of the king and of the princes, and gave tribute to the king of Assyria, but it did not help him.
In the time of his distress he became yet more faithless to YHWH — this same King Akhaz.

For he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus that had defeated him and said, Because the gods of the kings of Syria helped them, I will sacrifice to them that they may help me. But they were the ruin of him and of all Yisra'EL.

And Akhaz gathered together the vessels of the house of Creator and cut in pieces the vessels of the house of Creator, and he shut the doors of the house of YHWH, and he made himself altars at every corner in Yerushalayim.
And in every city of Yehudah he made high places to make offerings to other gods, provoking to anger YHWH, the Creator of his fathers.
Now the rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Yehudah and Yisra'EL.
And Akhaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, in Yerushalayim, for they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Yisra'EL. And Khizkiyahu his son reigned in his place.
Khizkiyahu began to reign when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Aviyah the daughter of Zekhariyahu.
And he did what was right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that Dawid his father had done.
In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of YHWH and repaired them.
He brought in the priests and the Levites and assembled them in the square on the east
And said to them, Hear me, Levites. Now consecrate yourselves, and consecrate the house of YHWH, the Creator of your fathers, and carry out the filth from the Holy Place.

For our fathers have been unfaithful and have done what was evil in the sight of YHWH our Creator. They have forsaken him and have turned away their faces from the habitation of YHWH and turned their backs.
They also shut the doors of the vestibule and put out the lamps and have not burned incense or offered burnt offerings in the Holy Place to the Creator of Yisra'EL.
Therefore the wrath of YHWH came on Yehudah and Yerushalayim, and he has made them an object of dread, of astonishment, and of hissing, as you see with your own eyes.
For behold, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity for this.
Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, in order that his fierce anger may turn away from us.
My sons, do not now be negligent, for YHWH has chosen you to stand in his presence, to minister to him and to be his ministers and make offerings to him.

Then the Levites arose, Makhat the son of Amasai and Yo'el the son of Azaryahu, of the sons of the Kohathites. And of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Avdi and Azaryahu the son of Yehallelel. And of the Gershonites, Yo'akh the son of Zimmah and Eden the son of Yo'akh.
And of the sons of Elizafan, Shimri and Ye'iel. And of the sons of Asaf, Zekhariyahu and Mattanyahu.
And of the sons of Heman, Yekhiel and Shim'i. And of the sons of Yedutun, Shemayahu and Uzzi'el.
They gathered their brothers and consecrated themselves and went in as the king had commanded, by the words of YHWH, to cleanse the house of YHWH.

The priests went into the inner part of the house of YHWH to cleanse it, and they brought out all the uncleanness that they found in the temple of YHWH into the court of the house of YHWH. And the Levites took it and carried it out to the brook Kidron.

They began to consecrate on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the vestibule of YHWH. Then for eight days they consecrated the house of YHWH, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.
Then they went in to Khizkiyahu the king and said, We have cleansed all the house of YHWH, the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the table for the showbread and all its utensils.
All the utensils that King Akhaz discarded in his reign when he was unfaithful, we have made ready and consecrated, and behold, they are before the altar of YHWH.
Then Khizkiyahu the king rose early and gathered the officials of the city and went up to the house of YHWH.

And they brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats for a sin offering for the kingdom and for the sanctuary and for Yehudah. And he commanded the priests the sons of Aharon to offer them on the altar of YHWH.

So they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests received the blood and threw it against the altar. And they slaughtered the rams, and their blood was thrown against the altar. And they slaughtered the lambs, and their blood was thrown against the altar.
Then the male goats for the sin offering were brought before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them,

And the priests slaughtered them and made a sin offering with their blood on the altar, to make atonement for all Yisra'EL. For the king commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering should be made for all Yisra'EL.

And he stationed the Levites in the house of YHWH with cymbals, harps, and lyres, according to the commandment of Dawid and of Gad the king's seer and of Natan the prophet, for the commandment was from YHWH through his prophets.
The Levites stood with the instruments of Dawid, and the priests with the trumpets.

Then Khizkiyahu commanded that the burnt offering be offered on the altar. And when the burnt offering began, the song to YHWH began also, and the trumpets, accompanied by the instruments of Dawid king of Yisra'EL.
And all the assembly worshiped, and the singers sang, and the trumpeters sounded. All this continued until the burnt offering was finished.
When the offering was finished, the king and all who were present with him bowed themselves and worshiped.

And Khizkiyahu the king and the officials commanded the Levites to sing praises to YHWH with the words of Dawid and of Asaf the seer. And they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed down and worshiped.

Then Khizkiyahu said, You have now consecrated yourselves to YHWH. Come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of YHWH. And the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and all who were of a willing heart brought burnt offerings.
The number of the burnt offerings that the assembly brought was 70 bulls, 100 rams, and 200 lambs. All these were for a burnt offering to YHWH.
And the consecrated offerings were 600 bulls and 3,000 sheep.

But the priests were too few and could not flay all the burnt offerings, so until other priests had consecrated themselves, their brothers the Levites helped them, until the work was finished — for the Levites were more upright in heart than the priests in consecrating themselves.
Besides the great number of burnt offerings, there were the fat of the peace offerings, and there were the drink offerings for the burnt offerings. Thus the service of the house of YHWH was restored.
And Khizkiyahu and all the people rejoiced because Creator had provided for the people, for the thing came about suddenly.

Khizkiyahu sent to all Yisra'EL and Yehudah, and wrote letters also to Efrayim and Menasheh, that they should come to the house of YHWH at Yerushalayim to keep the Passover to YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL.
For the king and his princes and all the assembly in Yerushalayim had taken counsel to keep the Passover in the second month —
For they could not keep it at that time because the priests had not consecrated themselves in sufficient number, nor had the people assembled in Yerushalayim —
The plan seemed right to the king and all the assembly.

So they decreed to make a proclamation throughout all Yisra'EL, from Be'er-Sheva to Dan, that the people should come and keep the Passover to YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, at Yerushalayim. For they had not kept it as often as prescribed.

So couriers went throughout all Yisra'EL and Yehudah with letters from the king and his princes, as the king had commanded, saying, O people of Yisra'EL, return to YHWH, the Creator of Avraham, Yitzkhak, and Yisra'EL, that he may turn again to the remnant of you who have escaped from the hand of the kings of Assyria.
Do not be like your fathers and your brothers, who were faithless to YHWH Creator of their fathers, so that he made them a desolation, as you see.

Do not now be stiff-necked as your fathers were, but yield yourselves to YHWH and come to his sanctuary, which he has consecrated forever, and serve YHWH your Creator, that his fierce anger may turn away from you.

For if you return to YHWH, your brothers and your children will find compassion with their captors and return to this land. For YHWH your Creator is gracious and merciful and will not turn away his face from you, if you return to him.
So the couriers went from city to city through the country of Efrayim and Menasheh, and as far as Zevulun, but they laughed at them and mocked them.
However, some men of Asher, of Menasheh, and of Zevulun humbled themselves and came to Yerushalayim.
The hand of Creator was also on Yehudah to give them one heart to do what the king and the princes commanded by the word of YHWH.
And many people came together in Yerushalayim to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month, a very great assembly.
They set to work and removed the altars that were in Yerushalayim, and all the altars for burning incense they took away and threw into the brook Kidron.

And they slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. And the priests and the Levites were ashamed, so that they consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings into the house of YHWH.
They took their accustomed posts according to the Torah of Mosheh the man of Creator. The priests threw the blood that they received from the hand of the Levites.
For there were many in the assembly who had not consecrated themselves. Therefore the Levites had to slaughter the Passover lamb for everyone who was not clean, to consecrate it to YHWH.

For a majority of the people, many of them from Efrayim, Menasheh, Yissachar, and Zevulun, had not cleansed themselves, yet they ate the Passover otherwise than as prescribed. For Khizkiyahu had prayed for them, saying, May the good YHWH pardon everyone
Who sets his heart to seek Creator, YHWH the Creator of his fathers, even though not according to the sanctuary's rules of cleanness.
And YHWH heard Khizkiyahu and healed the people.

And the people of Yisra'EL who were present at Yerushalayim kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with great gladness, and the Levites and the priests praised YHWH day by day, singing with all their might to YHWH.

And Khizkiyahu spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed good skill in the service of YHWH. So they ate the food of the feast for seven days, sacrificing peace offerings and giving thanks to YHWH, the Creator of their fathers.
Then the whole assembly agreed together to keep the feast for another seven days. So they kept it for another seven days with gladness.

For Khizkiyahu king of Yehudah gave the assembly 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep for offerings, and the princes gave the assembly 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep. And the priests consecrated themselves in great numbers.

The whole assembly of Yehudah, and the priests and the Levites, and the whole assembly that came out of Yisra'EL, and the sojourners who came out of the land of Yisra'EL, and the sojourners who lived in Yehudah, rejoiced.
So there was great joy in Yerushalayim, for since the time of Shelomoh the son of Dawid king of Yisra'EL there had been nothing like this in Yerushalayim.
Then the priests and the Levites arose and blessed the people, and their voice was heard, and their prayer came to his holy habitation in heaven.

Now when all this was finished, all Yisra'EL who were present went out to the cities of Yehudah and broke in pieces the pillars and cut down the Asherim and broke down the high places and the altars throughout all Yehudah and Binyamin, and in Efrayim and Menasheh, until they had destroyed them all. Then all the people of Yisra'EL returned to their cities, every man to his possession.

And Khizkiyahu appointed the divisions of the priests and of the Levites, division by division, each according to his service, the priests and the Levites, for burnt offerings and peace offerings, to minister in the gates of the camp of YHWH and to give thanks and praise.

The contribution of the king from his own possessions was for the burnt offerings: the burnt offerings of morning and evening, and the burnt offerings for the Shabbatot, the new moons, and the appointed feasts, as it is written in the Torah of YHWH.
And he commanded the people who lived in Yerushalayim to give the portion due to the priests and the Levites, that they might give themselves to the Torah of YHWH.

As soon as the command was spread abroad, the people of Yisra'EL gave in abundance the firstfruits of grain, wine, oil, honey, and of all the produce of the field. And they brought in abundantly the tithe of everything.

And the people of Yisra'EL and Yehudah who lived in the cities of Yehudah also brought in the tithe of cattle and sheep, and the tithe of the dedicated things that had been dedicated to YHWH their Creator, and laid them in heaps.
In the third month they began to pile up the heaps, and finished them in the seventh month.
When Khizkiyahu and the princes came and saw the heaps, they blessed YHWH and his people Yisra'EL.
And Khizkiyahu questioned the priests and the Levites about the heaps.

Azaryahu the chief priest, who was of the house of Tzadok, answered him, Since they began to bring the contributions into the house of YHWH, we have eaten and had enough and have plenty left, for YHWH has blessed his people, so that we have this large amount left.
Then Khizkiyahu commanded them to prepare chambers in the house of YHWH, and they prepared them.
And they faithfully brought in the contributions, the tithes, and the dedicated things. The chief officer in charge of them was Konaniyahu the Levite, with Shim'i his brother as second.

And Yekhiel, Azazyahu, Nakhat, Asahel, Yerimot, Yozavad, Eli'el, Yissachar, Makhbanai, and Benayahu were overseers assisting Konaniyahu and Shim'i his brother, by appointment of Khizkiyahu the king and Azaryahu the chief officer of the house of Creator.
And Kore the son of Yimna the Levite, keeper of the east gate, was over the freewill offerings to Creator, to apportion the contribution reserved for YHWH and the most holy offerings.
Eden, Minyamin, Yeshua, Shemayahu, Amaryahu, and Shekhanyahu were faithfully assisting him in the cities of the priests, to distribute to their brothers, old and young alike, by divisions,

Except those enrolled by genealogy, males from three years old and upward — all who entered the house of YHWH as the duty of each day required — for their service according to their offices, by their divisions.
The enrollment of the priests was according to their fathers' houses. The Levites from twenty years old and upward were enrolled according to their offices, by their divisions.
They were enrolled with all their little children, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, the whole assembly, for they were faithful in keeping themselves holy.

And for the sons of Aharon, the priests, who were in the fields of the pasturelands of their cities, there were men in the several cities who were designated by name to distribute portions to every male among the priests and to everyone among the Levites who was enrolled.
Thus Khizkiyahu did throughout all Yehudah, and he did what was good and right and faithful before YHWH his Creator.
And every work that he undertook in the service of the house of Creator and in accordance with the Torah and the commandments, seeking his Creator, he did with all his heart, and prospered.
After these things and these acts of faithfulness, Sennakherib king of Assyria came and invaded Yehudah and encamped against the fortified cities, thinking to win them for himself.
And when Khizkiyahu saw that Sennakherib had come and intended to fight against Yerushalayim,
He planned with his officers and his mighty men to stop the water of the springs that were outside the city, and they helped him.
A great many people were gathered, and they stopped all the springs and the brook that flowed through the land, saying, Why should the kings of Assyria come and find much water?

He set to work resolutely and built up all the wall that was broken down and raised towers upon it, and outside it he built another wall, and he strengthened the Millo in the city of Dawid. He also made weapons and shields in abundance.
And he set combat commanders over the people and gathered them together to him in the square at the gate of the city and spoke encouragingly to them, saying,
Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or dismayed before the king of Assyria and all the horde that is with him, for there is one greater with us than with him.
With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is YHWH our Creator, to help us and to fight our battles. And the people took confidence from the words of Khizkiyahu king of Yehudah.

After this, Sennakherib king of Assyria, who was besieging Lakhish with all his forces, sent his servants to Yerushalayim to Khizkiyahu king of Yehudah and to all the people of Yehudah who were in Yerushalayim, saying,
Thus says Sennakherib king of Assyria, On what are you trusting, that you endure the siege in Yerushalayim?
Is not Khizkiyahu misleading you, that he may give you over to die by famine and by thirst, when he tells you, YHWH our Creator will deliver us from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Has not this same Khizkiyahu taken away his high places and his altars and commanded Yehudah and Yerushalayim, You shall worship before one altar and on it you shall make your offerings?
Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were the gods of the nations of those lands at all able to deliver their lands out of my hand?
Who among all the gods of those nations that my fathers devoted to destruction was able to deliver his people from my hand, that your Creator should be able to deliver you from my hand?

Now, therefore, do not let Khizkiyahu deceive you or mislead you in this fashion, and do not believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand or from the hand of my fathers. How much less will your Creator deliver you out of my hand.
His servants said still more against YHWH Creator and against his servant Khizkiyahu.

And he wrote letters to cast contempt on YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'EL, and to speak against him, saying, Like the gods of the nations of the lands who have not delivered their people from my hands, so the Creator of Khizkiyahu will not deliver his people from my hand.
And they shouted it with a loud voice in the language of Yehudah to the people of Yerushalayim who were on the wall, to frighten and terrify them, in order that they might take the city.
And they spoke of the Creator of Yerushalayim as they spoke of the gods of the peoples of the earth, which are the work of men's hands.
Then Khizkiyahu the king and Yesha'yahu the prophet, the son of Amotz, prayed because of this and cried to heaven.

And YHWH sent an angel, who cut off all the mighty warriors and commanders and officers in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned with shame of face to his own land. And when he came into the house of his god, some of his own sons struck him down there with the sword.
So YHWH saved Khizkiyahu and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim from the hand of Sennakherib king of Assyria and from the hand of all his enemies, and he provided for them on every side.
And many brought gifts to YHWH to Yerushalayim and precious things to Khizkiyahu king of Yehudah, so that he was exalted in the sight of all nations from that time onward.
In those days Khizkiyahu became sick and was at the point of death, and he prayed to YHWH, and he answered him and gave him a sign.
But Khizkiyahu did not make return according to the benefit done to him, for his heart was proud. Therefore wrath came upon him and Yehudah and Yerushalayim.
But Khizkiyahu humbled himself for the pride of his heart, both he and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, so that the wrath of YHWH did not come upon them in the days of Khizkiyahu.
And Khizkiyahu had very great riches and honor, and he made himself treasuries for silver, for gold, for precious stones, for spices, for shields, and for all kinds of costly vessels.
Storehouses also for the yield of grain, wine, and oil, and stalls for all kinds of cattle, and sheepfolds.
He likewise provided cities for himself, and flocks and herds in abundance, for Creator had given him very great possessions.
This same Khizkiyahu closed the upper outlet of the waters of Gikkon and directed them down to the west side of the city of Dawid. And Khizkiyahu prospered in all his works.

And so in the matter of the envoys of the princes of Babylon, who had been sent to him to inquire about the sign that had been done in the land, Creator left him to himself, in order to test him and to know all that was in his heart.
Now the rest of the acts of Khizkiyahu and his good deeds, behold, they are written in the vision of Yesha'yahu the prophet the son of Amotz, in the Book of the Kings of Yehudah and Yisra'EL.

And Khizkiyahu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the upper part of the tombs of the sons of Dawid, and all Yehudah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim did him honor at his death. And Menasheh his son reigned in his place.
Menasheh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Yerushalayim.
And he did what was evil in the sight of YHWH, according to the abominations of the nations whom YHWH drove out before the people of Yisra'EL.
For he rebuilt the high places that his father Khizkiyahu had broken down, and he erected altars to the Ba'alim, and made Asherim, and worshiped all the host of heaven and served them.
And he built altars in the house of YHWH, of which YHWH had said, In Yerushalayim shall my name be forever.
And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of YHWH.

And he burned his sons as an offering in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, and used fortune-telling and omens and sorcery, and dealt with mediums and with necromancers. He did much evil in the sight of YHWH, provoking him to anger.

And the carved image of the idol that he had made he set in the house of Creator, of which Creator said to Dawid and to Shelomoh his son, In this house and in Yerushalayim, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Yisra'EL, I will put my name forever.
