And on the first day of the second month, they assembled the whole congregation together, who registered themselves by clans, by fathers' houses, according to the number of names from twenty years old and upward, head by head.

The people of Re'uven, Yisra'EL's firstborn, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of names, head by head, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war:
Their listing in the tribe of Re'uven was 46,500.
Of the people of Yehudah, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war:
Their listing in the tribe of Yehudah was 74,600.
These are those who were listed, whom Moshe and Aharon listed with the help of the chiefs of Yisra'EL, twelve men, each representing his fathers' house.
So all those listed of the people of Yisra'EL, by their fathers' houses, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war in Yisra'EL —
All those listed were 603,550.
But the Levites were not listed along with them by their ancestral tribe.

But appoint the Levites over the Mishkan of the testimony, and over all its furnishings, and over all that belongs to it. They are to carry the Mishkan and all its furnishings, and they shall take care of it and shall camp around the Mishkan.
When the Mishkan is to set out, the Levites shall take it down, and when the Mishkan is to be pitched, the Levites shall set it up. And if any outsider comes near, he shall be put to death.

But the Levites shall camp around the Mishkan of the testimony, so that there may be no wrath on the congregation of the people of Yisra'EL. And the Levites shall keep guard over the Mishkan of the testimony.
YHWH spoke to Moshe and Aharon, saying:
The people of Yisra'EL shall camp each by his own standard, with the banners of their fathers' houses. They shall camp facing the tent of meeting on every side.
Those to camp on the east side toward the sunrise shall be of the standard of the camp of Yehudah by their companies. The chief of the people of Yehudah being Nakhshon the son of Amminadav.
On the south side shall be the standard of the camp of Re'uven by their companies, the chief of the people of Re'uven being Elitzur the son of Shede'ur.
Then the tent of meeting shall set out, with the camp of the Levites in the midst of the camps — as they camp, so they shall set out, each in position, standard by standard.
On the west side shall be the standard of the camp of Efrayim by their companies, the chief of the people of Efrayim being Elishama the son of Ammihud.
On the north side shall be the standard of the camp of Dan by their companies, the chief of the people of Dan being Ahi'ezer the son of Ammishaddai.
These are the people of Yisra'EL as listed by their fathers' houses. All those listed in the camps by their companies were 603,550.
But the Levites were not listed among the people of Yisra'EL, as YHWH commanded Moshe.
Thus did the people of Yisra'EL. According to all that YHWH commanded Moshe, so they camped by their standards, and so they set out, each one in his clan, according to his fathers' house.
These are the generations of Aharon and Moshe at the time when YHWH spoke with Moshe on Mount Sinai.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Bring the tribe of Levi near, and set them before Aharon the priest, that they may minister to him.
They shall keep guard over him and over the whole congregation before the tent of meeting, as they minister at the Mishkan.
And you shall give the Levites to Aharon and his sons — they are wholly given to him from among the people of Yisra'EL.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Behold, I have taken the Levites from among the people of Yisra'EL instead of every firstborn who opens the womb among the people of Yisra'EL. The Levites shall be mine,

For all the firstborn are mine. On the day that I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated for my own all the firstborn in Yisra'EL, both of man and of beast. They shall be mine — I am YHWH.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe in the wilderness of Sinai, saying:
List the sons of Levi, by fathers' houses and by clans — every male from a month old and upward you shall list.
All those listed among the Levites, whom Moshe and Aharon listed at the commandment of YHWH, by clans, all the males from a month old and upward, were 22,000.
And YHWH said to Moshe: List all the firstborn males of the people of Yisra'EL, from a month old and upward, taking the number of their names.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the people of Yisra'EL, and the livestock of the Levites instead of their livestock. The Levites shall be mine — I am YHWH.
YHWH spoke to Moshe and Aharon, saying:
Take a census of the sons of Kehat from among the sons of Levi, by their clans and their fathers' houses,
From thirty years old up to fifty years old, all who can come on duty, to do the work in the tent of meeting.
This is the service of the sons of Kehat in the tent of meeting — the most holy things.

And when Aharon and his sons have finished covering the holy furnishings and all the holy utensils, when the camp is to set out, after that the sons of Kehat shall come to carry these, but they must not touch the holy things, lest they die.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe and Aharon, saying:
Let not the tribe of the clans of Kehat be destroyed from among the Levites,
But deal thus with them, that they may live and not die when they come near to the most holy things: Aharon and his sons shall go in and appoint each of them to his task and to his burden.
YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Take a census of the sons of Gershon also, by their fathers' houses and by their clans.
As for the sons of Merari, you shall list them by their clans and their fathers' houses.
Their listing was 8,580. According to the commandment of YHWH through Moshe, each one with his task of serving or carrying — thus they were listed by him, as YHWH commanded Moshe.
YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Command the people of Yisra'EL that they put out of the camp everyone who is leprous or has a discharge and everyone who is unclean through contact with the dead.
You shall put out both male and female, putting them outside the camp, that they may not defile their camp, in the midst of which I dwell.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the people of Yisra'EL: When a man or woman commits any of the sins that people commit by breaking faith with YHWH, and that person realizes his guilt,
He shall confess his sin that he has committed. And he shall make full restitution for his wrong, adding a fifth to it and giving it to him to whom he did the wrong.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the people of Yisra'EL, saying: If any man's wife goes astray and breaks faith with him,

And if the spirit of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife who has defiled herself, or if the spirit of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife, though she has not defiled herself —

Then the man shall bring his wife to the priest and bring the offering required of her, a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He shall pour no oil on it and put no frankincense on it, for it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance, bringing iniquity to remembrance.
This is the law in cases of jealousy, when a wife, though under her husband's authority, goes astray and defiles herself,
Or when the spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he is jealous of his wife. Then he shall set the woman before YHWH, and the priest shall carry out for her all this law.
The man shall be free from iniquity, but the woman shall bear her iniquity.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the people of Yisra'EL and say to them: When either a man or a woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to YHWH,
He shall separate himself from wine and strong drink. He shall drink no vinegar made from wine or strong drink and shall not drink any juice of grapes or eat grapes, fresh or dried.

All the days of his vow of separation, no razor shall touch his head. Until the time is completed for which he separates himself to YHWH, he shall be holy. He shall let the locks of hair of his head grow long.
All the days that he separates himself to YHWH he shall not go near a dead body.

This is the law of the Nazirite. But if he vows an offering to YHWH above his Nazirite vow, as he can afford, in addition to what the law of the Nazirite requires, so he shall do in keeping with the vow that he takes.
YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to Aharon and his sons, saying: Thus you shall bless the people of Yisra'EL — you shall say to them:
YHWH bless you and keep you.
YHWH make his face shine on you and be gracious to you.
YHWH lift up his countenance upon you and give you shalom.
So shall they put my name upon the people of Yisra'EL, and I will bless them.
On the day when Moshe had finished setting up the Mishkan and had anointed and consecrated it with all its furnishings and had anointed and consecrated the altar with all its utensils,
The chiefs of Yisra'EL, heads of their fathers' houses, who were the chiefs of the tribes, who were over those who were listed, approached
And brought their offerings before YHWH, six wagons and twelve oxen, a wagon for every two of the chiefs and for each one an ox. They brought them before the Mishkan.
And the chiefs offered offerings for the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed — and the chiefs offered their offering before the altar.
He who offered his offering the first day was Nakhshon the son of Amminadav, of the tribe of Yehudah.
This was the dedication offering for the altar on the day when it was anointed, from the chiefs of Yisra'EL: twelve silver plates, twelve silver basins, twelve golden dishes.

And when Moshe went into the tent of meeting to speak with YHWH, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat that was on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim — and it spoke to him.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to Aharon and say to him: When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light in front of the lampstand.
And Aharon did so — he set up its lamps in front of the lampstand, as YHWH commanded Moshe.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Take the Levites from among the people of Yisra'EL and cleanse them.
And you shall bring the Levites before YHWH, and the people of Yisra'EL shall lay their hands on the Levites.
And Aharon shall offer the Levites before YHWH as a wave offering from the people of Yisra'EL, that they may do the service of YHWH.
Thus you shall separate the Levites from among the people of Yisra'EL, and the Levites shall be mine.
For they are wholly given to me from among the people of Yisra'EL. Instead of all who open the womb, the firstborn of all the people of Yisra'EL, I have taken them for myself.
This applies to the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward they shall come to do duty in the service of the tent of meeting.
And from the age of fifty years they shall withdraw from the duty of the service and serve no more.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying:
Let the people of Yisra'EL keep the Pesach at its appointed time.
And there were certain men who were unclean through touching a dead body, so that they could not keep the Pesach on that day, and they came before Moshe and Aharon on that day.
And those men said to him: We are unclean through touching a dead body. Why are we kept from bringing YHWH's offering at its appointed time among the people of Yisra'EL?
And Moshe said to them: Wait, that I may hear what YHWH will command concerning you.
YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the people of Yisra'EL, saying: If any one of you or of your descendants is unclean through touching a dead body, or is on a long journey, he shall still keep the Pesach to YHWH.
In the second month on the fourteenth day at twilight they shall keep it. They shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
On the day that the Mishkan was set up, the cloud covered the Mishkan, the tent of the testimony. And at evening it was over the Mishkan like the appearance of fire until morning.
And whenever the cloud lifted from over the tent, after that the people of Yisra'EL set out, and in the place where the cloud settled down, there the people of Yisra'EL camped.
At the command of YHWH the people of Yisra'EL set out, and at the command of YHWH they camped. As long as the cloud rested over the Mishkan, they remained in camp.

Whether it was two days, or a month, or a longer time, that the cloud continued over the Mishkan, abiding there, the people of Yisra'EL remained in camp and did not set out, but when it lifted they set out.
At the command of YHWH they camped, and at the command of YHWH they set out. They kept the charge of YHWH, at the command of YHWH by Moshe.
YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Make two silver trumpets. Of hammered work you shall make them, and you shall use them for summoning the congregation and for breaking camp.

And when you go to war in your land against the adversary who oppresses you, then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets, that you may be remembered before YHWH your Creator, and you shall be saved from your enemies.

On the day of your gladness also, and at your appointed feasts and at the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings. They shall be a reminder of you before your Creator — I am YHWH your Creator.
In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud lifted from over the Mishkan of the testimony.
And the people of Yisra'EL set out by stages from the wilderness of Sinai. And the cloud settled down in the wilderness of Paran.

And Moshe said to Hovav the son of Re'uel the Midyanite, Moshe's father-in-law: We are setting out for the place of which YHWH said: I will give it to you. Come with us, and we will do good to you, for YHWH has promised good to Yisra'EL.
So they set out from the mount of YHWH three days' journey. And the ark of the covenant of YHWH went before them three days' journey, to seek out a resting place for them.
And whenever the ark set out, Moshe said: Arise, O YHWH, and let your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate you flee before you.
And when it rested, he said: Return, O YHWH, to the ten thousand thousands of Yisra'EL.

And the people complained in the hearing of YHWH about their misfortunes, and when YHWH heard it, his anger was kindled, and the fire of YHWH burned among them and consumed some outlying parts of the camp.
Now the rabble that was among them had a strong craving. And the people of Yisra'EL also wept again and said: Oh that we had meat to eat.
We remember the fish we ate in Egypt that cost nothing, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic.
But now our strength is dried up, and there is nothing at all but this manna to look at.
Moshe heard the people weeping throughout their clans, everyone at the door of his tent. And the anger of YHWH blazed hotly, and Moshe was displeased.
Moshe said to YHWH: Why have you dealt ill with your servant? And why have I not found favor in your sight, that you lay the burden of all this people on me?
I am not able to carry all this people alone — the burden is too heavy for me.
If you will treat me like this, kill me at once, if I find favor in your sight, that I may not see my wretchedness.

Then YHWH said to Moshe: Gather for me seventy men of the elders of Yisra'EL, whom you know to be the elders of the people and officers over them, and bring them to the tent of meeting, and let them take their stand there with you.

And I will come down and talk with you there. And I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them, and they shall bear the burden of the people with you, so that you may not bear it yourself alone.
So Moshe went out and told the people the words of YHWH. And he gathered seventy men of the elders of the people and placed them around the tent.

Then YHWH came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and took some of the Spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders. And as soon as the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied. But they did not continue doing it.

Now two men remained in the camp, one named Eldad, and the other named Medad, and the Spirit rested on them. They were among those registered, but they had not gone out to the tent, and so they prophesied in the camp.
And Yehoshua the son of Nun, the assistant of Moshe from his youth, said: My lord Moshe, stop them.
But Moshe said to him: Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all YHWH's people were prophets, that YHWH would put his Spirit on them.

Then a wind from YHWH sprang up, and it brought quail from the sea and let them fall beside the camp, about a day's journey on this side and a day's journey on the other side, around the camp, about two cubits above the ground.
While the meat was yet between their teeth, before it was consumed, the anger of YHWH was kindled against the people, and YHWH struck down the people with a very great plague.
Miryam and Aharon spoke against Moshe because of the Kushite woman whom he had married, for he had married a Kushite woman.
And they said: Has YHWH indeed spoken only through Moshe? Has he not spoken through us also? And YHWH heard it.
Now the man Moshe was very meek, more than all people who were on the face of the earth.
And suddenly YHWH said to Moshe and to Aharon and Miryam: Come out, you three, to the tent of meeting. And the three of them came out.
And YHWH came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent and called Aharon and Miryam, and they both came forward.
And he said: Hear my words: If there is a prophet among you, I YHWH make myself known to him in a vision — I speak with him in a dream.
Not so with my servant Moshe. He is faithful in all my house.
With him I speak mouth to mouth, clearly, and not in riddles, and he beholds the form of YHWH. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moshe?
And the anger of YHWH was kindled against them, and he departed.
When the cloud removed from over the tent, behold, Miryam was leprous, like snow. And Aharon turned toward Miryam, and behold, she was leprous.
And Moshe cried to YHWH: O YHWH, please heal her — please.
But YHWH said to Moshe: If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be shamed seven days? Let her be shut outside the camp seven days, and after that she may be brought in again.
So Miryam was shut outside the camp seven days, and the people did not set out on the march till Miryam was brought in again.
YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Send men to spy out the land of Kena'an, which I am giving to the people of Yisra'EL. From each tribe of their fathers you shall send a man, every one a chief among them.
From the tribe of Yehudah, Kalev the son of Yefunneh.
From the tribe of Efrayim, Hoshea the son of Nun.
These were the names of the men whom Moshe sent to spy out the land. And Moshe called Hoshea the son of Nun Yehoshua.
Moshe sent them to spy out the land of Kena'an and said to them: Go up into the Negev and go up into the hill country,
And whether the land is rich or poor, and whether there are trees in it or not. Be of good courage and bring some of the fruit of the land. Now the time was the season of the first ripe grapes.

And they came to the Valley of Eshkol and cut down from there a branch with a single cluster of grapes, and they carried it on a pole between two of them. They also brought some pomegranates and figs.
At the end of forty days they returned from spying out the land.
And they told him: We came to the land to which you sent us. It flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
However, the people who dwell in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large. And besides, we saw the descendants of Anak there.
But Kalev quieted the people before Moshe and said: Let us go up at once and occupy it, for we are well able to overcome it.
Then the men who had gone up with him said: We are not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we are.

So they brought to the people of Yisra'EL a bad report of the land that they had spied out, saying: The land, through which we have gone to spy it out, is a land that devours its inhabitants, and all the people that we saw in it are of great height.
And there we saw the Nephilim — the sons of Anak, who come from the Nephilim — and we seemed to ourselves like grasshoppers, and so we seemed to them.
Then all the congregation raised a loud cry, and the people wept that night.
And all the people of Yisra'EL grumbled against Moshe and Aharon. The whole congregation said to them: Would that we had died in the land of Egypt. Or would that we had died in this wilderness.
And they said to one another: Let us choose a leader and go back to Egypt.
And Yehoshua the son of Nun and Kalev the son of Yefunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their clothes
And said to all the congregation of the people of Yisra'EL: The land, which we passed through to spy it out, is an exceedingly good land.
If YHWH delights in us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land that flows with milk and honey.
Only do not rebel against YHWH. And do not fear the people of the land, for they are bread for us. Their protection is removed from them, and YHWH is with us. Do not fear them.
And YHWH said to Moshe: How long will this people despise me? And how long will they not believe in me, in spite of all the signs that I have done among them?
But Moshe said to YHWH: Then the Egyptians will hear of it, for you brought up this people in your might from among them.
And now, please let the power of YHWH be great as you have promised, saying:

YHWH is slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, forgiving iniquity and transgression, but he will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, to the third and the fourth generation.
Please pardon the iniquity of this people, according to the greatness of your steadfast love, just as you have forgiven this people, from Egypt until now.
Then YHWH said: I have pardoned, according to your word.
But truly, as I live, and as all the earth shall be filled with the glory of YHWH,
None of the men who have seen my glory and my signs that I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and yet have put me to the test these ten times and have not obeyed my voice,
Shall see the land that I swore to give to their fathers. And none of those who despised me shall see it.
But my servant Kalev, because he has a different spirit and has followed me fully, I will bring into the land into which he went, and his descendants shall possess it.
Your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness, and of all your number, listed in the census from twenty years old and upward, who have grumbled against me,
Not one shall come into the land where I swore that I would make you dwell, except Kalev the son of Yefunneh and Yehoshua the son of Nun.
And your children shall be shepherds in the wilderness forty years and shall suffer for your faithlessness, until the last of your dead bodies lies in the wilderness.
According to the number of the days in which you spied out the land, forty days, a year for each day, you shall bear your iniquity forty years, and you shall know my displeasure.
YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the people of Yisra'EL and say to them: When you come into the land you are to inhabit, which I am giving you,

And you offer to YHWH a food offering or a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering or at your appointed feasts, to make a pleasing aroma to YHWH, from the herd or from the flock,
And if a stranger is sojourning with you, or anyone is living permanently among you, and he wishes to offer a food offering with a pleasing aroma to YHWH, he shall do as you do.
For the assembly, there shall be one statute for you and for the stranger who sojourns with you, a statute forever throughout your generations. You and the sojourner shall be alike before YHWH.
But if you sin unintentionally, and do not observe all these commandments that YHWH has spoken to Moshe —
If one person sins unintentionally, he shall offer a female goat a year old for a sin offering.
But the person who does anything with a high hand, whether he is native or a sojourner, reviles YHWH, and that person shall be cut off from among his people.
While the people of Yisra'EL were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day.
And YHWH said to Moshe: The man shall be put to death — all the congregation shall stone him with stones outside the camp.
Speak to the people of Yisra'EL, and tell them to make tassels on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a cord of blue on the tassel of each corner.
And it shall be a tassel for you to look at and remember all the commandments of YHWH, to do them, not to follow after your own heart and your own eyes, which you are inclined to whore after.
So you shall remember and do all my commandments, and be holy to your Creator.
I am YHWH your Creator, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your Creator — I am YHWH your Creator.
Now Korakh the son of Yitzhar, son of Kehat, son of Levi, and Datan and Aviram the sons of Eli'av, and On the son of Pelet, sons of Re'uven, took men.
And they rose up before Moshe, with a number of the people of Yisra'EL, 250 chiefs of the congregation, chosen from the assembly, well-known men.

They assembled themselves together against Moshe and against Aharon and said to them: You have gone too far. For all in the congregation are holy, every one of them, and YHWH is among them. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of YHWH?
When Moshe heard it, he fell on his face.

Is it too small a thing for you that the Creator of Yisra'EL has separated you from the congregation of Yisra'EL, to bring you near to himself, to do service in the Mishkan of YHWH and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?
And Moshe sent to call Datan and Aviram the sons of Eli'av, and they said: We will not come up.
Is it a small thing that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, that you must also make yourself a prince over us?
And Moshe said: Hereby you shall know that YHWH has sent me to do all these works, and that it has not been of my own accord.
If these men die as all men die, or if they are visited by the fate of all mankind, then YHWH has not sent me.

But if YHWH creates something new, and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them up with all that belongs to them, and they go down alive into Sheol, then you shall know that these men have despised YHWH.
And as soon as he had finished speaking all these words, the ground under them split apart.
And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, with their households and all the people who belonged to Korakh and all their goods.
So they and all that belonged to them went down alive into Sheol, and the earth closed over them, and they perished from the midst of the assembly.
And fire came out from YHWH and consumed the 250 men offering the incense.

And Moshe said to Aharon: Take your censer, and put fire on it from off the altar and lay incense on it and carry it quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from YHWH — the plague has begun.
And he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped.
YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the people of Yisra'EL, and get from them staffs, one for each fathers' house, from all their chiefs according to their fathers' houses, twelve staffs. Write each man's name on his staff.
And write Aharon's name on the staff of Levi. For there shall be one staff for the head of each fathers' house.
And the man whom I choose shall bud his staff shall sprout. Thus I will make to cease from me the grumblings of the people of Yisra'EL, which they grumble against you.
And Moshe deposited the staffs before YHWH in the tent of the testimony.
On the next day Moshe went into the tent of the testimony, and behold, the staff of Aharon for the house of Levi had sprouted and put forth buds and produced blossoms, and it bore ripe almonds.
And YHWH said to Moshe: Put back the staff of Aharon before the testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebels, that you may make an end of their grumblings against me, lest they die.

So YHWH said to Aharon: You and your sons and your father's house with you shall bear iniquity connected with the sanctuary, and you and your sons with you shall bear iniquity connected with your priesthood.
And behold, I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the people of Yisra'EL. They are a gift to you, given to YHWH, to do the service of the tent of meeting.

Then YHWH spoke to Aharon: Behold, I have given you charge of the contributions made to me, all the consecrated things of the people of Yisra'EL. I have given them to you as a portion and to your sons as a perpetual due.

All the holy contributions that the people of Yisra'EL present to YHWH I give to you, and to your sons and daughters with you, as a perpetual due. It is a covenant of salt forever before YHWH for you and for your offspring with you.
And YHWH said to Aharon: You shall have no inheritance in their land, neither shall you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the people of Yisra'EL.
To the Levites I have given every tithe in Yisra'EL for an inheritance, in return for their service that they do, their service in the tent of meeting.
So you shall also present a contribution to YHWH from all your tithes that you receive from the people of Yisra'EL. And from it you shall give YHWH's contribution to Aharon the priest.
Now YHWH spoke to Moshe and to Aharon, saying:
This is the statute of the law that YHWH has commanded: Tell the people of Yisra'EL to bring you a red heifer without defect, in which there is no blemish, and on which a yoke has never come.
And you shall give it to El'azar the priest, and it shall be taken outside the camp and slaughtered before him.
And El'azar the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and sprinkle some of its blood toward the front of the tent of meeting seven times.
And the heifer shall be burned in his sight. Its skin, its flesh, and its blood, with its dung, shall be burned.

And a man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer and deposit them outside the camp in a clean place. And they shall be kept for the water of purification for the congregation of the people of Yisra'EL — it is a sin offering.
Whoever touches the dead body of any person shall be unclean seven days.
He shall cleanse himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day, and so be clean. But if he does not cleanse himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not become clean.
For the unclean they shall take some ashes of the burnt sin offering, and fresh water shall be added in a vessel.

Then a clean person shall take hyssop and dip it in the water and sprinkle it on the tent and on all the furnishings and on the persons who were there and on whoever touched the bone, or the slain or the dead or the grave.

But the man who is unclean and does not cleanse himself, that person shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly, since he has defiled the sanctuary of YHWH. Because the water for impurity has not been thrown on him, he is unclean.
And the people of Yisra'EL, the whole congregation, came into the wilderness of Tzin in the first month, and the people stayed in Kadesh. And Miryam died there and was buried there.
Now there was no water for the congregation. And they assembled themselves together against Moshe and against Aharon.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:

Take the staff, and assemble the congregation, you and Aharon your brother, and tell the rock before their eyes to yield its water. So you shall bring water out of the rock for them and give drink to the congregation and their cattle.
Then Moshe and Aharon gathered the assembly together before the rock, and he said to them: Hear now, you rebels — shall we bring water for you out of this rock?
And Moshe lifted up his hand and struck the rock with his staff twice, and water came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their livestock.

And YHWH said to Moshe and Aharon: Because you did not believe in me, to uphold me as holy in the eyes of the people of Yisra'EL, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.
And YHWH said to Moshe and Aharon at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom:
Aharon shall be gathered to his people, for he shall not enter the land that I have given to the people of Yisra'EL, because you rebelled against my command at the waters of Merivah.
Take Aharon and El'azar his son and bring them up to Mount Hor.
And strip Aharon of his garments and put them on El'azar his son. And Aharon shall be gathered to his people and shall die there.
And Moshe stripped Aharon of his garments and put them on El'azar his son. And Aharon died there on the top of the mountain. Then Moshe and El'azar came down from the mountain.
And when all the congregation saw that Aharon had perished, all the house of Yisra'EL wept for Aharon thirty days.
From Mount Hor they set out by the way to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. And the people became impatient on the way.
And the people spoke against The Creator and against Moshe: Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no food and no water, and we loathe this worthless food.
Then YHWH sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people, so that many people of Yisra'EL died.
And the people came to Moshe and said: We have sinned, for we have spoken against YHWH and against you. Pray to YHWH, that he take away the serpents from us. So Moshe prayed for the people.
And YHWH said to Moshe: Make a fiery serpent and set it on a pole, and everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live.
So Moshe made a bronze serpent and set it on a pole. And if a serpent bit anyone, he would look at the bronze serpent and live.
Then Yisra'EL sang this song: Spring up, O well — sing to it.
The well that the princes made, that the nobles of the people dug, with the scepter and with their staffs. And from the wilderness they went on to Mattanah.
Then Yisra'EL sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying:
Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into field or vineyard. We will not drink the water of a well. We will go by the King's Highway until we have passed through your territory.
But Sihon would not allow Yisra'EL to pass through his territory. He gathered all his people together and went out against Yisra'EL to the wilderness and came to Yahatz and fought against Yisra'EL.
And Yisra'EL defeated him with the edge of the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Yabbok, as far as to the Ammonites.
Then they turned and went up by the way to Bashan. And Og the king of Bashan came out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edre'i.
But YHWH said to Moshe: Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand, and all his people, and his land. And you shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.
So they defeated him and his sons and all his people, until he had no survivor left. And they possessed his land.
Then the people of Yisra'EL set out and camped in the plains of Mo'av beyond the Yarden at Yeriho.
And Balak the son of Tzippor saw all that Yisra'EL had done to the Amorites.
And Mo'av was in great dread of the people, because they were many. Mo'av was overcome with fear of the people of Yisra'EL.

He sent messengers to Bila'am the son of Be'or at Petor, which is near the River in the land of the people of Amaw, to call him, saying: Behold, a people has come out of Egypt. They cover the face of the earth, and they are dwelling opposite me.

Come now, curse this people for me, since they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I shall be able to defeat them and drive them from the land, for I know that he whom you bless is blessed, and he whom you curse is cursed.
And The Creator said to Bila'am: You shall not go with them. You shall not curse the people, for they are blessed.
And The Creator came to Bila'am at night and said to him: If the men have come to call you, rise, go with them. But only do what I tell you.
But The Creator's anger was kindled because he went, and the angel of YHWH took his stand in the way as his adversary. Now he was riding on the donkey, and his two servants were with him.
Then YHWH opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Bila'am: What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?
Then YHWH opened the eyes of Bila'am, and he saw the angel of YHWH standing in the way, with his drawn sword in his hand. And he bowed down and fell on his face.
And the angel of YHWH said to Bila'am: Go with the men, but speak only the word that I tell you. So Bila'am went on with the princes of Balak.
And Bila'am took up his discourse and said: From Aram Balak has brought me, the king of Mo'av from the eastern mountains — Come, curse Yaakov for me, and come, denounce Yisra'EL.
How can I curse whom The Creator has not cursed? How can I denounce whom YHWH has not denounced?
For from the top of the crags I see him, from the hills I behold him. Behold, a people dwelling alone, and not counting itself among the nations.
Who can count the dust of Yaakov or number the fourth part of Yisra'EL? Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his.
The Creator is not a man, that he should lie, or a son of man, that he should change his mind. Has he said, and will he not do it? Or has he spoken, and will he not fulfill it?
Behold, I received a command to bless — he has blessed, and I cannot revoke it.
He has not beheld misfortune in Yaakov, nor has he seen trouble in Yisra'EL. YHWH their Creator is with them, and the shout of a king is among them.
For there is no enchantment against Yaakov, no divination against Yisra'EL. Now it shall be said of Yaakov and Yisra'EL: What has The Creator done?
And Bila'am lifted up his eyes and saw Yisra'EL camping tribe by tribe. And the Spirit of The Creator came upon him.
And he took up his discourse and said: The oracle of Bila'am the son of Be'or, the oracle of the man whose eye is opened,
The oracle of one who hears the words of The Creator, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down with his eyes uncovered:
How lovely are your tents, O Yaakov, your encampments, O Yisra'EL.
Water shall flow from his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters. His king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.
He crouched, he lay down like a lion and like a lioness — who will rouse him up? Blessed are those who bless you, and cursed are those who curse you.
And he took up his discourse and said: The oracle of Bila'am the son of Be'or, the oracle of the man whose eye is opened,
The oracle of one who hears the words of The Creator, and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down with his eyes uncovered:

I see him, but not now — I behold him, but not near. A star shall come out of Yaakov, and a scepter shall rise out of Yisra'EL. It shall crush the forehead of Mo'av and break down all the sons of Sheth.
Edom shall be dispossessed — Se'ir also, his enemies, shall be dispossessed. Yisra'EL is doing valiantly.
Then Bila'am rose and went back to his place. And Balak also went his way.
While Yisra'EL lived in Shittim, the people began to whore with the daughters of Mo'av.
These invited the people to the sacrifices of their deities, and the people ate and bowed down to their deities.
So Yisra'EL yoked himself to Baal of Pe'or. And the anger of YHWH was kindled against Yisra'EL.

And behold, one of the people of Yisra'EL came and brought a Midyanite woman to his family, in the sight of Moshe and in the sight of the whole congregation of the people of Yisra'EL, while they were weeping in the entrance of the tent of meeting.
When Pinkhas the son of El'azar, son of Aharon the priest, saw it, he rose and left the congregation and took a spear in his hand
And went after the man of Yisra'EL into the chamber and pierced both of them, the man of Yisra'EL and the woman through her belly. Thus the plague on the people of Yisra'EL was stopped.
Nevertheless, those who died by the plague were 24,000.

Pinkhas the son of El'azar, son of Aharon the priest, has turned back my wrath from the people of Yisra'EL, in that he was jealous with my jealousy among them, so that I did not consume the people of Yisra'EL in my jealousy.
Therefore say: Behold, I give to him my covenant of peace,
And it shall be to him and to his descendants after him the covenant of a perpetual priesthood, because he was jealous for his Creator and made atonement for the people of Yisra'EL.
After the plague, YHWH said to Moshe and to El'azar the son of Aharon the priest,
Take a census of all the congregation of the people of Yisra'EL, from twenty years old and upward, by their fathers' houses, all in Yisra'EL who are able to go to war.
This was the list of the people of Yisra'EL, 601,730.
YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Among these the land shall be divided for inheritance according to the number of names.
But the land shall be divided by lot. According to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit.
These were those listed by Moshe and El'azar the priest, who listed the people of Yisra'EL in the plains of Mo'av by the Yarden at Yeriho.
But among these there was not one of those listed by Moshe and Aharon the priest, who had listed the people of Yisra'EL in the wilderness of Sinai.
For YHWH had said of them: They shall die in the wilderness. Not one of them was left, except Kalev the son of Yefunneh and Yehoshua the son of Nun.

Then drew near the daughters of Tzelofkhad the son of Hefer, son of Gil'ad, son of Makhir, son of Menasheh, from the clans of Menasheh the son of Yosef. The names of his daughters were: Makhlah, No'ah, Hoglah, Milkah, and Tirzah.
And they stood before Moshe and before El'azar the priest and before the chiefs and all the congregation, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, saying:
Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the company of those who gathered themselves against YHWH in the company of Korakh, but died for his own sin. And he had no sons.
Why should the name of our father be taken away from his clan because he had no son? Give to us a possession among our father's brothers.
Moshe brought their case before YHWH.
And YHWH said to Moshe:
The daughters of Tzelofkhad are right. You shall give them possession of an inheritance among their father's brothers and transfer the inheritance of their father to them.
And you shall speak to the people of Yisra'EL, saying: If a man dies and has no son, then you shall transfer his inheritance to his daughter.
YHWH said to Moshe: Go up into this mountain of Avarim and see the land that I have given to the people of Yisra'EL.
When you have seen it, you also shall be gathered to your people, as your brother Aharon was gathered,
Let YHWH, The Creator of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation
Who shall go out before them and come in before them, who shall lead them out and bring them in, that the congregation of YHWH may not be as sheep that have no shepherd.
So YHWH said to Moshe: Take Yehoshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand on him.
You shall invest him with some of your authority, that all the congregation of the people of Yisra'EL may obey.
And Moshe did as YHWH commanded him. He took Yehoshua and made him stand before El'azar the priest and the whole congregation,
And he laid his hands on him and commissioned him as YHWH directed through Moshe.
YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Command the people of Yisra'EL and say to them: My offering, my food for my food offerings, my pleasing aroma, you shall be careful to offer to me at its appointed time.
And you shall say to them: This is the food offering that you shall offer to YHWH — two male lambs a year old without blemish, as a regular burnt offering each day.
On the Sabbath day, two male lambs a year old without blemish, and two tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with oil, and its drink offering.
At the beginnings of your months, you shall offer a burnt offering to YHWH: two bulls from the herd, one ram, seven male lambs a year old without blemish.
On the fourteenth day of the first month is the Pesach of YHWH.
And on the fifteenth day of this month is a feast. Seven days shall unleavened bread be eaten.
On the day of the firstfruits, when you offer a grain offering of new grain to YHWH at your Feast of Weeks, you shall have a holy convocation. You shall not do any ordinary work.
On the first day of the seventh month you shall have a holy convocation. You shall not do any ordinary work. It is a day for you to blow the trumpets.
On the tenth day of this seventh month you shall have a holy convocation and afflict yourselves. You shall do no work.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month you shall have a holy convocation. You shall not do any ordinary work, and you shall keep a feast to YHWH seven days.
On the eighth day you shall have a solemn assembly. You shall not do any ordinary work.

These you shall offer to YHWH at your appointed feasts, in addition to your vow offerings and your freewill offerings, for your burnt offerings, and for your grain offerings, and for your drink offerings, and for your peace offerings.
Moshe spoke to the heads of the tribes of the people of Yisra'EL, saying: This is what YHWH has commanded.
If a man vows a vow to YHWH, or swears an oath to bind himself by a pledge, he shall not break his word. He shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth.
If a woman vows a vow to YHWH and binds herself by a pledge, while within her father's house in her youth,
And her father hears of her vow and of her pledge by which she has bound herself and says nothing to her, then all her vows shall stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself shall stand.
But any vow of a widow or of a divorced woman, anything by which she has bound herself, shall stand against her.
YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Avenge the people of Yisra'EL on the Midyanites. Afterward you shall be gathered to your people.
So Moshe spoke to the people, saying: Arm men from among you for the war, that they may go against Midyan to execute YHWH's vengeance on Midyan.
They warred against Midyan, as YHWH commanded Moshe, and killed every male.
They killed the kings of Midyan with the rest of their slain: Evi, Rekem, Tzur, Hur, and Reva — the five kings of Midyan. And they also killed Bila'am the son of Be'or with the sword.
Behold, these, on Bila'am's advice, caused the people of Yisra'EL to act treacherously against YHWH in the incident of Pe'or, and so the plague came among the congregation of YHWH.
Now the people of Re'uven and the people of Gad had a very great number of livestock, and they saw the land of Ya'zer and the land of Gil'ad, and behold, the place was a place for livestock.
And the people of Gad and the people of Re'uven came and said to Moshe and to El'azar the priest and to the chiefs of the congregation:
The land that YHWH struck down before the congregation of Yisra'EL is a land for livestock, and your servants have livestock.
And they said: If we have found favor in your sight, let this land be given to your servants for a possession. Do not take us across the Yarden.
But Moshe said to the people of Gad and to the people of Re'uven: Shall your brothers go to the war while you sit here?
Then they came near to him and said: We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock, and cities for our little ones.

But we will take up arms, ready to go before the people of Yisra'EL, until we have brought them to their place. And our little ones shall live in the fortified cities because of the inhabitants of the land.
So Moshe said to them: If you will do this, if you will take up arms to go before YHWH for the war,
And the land is subdued before YHWH — then after that you shall return and be free of obligation to YHWH and to Yisra'EL, and this land shall be your possession before YHWH.

And Moshe gave to them — to the people of Gad and to the people of Re'uven and to the half-tribe of Menasheh the son of Yosef — the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land and its cities with their territories.
These are the stages of the people of Yisra'EL, when they went out of the land of Egypt by their companies under the leadership of Moshe and Aharon.
Moshe wrote down their starting places, stage by stage, by command of YHWH, and these are their stages according to their starting places.
They set out from Ra'amses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Pesach, the people of Yisra'EL went out triumphantly in the sight of all the Egyptians.

And Aharon the priest went up Mount Hor at the command of YHWH and died there, in the fortieth year after the people of Yisra'EL had come out of the land of Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe in the plains of Mo'av by the Yarden at Yeriho, saying:
Speak to the people of Yisra'EL and say to them: When you pass over the Yarden into the land of Kena'an,
Then you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you and destroy all their figured stones and destroy all their metal images and demolish all their high places.
And you shall take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given the land to you to possess it.
YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Command the people of Yisra'EL, and say to them: When you enter the land of Kena'an — this is the land that shall fall to you for an inheritance, the land of Kena'an as defined by its borders —
Your south side shall be from the wilderness of Tzin alongside Edom, and your southern border shall run from the end of the Dead Sea on the east.
For the western border, you shall have the Great Sea and its coast. This shall be your western border.
This shall be your northern border: from the Great Sea you shall draw a line to Mount Hor.
You shall draw your eastern border from Hatzar-Enan to Shefam.
Moshe commanded the people of Yisra'EL, saying: This is the land that you shall inherit by lot, which YHWH has commanded to give to the nine tribes and to the half-tribe.
These are the names of the men who shall divide the land to you for inheritance: El'azar the priest and Yehoshua the son of Nun.
YHWH spoke to Moshe in the plains of Mo'av by the Yarden at Yeriho, saying:
Command the people of Yisra'EL to give to the Levites some of the inheritance of their possession as cities to dwell in. And you shall give to the Levites pasturelands around the cities.
The cities that you give to the Levites shall be the six cities of refuge, where you shall permit the manslayer to flee, and in addition to them you shall give forty-two cities.
And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the people of Yisra'EL and say to them: When you cross the Yarden into the land of Kena'an,
Then you shall select cities to be cities of refuge for you, that the manslayer who kills any person without intent may flee there.
The cities shall be for you a refuge from the avenger, that the manslayer may not die until he stands before the congregation for judgment.
These six cities shall be for refuge for the people of Yisra'EL, and for the stranger and for the sojourner among them, that anyone who kills any person without intent may flee there.
If anyone kills a person, the murderer shall be put to death on the evidence of witnesses. But no person shall be put to death on the testimony of one witness.
Moreover, you shall accept no ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death, but he shall be put to death.
You shall not pollute the land in which you live, for blood pollutes the land, and no atonement can be made for the land for the blood that is shed in it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.

The heads of the fathers' houses of the clan of the people of Gil'ad the son of Makhir, son of Menasheh, from the clans of the people of Yosef, came near and spoke before Moshe and before the chiefs, the heads of the fathers' houses of the people of Yisra'EL.

They said: YHWH commanded my lord to give the land for inheritance by lot to the people of Yisra'EL, and my lord was commanded by YHWH to give the inheritance of Tzelofkhad our brother to his daughters.

But if they are married to any of the sons of the other tribes of the people of Yisra'EL, then their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our fathers and added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry. So it will be taken away from the lot of our inheritance.
And Moshe commanded the people of Yisra'EL according to the word of YHWH, saying: The tribe of the people of Yosef is right.
This is what YHWH commands concerning the daughters of Tzelofkhad: Let them marry whom they think best, only they shall marry within the clan of the tribe of their father.
The daughters of Tzelofkhad did as YHWH commanded Moshe.
Makhlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milkah, and No'ah, the daughters of Tzelofkhad, married sons of their father's brothers.
These are the commandments and the rules that YHWH commanded through Moshe to the people of Yisra'EL in the plains of Mo'av by the Yarden at Yeriho.
These are the words that Moshe spoke to all Yisra'EL beyond the Yarden in the wilderness, in the Aravah opposite Suf, between Paran and Tofel, Lavan, Hatzerot, and Di-Zahav.
It is eleven days' journey from Horev by the way of Mount Se'ir to Kadesh-Barnea.
In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moshe spoke to the people of Yisra'EL according to all that YHWH had given him in commandment to them.
YHWH our Creator said to us in Horev: You have stayed long enough at this mountain.

Turn and take your journey, and go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors in the Aravah, in the hill country and in the lowland and in the Negev and by the seacoast, the land of the Kena'ani, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Perat.
See, I have set the land before you. Go in and take possession of the land that YHWH swore to your fathers, to Avraham, to Yitzhak, and to Yaakov, to give to them and to their offspring after them.
And I charged your judges at that time: Hear the cases between your brothers, and judge righteously between a man and his brother or the alien who is with him.

You shall not be partial in judgment. You shall hear the small and the great alike. You shall not be intimidated by anyone, for the judgment is The Creator's. And the case that is too hard for you, you shall bring to me, and I will hear it.
See, YHWH your Creator has set the land before you. Go up, take possession, as YHWH, The Creator of your fathers, has told you. Do not fear or be dismayed.
Yet you would not go up, but rebelled against the command of YHWH your Creator.
YHWH your Creator who goes before you will himself fight for you, just as he did for you in Egypt before your eyes,
And in the wilderness, where you have seen how YHWH your Creator carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way that you went until you came to this place.
Not one of these men of this evil generation shall see the good land that I swore to give to your fathers,
Except Kalev the son of Yefunneh. He shall see it, and to him and to his children I will give the land on which he trod, because he has wholly followed YHWH.
Even with me YHWH was angry on your account and said: You also shall not go in there.
Yehoshua the son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall enter. Encourage him, for he shall cause Yisra'EL to inherit it.
Then we turned and journeyed into the wilderness in the direction of the Red Sea, as YHWH told me. And for many days we traveled around Mount Se'ir.
And command the people: You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the people of Esav, who live in Se'ir. And they will be afraid of you. So be very careful.
Do not contend with them, for I will not give you any of their land, no, not so much as for the sole of the foot to tread on, because I have given Mount Se'ir to Esav as a possession.
For YHWH your Creator has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He knows your going through this great wilderness. These forty years YHWH your Creator has been with you. You have lacked nothing.
And YHWH said to me: Do not harass Mo'av or contend with them in battle, for I will not give you any of their land for a possession, because I have given Ar to the people of Lot for a possession.

And when you approach the territory of the people of Ammon, do not harass them or contend with them, for I will not give you any of the land of the people of Ammon as a possession, because I have given it to the sons of Lot for a possession.

Rise up, set out on your journey and go over the valley of the Arnon. Behold, I have given into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to take possession, and contend with him in battle.
But Sihon the king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him, for YHWH your Creator hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, that he might give him into your hand, as he is this day.
And YHWH our Creator gave him over to us, and we defeated him and his sons and all his people.
Then we turned and went up the way to Bashan. And Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edre'i.
But YHWH said to me: Do not fear him, for I have given him and all his people and his land into your hand. And you shall do to him as you did to Sihon the king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.

For only Og the king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Refaim. Behold, his bed was a bed of iron. Is it not in Rabbah of the Ammonites? Nine cubits was its length and four cubits its breadth, according to the common cubit.
And I pleaded with YHWH at that time, saying:
Please let me go over and see the good land beyond the Yarden, that good hill country and Lebanon.
But YHWH was angry with me because of you and would not listen to me. And YHWH said to me: Enough from you — do not speak to me of this matter again.
Go up to the top of Pisgah and lift up your eyes westward and northward and southward and eastward, and look at it with your eyes, for you shall not go over this Yarden.
But commission Yehoshua, and encourage and strengthen him, for he shall go over at the head of this people, and he shall put them in possession of the land that you shall see.

And now, O Yisra'EL, listen to the statutes and the rules that I am teaching you, and do them, that you may live, and go in and take possession of the land that YHWH, The Creator of your fathers, is giving you.
You shall not add to the word that I command you, nor take from it, that you may keep the commandments of YHWH your Creator that I command you.
For what great nation is there that has a deity so near to it as YHWH our Creator is to us, whenever we call upon him?
And what great nation is there, that has statutes and rules so righteous as all this law that I set before you today?

Only take care, and keep your soul diligently, lest you forget the things that your eyes have seen, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life. Make them known to your children and your children's children.

How on the day that you stood before YHWH your Creator at Horev, YHWH said to me: Gather the people to me, that I may let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days that they live on the earth, and that they may teach their children so.
Then YHWH spoke to you out of the midst of the fire. You heard the sound of words, but saw no form — there was only a voice.
Therefore watch yourselves very carefully. Since you saw no form on the day that YHWH spoke to you at Horev out of the midst of the fire,
Beware lest you act corruptly by making a carved image for yourselves, in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female.
Take care, lest you forget the covenant of YHWH your Creator, which he made with you, and make a carved image, the form of anything that YHWH your Creator has forbidden you.
But from there you will seek YHWH your Creator and you will find him, if you search after him with all your heart and with all your soul.
When you are in tribulation, and all these things come upon you in the latter days, you will return to YHWH your Creator and obey his voice.
For YHWH your Creator is a merciful Creator. He will not leave you or destroy you or forget the covenant with your fathers that he swore to them.

For ask now of the days that are past, which were before you, since the day that The Creator created man on the earth, and ask from one end of heaven to the other, whether such a great thing as this has ever happened or was ever heard of.
To you it was shown, that you might know that YHWH is The Creator — there is no other besides him.
Know therefore today, and lay it to your heart, that YHWH is The Creator in heaven above and on the earth beneath — there is no other.

Therefore you shall keep his statutes and his commandments, which I command you today, that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and that you may prolong your days in the land that YHWH your Creator is giving you for all time.
And Moshe summoned all Yisra'EL and said to them: Hear, O Yisra'EL, the statutes and the rules that I speak in your hearing today, and you shall learn them and be careful to do them.
YHWH our Creator made a covenant with us in Horev.
Not with our fathers did YHWH make this covenant, but with us, who are all of us here alive today.
I am YHWH your Creator, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You shall have no other deities before me.
You shall not make for yourself a carved image, or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is on the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth.
You shall not take the name of YHWH your Creator in vain, for YHWH will not hold him guiltless who takes his name in vain.
Observe the Sabbath day, to keep it holy, as YHWH your Creator commanded you.
Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

But the seventh day is a Sabbath to YHWH your Creator. On it you shall not do any work, you or your son or your daughter or your male servant or your female servant, or your ox or your donkey or any of your livestock, or the sojourner who is within your gates, that your male servant and your female servant may rest as well as you.

You shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and YHWH your Creator brought you out from there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore YHWH your Creator commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
Honor your father and your mother, as YHWH your Creator commanded you, that your days may be long, and that it may go well with you in the land that YHWH your Creator is giving you.
You shall not murder.
And you shall not commit adultery.
And you shall not steal.
And you shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

And you shall not covet your neighbor's wife. And you shall not desire your neighbor's house, his field, or his male servant, or his female servant, his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor's.

These words YHWH spoke to all your assembly at the mountain out of the midst of the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness, with a loud voice — and he added no more. And he wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
Oh that they had such a heart as this always, to fear me and to keep all my commandments, that it might go well with them and with their descendants forever.
Now this is the commandment — the statutes and the rules — that YHWH your Creator commanded me to teach you, that you may do them in the land to which you are going over, to possess it,

That you may fear YHWH your Creator, you and your son and your son's son, by keeping all his statutes and his commandments, which I command you, all the days of your life, and that your days may be long.

Hear therefore, O Yisra'EL, and be careful to do them, that it may go well with you, and that you may multiply greatly, as YHWH, The Creator of your fathers, has promised you, in a land flowing with milk and honey.
Hear, O Yisra'EL: YHWH our Creator, YHWH is one.
You shall love YHWH your Creator with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might.
And these words that I command you today shall be on your heart.
You shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise.
You shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.
You shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
And when YHWH your Creator brings you into the land that he swore to your fathers, to Avraham, to Yitzhak, and to Yaakov, to give you — with great and good cities that you did not build,
Then take care lest you forget YHWH, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
It is YHWH your Creator you shall fear. Him you shall serve and by his name you shall swear.
When your son asks you in time to come: What is the meaning of the testimonies and the statutes and the rules that YHWH our Creator has commanded you?
Then you shall say to your son: We were Pharaoh's slaves in Egypt. And YHWH brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
And YHWH commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear YHWH our Creator, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive, as we are this day.
And it will be righteousness for us, if we are careful to do all this commandment before YHWH our Creator, as he has commanded us.

When YHWH your Creator brings you into the land that you are entering to take possession of it, and clears away many nations before you — the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Kena'anim, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Yevusim, seven nations more numerous and mightier than you —
And when YHWH your Creator gives them over to you, and you defeat them, then you must devote them to complete destruction. You shall make no covenant with them and show no mercy to them.
For you are a people holy to YHWH your Creator. YHWH your Creator has chosen you to be a people for his treasured possession, out of all the peoples who are on the face of the earth.
It was not because you were more in number than any other people that YHWH set his love on you and chose you, for you were the fewest of all peoples,

But it is because YHWH loves you and is keeping the oath that he swore to your fathers, that YHWH has brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
Know therefore that YHWH your Creator is The Creator, the faithful Creator who keeps covenant and steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments, to a thousand generations,
And because you listen to these rules and keep and do them, YHWH your Creator will keep with you the covenant and the steadfast love that he swore to your fathers.

And you shall remember the whole way that YHWH your Creator has led you these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble you, testing you to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments or not.

And he humbled you and let you hunger and fed you with manna, which you did not know, nor did your fathers know, that he might make you know that man does not live by bread alone, but man lives by every word that comes from the mouth of YHWH.
Your clothing did not wear out on you and your foot did not swell these forty years.
Know then in your heart that, as a man disciplines his son, YHWH your Creator disciplines you.
For YHWH your Creator is bringing you into a good land, a land of brooks of water, of fountains and springs, flowing out in the valleys and hills,
And you shall eat and be full, and you shall bless YHWH your Creator for the good land he has given you.
Take care lest you forget YHWH your Creator by not keeping his commandments and his rules and his statutes, which I command you today,
Then your heart be lifted up, and you forget YHWH your Creator, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Beware lest you say in your heart: My power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth.
You shall remember YHWH your Creator, for it is he who gives you power to get wealth, that he may confirm his covenant that he swore to your fathers, as it is this day.
Hear, O Yisra'EL: You are to cross over the Yarden today, to go in to dispossess nations greater and mightier than you, cities great and fortified up to heaven,
Do not say in your heart, after YHWH your Creator has thrust them out before you: It is because of my righteousness that YHWH has brought me in to possess this land.

Not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart are you going in to possess their land, but because of the wickedness of these nations YHWH your Creator is driving them out from before you, and that he may confirm the word that YHWH swore to your fathers, to Avraham, to Yitzhak, and to Yaakov.
Know, therefore, that YHWH your Creator is not giving you this good land to possess because of your righteousness, for you are a stubborn people.

When I went up the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that YHWH made with you, I remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I neither ate bread nor drank water.

And YHWH gave me the two tablets of stone written with the finger of The Creator, and on them were all the words that YHWH had spoken with you on the mountain out of the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly.

Then I lay prostrate before YHWH as before, forty days and forty nights. I neither ate bread nor drank water, because of all the sin that you had committed, in doing what was evil in the sight of YHWH to provoke him to anger.
For I was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure that YHWH bore against you, so that he was ready to destroy you. But YHWH listened to me that time also.
Remember your servants, Avraham, Yitzhak, and Yaakov. Do not regard the stubbornness of this people, or their wickedness, or their sin.
At that time YHWH said to me: Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and come up to me on the mountain and make an ark of wood.

And he wrote on the tablets, in the same writing as before, the Ten Words that YHWH had spoken to you on the mountain out of the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly. And YHWH gave them to me.
Then I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark that I had made. And there they are, as YHWH commanded me.

And now, Yisra'EL, what does YHWH your Creator require of you, but to fear YHWH your Creator, to walk in all his ways, to love him, to serve YHWH your Creator with all your heart and with all your soul,
And to keep the commandments and statutes of YHWH, which I am commanding you today for your good?
Behold, to YHWH your Creator belong heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth with all that is in it.
Yet YHWH set his heart in love on your fathers and chose their offspring after them, you above all peoples, as you are this day.
Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no longer stubborn.
He executes justice for the fatherless and the widow, and loves the sojourner, giving him food and clothing.
Love the sojourner, therefore, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
You shall therefore love YHWH your Creator and keep his charge, his statutes, his rules, and his commandments always.
You shall therefore keep the whole commandment that I command you today, that you may be strong, and go in and take possession of the land that you are going over to possess,
For the land that you are entering to take possession of it is not like the land of Egypt, from which you have come, where you sowed your seed and irrigated it, like a garden of vegetables.
But the land that you are going over to possess is a land of hills and valleys, which drinks water by the rain from heaven,
A land that YHWH your Creator cares for. The eyes of YHWH your Creator are always upon it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
And if you will indeed obey my commandments that I command you today, to love YHWH your Creator, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul,
He will give the rain for your land in its season, the early rain and the later rain, that you may gather in your grain and your wine and your oil.
You shall therefore lay up these words of mine in your heart and in your soul, and you shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.
See, I am setting before you today a blessing and a curse:
The blessing, if you obey the commandments of YHWH your Creator, which I command you today,
And the curse, if you do not obey the commandments of YHWH your Creator, but turn aside from the way that I am commanding you today, to go after other deities that you have not known.
And when YHWH your Creator brings you into the land that you are entering to take possession of it, you shall set the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Eval.
These are the statutes and rules that you shall be careful to do in the land that YHWH, The Creator of your fathers, has given you to possess, all the days that you live on the earth.
You shall surely destroy all the places where the nations whom you shall dispossess served their deities, on the high mountains and on the hills and under every green tree.
You shall not worship YHWH your Creator in that way.
But you shall seek the place that YHWH your Creator will choose out of all your tribes to put his name and make his habitation there. There you shall go,

And there you shall bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution that you present, your vow offerings, your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.

Then to the place that YHWH your Creator will choose, to make his name dwell there, there you shall bring all that I command you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution that you present, and all your finest vow offerings that you vow to YHWH.
Take care that you do not offer your burnt offerings at any place that you see,
But at the place that YHWH will choose in one of your tribes, there you shall offer your burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I am commanding you.
Only be sure that you do not eat the blood, for the blood is the life, and you shall not eat the life with the flesh.
Be careful to obey all these words that I command you, that it may go well with you and with your children after you forever, when you do what is good and right in the sight of YHWH your Creator.
If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and gives you a sign or a wonder,
And the sign or wonder that he tells you comes to pass, and if he says: Let us go after other deities, which you have not known, and let us serve them,

You shall not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams. For YHWH your Creator is testing you, to know whether you love YHWH your Creator with all your heart and with all your soul.
You shall walk after YHWH your Creator and fear him and keep his commandments and obey his voice, and you shall serve him and hold fast to him.

But that prophet or that dreamer of dreams shall be put to death, because he has taught rebellion against YHWH your Creator, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you out of the house of slavery, to make you leave the way in which YHWH your Creator commanded you to walk. So you shall purge the evil from your midst.

If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or your daughter or the wife you embrace or your friend who is as your own soul entices you secretly, saying: Let us go and serve other deities, which neither you nor your fathers have known —
You shall not yield to him or listen to him, nor shall your eye pity him, nor shall you spare him, nor shall you conceal him.
You are the sons of YHWH your Creator. You shall not cut yourselves or make any baldness on your foreheads for the dead.
For you are a people holy to YHWH your Creator, and YHWH has chosen you to be a people for his treasured possession, out of all the peoples who are on the face of the earth.
You shall not eat any abomination.
These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat,
And every animal that parts the hoof and has the hoof cloven in two and chews the cud, among the animals, you may eat.
Of all that are in the waters you may eat these: whatever has fins and scales you may eat.

You shall not eat anything that has died naturally. You may give it to the sojourner who is within your towns, that he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner. For you are a people holy to YHWH your Creator.
You shall tithe all the yield of your seed that comes from the field year by year.
At the end of every three years you shall bring out all the tithe of your produce in the same year and lay it up within your towns.

And the Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance with you, and the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow, who are within your towns, shall come and eat and be filled, that YHWH your Creator may bless you in all the work of your hands that you do.
At the end of every seven years you shall grant a release.
And this is the manner of the release: every creditor shall release what he has lent to his neighbor. He shall not exact it of his neighbor, his brother, because YHWH's release has been proclaimed.
But there will be no poor among you — for YHWH will bless you in the land that YHWH your Creator is giving you for an inheritance to possess —

If among you, one of your brothers should become poor, in any of your towns within your land that YHWH your Creator is giving you, you shall not harden your heart or shut your hand against your poor brother,
But you shall open wide your hand to him and lend him sufficient for his need, whatever it may be.

Take care lest there be an unworthy thought in your heart and you say: The seventh year, the year of release is near, and your eye look grudgingly on your poor brother, and you give him nothing, and he cry to YHWH against you, and you be guilty of sin.
You shall give to him freely, and your heart shall not be grudging when you give to him, because for this YHWH your Creator will bless you in all your work and in all that you undertake.
For there will never cease to be poor in the land. Therefore I command you: You shall open wide your hand to your brother, to the needy and to the poor, in your land.
You shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and YHWH your Creator redeemed you — therefore I command you this today.
